<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-actions">actions</h1>

Endpoints to manage GitHub Actions using the REST API.

## Get GitHub Actions cache retention limit for an enterprise

<a id="opIdactions/get-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/actions/cache/retention-limit \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/actions/cache/retention-limit`

Gets GitHub Actions cache retention limit for an enterprise. All organizations and repositories under this
enterprise may not set a higher cache retention limit.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/cache#get-github-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-github-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "max_cache_retention_days": 80
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-github-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-an-enterprise-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[actions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise](#schemaactions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set GitHub Actions cache retention limit for an enterprise

<a id="opIdactions/set-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/actions/cache/retention-limit \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "max_cache_retention_days": 80
  }'
```

`PUT /enterprises/{enterprise}/actions/cache/retention-limit`

Sets GitHub Actions cache retention limit for an enterprise. All organizations and repositories under this
enterprise may not set a higher cache retention limit.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/cache#set-github-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "max_cache_retention_days": 80
}
```

<h3 id="set-github-actions-cache-retention-limit-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|[actions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise](#schemaactions-cache-retention-limit-for-enterprise)|true|none|
|» max_cache_retention_days|body|integer|false|For repositories & organizations in an enterprise, the maximum duration, in days, for which caches in a repository may be retained.|

## Get GitHub Actions cache usage for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/get-actions-cache-usage-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/cache/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/cache/usage`

Gets the total GitHub Actions cache usage for an organization.
The data fetched using this API is refreshed approximately every 5 minutes, so values returned from this endpoint may take at least 5 minutes to get updated.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/cache#get-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_active_caches_size_in_bytes": 3344284,
  "total_active_caches_count": 5
}
```

<h3 id="get-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[actions-cache-usage-org-enterprise](#schemaactions-cache-usage-org-enterprise)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List repositories with GitHub Actions cache usage for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/get-actions-cache-usage-by-repo-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/cache/usage-by-repository \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/cache/usage-by-repository`

Lists repositories and their GitHub Actions cache usage for an organization.
The data fetched using this API is refreshed approximately every 5 minutes, so values returned from this endpoint may take at least 5 minutes to get updated.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/cache#list-repositories-with-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repositories-with-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 2,
  "repository_cache_usages": [
    {
      "full_name": "octo-org/Hello-World",
      "active_caches_size_in_bytes": 2322142,
      "active_caches_count": 3
    },
    {
      "full_name": "octo-org/server",
      "active_caches_size_in_bytes": 1022142,
      "active_caches_count": 2
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-repositories-with-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-repositories-with-github-actions-cache-usage-for-an-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|
|repository_cache_usages|[[actions-cache-usage-by-repository](#schemaactions-cache-usage-by-repository)]|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List GitHub-hosted runners for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/list-hosted-runners-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/hosted-runners \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/hosted-runners`

Lists all GitHub-hosted runners configured in an organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `manage_runner:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/hosted-runners#list-github-hosted-runners-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-github-hosted-runners-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Create a GitHub-hosted runner for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/create-hosted-runner-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/hosted-runners \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Hosted runner",
    "image": {
      "id": "ubuntu-latest",
      "source": "github"
    },
    "runner_group_id": 1,
    "size": "4-core",
    "maximum_runners": 50,
    "enable_static_ip": false
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/actions/hosted-runners`

Creates a GitHub-hosted runner for an organization.
OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `manage_runners:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/hosted-runners#create-a-github-hosted-runner-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My Hosted runner",
  "image": {
    "id": "ubuntu-latest",
    "source": "github"
  },
  "runner_group_id": 1,
  "size": "4-core",
  "maximum_runners": 50,
  "enable_static_ip": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-github-hosted-runner-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the runner. Must be between 1 and 64 characters and may only contain upper and lowercase letters a-z, numbers 0-9, '.', '-', and '_'.|
|» image|body|object|true|The image of runner. To list all available images, use `GET /actions/hosted-runners/images/github-owned` or `GET /actions/hosted-runners/images/partner`.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the runner image.|
|» » source|body|string|false|The source of the runner image.|
|» » version|body|string \| null|false|The version of the runner image to deploy. This is relevant only for runners using custom images.|
|» size|body|string|true|The machine size of the runner. To list available sizes, use `GET actions/hosted-runners/machine-sizes`|
|» runner_group_id|body|integer|true|The existing runner group to add this runner to.|
|» maximum_runners|body|integer|false|The maximum amount of runners to scale up to. Runners will not auto-scale above this number. Use this setting to limit your cost.|
|» enable_static_ip|body|boolean|false|Whether this runner should be created with a static public IP. Note limit on account. To list limits on account, use `GET actions/hosted-runners/limits`|
|» image_gen|body|boolean|false|Whether this runner should be used to generate custom images.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » source|github|
|» » source|partner|
|» » source|custom|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 5,
  "name": "My hosted ubuntu runner",
  "runner_group_id": 2,
  "platform": "linux-x64",
  "image": {
    "id": "ubuntu-20.04",
    "size": 86
  },
  "machine_size_details": {
    "id": "4-core",
    "cpu_cores": 4,
    "memory_gb": 16,
    "storage_gb": 150
  },
  "status": "Ready",
  "maximum_runners": 10,
  "public_ip_enabled": true,
  "public_ips": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "prefix": "20.80.208.150",
      "length": 31
    }
  ],
  "last_active_on": "2022-10-09T23:39:01Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-github-hosted-runner-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[actions-hosted-runner](#schemaactions-hosted-runner)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update a GitHub-hosted runner for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/update-hosted-runner-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/hosted-runners/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My larger runner",
    "runner_group_id": 1,
    "maximum_runners": 50,
    "enable_static_ip": false
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/actions/hosted-runners/{hosted_runner_id}`

Updates a GitHub-hosted runner for an organization.
OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `manage_runners:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/hosted-runners#update-a-github-hosted-runner-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My larger runner",
  "runner_group_id": 1,
  "maximum_runners": 50,
  "enable_static_ip": false
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-github-hosted-runner-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|hosted_runner_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the GitHub-hosted runner.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the runner. Must be between 1 and 64 characters and may only contain upper and lowercase letters a-z, numbers 0-9, '.', '-', and '_'.|
|» runner_group_id|body|integer|false|The existing runner group to add this runner to.|
|» maximum_runners|body|integer|false|The maximum amount of runners to scale up to. Runners will not auto-scale above this number. Use this setting to limit your cost.|
|» enable_static_ip|body|boolean|false|Whether this runner should be updated with a static public IP. Note limit on account. To list limits on account, use `GET actions/hosted-runners/limits`|
|» size|body|string|false|The machine size of the runner. To list available sizes, use `GET actions/hosted-runners/machine-sizes`|
|» image_source|body|string|false|The source type of the runner image to use. Must match the source of the image specified by `image_id`. Can be one of `github`, `partner`, or `custom`.|
|» image_id|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the runner image. To list available images, use `GET /actions/hosted-runners/images/github-owned`, `GET /actions/hosted-runners/images/partner`, or `GET /actions/hosted-runners/images/custom`.|
|» image_version|body|string \| null|false|The version of the runner image to deploy. This is relevant only for runners using custom images.|
|» image_gen|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable image generation for this runner pool. When enabled, the runner pool is used to build and publish custom runner images.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» image_source|github|
|» image_source|partner|
|» image_source|custom|

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/permissions/repositories`

To use this endpoint, the organization permission policy for `enabled_repositories` must be configured to `selected`. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

## Set selected repositories enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization

<a id="opIdactions/set-selected-repositories-enabled-github-actions-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/permissions/repositories \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      32,
      42
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/permissions/repositories`

Replaces the list of selected repositories that are enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization. To use this endpoint, the organization permission policy for `enabled_repositories` must be configured to `selected`. For more information, see "[Set GitHub Actions permissions for an organization](#set-github-actions-permissions-for-an-organization)."


OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/permissions#set-selected-repositories-enabled-for-github-actions-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    32,
    42
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-enabled-for-github-actions-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|List of repository IDs to enable for GitHub Actions.|

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-enabled-for-github-actions-in-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set allowed actions and reusable workflows for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/set-allowed-actions-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/permissions/selected-actions \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "github_owned_allowed": true,
    "verified_allowed": false,
    "patterns_allowed": [
      "monalisa/octocat@*",
      "docker/*"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/permissions/selected-actions`

Sets the actions and reusable workflows that are allowed in an organization. To use this endpoint, the organization permission policy for `allowed_actions` must be configured to `selected`. For more information, see "[Set GitHub Actions permissions for an organization](#set-github-actions-permissions-for-an-organization)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/permissions#set-allowed-actions-and-reusable-workflows-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "github_owned_allowed": true,
  "verified_allowed": false,
  "patterns_allowed": [
    "monalisa/octocat@*",
    "docker/*"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-allowed-actions-and-reusable-workflows-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[selected-actions](#schemaselected-actions)|false|none|
|» github_owned_allowed|body|boolean|false|Whether GitHub-owned actions are allowed. For example, this includes the actions in the `actions` organization.|
|» verified_allowed|body|boolean|false|Whether actions from GitHub Marketplace verified creators are allowed. Set to `true` to allow all actions by GitHub Marketplace verified creators.|
|» patterns_allowed|body|[string]|false|Specifies a list of string-matching patterns to allow specific action(s) and reusable workflow(s). Wildcards, tags, and SHAs are allowed. For example, `monalisa/octocat@*`, `monalisa/octocat@v2`, `monalisa/*`.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> The `patterns_allowed` setting only applies to public repositories.|

|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

  "default_workflow_permissions": "read",

## Set default workflow permissions for an organization

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/permissions/workflow`

Sets the default workflow permissions granted to the `GITHUB_TOKEN` when running workflows in an organization, and sets if GitHub Actions
can submit approving pull request reviews. For more information, see
"[Setting the permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN for your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization#setting-the-permissions-of-the-github_token-for-your-organization)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/permissions#set-default-workflow-permissions-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_workflow_permissions": "read",
  "can_approve_pull_request_reviews": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-default-workflow-permissions-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[actions-set-default-workflow-permissions](#schemaactions-set-default-workflow-permissions)|false|none|
|» default_workflow_permissions|body|[actions-default-workflow-permissions](#schemaactions-default-workflow-permissions)|false|The default workflow permissions granted to the GITHUB_TOKEN when running workflows.|
|» can_approve_pull_request_reviews|body|[actions-can-approve-pull-request-reviews](#schemaactions-can-approve-pull-request-reviews)|false|Whether GitHub Actions can approve pull requests. Enabling this can be a security risk.|

## Create an organization Actions policy

<a id="opIdactions/create-org-actions-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Require approved actors",
    "enforcement": "active",
    "rules": [
      {
        "type": "restrict_actions_actors",
        "parameters": {
          "allowed_actors": [
            {
              "id": 1234,
              "type": "Team"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/actions/policies`

Create an Actions policy for an organization.
Omitting `workflow_path` targets all workflows without storing an explicit condition.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/policies#create-an-organization-actions-policy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Require approved actors",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "rules": [
    {
      "type": "restrict_actions_actors",
      "parameters": {
        "allowed_actors": [
          {
            "id": 1234,
            "type": "Team"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-actions-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|Request body|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the policy.|
|» enforcement|body|[repository-rule-enforcement](#schemarepository-rule-enforcement)|true|The enforcement level of the ruleset. `evaluate` allows admins to test rules before enforcing them. Admins can view insights on the Rule Insights page (`evaluate` is only available with GitHub Enterprise).|
|» conditions|body|[actions-policy-org-conditions](#schemaactions-policy-org-conditions)|false|Conditions for an organization Actions policy. The conditions object should contain one of<br>`repository_name`, `repository_id`, or `repository_property`, and may also contain `workflow_path`.|
|» rules|body|[[actions-rule](#schemaactions-rule)]|false|An array of rules within the policy.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» enforcement|disabled|
|» enforcement|active|
|» enforcement|evaluate|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Restrict workflow modifications",
  "target": "actions",
  "source_type": "Enterprise",
  "source": "enterprise",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": {
    "organization_name": {
      "include": [
        "octo-org"
      ],
      "exclude": []
    },
    "repository_name": {
      "include": [
        "octo-repo"

## Create a self-hosted runner group for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/create-self-hosted-runner-group-for-org"></a>

curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runner-groups \

    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/actions/runner-groups`

Creates a new self-hosted runner group for an organization.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runner-groups#create-a-self-hosted-runner-group-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Expensive hardware runners",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    32,
    91
  ],
  "runners": [
    9,
    2
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-self-hosted-runner-group-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the runner group.|
|» visibility|body|string|false|Visibility of a runner group. You can select all repositories, select individual repositories, or limit access to private repositories.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs that can access the runner group.|
|» runners|body|[integer]|false|List of runner IDs to add to the runner group.|
|» allows_public_repositories|body|boolean|false|Whether the runner group can be used by `public` repositories.|
|» restricted_to_workflows|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the runner group will be restricted to running only the workflows specified in the `selected_workflows` array.|
|» selected_workflows|body|[string]|false|List of workflows the runner group should be allowed to run. This setting will be ignored unless `restricted_to_workflows` is set to `true`.|
|» network_configuration_id|body|string|false|The identifier of a hosted compute network configuration.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|selected|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|

## List repository access to a self-hosted runner group in an organization

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runner-groups/0/repositories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/runner-groups/{runner_group_id}/repositories`

Lists the repositories with access to a self-hosted runner group configured in an organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runner-groups#list-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

|runner_group_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner group.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Set repository access for a self-hosted runner group in an organization

<a id="opIdactions/set-repo-access-to-self-hosted-runner-group-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runner-groups/0/repositories \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      32,
      91
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/runner-groups/{runner_group_id}/repositories`

Replaces the list of repositories that have access to a self-hosted runner group configured in an organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runner-groups#set-repository-access-for-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    32,
    91
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-repository-access-for-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|runner_group_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner group.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|List of repository IDs that can access the runner group.|

<h3 id="set-repository-access-for-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add repository access to a self-hosted runner group in an organization

<a id="opIdactions/add-repo-access-to-self-hosted-runner-group-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runner-groups/0/repositories/0 \
  -X PUT
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/runner-groups/{runner_group_id}/repositories/{repository_id}`

Adds a repository to the list of repositories that can access a self-hosted runner group. The runner group must have `visibility` set to `selected`. For more information, see "[Create a self-hosted runner group for an organization](#create-a-self-hosted-runner-group-for-an-organization)."

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runner-groups#add-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="add-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|runner_group_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner group.|
|repository_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the repository.|

<h3 id="add-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove repository access to a self-hosted runner group in an organization

<a id="opIdactions/remove-repo-access-to-self-hosted-runner-group-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runner-groups/0/repositories/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/actions/runner-groups/{runner_group_id}/repositories/{repository_id}`

Removes a repository from the list of selected repositories that can access a self-hosted runner group. The runner group must have `visibility` set to `selected`. For more information, see "[Create a self-hosted runner group for an organization](#create-a-self-hosted-runner-group-for-an-organization)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runner-groups#remove-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|runner_group_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner group.|
|repository_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the repository.|

<h3 id="remove-repository-access-to-a-self-hosted-runner-group-in-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

## List self-hosted runners in a group for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/list-self-hosted-runners-in-group-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

## Get runner version end-of-life schedule for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/get-runner-version-deprecation-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runners/deprecations/2.328.0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/actions/runners/deprecations/{version}`

Gets the end-of-life schedule for a specific runner version in an organization. Returns the runner version
and the dates when registration and runtime support will end.

Authenticated users must have admin access to the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|version|path|string|true|The runner version to look up.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "runner_version": "2.328.0",
  "registration_deprecates_at": "2026-09-29T00:00:00Z",
  "runtime_deprecates_at": "2025-12-16T17:40:26Z"
}
```

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-an-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runner_version|string|true|none|The runner version string.|
|registration_deprecates_at|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|The date after which this runner version can no longer register. Only set for runner versions below the minimum version required to register (currently 2.329.0); `null` for versions with no registration end date.|
|runtime_deprecates_at|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|The date after which jobs will no longer be dispatched to runners on this version. `null` when no newer runner release exists yet.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create configuration for a just-in-time runner for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/generate-runner-jitconfig-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runners/generate-jitconfig \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "New runner",
    "runner_group_id": 1,
    "labels": [
      "self-hosted",
      "X64",
      "macOS",
      "no-gpu"
    ],
    "work_folder": "_work"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/actions/runners/generate-jitconfig`

Generates a configuration that can be passed to the runner application at startup.

The authenticated user must have admin access to the organization.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the`admin:org` scope to use this endpoint. If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-configuration-for-a-just-in-time-runner-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New runner",
  "runner_group_id": 1,
  "labels": [
    "self-hosted",
    "X64",
    "macOS",
    "no-gpu"
  ],
  "work_folder": "_work"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new runner.|
|» runner_group_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the runner group to register the runner to.|
|» labels|body|[string]|true|The names of the custom labels to add to the runner. **Minimum items**: 1. **Maximum items**: 100.|
|» work_folder|body|string|false|The working directory to be used for job execution, relative to the runner install directory.|

{
  "runner": {

        "name": "macOS",
        "type": "read-only"
      },
      {
        "id": 21,
        "name": "no-gpu",
        "type": "custom"
      }
    ]

}

  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",

  "status": "string"

  "message": "string",

## Create a registration token for an organization

<a id="opIdactions/create-registration-token-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/runners/registration-token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/actions/runners/registration-token`

Returns a token that you can pass to the `config` script. The token expires after one hour.

For example, you can replace `TOKEN` in the following example with the registration token provided by this endpoint to configure your self-hosted runner:

```
./config.sh --url https://github.com/octo-org --token TOKEN
```

Authenticated users must have admin access to the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the`admin:org` scope to use this endpoint. If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-a-registration-token-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "token": "LLBF3JGZDX3P5PMEXLND6TS6FCWO6",
  "expires_at": "2020-01-22T12:13:35.123-08:00"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-registration-token-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[authentication-token](#schemaauthentication-token)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update an organization secret

<a id="opIdactions/create-or-update-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/actions/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "visibility": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      1296269,
      1296280
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/actions/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates an organization secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the`admin:org` scope to use this endpoint. If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "visibility": "selected",

You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. |Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the variable.|
|» value|body|string|false|The value of the variable.|
|» visibility|body|string|false|The type of repositories in the organization that can access the variable. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the variable.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository ids that can access the organization variable. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`.|

|Parameter|Value|

|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|

<h3 id="list-github-actions-caches-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Get a concurrency group for a repository

<a id="opIdactions/get-concurrency-group-for-repository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/concurrency_groups/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/concurrency_groups/{concurrency_group_name}`

Gets a specific concurrency group for a repository, including all instances in the group's queue.
Returns 404 if the group is inactive or does not exist.

Optionally, pass `ahead_of_run` or `ahead_of_job` to filter the results to only the items
ahead of the specified workflow run or job in the queue, plus the specified item itself
(returned as the last element). This is useful for determining what is blocking a particular
run or job. Returns 422 if the specified run or job is not in this concurrency group.

When using `ahead_of_run`, this matches workflow-level concurrency and any reusable-workflow
leases held on behalf of that run. Job-level leases within the run are not considered to
block the run as a whole. Use `ahead_of_job` to match job-level concurrency and reusable-workflow
leases on the job's ancestor paths.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/concurrency-groups#get-a-concurrency-group-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-concurrency-group-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|concurrency_group_name|path|string|true|The name of the concurrency group.|
|ahead_of_run|query|integer|false|Filter to items ahead of this workflow run ID in the queue, plus the run itself.<br>Matches workflow-level concurrency and reusable-workflow leases held on behalf of<br>the run. Mutually exclusive with `ahead_of_job`.|
|ahead_of_job|query|integer|false|Filter to items ahead of this job ID in the queue, plus the job itself.<br>Matches job-level concurrency and reusable-workflow leases on the job's<br>ancestor paths. Mutually exclusive with `ahead_of_run`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

    {

## Download job logs for a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/download-job-logs-for-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/jobs/0/logs
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs`

Gets a redirect URL to download a plain text file of logs for a workflow job. This link expires after 1 minute. Look
for `Location:` in the response header to find the URL for the download.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|job_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the job.|

<h3 id="download-job-logs-for-a-workflow-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|302|Found|Response|None|

## Download step logs for a workflow run job

<a id="opIdactions/download-step-logs-for-workflow-run-job"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/jobs/0/steps/0/logs
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/steps/{step_number}/logs`

Gets a redirect URL to download a plain text file of logs for a specific step of a workflow job. This link expires after
1 minute. Look for `Location:` in the response header to find the URL for the download.

This endpoint is intended for selective retrieval of one step. To download complete job logs, use the
[job logs endpoint](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#download-job-logs-for-a-workflow-run).

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#download-step-logs-for-a-workflow-run-job">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|job_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the job.|
|step_number|path|integer|true|The number assigned to the step, as shown in the `number` field of the workflow job's `steps` array.|

## Set the customization template for an OIDC subject claim for a repository

<a id="opIdactions/set-custom-oidc-sub-claim-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/oidc/customization/sub \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "use_default": false,
    "include_claim_keys": [
      "repo",
      "context"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/oidc/customization/sub`

Sets the customization template and `opt-in` or `opt-out` flag for an OpenID Connect (OIDC) subject claim for a repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/oidc#set-the-customization-template-for-an-oidc-subject-claim-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "use_default": false,
  "include_claim_keys": [
    "repo",
    "context"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-customization-template-for-an-oidc-subject-claim-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» use_default|body|boolean|true|Whether to use the default template or not. If `true`, the `include_claim_keys` field is ignored.|
|» include_claim_keys|body|[string]|false|Array of unique strings. Each claim key can only contain alphanumeric characters and underscores.|
|» use_immutable_subject|body|boolean|false|Whether to opt in to the immutable OIDC subject claim format for this repository. When `true`, OIDC tokens will use a stable, repository-ID-based `sub` claim.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-customization-template-for-an-oidc-subject-claim-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Empty response|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error-simple](#schemavalidation-error-simple)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a repository Actions policy

<a id="opIdactions/create-repo-actions-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Require approved actors",
    "enforcement": "active",
    "rules": [
      {
        "type": "restrict_actions_actors",
        "parameters": {
          "allowed_actors": [
            {
              "id": 1234,
              "type": "Team"
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/policies`

Create an Actions policy for a repository.
Omitting `workflow_path` targets all workflows without storing an explicit condition.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/policies#create-a-repository-actions-policy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Require approved actors",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "rules": [
    {
      "type": "restrict_actions_actors",
      "parameters": {
        "allowed_actors": [
          {
            "id": 1234,
            "type": "Team"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-actions-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|Request body|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the policy.|
|» enforcement|body|[repository-rule-enforcement](#schemarepository-rule-enforcement)|true|The enforcement level of the ruleset. `evaluate` allows admins to test rules before enforcing them. Admins can view insights on the Rule Insights page (`evaluate` is only available with GitHub Enterprise).|
|» conditions|body|[actions-policy-repo-conditions](#schemaactions-policy-repo-conditions)|false|Conditions for a repository Actions policy. The object may be empty to preserve or use the<br>default workflow targeting, or contain only `workflow_path`.|
|» rules|body|[[actions-rule](#schemaactions-rule)]|false|An array of rules within the policy.|

|» enforcement|active|

## Get runner version end-of-life schedule for a repository

<a id="opIdactions/get-runner-version-deprecation-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/deprecations/{version}`

Gets the end-of-life schedule for a specific runner version in a repository. Returns the runner version
and the dates when registration and runtime support will end.

Authenticated users must have admin access to the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|version|path|string|true|The runner version to look up.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "runner_version": "2.328.0",
  "registration_deprecates_at": "2026-09-29T00:00:00Z",
  "runtime_deprecates_at": "2025-12-16T17:40:26Z"
}
```

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-runner-version-end-of-life-schedule-for-a-repository-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runner_version|string|true|none|The runner version string.|
|registration_deprecates_at|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|The date after which this runner version can no longer register. Only set for runner versions below the minimum version required to register (currently 2.329.0); `null` for versions with no registration end date.|
|runtime_deprecates_at|string \| null(date-time)|false|none|The date after which jobs will no longer be dispatched to runners on this version. `null` when no newer runner release exists yet.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the`repo` scope to use this endpoint.

## Create a registration token for a repository

<a id="opIdactions/create-registration-token-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runners/registration-token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/registration-token`

Returns a token that you can pass to the `config` script. The token expires after one hour.

For example, you can replace `TOKEN` in the following example with the registration token provided by this endpoint to configure your self-hosted runner:

```
./config.sh --url https://github.com/octo-org --token TOKEN
```

Authenticated users must have admin access to the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners#create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "token": "LLBF3JGZDX3P5PMEXLND6TS6FCWO6",
  "expires_at": "2020-01-22T12:13:35.123-08:00"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-registration-token-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[authentication-token](#schemaauthentication-token)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/remove-token`

For example, you can replace `TOKEN` in the following example with the registration token provided by this endpoint to remove your self-hosted runner from an organization:

## List workflow runs for a repository

<a id="opIdactions/list-workflow-runs-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs`

Lists all workflow runs for a repository. You can use parameters to narrow the list of results. For more information about using parameters, see [Parameters](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#parameters).

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

This endpoint will return up to 1,000 results for each search when using the following parameters: `actor`, `branch`, `check_suite_id`, `created`, `event`, `head_sha`, `status`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-workflow-runs-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|actor|query|string|false|Returns someone's workflow runs. Use the login for the user who created the `push` associated with the check suite or workflow run.|
|branch|query|string|false|Returns workflow runs associated with a branch. Use the name of the branch of the `push`.|
|event|query|string|false|Returns workflow run triggered by the event you specify. For example, `push`, `pull_request` or `issue`. For more information, see "[Events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)."|
|status|query|string|false|Returns workflow runs with the check run `status` or `conclusion` that you specify. For example, a conclusion can be `success` or a status can be `in_progress`. Only GitHub Actions can set a status of `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|created|query|string(date-time)|false|Returns workflow runs created within the given date-time range. For more information on the syntax, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."|
|exclude_pull_requests|query|boolean|false|If `true` pull requests are omitted from the response (empty array).|
|check_suite_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Returns workflow runs with the `check_suite_id` that you specify.|
|head_sha|query|string|false|Only returns workflow runs that are associated with the specified `head_sha`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|completed|
|status|action_required|
|status|cancelled|
|status|failure|
|status|neutral|
|status|skipped|
|status|stale|
|status|success|
|status|timed_out|
|status|in_progress|
|status|queued|
|status|requested|
|status|waiting|
|status|pending|

## Get a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/get-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}`

Gets a specific workflow run.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#get-a-workflow-run">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-workflow-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|exclude_pull_requests|query|boolean|false|If `true` pull requests are omitted from the response (empty array).|

## Delete a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/delete-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}`

Deletes a specific workflow run.

Anyone with write access to the repository can use this endpoint.

If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#delete-a-workflow-run">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-workflow-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|

<h3 id="delete-a-workflow-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Approve a workflow run for a fork pull request

<a id="opIdactions/approve-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/approve`

Approves a workflow run for a pull request from a public fork of a first time contributor. For more information, see ["Approving workflow runs from public forks](https://docs.github.com/actions/managing-workflow-runs/approving-workflow-runs-from-public-forks)."

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#approve-a-workflow-run-for-a-fork-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="approve-a-workflow-run-for-a-fork-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="approve-a-workflow-run-for-a-fork-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List workflow run artifacts

<a id="opIdactions/list-workflow-run-artifacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/artifacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/artifacts`

Lists artifacts for a workflow run.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/artifacts#list-workflow-run-artifacts">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-workflow-run-artifacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|name|query|string|false|The name field of an artifact. When specified, only artifacts with this name will be returned.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get a workflow run attempt

<a id="opIdactions/get-workflow-run-attempt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/attempts/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/attempts/{attempt_number}`

Gets a specific workflow run attempt.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#get-a-workflow-run-attempt">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-workflow-run-attempt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|attempt_number|path|integer|true|The attempt number of the workflow run.|
|exclude_pull_requests|query|boolean|false|If `true` pull requests are omitted from the response (empty array).|

## List jobs for a workflow run attempt

<a id="opIdactions/list-jobs-for-workflow-run-attempt"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/attempts/0/jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/attempts/{attempt_number}/jobs`

Lists jobs for a specific workflow run attempt. You can use parameters to narrow the list of results. For more information
about using parameters, see [Parameters](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#parameters).

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint  with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-attempt">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-attempt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|attempt_number|path|integer|true|The attempt number of the workflow run.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List concurrency groups for a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/list-concurrency-groups-for-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/concurrency_groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/concurrency_groups`

Lists all concurrency groups associated with a workflow run or its jobs.

The set of groups is derived from the run's configuration, so a group is
included even when the run no longer has any items currently holding or
waiting in it. In that case the `group_members` array will be empty.
`total_count` reflects the number of groups the run participates in by
configuration, not the number with active items.

This differs from `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/concurrency_groups/{group_name}`,
which returns 404 when a group has no active items. That endpoint reports
the live state of a group repo-wide, while this endpoint reports the
groups associated with a specific run by configuration.

Results are sorted by group name and support cursor-based pagination via
`before` and `after`. The `after` cursor paginates forward only and does
not emit a `rel="prev"` Link; use `before` to page backward from a
forward page's `next` cursor.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/concurrency-groups#list-concurrency-groups-for-a-workflow-run">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-concurrency-groups-for-a-workflow-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

## Review custom deployment protection rules for a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/review-custom-gates-for-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

    "comment": "All health checks passed."
  }'

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/deployment_protection_rule`

Approve or reject custom deployment protection rules provided by a GitHub App for a workflow run. For more information, see "[Using environments for deployment](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/targeting-different-environments/using-environments-for-deployment)."

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub Apps can only review their own custom deployment protection rules. To approve or reject pending deployments that are waiting for review from a specific person or team, see [`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/pending_deployments`](/rest/actions/workflow-runs#review-pending-deployments-for-a-workflow-run).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

}

## List jobs for a workflow run

<a id="opIdactions/list-jobs-for-workflow-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/jobs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs`

Lists jobs for a workflow run. You can use parameters to narrow the list of results. For more information
about using parameters, see [Parameters](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#parameters).

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|
|filter|query|string|false|Filters jobs by their `completed_at` timestamp. `latest` returns jobs from the most recent execution of the workflow run. `all` returns all jobs for a workflow run, including from old executions of the workflow run.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|latest|
|filter|all|

## Get workflow run usage

<a id="opIdactions/get-workflow-run-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/runs/0/timing \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/timing`

> [!WARNING]  
> This endpoint is in the process of closing down. Refer to "[Actions Get workflow usage and Get workflow run usage endpoints closing down](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-02-actions-get-workflow-usage-and-get-workflow-run-usage-endpoints-closing-down/)" for more information.

Gets the number of billable minutes and total run time for a specific workflow run. Billable minutes only apply to workflows in private repositories that use GitHub-hosted runners. Usage is listed for each GitHub-hosted runner operating system in milliseconds. Any job re-runs are also included in the usage. The usage does not include the multiplier for macOS and Windows runners and is not rounded up to the nearest whole minute. For more information, see "[Managing billing for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/github/setting-up-and-managing-billing-and-payments-on-github/managing-billing-for-github-actions)".

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#get-workflow-run-usage">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-workflow-run-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|run_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the workflow run.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "billable": {
    "UBUNTU": {
      "total_ms": 180000,
      "jobs": 1,
      "job_runs": [
        {
          "job_id": 1,
          "duration_ms": 180000
        }
      ]
    },
    "MACOS": {
      "total_ms": 240000,
      "jobs": 4,
      "job_runs": [
        {
          "job_id": 2,
          "duration_ms": 60000
        },
        {
          "job_id": 3,
          "duration_ms": 60000
        },
        {
          "job_id": 4,
          "duration_ms": 60000
        },
        {
          "job_id": 5,
          "duration_ms": 60000
        }
      ]
    },
    "WINDOWS": {
      "total_ms": 300000,
      "jobs": 2,
      "job_runs": [
        {
          "job_id": 6,
          "duration_ms": 150000
        },
        {
          "job_id": 7,
          "duration_ms": 150000
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "run_duration_ms": 500000
}
```

## Create or update a repository secret

<a id="opIdactions/create-or-update-repo-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates a repository secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#create-or-update-a-repository-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|true|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get a repository public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#get-a-repository-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>
