## Create a workflow dispatch event

<a id="opIdactions/create-workflow-dispatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/workflows/0/dispatches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ref": "topic-branch",
    "inputs": {
      "name": "Mona the Octocat",
      "home": "San Francisco, CA"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches`

You can use this endpoint to manually trigger a GitHub Actions workflow run. You can replace `workflow_id` with the workflow file name. For example, you could use `main.yaml`.

You must configure your GitHub Actions workflow to run when the [`workflow_dispatch` webhook](/developers/webhooks-and-events/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_dispatch) event occurs. The `inputs` are configured in the workflow file. For more information about how to configure the `workflow_dispatch` event in the workflow file, see "[Events that trigger workflows](/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_dispatch)."

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "topic-branch",
  "inputs": {
    "name": "Mona the Octocat",
    "home": "San Francisco, CA"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-workflow-dispatch-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|workflow_id|path|integer \| string|true|The ID of the workflow. You can also pass the workflow file name as a string.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ref|body|string|true|The git reference for the workflow. The reference can be a branch or tag name.|
|» inputs|body|object|false|Input keys and values configured in the workflow file. The maximum number of properties is 25. Any default properties configured in the workflow file will be used when `inputs` are omitted.|
|» return_run_details|body|boolean|false|Whether the response should include the workflow run ID and URLs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "workflow_run_id": 1,
  "run_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octo-org/octo-repo/actions/runs/1",
  "html_url": "https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo/actions/runs/1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-workflow-dispatch-event-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response including the workflow run ID and URLs when `return_run_details` parameter is `true`.|[workflow-dispatch-response](#schemaworkflow-dispatch-response)|
|204|No Content|Empty response when `return_run_details` parameter is `false`.|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List workflow runs for a workflow

<a id="opIdactions/list-workflow-runs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/workflows/0/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs`

List all workflow runs for a workflow. You can replace `workflow_id` with the workflow file name. For example, you could use `main.yaml`. You can use parameters to narrow the list of results. For more information about using parameters, see [Parameters](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#parameters).

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

This endpoint will return up to 1,000 results for each search when using the following parameters: `actor`, `branch`, `check_suite_id`, `created`, `event`, `head_sha`, `status`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-workflow-runs-for-a-workflow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|workflow_id|path|integer \| string|true|The ID of the workflow. You can also pass the workflow file name as a string.|
|actor|query|string|false|Returns someone's workflow runs. Use the login for the user who created the `push` associated with the check suite or workflow run.|
|branch|query|string|false|Returns workflow runs associated with a branch. Use the name of the branch of the `push`.|
|event|query|string|false|Returns workflow run triggered by the event you specify. For example, `push`, `pull_request` or `issue`. For more information, see "[Events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)."|
|status|query|string|false|Returns workflow runs with the check run `status` or `conclusion` that you specify. For example, a conclusion can be `success` or a status can be `in_progress`. Only GitHub Actions can set a status of `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|created|query|string(date-time)|false|Returns workflow runs created within the given date-time range. For more information on the syntax, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."|
|exclude_pull_requests|query|boolean|false|If `true` pull requests are omitted from the response (empty array).|
|check_suite_id|query|integer(int64)|false|Returns workflow runs with the `check_suite_id` that you specify.|
|head_sha|query|string|false|Only returns workflow runs that are associated with the specified `head_sha`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|completed|
|status|action_required|
|status|cancelled|
|status|failure|
|status|neutral|
|status|skipped|
|status|stale|
|status|success|
|status|timed_out|
|status|in_progress|
|status|queued|
|status|requested|
|status|waiting|
|status|pending|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 1,
  "workflow_runs": [
    {
      "id": 30433642,
      "name": "Build",
      "node_id": "MDEyOldvcmtmbG93IFJ1bjI2OTI4OQ==",
      "check_suite_id": 42,
```

## Get workflow usage

<a id="opIdactions/get-workflow-usage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/actions/workflows/0/timing \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/timing`

> [!WARNING]  
> This endpoint is in the process of closing down. Refer to "[Actions Get workflow usage and Get workflow run usage endpoints closing down](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-02-actions-get-workflow-usage-and-get-workflow-run-usage-endpoints-closing-down/)" for more information.

Gets the number of billable minutes used by a specific workflow during the current billing cycle. Billable minutes only apply to workflows in private repositories that use GitHub-hosted runners. Usage is listed for each GitHub-hosted runner operating system in milliseconds. Any job re-runs are also included in the usage. The usage does not include the multiplier for macOS and Windows runners and is not rounded up to the nearest whole minute. For more information, see "[Managing billing for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/github/setting-up-and-managing-billing-and-payments-on-github/managing-billing-for-github-actions)".

You can replace `workflow_id` with the workflow file name. For example, you could use `main.yaml`.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflows#get-workflow-usage">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-workflow-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|workflow_id|path|integer \| string|true|The ID of the workflow. You can also pass the workflow file name as a string.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "billable": {
    "UBUNTU": {
      "total_ms": 180000
    },
    "MACOS": {
      "total_ms": 240000
    },
    "WINDOWS": {
      "total_ms": 300000
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-workflow-usage-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[workflow-usage](#schemaworkflow-usage)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List environment secrets

<a id="opIdactions/list-environment-secrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}/secrets`

Lists all secrets available in an environment without revealing their
encrypted values.

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#list-environment-secrets">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-environment-secrets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 2,
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "GH_TOKEN",
      "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z"
    },
    {
      "name": "GIST_ID",
      "created_at": "2020-01-10T10:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-11T11:59:22Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-environment-secrets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-environment-secrets-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|
|secrets|[[actions-secret](#schemaactions-secret)]|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

## Get an environment public key

<a id="opIdactions/get-environment-public-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string/secrets/public-key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}/secrets/public-key`

Get the public key for an environment, which you need to encrypt environment
secrets. You need to encrypt a secret before you can create or update secrets.

Anyone with read access to the repository can use this endpoint.

If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#get-an-environment-public-key">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-environment-public-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-environment-public-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[actions-public-key](#schemaactions-public-key)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

## Create or update an environment secret

<a id="opIdactions/create-or-update-environment-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates an environment secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#create-or-update-an-environment-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-environment-secret-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|true|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get an environment public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/secrets#get-an-environment-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

## Get feeds

<a id="opIdactivity/get-feeds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/feeds \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /feeds`

Lists the feeds available to the authenticated user. The response provides a URL for each feed. You can then get a specific feed by sending a request to one of the feed URLs.

*   **Timeline**: The GitHub global public timeline
*   **User**: The public timeline for any user, using `uri_template`. For more information, see "[Hypermedia](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#hypermedia)."
*   **Current user public**: The public timeline for the authenticated user
*   **Current user**: The private timeline for the authenticated user
*   **Current user actor**: The private timeline for activity created by the authenticated user
*   **Current user organizations**: The private timeline for the organizations the authenticated user is a member of.
*   **Security advisories**: A collection of public announcements that provide information about security-related vulnerabilities in software on GitHub.

By default, timeline resources are returned in JSON. You can specify the `application/atom+xml` type in the `Accept` header to return timeline resources in Atom format. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

> [!NOTE]
> Private feeds are only returned when [authenticating via Basic Auth](https://docs.github.com/rest/authentication/authenticating-to-the-rest-api#using-basic-authentication) since current feed URIs use the older, non revocable auth tokens.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/feeds#get-feeds">API method documentation</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "timeline_url": "https://github.com/timeline",
  "user_url": "https://github.com/{user}",
  "current_user_public_url": "https://github.com/octocat",
  "current_user_url": "https://github.com/octocat.private?token=abc123",
  "current_user_actor_url": "https://github.com/octocat.private.actor?token=abc123",
  "current_user_organization_url": "",
  "current_user_organization_urls": [
    "https://github.com/organizations/github/octocat.private.atom?token=abc123"
  ],
  "security_advisories_url": "https://github.com/security-advisories",
  "_links": {
    "timeline": {
      "href": "https://github.com/timeline",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    },
    "user": {
      "href": "https://github.com/{user}",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    },
    "current_user_public": {
      "href": "https://github.com/octocat",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    },
    "current_user": {
      "href": "https://github.com/octocat.private?token=abc123",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    },
    "current_user_actor": {
      "href": "https://github.com/octocat.private.actor?token=abc123",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    },
    "current_user_organization": {
      "href": "",
      "type": ""
    },
    "current_user_organizations": [
      {
        "href": "https://github.com/organizations/github/octocat.private.atom?token=abc123",
        "type": "application/atom+xml"
      }
    ],
    "security_advisories": {
      "href": "https://github.com/security-advisories",
      "type": "application/atom+xml"
    }
  }
}
```

## List notifications for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdactivity/list-notifications-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /notifications`

List all notifications for the current user, sorted by most recently updated.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|all|query|boolean|false|If `true`, show notifications marked as read.|
|participating|query|boolean|false|If `true`, only shows notifications in which the user is directly participating or mentioned.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|before|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show notifications updated before the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 50). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "repository": {
      "id": 1296269,
      "node_id": "MDEwOlJlcG9zaXRvcnkxMjk2MjY5",
      "name": "Hello-World",
      "full_name": "octocat/Hello-World",
      "owner": {
        "login": "octocat",
        "id": 1,
        "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjE=",
```

## Mark notifications as read

<a id="opIdactivity/mark-notifications-as-read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "last_read_at": "2022-06-10T00:00:00Z",
    "read": true
  }'
```

`PUT /notifications`

Marks all notifications as "read" for the current user. If the number of notifications is too large to complete in one request, you will receive a `202 Accepted` status and GitHub will run an asynchronous process to mark notifications as "read." To check whether any "unread" notifications remain, you can use the [List notifications for the authenticated user](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user) endpoint and pass the query parameter `all=false`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#mark-notifications-as-read">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "last_read_at": "2022-06-10T00:00:00Z",
  "read": true
}
```

<h3 id="mark-notifications-as-read-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» last_read_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Describes the last point that notifications were checked. Anything updated since this time will not be marked as read. If you omit this parameter, all notifications are marked as read. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. Default: The current timestamp.|
|» read|body|boolean|false|Whether the notification has been read.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Unread notifications couldn't be marked in a single request. Notifications are being marked as read in the background."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="mark-notifications-as-read-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Response|Inline|
|205|Reset Content|Reset Content|None|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Requires authentication|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h3 id="mark-notifications-as-read-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|

## Mark a thread as done

<a id="opIdactivity/mark-thread-as-done"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /notifications/threads/{thread_id}`

Marks a thread as "done." Marking a thread as "done" is equivalent to marking a notification in your notification inbox on GitHub as done: https://github.com/notifications.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#mark-a-thread-as-done">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="mark-a-thread-as-done-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|thread_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the notification thread. This corresponds to the value returned in the `id` field when you retrieve notifications (for example with the [`GET /notifications` operation](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user)).|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No content|None|

This operation does not require authentication

## Get a thread subscription for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdactivity/get-thread-subscription-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/0/subscription \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /notifications/threads/{thread_id}/subscription`

This checks to see if the current user is subscribed to a thread. You can also [get a repository subscription](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/watching#get-a-repository-subscription).

Note that subscriptions are only generated if a user is participating in a conversation--for example, they've replied to the thread, were **@mentioned**, or manually subscribe to a thread.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#get-a-thread-subscription-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-thread-subscription-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the notification thread. This corresponds to the value returned in the `id` field when you retrieve notifications (for example with the [`GET /notifications` operation](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user)).|

```json
{
  "subscribed": true,
  "ignored": false,
```

## Set a thread subscription

<a id="opIdactivity/set-thread-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/0/subscription \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ignored": false
  }'
```

`PUT /notifications/threads/{thread_id}/subscription`

If you are watching a repository, you receive notifications for all threads by default. Use this endpoint to ignore future notifications for threads until you comment on the thread or get an **@mention**.

You can also use this endpoint to subscribe to threads that you are currently not receiving notifications for or to subscribed to threads that you have previously ignored.

Unsubscribing from a conversation in a repository that you are not watching is functionally equivalent to the [Delete a thread subscription](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#delete-a-thread-subscription) endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#set-a-thread-subscription">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ignored": false
}
```

<h3 id="set-a-thread-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the notification thread. This corresponds to the value returned in the `id` field when you retrieve notifications (for example with the [`GET /notifications` operation](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user)).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ignored|body|boolean|false|Whether to block all notifications from a thread.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "subscribed": true,
  "ignored": false,
  "reason": null,
  "created_at": "2012-10-06T21:34:12Z",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/1/subscription",
  "thread_url": "https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/1"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response


## Delete a thread subscription

<a id="opIdactivity/delete-thread-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/notifications/threads/0/subscription \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /notifications/threads/{thread_id}/subscription`

Mutes all future notifications for a conversation until you comment on the thread or get an **@mention**. If you are watching the repository of the thread, you will still receive notifications. To ignore future notifications for a repository you are watching, use the [Set a thread subscription](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#set-a-thread-subscription) endpoint and set `ignore` to `true`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#delete-a-thread-subscription">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-thread-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|thread_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the notification thread. This corresponds to the value returned in the `id` field when you retrieve notifications (for example with the [`GET /notifications` operation](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user)).|

> Example responses

```json
  "message": "string",

  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

## List repository notifications for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdactivity/list-repo-notifications-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/notifications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/notifications`

Lists all notifications for the current user in the specified repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-repository-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|all|query|boolean|false|If `true`, show notifications marked as read.|
|participating|query|boolean|false|If `true`, only shows notifications in which the user is directly participating or mentioned.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|before|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show notifications updated before the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Mark repository notifications as read

<a id="opIdactivity/mark-repo-notifications-as-read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/notifications \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "last_read_at": "2019-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/notifications`

Marks all notifications in a repository as "read" for the current user. If the number of notifications is too large to complete in one request, you will receive a `202 Accepted` status and GitHub will run an asynchronous process to mark notifications as "read." To check whether any "unread" notifications remain, you can use the [List repository notifications for the authenticated user](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-repository-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user) endpoint and pass the query parameter `all=false`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#mark-repository-notifications-as-read">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "last_read_at": "2019-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="mark-repository-notifications-as-read-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» last_read_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Describes the last point that notifications were checked. Anything updated since this time will not be marked as read. If you omit this parameter, all notifications are marked as read. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. Default: The current timestamp.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Unread notifications couldn't be marked in a single request. Notifications are being marked as read in the background."
}
```

<h3 id="mark-repository-notifications-as-read-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Response|Inline|
|205|Reset Content|Reset Content|None|

<h3 id="mark-repository-notifications-as-read-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|url|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get repository star history

<a id="opIdactivity/get-stargazer-history-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/stargazers/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stargazers/history`

Returns repository stars grouped by calendar weeks, most recent first. Pages move backward toward the repository's creation week, and weeks within a page are ordered newest to oldest, so concatenating pages produces one continuous series. Weeks without stars contain zero counts. Week and day boundaries are not guaranteed to align with UTC. The `days` array contains the number of stars created on each day of the week, starting on Sunday.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/starring#get-repository-star-history">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-repository-star-history-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 30). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "week": 1754784000,
    "total": 19,
    "days": [
      0,
      12,
      7,
      0,
      0,
      0,
      0
    ]
  }
]
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-repository-star-history-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Repository star history|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

<h3 id="get-repository-star-history-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[stargazer-history](#schemastargazer-history)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set a repository subscription

<a id="opIdactivity/set-repo-subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/subscription \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "subscribed": true,
    "ignored": false
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/subscription`

If you would like to watch a repository, set `subscribed` to `true`. If you would like to ignore notifications made within a repository, set `ignored` to `true`. If you would like to stop watching a repository, [delete the repository's subscription](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/watching#delete-a-repository-subscription) completely.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/watching#set-a-repository-subscription">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subscribed": true,
  "ignored": false
}
```

<h3 id="set-a-repository-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» subscribed|body|boolean|false|Determines if notifications should be received from this repository.|
|» ignored|body|boolean|false|Determines if all notifications should be blocked from this repository.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "subscribed": true,
  "ignored": false,
  "reason": null,
  "created_at": "2012-10-06T21:34:12Z",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/example/subscription",
  "repository_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/example"
}
```

<h3 id="set-a-repository-subscription-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[repository-subscription](#schemarepository-subscription)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List events for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdactivity/list-events-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/events`

If you are authenticated as the given user, you will see your private events. Otherwise, you'll only see public events. _Optional_: use the fine-grained token with following permission set to view private events: "Events" user permissions (read).

> [!NOTE]
> This API is not built to serve real-time use cases. Depending on the time of day, event latency can be anywhere from 30s to 6h.

These are events that you've received by watching repositories and following users. If you are authenticated as the
given user, you will see private events. Otherwise, you'll only see public events.

> [!NOTE]
> This API is not built to serve real-time use cases. Depending on the time of day, event latency can be anywhere from 30s to 6h.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/events#list-events-received-by-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List repositories starred by a user

<a id="opIdactivity/list-repos-starred-by-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/starred \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/starred`

Lists repositories a user has starred.

If the specified user has a [private profile](https://docs.github.com/account-and-profile/concepts/personal-profile#private-profiles), this endpoint returns an empty list unless the request is authenticated as that user. A request authenticated as the specified user returns starred repositories visible to the token even if the token has no OAuth scopes.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.star+json`**: Includes a timestamp of when the star was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/starring#list-repositories-starred-by-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repositories-starred-by-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by. `created` means when the repository was starred. `updated` means when the repository was last pushed to.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get the authenticated app

<a id="opIdapps/get-authenticated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /app`

Returns the GitHub App associated with the authentication credentials used. To see how many app installations are associated with this GitHub App, see the `installations_count` in the response. For more details about your app's installations, see the "[List installations for the authenticated app](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#list-installations-for-the-authenticated-app)" endpoint.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

## Create a GitHub App from a manifest

<a id="opIdapps/create-from-manifest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app-manifests/string/conversions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions`

Use this endpoint to complete the handshake necessary when implementing the [GitHub App Manifest flow](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/creating-github-apps-from-a-manifest/). When you create a GitHub App with the manifest flow, you receive a temporary `code` used to retrieve the GitHub App's `id`, `pem` (private key), and `webhook_secret`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#create-a-github-app-from-a-manifest">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-a-github-app-from-a-manifest-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|path|string|true|none|

## Get a webhook configuration for an app

<a id="opIdapps/get-webhook-config-for-app"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app/hook/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /app/hook/config`

Returns the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

```json
  "url": "https://example.com/webhook"
}
```

## Update a webhook configuration for an app

<a id="opIdapps/update-webhook-config-for-app"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app/hook/config \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "content_type": "json",
    "insecure_ssl": "0",
    "secret": "********",
    "url": "https://example.com/webhook"
  }'
```

`PATCH /app/hook/config`

Updates the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/webhooks#update-a-webhook-configuration-for-an-app">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content_type": "json",
  "insecure_ssl": "0",
  "secret": "********",
  "url": "https://example.com/webhook"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-configuration-for-an-app-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» url|body|[webhook-config-url](#schemawebhook-config-url)|false|The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.|
|» content_type|body|[webhook-config-content-type](#schemawebhook-config-content-type)|false|The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.|
|» secret|body|[webhook-config-secret](#schemawebhook-config-secret)|false|If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).|
|» insecure_ssl|body|[webhook-config-insecure-ssl](#schemawebhook-config-insecure-ssl)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "content_type": "json",
  "insecure_ssl": "0",
  "secret": "********",
  "url": "https://example.com/webhook"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-configuration-for-an-app-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[webhook-config](#schemawebhook-config)|

## List deliveries for an app webhook

<a id="opIdapps/list-webhook-deliveries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app/hook/deliveries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /app/hook/deliveries`

Returns a list of webhook deliveries for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/webhooks#list-deliveries-for-an-app-webhook">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-deliveries-for-an-app-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|cursor|query|string|false|Used for pagination: the starting delivery from which the page of deliveries is fetched. Refer to the `link` header for the next and previous page cursors.|
|status|query|string|false|Returns webhook deliveries filtered by delivery outcome classification based on `status_code` range. A `status` of `success` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 200-399 range (inclusive). A `status` of `failure` returns deliveries with a `status_code` in the 400-599 range (inclusive).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|success|
|status|failure|

## Create an installation access token for an app

<a id="opIdapps/create-installation-access-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app/installations/1/access_tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repositories": [
      "Hello-World"
    ],
    "permissions": {
      "issues": "write",
      "contents": "read"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /app/installations/{installation_id}/access_tokens`

Creates an installation access token that enables a GitHub App to make authenticated API requests for the app's installation on an organization or individual account. Installation tokens expire one hour from the time you create them. Using an expired token produces a status code of `401 - Unauthorized`, and requires creating a new installation token. By default the installation token has access to all repositories that the installation can access.

> [!NOTE]
> Starting April 27, 2026, GitHub began a staged rollout of a stateless format (`ghs_APPID_JWT`) to all newly minted GitHub App installation tokens, making them more performant and improving the reliability of our API surface. If your application expects or relies on installation tokens being exactly 40 characters long, it may not handle this new token format correctly. You can now validate your apps and workflows using a temporary request header that lets you enable the token format on demand. For more information about the temporary header, see [the GitHub blog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-15-github-app-installation-tokens-per-request-override-header).

Optionally, you can use the `repositories` or `repository_ids` body parameters to specify individual repositories that the installation access token can access. If you don't use `repositories` or `repository_ids` to grant access to specific repositories, the installation access token will have access to all repositories that the installation was granted access to. The installation access token cannot be granted access to repositories that the installation was not granted access to. Up to 500 repositories can be listed in this manner.

Optionally, use the `permissions` body parameter to specify the permissions that the installation access token should have. If `permissions` is not specified, the installation access token will have all of the permissions that were granted to the app. The installation access token cannot be granted permissions that the app was not granted.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#create-an-installation-access-token-for-an-app">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    "Hello-World"
  ],
  "permissions": {
    "issues": "write",
    "contents": "read"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-installation-access-token-for-an-app-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|installation_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the installation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» repositories|body|[string]|false|List of repository names that the token should have access to|
|» repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs that the token should have access to|
|» permissions|body|[app-permissions](#schemaapp-permissions)|false|The permissions granted to the fine-grained access token.|

## Suspend an app installation

<a id="opIdapps/suspend-installation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/app/installations/1/suspended \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /app/installations/{installation_id}/suspended`

Suspends a GitHub App on a user, organization, or enterprise account, which blocks the app from accessing the account's resources. When a GitHub App is suspended, the app's access to the GitHub API or webhook events is blocked for that account.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#suspend-an-app-installation">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="suspend-an-app-installation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Delete an app authorization

<a id="opIdapps/delete-authorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/applications/Iv1.8a61f9b3a7aba766/grant \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "e72e16c7e42f292c6912e7710c838347ae178b4a"
  }'
```

`DELETE /applications/{client_id}/grant`

OAuth and GitHub application owners can revoke a grant for their application and a specific user. You must provide a valid OAuth `access_token` as an input parameter and the grant for the token's owner will be deleted.
Deleting an application's grant will also delete all OAuth tokens associated with the application for the user. Once deleted, the application will have no access to the user's account and will no longer be listed on [the application authorizations settings screen within GitHub](https://github.com/settings/applications#authorized).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/oauth-applications#delete-an-app-authorization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "e72e16c7e42f292c6912e7710c838347ae178b4a"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-app-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|path|string|true|The client ID of the GitHub app.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» access_token|body|string|true|The OAuth access token used to authenticate to the GitHub API.|

## Create a scoped access token

<a id="opIdapps/scope-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/applications/Iv1.8a61f9b3a7aba766/token/scoped \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "e72e16c7e42f292c6912e7710c838347ae178b4a",
    "target": "octocat",
    "permissions": {
      "metadata": "read",
      "issues": "write",
      "contents": "read"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /applications/{client_id}/token/scoped`

Use a non-scoped user access token to create a repository-scoped and/or permission-scoped user access token. You can specify
which repositories the token can access and which permissions are granted to the
token.

Invalid tokens will return `404 NOT FOUND`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#create-a-scoped-access-token">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access_token": "e72e16c7e42f292c6912e7710c838347ae178b4a",
  "target": "octocat",
  "permissions": {
    "metadata": "read",
    "issues": "write",
    "contents": "read"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-scoped-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|path|string|true|The client ID of the GitHub app.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» access_token|body|string|true|The access token used to authenticate to the GitHub API.|
|» target|body|string|false|The name of the user or organization to scope the user access token to. **Required** unless `target_id` is specified.|
|» target_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the user or organization to scope the user access token to. **Required** unless `target` is specified.|
|» repositories|body|[string]|false|The list of repository names to scope the user access token to. `repositories` may not be specified if `repository_ids` is specified.|
|» repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|The list of repository IDs to scope the user access token to. `repository_ids` may not be specified if `repositories` is specified.|
|» permissions|body|[app-permissions](#schemaapp-permissions)|false|The permissions granted to the fine-grained access token.|

## Revoke an installation access token

<a id="opIdapps/revoke-installation-access-token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/installation/token \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /installation/token`

Revokes the installation token you're using to authenticate as an installation and access this endpoint.

Once an installation token is revoked, the token is invalidated and cannot be used. Other endpoints that require the revoked installation token must have a new installation token to work. You can create a new token using the "[Create an installation access token for an app](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps#create-an-installation-access-token-for-an-app)" endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/installations#revoke-an-installation-access-token">API method documentation</a>

## List accounts for a plan

<a id="opIdapps/list-accounts-for-plan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/marketplace_listing/plans/0/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /marketplace_listing/plans/{plan_id}/accounts`

Returns user and organization accounts associated with the specified plan, including free plans. For per-seat pricing, you see the list of accounts that have purchased the plan, including the number of seats purchased. When someone submits a plan change that won't be processed until the end of their billing cycle, you will also see the upcoming pending change.

GitHub Apps must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint. OAuth apps must use [basic authentication](https://docs.github.com/rest/authentication/authenticating-to-the-rest-api#using-basic-authentication) with their client ID and client secret to access this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace#list-accounts-for-a-plan">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-accounts-for-a-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|plan_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the plan.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|To return the oldest accounts first, set to `asc`. Ignored without the `sort` parameter.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

|---|---|

|direction|desc|

## Get a repository installation for the authenticated app

## List app installations accessible to the user access token

<a id="opIdapps/list-installations-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/installations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/installations`

Lists installations of your GitHub App that the authenticated user has explicit permission (`:read`, `:write`, or `:admin`) to access.

The authenticated user has explicit permission to access repositories they own, repositories where they are a collaborator, and repositories that they can access through an organization membership.

You can find the permissions for the installation under the `permissions` key.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/installations#list-app-installations-accessible-to-the-user-access-token">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-app-installations-accessible-to-the-user-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List repositories accessible to the user access token

<a id="opIdapps/list-installation-repos-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/installations/1/repositories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/installations/{installation_id}/repositories`

List repositories that the authenticated user has explicit permission (`:read`, `:write`, or `:admin`) to access for an installation.

The authenticated user has explicit permission to access repositories they own, repositories where they are a collaborator, and repositories that they can access through an organization membership.

The access the user has to each repository is included in the hash under the `permissions` key.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/installations#list-repositories-accessible-to-the-user-access-token">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repositories-accessible-to-the-user-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|installation_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the installation.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Remove a repository from an app installation

<a id="opIdapps/remove-repo-from-installation-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/installations/1/repositories/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /user/installations/{installation_id}/repositories/{repository_id}`

Remove a single repository from an installation. The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository. The installation must have the `repository_selection` of `selected`.

To use a PAT (classic) with this endpoint, the `repo` scope is required

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-billing">billing</h1>

Monitor charges and usage from Actions and Packages.

## Get billing AI credit usage report for an organization

<a id="opIdbilling/get-github-billing-ai-credit-usage-report-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/organizations/string/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage`

Gets a report of AI credit usage for an organization. To use this endpoint, you must be an administrator of an organization within an enterprise or an organization account.

**Note:** Only data from the past 24 months is accessible via this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/billing/usage#get-billing-ai-credit-usage-report-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-billing-ai-credit-usage-report-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|year|query|integer|false|If specified, only return results for a single year. The value of `year` is an integer with four digits representing a year. For example, `2025`. Default value is the current year.|
|month|query|integer|false|If specified, only return results for a single month. The value of `month` is an integer between `1` and `12`. Default value is the current month. If no year is specified the default `year` is used.|
|day|query|integer|false|If specified, only return results for a single day. The value of `day` is an integer between `1` and `31`. If no `year` or `month` is specified, the default `year` and `month` are used.|
|user|query|string|false|The user name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.|
|model|query|string|false|The model name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.|
|product|query|string|false|The product name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "timePeriod": {
    "year": 2025
  },
  "organization": "GitHub",
  "usageItems": [
```

## Get all budgets for an organization

<a id="opIdbilling/get-all-budgets-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/organizations/string/settings/billing/budgets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/budgets`

Gets all budgets for an organization. The authenticated user must be an organization admin or billing manager.
Each page returns up to 100 budgets.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/billing/budgets#get-all-budgets-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-all-budgets-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|scope|query|string|false|Filter budgets by scope type.<br><br>- `organization`: Budgets scoped to the organization.<br>- `repository`: Budgets scoped to a repository.<br>- `multi_user_customer`: Universal budgets that apply to all users in the organization.<br>- `user`: Budgets scoped to an individual user.|
|user|query|string|false|Filter consumed amount details for budgets by the specified user login.|

|scope|repository|
|scope|cost_center|
|scope|multi_user_customer|

## Create a budget for an organization

<a id="opIdbilling/create-organization-budget"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/organizations/string/settings/billing/budgets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "budget_amount": 500,
    "prevent_further_usage": true,
    "budget_scope": "organization",
    "budget_entity_name": "",
    "budget_type": "ProductPricing",
    "budget_product_sku": "actions",
    "budget_alerting": {
      "will_alert": false,
      "alert_recipients": []
    }
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/budgets`

Creates a new budget for an organization. The authenticated user must be an
organization admin or billing manager.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/billing/budgets#create-a-budget-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "budget_amount": 500,
  "prevent_further_usage": true,
  "budget_scope": "organization",
  "budget_entity_name": "",
  "budget_type": "ProductPricing",
  "budget_product_sku": "actions",
  "budget_alerting": {
    "will_alert": false,
    "alert_recipients": []
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-budget-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» budget_amount|body|integer|false|The budget amount in whole dollars. For license-based products, this represents the number of licenses.|
|» prevent_further_usage|body|boolean|false|Whether to prevent additional spending once the budget is exceeded. For `user` and `multi_user_customer` scopes, this must be `true`.|
|» budget_alerting|body|object|false|none|
|» » will_alert|body|boolean|false|Whether alerts are enabled for this budget. Rejected for user-scope as alerting is always disabled for them.|
|» » alert_recipients|body|[string]|false|Array of user login names who will receive alerts. Rejected for user-scope as alerting is always disabled for them.|
|» budget_scope|body|string|false|The scope of the budget for this organization.<br><br>- `organization`: Apply the budget to the organization.<br>- `repository`: Apply the budget to a specific repository in the organization.<br>- `multi_user_customer`: Apply a universal budget to all users in the organization.<br>- `user`: Apply the budget to a single user in the organization.<br><br>`user` and `multi_user_customer` scopes are only supported when<br>`budget_product_sku` is `ai_credits` or `premium_requests`.|
|» budget_entity_name|body|string|false|The entity to apply the budget to. The expected value depends on `budget_scope`.<br><br>- `repository`: The repository name, or `owner/repo`.<br>- `organization`, `multi_user_customer`, and `user`: Not used. For `user`, set the `user` field instead.|
|» budget_type|body|string|false|The type of pricing model used by the budget. Determines how `budget_product_sku` is interpreted.<br><br>- `BundlePricing`: Covers all AI credit SKUs. Set `budget_product_sku` to `ai_credits`.<br>- `ProductPricing`: Covers all SKUs that belong to a product. Set `budget_product_sku` to a product such as `actions` or `packages`.<br>- `SkuPricing`: Covers a single, specific SKU. Set `budget_product_sku` to a SKU such as `actions_linux`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» budget_product_sku|body|string|false|A single product or SKU that will be covered in the budget|
|» user|body|string|false|The username of the user for `user` scope budgets. This field is required when `budget_scope` is `user`.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date)|false|The date the budget will expire in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Only dates in the future are accepted.<br>If not provided, the budget will not expire.<br><br>Only supported for budgets with `budget_scope` of `user`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» budget_scope|organization|
|» budget_scope|repository|
|» budget_scope|multi_user_customer|
|» budget_scope|user|
|» » *oneOf*|BundlePricing|
|» » *oneOf*|ProductPricing|
|» » *oneOf*|SkuPricing|

## Get billing premium request usage report for an organization

<a id="opIdbilling/get-github-billing-premium-request-usage-report-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/organizations/string/settings/billing/premium_request/usage \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/premium_request/usage`

Gets a report of premium request usage for an organization. To use this endpoint, you must be an administrator of an organization within an enterprise or an organization account.

**Note:** Only data from the past 24 months is accessible via this endpoint.

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-checks">checks</h1>

Rich interactions with checks run by your integrations.

## Create a check run

<a id="opIdchecks/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "mighty_readme",
    "head_sha": "ce587453ced02b1526dfb4cb910479d431683101",
    "status": "in_progress",
    "external_id": "42",
    "started_at": "2018-05-04T01:14:52Z",
    "output": {
      "title": "Mighty Readme report",
      "summary": "",
      "text": ""
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs`

Creates a new check run for a specific commit in a repository.

To create a check run, you must use a GitHub App. OAuth apps and authenticated users are not able to create a check suite.

In a check suite, GitHub limits the number of check runs with the same name to 1000. Once these check runs exceed 1000, GitHub will start to automatically delete older check runs.

> [!NOTE]
> The Checks API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#create-a-check-run">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "mighty_readme",
  "head_sha": "ce587453ced02b1526dfb4cb910479d431683101",
  "status": "in_progress",
  "external_id": "42",
  "started_at": "2018-05-04T01:14:52Z",
  "output": {
    "title": "Mighty Readme report",
    "summary": "",
    "text": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-check-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the check. For example, "code-coverage".|
|» head_sha|body|string|true|The SHA of the commit.|
|» details_url|body|string|false|The URL of the integrator's site that has the full details of the check. If the integrator does not provide this, then the homepage of the GitHub app is used.|
|» external_id|body|string|false|A reference for the run on the integrator's system.|
|» status|body|string|false|The current status of the check run. Only GitHub Actions can set a status of `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.|
|» started_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The time that the check run began. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» conclusion|body|string|false|**Required if you provide `completed_at` or a `status` of `completed`**. The final conclusion of the check. <br>**Note:** Providing `conclusion` will automatically set the `status` parameter to `completed`. You cannot change a check run conclusion to `stale`, only GitHub can set this.|
|» completed_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The time the check completed. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» output|body|object|false|Check runs can accept a variety of data in the `output` object, including a `title` and `summary` and can optionally provide descriptive details about the run.|
|» » title|body|string|true|The title of the check run.|
|» » summary|body|string|true|The summary of the check run. This parameter supports Markdown. **Maximum length**: 65535 characters.|
|» » text|body|string|false|The details of the check run. This parameter supports Markdown. **Maximum length**: 65535 characters.|
|» » annotations|body|[object]|false|Adds information from your analysis to specific lines of code. Annotations are visible on GitHub in the **Checks** and **Files changed** tab of the pull request. The Checks API limits the number of annotations to a maximum of 50 per API request. To create more than 50 annotations, you have to make multiple requests to the [Update a check run](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#update-a-check-run) endpoint. Each time you update the check run, annotations are appended to the list of annotations that already exist for the check run. GitHub Actions are limited to 10 warning annotations and 10 error annotations per step. For details about how you can view annotations on GitHub, see "[About status checks](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-status-checks#checks)".|
|» » » path|body|string|true|The path of the file to add an annotation to. For example, `assets/css/main.css`.|
|» » » start_line|body|integer|true|The start line of the annotation. Line numbers start at 1.|
|» » » end_line|body|integer|true|The end line of the annotation.|
|» » » start_column|body|integer|false|The start column of the annotation. Annotations only support `start_column` and `end_column` on the same line. Omit this parameter if `start_line` and `end_line` have different values. Column numbers start at 1.|
|» » » end_column|body|integer|false|The end column of the annotation. Annotations only support `start_column` and `end_column` on the same line. Omit this parameter if `start_line` and `end_line` have different values.|
|» » » annotation_level|body|string|true|The level of the annotation.|
|» » » message|body|string|true|A short description of the feedback for these lines of code. The maximum size is 64 KB.|
|» » » title|body|string|false|The title that represents the annotation. The maximum size is 255 characters.|
|» » » raw_details|body|string|false|Details about this annotation. The maximum size is 64 KB.|
|» » images|body|[object]|false|Adds images to the output displayed in the GitHub pull request UI.|
|» » » alt|body|string|true|The alternative text for the image.|
|» » » image_url|body|string|true|The full URL of the image.|
|» » » caption|body|string|false|A short image description.|
|» actions|body|[object]|false|Displays a button on GitHub that can be clicked to alert your app to do additional tasks. For example, a code linting app can display a button that automatically fixes detected errors. The button created in this object is displayed after the check run completes. When a user clicks the button, GitHub sends the [`check_run.requested_action` webhook](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#check_run) to your app. Each action includes a `label`, `identifier` and `description`. A maximum of three actions are accepted. To learn more about check runs and requested actions, see "[Check runs and requested actions](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-the-rest-api-to-interact-with-checks#check-runs-and-requested-actions)."|
|» » label|body|string|true|The text to be displayed on a button in the web UI. The maximum size is 20 characters.|
|» » description|body|string|true|A short explanation of what this action would do. The maximum size is 40 characters.|
|» » identifier|body|string|true|A reference for the action on the integrator's system. The maximum size is 20 characters.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» status|body|string|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|none|

## Get a check run

<a id="opIdchecks/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-runs/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}`

Gets a single check run using its `id`.

> [!NOTE]
> The Checks API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#get-a-check-run">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_run_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the check run.|

```json
      ]
    }
```
```bash
  }'
```
