|» » images|body|[object]|false|Adds images to the output displayed in the GitHub pull request UI.|
|» » » alt|body|string|true|The alternative text for the image.|
|» » » image_url|body|string|true|The full URL of the image.|
|» » » caption|body|string|false|A short image description.|
|» actions|body|[object]|false|Possible further actions the integrator can perform, which a user may trigger. Each action includes a `label`, `identifier` and `description`. A maximum of three actions are accepted. To learn more about check runs and requested actions, see "[Check runs and requested actions](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-the-rest-api-to-interact-with-checks#check-runs-and-requested-actions)."|
|» » label|body|string|true|The text to be displayed on a button in the web UI. The maximum size is 20 characters.|
|» » description|body|string|true|A short explanation of what this action would do. The maximum size is 40 characters.|
|» » identifier|body|string|true|A reference for the action on the integrator's system. The maximum size is 20 characters.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|none|

## List check run annotations

<a id="opIdchecks/list-annotations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-runs/0/annotations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}/annotations`

Lists annotations for a check run using the annotation `id`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#list-check-run-annotations">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-check-run-annotations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_run_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the check run.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "path": "README.md",
    "start_line": 2,
    "end_line": 2,
    "start_column": 5,
    "end_column": 10,
    "annotation_level": "warning",
    "title": "Spell Checker",
    "message": "Check your spelling for 'banaas'.",
    "raw_details": "Do you mean 'bananas' or 'banana'?",
    "blob_href": "https://api.github.com/repos/github/rest-api-description/git/blobs/abc"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-check-run-annotations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-check-run-annotations-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[check-annotation](#schemacheck-annotation)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

## Rerequest a check run

<a id="opIdchecks/rerequest-run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-runs/0/rerequest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs/{check_run_id}/rerequest`

Triggers GitHub to rerequest an existing check run, without pushing new code to a repository. This endpoint will trigger the [`check_run` webhook](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#check_run) event with the action `rerequested`. When a check run is `rerequested`, the `status` of the check suite it belongs to is reset to `queued` and the `conclusion` is cleared. The check run itself is not updated. GitHub apps recieving the [`check_run` webhook](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#check_run) with the `rerequested` action should then decide if the check run should be reset or updated and call the [update `check_run` endpoint](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#update-a-check-run) to update the check_run if desired.

For more information about how to re-run GitHub Actions jobs, see "[Re-run a job from a workflow run](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs#re-run-a-job-from-a-workflow-run)".

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#rerequest-a-check-run">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="rerequest-a-check-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_run_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the check run.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rerequest-a-check-run-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden if the check run is not rerequestable or doesn't belong to the authenticated GitHub App|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation error if the check run is not rerequestable|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a check suite

<a id="opIdchecks/create-suite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-suites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "head_sha": "d6fde92930d4715a2b49857d24b940956b26d2d3"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-suites`

Creates a check suite manually. By default, check suites are automatically created when you create a [check run](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs). You only need to use this endpoint for manually creating check suites when you've disabled automatic creation using "[Update repository preferences for check suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#update-repository-preferences-for-check-suites)".

> [!NOTE]
> The Checks API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

OAuth apps and personal access tokens (classic) cannot use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#create-a-check-suite">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "head_sha": "d6fde92930d4715a2b49857d24b940956b26d2d3"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-check-suite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» head_sha|body|string|true|The sha of the head commit.|

## Update repository preferences for check suites

<a id="opIdchecks/set-suites-preferences"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-suites/preferences \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "auto_trigger_checks": [
      {
        "app_id": 4,
        "setting": false
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-suites/preferences`

Changes the default automatic flow when creating check suites. By default, a check suite is automatically created each time code is pushed to a repository. When you disable the automatic creation of check suites, you can manually [Create a check suite](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#create-a-check-suite).
You must have admin permissions in the repository to set preferences for check suites.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#update-repository-preferences-for-check-suites">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_trigger_checks": [
    {
      "app_id": 4,
      "setting": false
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-repository-preferences-for-check-suites-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» auto_trigger_checks|body|[object]|false|Enables or disables automatic creation of CheckSuite events upon pushes to the repository. Enabled by default.|
|» » app_id|body|integer|true|The `id` of the GitHub App.|
|» » setting|body|boolean|true|Set to `true` to enable automatic creation of CheckSuite events upon pushes to the repository, or `false` to disable them.|

## Get a check suite

<a id="opIdchecks/get-suite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-suites/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-suites/{check_suite_id}`

Gets a single check suite using its `id`.

> [!NOTE]
> The Checks API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#get-a-check-suite">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-check-suite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_suite_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the check suite.|

## List check runs in a check suite

<a id="opIdchecks/list-for-suite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-suites/0/check-runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-suites/{check_suite_id}/check-runs`

Lists check runs for a check suite using its `id`.

> [!NOTE]
> The endpoints to manage checks only look for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#list-check-runs-in-a-check-suite">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-check-runs-in-a-check-suite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_suite_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the check suite.|
|check_name|query|string|false|Returns check runs with the specified `name`.|
|status|query|string|false|Returns check runs with the specified `status`.|
|filter|query|string|false|Filters check runs by their `completed_at` timestamp. `latest` returns the most recent check runs.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|in_progress|
|status|completed|
|filter|latest|
|filter|all|

## Rerequest a check suite

<a id="opIdchecks/rerequest-suite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/check-suites/0/rerequest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-suites/{check_suite_id}/rerequest`

Triggers GitHub to rerequest an existing check suite, without pushing new code to a repository. This endpoint will trigger the [`check_suite` webhook](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#check_suite) event with the action `rerequested`. When a check suite is `rerequested`, its `status` is reset to `queued` and the `conclusion` is cleared.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#rerequest-a-check-suite">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="rerequest-a-check-suite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|check_suite_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the check suite.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List check runs for a Git reference

<a id="opIdchecks/list-for-ref"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string/check-runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs`

Lists check runs for a commit ref. The `ref` can be a SHA, branch name, or a tag name.

> [!NOTE]
> The endpoints to manage checks only look for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array.

If there are more than 1000 check suites on a single git reference, this endpoint will limit check runs to the 1000 most recent check suites. To iterate over all possible check runs, use the [List check suites for a Git reference](https://docs.github.com/rest/reference/checks#list-check-suites-for-a-git-reference) endpoint and provide the `check_suite_id` parameter to the [List check runs in a check suite](https://docs.github.com/rest/reference/checks#list-check-runs-in-a-check-suite) endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#list-check-runs-for-a-git-reference">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-check-runs-for-a-git-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|path|string|true|The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|
|check_name|query|string|false|Returns check runs with the specified `name`.|
|status|query|string|false|Returns check runs with the specified `status`.|
|filter|query|string|false|Filters check runs by their `completed_at` timestamp. `latest` returns the most recent check runs.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|app_id|query|integer|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|queued|
|status|in_progress|
|status|completed|
|filter|latest|
|filter|all|

## List check suites for a Git reference

<a id="opIdchecks/list-suites-for-ref"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string/check-suites \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-suites`

Lists check suites for a commit `ref`. The `ref` can be a SHA, branch name, or a tag name.

> [!NOTE]
> The endpoints to manage checks only look for pushes in the repository where the check suite or check run were created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint on a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#list-check-suites-for-a-git-reference">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-check-suites-for-a-git-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|path|string|true|The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|
|app_id|query|integer|false|Filters check suites by GitHub App `id`.|
|check_name|query|string|false|Returns check runs with the specified `name`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-code-scanning">code-scanning</h1>

Retrieve code scanning alerts from a repository.

## Get the AI Scan setting for an organization

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-ai-scan-enablement-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-scanning/ai-scan \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/ai-scan`

Gets the AI Scan setting stored on an organization.

The response reports the value stored on the organization. Organization respects enterprise policy.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org`, `repo`, or `write:org` scope to use this endpoint. Organization owners can use `admin:org` or `repo`; security managers need `write:org`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-the-ai-scan-setting-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-ai-scan-setting-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pr_scan": "enabled"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-ai-scan-setting-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[code-scanning-ai-scan-org-settings](#schemacode-scanning-ai-scan-org-settings)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update the AI Scan setting for an organization

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/update-ai-scan-enablement-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-scanning/ai-scan \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "pr_scan": "enabled"
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/ai-scan`

Updates the AI Scan setting stored on an organization.

The organization respects the enterprise policy, so enabling is rejected when the enterprise disallows AI Scan.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org`, `repo`, or `write:org` scope to use this endpoint. Organization owners can use `admin:org` or `repo`; security managers need `write:org`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#update-the-ai-scan-setting-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pr_scan": "enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-ai-scan-setting-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[code-scanning-ai-scan-org-enablement-update](#schemacode-scanning-ai-scan-org-enablement-update)|true|none|
|» pr_scan|body|string|false|Whether AI Scan is enabled for the organization. Organization respects enterprise policy. Disabled organizations prevent repositories from enabling AI Scan. Enabled organizations enable AI Scan for their repositories, but individual repositories can opt out.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» pr_scan|enabled|
|» pr_scan|disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pr_scan": "enabled"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[code-scanning-ai-scan-org-settings](#schemacode-scanning-ai-scan-org-settings)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

## List code scanning alerts for an organization

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/list-alerts-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-scanning/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/alerts`

Lists code scanning alerts for the default branch for all eligible repositories in an organization. Eligible repositories are repositories that are owned by organizations that you own or for which you are a security manager. For more information, see "[Managing security managers in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/managing-security-managers-in-your-organization)."

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` or `repo`s cope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#list-code-scanning-alerts-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-code-scanning-alerts-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|tool_name|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-name](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-name)|false|The name of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_name` or `tool_guid`, but not both.|
|tool_guid|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-guid](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-guid)|false|The GUID of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. Note that some code scanning tools may not include a GUID in their analysis data. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_guid` or `tool_name`, but not both.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|state|query|[code-scanning-alert-state-query](#schemacode-scanning-alert-state-query)|false|If specified, only code scanning alerts with this state will be returned.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.|
|severity|query|[code-scanning-alert-severity](#schemacode-scanning-alert-severity)|false|If specified, only code scanning alerts with this severity will be returned.|
|assignees|query|string|false|Filter alerts by assignees. Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`).<br>Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.<br>|

## Get AI Scan enablement for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-ai-scan-enablement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/ai-scan \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/ai-scan`

Gets whether AI Scan is enabled for a repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-ai-scan-enablement-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-ai-scan-enablement-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "pr_scan": "enabled"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-ai-scan-enablement-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[code-scanning-ai-scan-enablement](#schemacode-scanning-ai-scan-enablement)|
|403|Forbidden|Response if GitHub Advanced Security is not enabled for this repository|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Update AI Scan enablement for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/update-ai-scan-enablement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/ai-scan \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "pr_scan": "enabled"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/ai-scan`

Updates whether AI Scan is enabled for a repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#update-ai-scan-enablement-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pr_scan": "enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="update-ai-scan-enablement-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[code-scanning-ai-scan-enablement-update](#schemacode-scanning-ai-scan-enablement-update)|true|none|
|» pr_scan|body|string|false|Whether to enable or disable AI Scan for the repository.|

|---|---|
|» pr_scan|enabled|

## List code scanning alerts for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/list-alerts-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts`

Lists code scanning alerts.

The response includes a `most_recent_instance` object.
This provides details of the most recent instance of this alert
for the default branch (or for the specified Git reference if you used `ref` in the request).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#list-code-scanning-alerts-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-code-scanning-alerts-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|tool_name|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-name](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-name)|false|The name of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_name` or `tool_guid`, but not both.|
|tool_guid|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-guid](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-guid)|false|The GUID of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. Note that some code scanning tools may not include a GUID in their analysis data. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_guid` or `tool_name`, but not both.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|ref|query|[code-scanning-ref](#schemacode-scanning-ref)|false|The Git reference for the results you want to list. The `ref` for a branch can be formatted either as `refs/heads/<branch name>` or simply `<branch name>`. To reference a pull request use `refs/pull/<number>/merge`.|

|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.|
|state|query|[code-scanning-alert-state-query](#schemacode-scanning-alert-state-query)|false|If specified, only code scanning alerts with this state will be returned.|
|severity|query|[code-scanning-alert-severity](#schemacode-scanning-alert-severity)|false|If specified, only code scanning alerts with this severity will be returned.|
|assignees|query|string|false|Filter alerts by assignees. Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`).<br>Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.<br>|

## Get a code scanning alert

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/alerts/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}`

Gets a single code scanning alert.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-a-code-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-code-scanning-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|

## Update a code scanning alert

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/update-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/alerts/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "state": "dismissed",
    "dismissed_reason": "false positive",
    "dismissed_comment": "This alert is not actually correct, because there'\''s a sanitizer included in the library.",
    "create_request": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}`

Updates the status of a single code scanning alert.
OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#update-a-code-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "dismissed",
  "dismissed_reason": "false positive",
  "dismissed_comment": "This alert is not actually correct, because there's a sanitizer included in the library.",
  "create_request": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-code-scanning-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» state|body|[code-scanning-alert-set-state](#schemacode-scanning-alert-set-state)|false|Sets the state of the code scanning alert. You must provide `dismissed_reason` when you set the state to `dismissed`.|
|» dismissed_reason|body|[code-scanning-alert-dismissed-reason](#schemacode-scanning-alert-dismissed-reason)|false|**Required when the state is dismissed.** The reason for dismissing or closing the alert.|
|» dismissed_comment|body|[code-scanning-alert-dismissed-comment](#schemacode-scanning-alert-dismissed-comment)|false|The dismissal comment associated with the dismissal of the alert.|
|» create_request|body|[code-scanning-alert-create-request](#schemacode-scanning-alert-create-request)|false|If `true`, attempt to create an alert dismissal request.|
|» assignees|body|[code-scanning-alert-assignees](#schemacode-scanning-alert-assignees)|false|The list of users to assign to the code scanning alert. An empty array unassigns all previous assignees from the alert.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|open|
|» state|dismissed|
|» dismissed_reason|false positive|
|» dismissed_reason|won't fix|
|» dismissed_reason|used in tests|
|» dismissed_reason|mitigated|
|» dismissed_reason|null|

## Get the status of an autofix for a code scanning alert

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-autofix"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/alerts/0/autofix \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}/autofix`

Gets the status and description of an autofix for a code scanning alert on the repository's default branch.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-the-status-of-an-autofix-for-a-code-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-status-of-an-autofix-for-a-code-scanning-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "description": "This fixes an XSS vulnerability by escaping the user input.",
```

## Create an autofix for a code scanning alert

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}/autofix`

Creates an autofix for a code scanning alert from the repository's default branch.

If a new autofix is to be created as a result of this request or is currently being generated, then this endpoint will return a 202 Accepted response.

If an autofix already exists for a given alert, then this endpoint will return a 200 OK response.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|

## List code scanning analyses for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/list-recent-analyses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/analyses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses`

Lists the details of all code scanning analyses for a repository,
starting with the most recent.
The response is paginated and you can use the `page` and `per_page` parameters
to list the analyses you're interested in.
By default 30 analyses are listed per page.

The `rules_count` field in the response give the number of rules
that were run in the analysis.
For very old analyses this data is not available,
and `0` is returned in this field.

> [!WARNING]
> **Closing down notice:** The `tool_name` field is closing down and will, in future, not be included in the response for this endpoint. The example response reflects this change. The tool name can now be found inside the `tool` field.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#list-code-scanning-analyses-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-code-scanning-analyses-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|tool_name|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-name](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-name)|false|The name of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_name` or `tool_guid`, but not both.|
|tool_guid|query|[code-scanning-analysis-tool-guid](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-tool-guid)|false|The GUID of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. Note that some code scanning tools may not include a GUID in their analysis data. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_guid` or `tool_name`, but not both.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|pr|query|integer|false|The number of the pull request for the results you want to list.|
|ref|query|[code-scanning-ref](#schemacode-scanning-ref)|false|The Git reference for the analyses you want to list. The `ref` for a branch can be formatted either as `refs/heads/<branch name>` or simply `<branch name>`. To reference a pull request use `refs/pull/<number>/merge`.|
|sarif_id|query|[code-scanning-analysis-sarif-id](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-sarif-id)|false|Filter analyses belonging to the same SARIF upload.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.|

## Get a code scanning analysis for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-analysis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/analyses/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses/{analysis_id}`

Gets a specified code scanning analysis for a repository.

The default JSON response contains fields that describe the analysis.
This includes the Git reference and commit SHA to which the analysis relates,
the datetime of the analysis, the name of the code scanning tool,
and the number of alerts.

The `rules_count` field in the default response give the number of rules
that were run in the analysis.
For very old analyses this data is not available,
and `0` is returned in this field.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/sarif+json`**: Instead of returning a summary of the analysis, this endpoint returns a subset of the analysis data that was uploaded. The data is formatted as [SARIF version 2.1.0](https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/cs01/sarif-v2.1.0-cs01.html). It also returns additional data such as the `github/alertNumber` and `github/alertUrl` properties.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-a-code-scanning-analysis-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-code-scanning-analysis-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|analysis_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the analysis, as returned from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses` operation.|

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/analyses/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses/{analysis_id}`

Deletes a specified code scanning analysis from a repository.

You can delete one analysis at a time.
To delete a series of analyses, start with the most recent analysis and work backwards.
Conceptually, the process is similar to the undo function in a text editor.

When you list the analyses for a repository,
one or more will be identified as deletable in the response:

```
"deletable": true
```

An analysis is deletable when it's the most recent in a set of analyses.
Typically, a repository will have multiple sets of analyses
for each enabled code scanning tool,
where a set is determined by a unique combination of analysis values:

* `ref`
* `tool`
* `category`

If you attempt to delete an analysis that is not the most recent in a set,
you'll get a 400 response with the message:

```
Analysis specified is not deletable.
```

The response from a successful `DELETE` operation provides you with
two alternative URLs for deleting the next analysis in the set:
`next_analysis_url` and `confirm_delete_url`.
Use the `next_analysis_url` URL if you want to avoid accidentally deleting the final analysis
in a set. This is a useful option if you want to preserve at least one analysis
for the specified tool in your repository.
Use the `confirm_delete_url` URL if you are content to remove all analyses for a tool.
When you delete the last analysis in a set, the value of `next_analysis_url` and `confirm_delete_url`
in the 200 response is `null`.

As an example of the deletion process,
let's imagine that you added a workflow that configured a particular code scanning tool
to analyze the code in a repository. This tool has added 15 analyses:
10 on the default branch, and another 5 on a topic branch.
You therefore have two separate sets of analyses for this tool.
You've now decided that you want to remove all of the analyses for the tool.
To do this you must make 15 separate deletion requests.
To start, you must find an analysis that's identified as deletable.
Each set of analyses always has one that's identified as deletable.
Having found the deletable analysis for one of the two sets,
delete this analysis and then continue deleting the next analysis in the set until they're all deleted.
Then repeat the process for the second set.
The procedure therefore consists of a nested loop:

**Outer loop**:
* List the analyses for the repository, filtered by tool.
* Parse this list to find a deletable analysis. If found:

  **Inner loop**:
  * Delete the identified analysis.
  * Parse the response for the value of `confirm_delete_url` and, if found, use this in the next iteration.

The above process assumes that you want to remove all trace of the tool's analyses from the GitHub user interface, for the specified repository, and it therefore uses the `confirm_delete_url` value. Alternatively, you could use the `next_analysis_url` value, which would leave the last analysis in each set undeleted to avoid removing a tool's analysis entirely.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#delete-a-code-scanning-analysis-from-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-code-scanning-analysis-from-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|analysis_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the analysis, as returned from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses` operation.|
|confirm_delete|query|string \| null|false|Allow deletion if the specified analysis is the last in a set. If you attempt to delete the final analysis in a set without setting this parameter to `true`, you'll get a 400 response with the message: `Analysis is last of its type and deletion may result in the loss of historical alert data. Please specify confirm_delete.`|

## Get a CodeQL database for a repository

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-codeql-database"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/codeql/databases/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/codeql/databases/{language}`

Gets a CodeQL database for a language in a repository.

By default this endpoint returns JSON metadata about the CodeQL database. To
download the CodeQL database binary content, set the `Accept` header of the request
to [`application/zip`](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types), and make sure
your HTTP client is configured to follow redirects or use the `Location` header
to make a second request to get the redirect URL.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-a-codeql-database-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|language|path|string|true|The language of the CodeQL database.|

## Create a CodeQL variant analysis

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/create-variant-analysis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/codeql/variant-analyses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "language": "csharp",
    "query_pack": "aGVsbG8=",
    "repositories": [
      "octocat/Hello-World",
      "octocat/example"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/codeql/variant-analyses`

Creates a new CodeQL variant analysis, which will run a CodeQL query against one or more repositories.

Get started by learning more about [running CodeQL queries at scale with Multi-Repository Variant Analysis](https://docs.github.com/code-security/codeql-for-vs-code/getting-started-with-codeql-for-vs-code/running-codeql-queries-at-scale-with-multi-repository-variant-analysis).

Use the `owner` and `repo` parameters in the URL to specify the controller repository that
will be used for running GitHub Actions workflows and storing the results of the CodeQL variant analysis.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#create-a-codeql-variant-analysis">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "language": "csharp",
  "query_pack": "aGVsbG8=",
  "repositories": [
    "octocat/Hello-World",
    "octocat/example"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codeql-variant-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» language|body|[code-scanning-variant-analysis-language](#schemacode-scanning-variant-analysis-language)|true|The language targeted by the CodeQL query|
|» query_pack|body|string|true|A Base64-encoded tarball containing a CodeQL query and all its dependencies|
|» repositories|body|[string]|false|List of repository names (in the form `owner/repo-name`) to run the query against. Precisely one property from `repositories`, `repository_lists` and `repository_owners` is required.|
|» repository_lists|body|[string]|false|List of repository lists to run the query against. Precisely one property from `repositories`, `repository_lists` and `repository_owners` is required.|
|» repository_owners|body|[string]|false|List of organization or user names whose repositories the query should be run against. Precisely one property from `repositories`, `repository_lists` and `repository_owners` is required.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» language|actions|
|» language|cpp|
|» language|csharp|
|» language|go|
|» language|java|
|» language|javascript|
|» language|python|
|» language|ruby|
|» language|rust|
|» language|swift|

## Get the analysis status of a repository in a CodeQL variant analysis

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-variant-analysis-repo-task"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/codeql/variant-analyses/0/repos/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/codeql/variant-analyses/{codeql_variant_analysis_id}/repos/{repo_owner}/{repo_name}`

Gets the analysis status of a repository in a CodeQL variant analysis.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-the-analysis-status-of-a-repository-in-a-codeql-variant-analysis">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-analysis-status-of-a-repository-in-a-codeql-variant-analysis-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the controller repository.|
|codeql_variant_analysis_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the variant analysis.|
|repo_owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the variant analysis repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo_name|path|string|true|The name of the variant analysis repository.|

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/default-setup`

Gets a code scanning default setup configuration.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-a-code-scanning-default-setup-configuration">API method documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Update a code scanning default setup configuration

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/update-default-setup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/default-setup \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "state": "configured",
    "threat_model": "remote_and_local"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/default-setup`

Updates a code scanning default setup configuration.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#update-a-code-scanning-default-setup-configuration">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "configured",
  "threat_model": "remote_and_local"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-code-scanning-default-setup-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[code-scanning-default-setup-update](#schemacode-scanning-default-setup-update)|true|none|
|» state|body|string|false|The desired state of code scanning default setup.|
|» runner_type|body|string|false|Runner type to be used.|
|» runner_label|body|string \| null|false|Runner label to be used if the runner type is labeled.|
|» query_suite|body|string|false|CodeQL query suite to be used.|
|» threat_model|body|string|false|Threat model to be used for code scanning analysis. Use `remote` to analyze only network sources and `remote_and_local` to include local sources like filesystem access, command-line arguments, database reads, environment variable and standard input.|
|» languages|body|[string]|false|CodeQL languages to be analyzed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|configured|
|» state|not-configured|
|» runner_type|standard|
|» runner_type|labeled|
|» query_suite|default|
|» query_suite|extended|
|» threat_model|remote|
|» threat_model|remote_and_local|
|» languages|actions|
|» languages|c-cpp|
|» languages|csharp|
|» languages|go|
|» languages|java-kotlin|
|» languages|javascript-typescript|
|» languages|python|
|» languages|ruby|
|» languages|swift|


```json
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-code-scanning-default-setup-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|202|Accepted|Response|[code-scanning-default-setup-update-response](#schemacode-scanning-default-setup-update-response)|
|403|Forbidden|Response if the repository is archived or if GitHub Advanced Security is not enabled for this repository|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|409|Conflict|Response if there is already a validation run in progress with a different default setup configuration|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Response if the configuration change cannot be made because the repository is not in the required state|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable|Inline|

## Upload an analysis as SARIF data

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/upload-sarif"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/sarifs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "commit_sha": "4b6472266afd7b471e86085a6659e8c7f2b119da",
    "ref": "refs/heads/master",
    "sarif": ""
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/sarifs`

Uploads SARIF data containing the results of a code scanning analysis to make the results available in a repository. For troubleshooting information, see "[Troubleshooting SARIF uploads](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/troubleshooting-sarif)."

There are two places where you can upload code scanning results.
 - If you upload to a pull request, for example `--ref refs/pull/42/merge` or `--ref refs/pull/42/head`, then the results appear as alerts in a pull request check. For more information, see "[Triaging code scanning alerts in pull requests](/code-security/secure-coding/triaging-code-scanning-alerts-in-pull-requests)."
 - If you upload to a branch, for example `--ref refs/heads/my-branch`, then the results appear in the **Security** tab for your repository. For more information, see "[Managing code scanning alerts for your repository](/code-security/secure-coding/managing-code-scanning-alerts-for-your-repository#viewing-the-alerts-for-a-repository)."

You must compress the SARIF-formatted analysis data that you want to upload, using `gzip`, and then encode it as a Base64 format string. For example:

```
gzip -c analysis-data.sarif | base64 -w0
```

SARIF upload supports a maximum number of entries per the following data objects, and an analysis will be rejected if any of these objects is above its maximum value. For some objects, there are additional values over which the entries will be ignored while keeping the most important entries whenever applicable.
To get the most out of your analysis when it includes data above the supported limits, try to optimize the analysis configuration. For example, for the CodeQL tool, identify and remove the most noisy queries. For more information, see "[SARIF results exceed one or more limits](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/troubleshooting-sarif/results-exceed-limit)."


| **SARIF data**                   | **Maximum values** | **Additional limits**                                                            |
|----------------------------------|:------------------:|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Runs per file                    |         20         |                                                                                  |
| Results per run                  |       25,000       | Only the top 5,000 results will be included, prioritized by severity.            |
| Rules per run                    |       25,000       |                                                                                  |
| Tool extensions per run          |        100         |                                                                                  |
| Thread Flow Locations per result |       10,000       | Only the top 1,000 Thread Flow Locations will be included, using prioritization. |
| Location per result	             |       1,000        | Only 100 locations will be included.                                             |
| Tags per rule	                   |         20         | Only 10 tags will be included.                                                   |


The `202 Accepted` response includes an `id` value.
You can use this ID to check the status of the upload by using it in the `/sarifs/{sarif_id}` endpoint.
For more information, see "[Get information about a SARIF upload](/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-information-about-a-sarif-upload)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

This endpoint is limited to 1,000 requests per hour for each user or app installation calling it.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#upload-an-analysis-as-sarif-data">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commit_sha": "4b6472266afd7b471e86085a6659e8c7f2b119da",
  "ref": "refs/heads/master",
  "sarif": ""
}
```

<h3 id="upload-an-analysis-as-sarif-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» commit_sha|body|[code-scanning-analysis-commit-sha](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-commit-sha)|true|The SHA of the commit to which the analysis you are uploading relates.|
|» ref|body|[code-scanning-ref-full](#schemacode-scanning-ref-full)|true|The full Git reference, formatted as `refs/heads/<branch name>`,<br>`refs/tags/<tag>`, `refs/pull/<number>/merge`, or `refs/pull/<number>/head`.|
|» sarif|body|[code-scanning-analysis-sarif-file](#schemacode-scanning-analysis-sarif-file)|true|A Base64 string representing the SARIF file to upload. You must first compress your SARIF file using [`gzip`](http://www.gnu.org/software/gzip/manual/gzip.html) and then translate the contents of the file into a Base64 encoding string. For more information, see "[SARIF support for code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secure-coding/sarif-support-for-code-scanning)."|
|» checkout_uri|body|string(uri)|false|The base directory used in the analysis, as it appears in the SARIF file.<br>This property is used to convert file paths from absolute to relative, so that alerts can be mapped to their correct location in the repository.|
|» started_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The time that the analysis run began. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» tool_name|body|string|false|The name of the tool used to generate the code scanning analysis. If this parameter is not used, the tool name defaults to "API". If the uploaded SARIF contains a tool GUID, this will be available for filtering using the `tool_guid` parameter of operations such as `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts`.|
|» validate|body|boolean|false|Whether the SARIF file will be validated according to the code scanning specifications.<br>This parameter is intended to help integrators ensure that the uploaded SARIF files are correctly rendered by code scanning.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "id": "47177e22-5596-11eb-80a1-c1e54ef945c6",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/hello-world/code-scanning/sarifs/47177e22-5596-11eb-80a1-c1e54ef945c6"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="upload-an-analysis-as-sarif-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Response|[code-scanning-sarifs-receipt](#schemacode-scanning-sarifs-receipt)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request if the sarif field is invalid|None|
|403|Forbidden|Response if the repository is archived or if GitHub Advanced Security is not enabled for this repository|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large if the sarif field is too large|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable|Inline|

<h3 id="upload-an-analysis-as-sarif-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **503**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|none|none|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Get information about a SARIF upload

<a id="opIdcode-scanning/get-sarif"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/code-scanning/sarifs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/sarifs/{sarif_id}`

Gets information about a SARIF upload, including the status and the URL of the analysis that was uploaded so that you can retrieve details of the analysis. For more information, see "[Get a code scanning analysis for a repository](/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-a-code-scanning-analysis-for-a-repository)."
OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint with private or public repositories, or the `public_repo` scope to use this endpoint with only public repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#get-information-about-a-sarif-upload">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-information-about-a-sarif-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|sarif_id|path|string|true|The SARIF ID obtained after uploading.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "processing_status": "complete",
  "analyses_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/hello-world/code-scanning/analyses?sarif_id=47177e22-5596-11eb-80a1-c1e54ef945c6"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-information-about-a-sarif-upload-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[code-scanning-sarifs-status](#schemacode-scanning-sarifs-status)|
|403|Forbidden|Response if GitHub Advanced Security is not enabled for this repository|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found if the sarif id does not match any upload|None|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable|Inline|

<h3 id="get-information-about-a-sarif-upload-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **503**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|none|none|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|none|

```json
{
  "key": "contributor_covenant",
  "name": "Contributor Covenant",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/codes_of_conduct/contributor_covenant",
  "body": "# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct\n\n## Our Pledge\n\nIn the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.\n\n## Our Standards\n\nExamples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:\n\n* Using welcoming and inclusive language\n* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences\n* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism\n* Focusing on what is best for the community\n* Showing empathy towards other community members\n\nExamples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:\n\n* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances\n* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks\n* Public or private harassment\n* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission\n* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting\n\n## Our Responsibilities\n\nProject maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response\n                  to any instances of unacceptable behavior.\n\nProject maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail address,\n                  posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be further defined and clarified by project maintainers.\n\n## Enforcement\n\nInstances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting the project team at [EMAIL]. The project team will review and investigate all complaints, and will respond in a way that it deems appropriate to the circumstances. The project team is obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.\n\nProject maintainers who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the project's leadership.\n\n## Attribution\n\nThis Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](http://contributor-covenant.org), version 1.4, available at [http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4](http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).\n",
  "html_url": "http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/"
}
```
