<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-dependabot">dependabot</h1>

Endpoints to manage Dependabot.

## List Dependabot alerts for an enterprise

<a id="opIddependabot/list-alerts-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/dependabot/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/dependabot/alerts`

Lists Dependabot alerts for repositories that are owned by the specified enterprise.

The authenticated user must be a member of the enterprise to use this endpoint.

Alerts are only returned for organizations in the enterprise for which you are an organization owner or a security manager. For more information about security managers, see "[Managing security managers in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/managing-security-managers-in-your-organization)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts#list-dependabot-alerts-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-dependabot-alerts-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|classification|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of vulnerability classifications. If specified, only alerts for vulnerabilities with these classifications will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `malware`, `general`|
|state|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of states. If specified, only alerts with these states will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `auto_dismissed`, `dismissed`, `fixed`, `open`|
|severity|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of severities. If specified, only alerts with these severities will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`|
|ecosystem|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of ecosystems. If specified, only alerts for these ecosystems will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `composer`, `go`, `maven`, `npm`, `nuget`, `pip`, `pub`, `rubygems`, `rust`|
|package|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of package names. If specified, only alerts for these packages will be returned.|
|epss_percentage|query|string|false|CVE Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage. Can be specified as:<br>- An exact number (`n`)<br>- Comparators such as `>n`, `<n`, `>=n`, `<=n`<br>- A range like `n..n`, where `n` is a number from 0.0 to 1.0<br><br>Filters the list of alerts based on EPSS percentages. If specified, only alerts with the provided EPSS percentages will be returned.|
|has|query|string \| [string]|false|Filters the list of alerts based on whether the alert has the given value. If specified, only alerts meeting this criterion will be returned.<br>Multiple `has` filters can be passed to filter for alerts that have all of the values. Currently, only `patch` is supported.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Filter alerts by assignees.<br>Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`) to return alerts assigned to any of the specified users.<br>Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.|
|scope|query|string|false|The scope of the vulnerable dependency. If specified, only alerts with this scope will be returned.|
|relationship|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of relationships of the vulnerable dependency to your project. If specified, only alerts with these relationships will be returned.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> We are rolling out support for dependency relationship across ecosystems. This value will be "unknown" for all dependencies in unsupported ecosystems.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.<br>`created` means when the alert was created.<br>`updated` means when the alert's state last changed.<br>`epss_percentage` sorts alerts by the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|development|
|scope|runtime|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|epss_percentage|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Lists the repositories Dependabot can access in an enterprise

<a id="opIddependabot/repository-access-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/dependabot/repository-access \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/dependabot/repository-access`

Lists repositories that enterprise admins have allowed Dependabot to access when updating dependencies across organizations in the enterprise.

The authenticated user must be an enterprise owner to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#lists-the-repositories-dependabot-can-access-in-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="lists-the-repositories-dependabot-can-access-in-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results per page.|

## Updates Dependabot's repository access list for an enterprise

<a id="opIddependabot/update-repository-access-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/dependabot/repository-access \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository_ids_to_add": [
      123,
      456
    ],
    "repository_ids_to_remove": [
      789
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /enterprises/{enterprise}/dependabot/repository-access`

Updates repositories according to the list of repositories that enterprise admins have given Dependabot access to when they've updated dependencies across organizations in the enterprise.

The authenticated user must be an enterprise owner to use this endpoint.

**Example request body:**
```json
{
  "repository_ids_to_add": [123, 456],
  "repository_ids_to_remove": [789]
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#updates-dependabots-repository-access-list-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository_ids_to_add": [
    123,
    456
  ],
  "repository_ids_to_remove": [
    789
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updates-dependabots-repository-access-list-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repository_ids_to_add|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs to add.|
|» repository_ids_to_remove|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs to remove.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

## Set the default repository access level for Dependabot in an enterprise

<a id="opIddependabot/set-repository-access-default-level-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/dependabot/repository-access/default-level \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "default_level": "public"
  }'
```

`PUT /enterprises/{enterprise}/dependabot/repository-access/default-level`

Sets the default level of repository access Dependabot will have while performing an update across organizations in the enterprise. Available values are:
- 'public' - Dependabot will only have access to public repositories, unless access is explicitly granted to non-public repositories.
- 'internal' - Dependabot will only have access to public and internal repositories, unless access is explicitly granted to private repositories.

The authenticated user must be an enterprise owner to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#set-the-default-repository-access-level-for-dependabot-in-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_level": "public"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-default-repository-access-level-for-dependabot-in-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» default_level|body|string|true|The default repository access level for Dependabot updates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» default_level|public|
|» default_level|internal|

> Example responses

```json

  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## List Dependabot alerts for an organization

<a id="opIddependabot/list-alerts-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/dependabot/alerts`

Lists Dependabot alerts for an organization.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts#list-dependabot-alerts-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-dependabot-alerts-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|classification|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of vulnerability classifications. If specified, only alerts for vulnerabilities with these classifications will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `malware`, `general`|
|state|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of states. If specified, only alerts with these states will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `auto_dismissed`, `dismissed`, `fixed`, `open`|
|severity|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of severities. If specified, only alerts with these severities will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`|
|ecosystem|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of ecosystems. If specified, only alerts for these ecosystems will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `composer`, `go`, `maven`, `npm`, `nuget`, `pip`, `pub`, `rubygems`, `rust`|
|package|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of package names. If specified, only alerts for these packages will be returned.|
|epss_percentage|query|string|false|CVE Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage. Can be specified as:<br>- An exact number (`n`)<br>- Comparators such as `>n`, `<n`, `>=n`, `<=n`<br>- A range like `n..n`, where `n` is a number from 0.0 to 1.0<br><br>Filters the list of alerts based on EPSS percentages. If specified, only alerts with the provided EPSS percentages will be returned.|
|artifact_registry_url|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of artifact registry URLs. If specified, only alerts for repositories with storage records matching these URLs will be returned.|
|artifact_registry|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of Artifact Registry name strings. If specified, only alerts for repositories with storage records matching these registries will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `jfrog-artifactory`|
|has|query|string \| [string]|false|Filters the list of alerts based on whether the alert has the given value. If specified, only alerts meeting this criterion will be returned.<br>Multiple `has` filters can be passed to filter for alerts that have all of the values.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Filter alerts by assignees.<br>Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`) to return alerts assigned to any of the specified users.<br>Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.|
|runtime_risk|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of runtime risk strings. If specified, only alerts for repositories with deployment records matching these risks will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `critical-resource`, `internet-exposed`, `sensitive-data`, `lateral-movement`|
|scope|query|string|false|The scope of the vulnerable dependency. If specified, only alerts with this scope will be returned.|
|relationship|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of relationships of the vulnerable dependency to your project. If specified, only alerts with these relationships will be returned.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> We are rolling out support for dependency relationship across ecosystems. This value will be "unknown" for all dependencies in unsupported ecosystems.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.<br>`created` means when the alert was created.<br>`updated` means when the alert's state last changed.<br>`epss_percentage` sorts alerts by the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|development|
|scope|runtime|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|epss_percentage|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Lists the repositories Dependabot can access in an organization

<a id="opIddependabot/repository-access-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/repository-access \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/dependabot/repository-access`

Lists repositories that organization admins have allowed Dependabot to access when updating dependencies.
> [!NOTE]
>    This operation supports both server-to-server and user-to-server access.
Unauthorized users will not see the existence of this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#lists-the-repositories-dependabot-can-access-in-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="lists-the-repositories-dependabot-can-access-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of results per page.|

## Updates Dependabot's repository access list for an organization

<a id="opIddependabot/update-repository-access-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/repository-access \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository_ids_to_add": [
      123,
      456
    ],
    "repository_ids_to_remove": [
      789
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/dependabot/repository-access`

Updates repositories according to the list of repositories that organization admins have given Dependabot access to when they've updated dependencies.

> [!NOTE]
>    This operation supports both server-to-server and user-to-server access.
Unauthorized users will not see the existence of this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

**Example request body:**
```json
{
  "repository_ids_to_add": [123, 456],
  "repository_ids_to_remove": [789]
}
```

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#updates-dependabots-repository-access-list-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository_ids_to_add": [
    123,
    456
  ],
  "repository_ids_to_remove": [
    789
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updates-dependabots-repository-access-list-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repository_ids_to_add|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs to add.|
|» repository_ids_to_remove|body|[integer]|false|List of repository IDs to remove.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="updates-dependabots-repository-access-list-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|204|No Content|Response|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Set the default repository access level for Dependabot

<a id="opIddependabot/set-repository-access-default-level"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/repository-access/default-level \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "default_level": "public"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/dependabot/repository-access/default-level`

Sets the default level of repository access Dependabot will have while performing an update.  Available values are:
- 'public' - Dependabot will only have access to public repositories, unless access is explicitly granted to non-public repositories.
- 'internal' - Dependabot will only have access to public and internal repositories, unless access is explicitly granted to private repositories.

Unauthorized users will not see the existence of this endpoint.

This operation supports both server-to-server and user-to-server access.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/repository-access#set-the-default-repository-access-level-for-dependabot">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_level": "public"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-default-repository-access-level-for-dependabot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» default_level|body|string|true|The default repository access level for Dependabot updates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» default_level|public|
|» default_level|internal|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

|204|No Content|Response|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## List organization secrets

<a id="opIddependabot/list-org-secrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/dependabot/secrets`

Lists all secrets available in an organization without revealing their
encrypted values.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#list-organization-secrets">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-secrets-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 3,
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "MY_ARTIFACTORY_PASSWORD",
      "created_at": "2021-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-12-10T14:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "private"
    },
    {
      "name": "NPM_TOKEN",
      "created_at": "2021-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-12-10T14:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "all"
    },
    {
      "name": "GH_TOKEN",
      "created_at": "2021-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-12-10T14:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "selected",
      "selected_repositories_url": "https://api.github.com/orgs/octo-org/dependabot/secrets/SUPER_SECRET/repositories"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|

`GET /orgs/{org}/dependabot/secrets/public-key`

## Create or update an organization secret

<a id="opIddependabot/create-or-update-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "visibility": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      1296269,
      1296280
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/dependabot/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates an organization secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    1296269,
    1296280
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-organization-secret-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get an organization public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#get-an-organization-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Which type of organization repositories have access to the organization secret. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the secret.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer \| string]|false|An array of repository ids that can access the organization secret. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#list-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-organization-secret-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set selected repositories for an organization secret

<a id="opIddependabot/set-selected-repos-for-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/dependabot/secrets/string/repositories \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      64780797
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/dependabot/secrets/{secret_name}/repositories`

Replaces all repositories for an organization secret when the `visibility`
for repository access is set to `selected`. The visibility is set when you [Create
or update an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    64780797
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array of repository ids that can access the organization secret. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can add and remove individual repositories using the [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret) and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints.|

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List Dependabot alerts for a repository

<a id="opIddependabot/list-alerts-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts`

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts#list-dependabot-alerts-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-dependabot-alerts-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|classification|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of vulnerability classifications. If specified, only alerts for vulnerabilities with these classifications will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `malware`, `general`|
|state|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of states. If specified, only alerts with these states will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `auto_dismissed`, `dismissed`, `fixed`, `open`|
|severity|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of severities. If specified, only alerts with these severities will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`|
|ecosystem|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of ecosystems. If specified, only alerts for these ecosystems will be returned.<br><br>Can be: `composer`, `go`, `maven`, `npm`, `nuget`, `pip`, `pub`, `rubygems`, `rust`|
|package|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of package names. If specified, only alerts for these packages will be returned.|
|manifest|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of full manifest paths. If specified, only alerts for these manifests will be returned.|
|epss_percentage|query|string|false|CVE Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage. Can be specified as:<br>- An exact number (`n`)<br>- Comparators such as `>n`, `<n`, `>=n`, `<=n`<br>- A range like `n..n`, where `n` is a number from 0.0 to 1.0<br><br>Filters the list of alerts based on EPSS percentages. If specified, only alerts with the provided EPSS percentages will be returned.|
|has|query|string \| [string]|false|Filters the list of alerts based on whether the alert has the given value. If specified, only alerts meeting this criterion will be returned.<br>Multiple `has` filters can be passed to filter for alerts that have all of the values. Currently, only `patch` is supported.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Filter alerts by assignees.<br>Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`) to return alerts assigned to any of the specified users.<br>Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.|
|scope|query|string|false|The scope of the vulnerable dependency. If specified, only alerts with this scope will be returned.|
|relationship|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of relationships of the vulnerable dependency to your project. If specified, only alerts with these relationships will be returned.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> We are rolling out support for dependency relationship across ecosystems. This value will be "unknown" for all dependencies in unsupported ecosystems.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.<br>`created` means when the alert was created.<br>`updated` means when the alert's state last changed.<br>`epss_percentage` sorts alerts by the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|development|
|scope|runtime|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|epss_percentage|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get a Dependabot alert

<a id="opIddependabot/get-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/alerts/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts/{alert_number}`

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts#get-a-dependabot-alert">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-dependabot-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies a Dependabot alert in its repository.<br>You can find this at the end of the URL for a Dependabot alert within GitHub,<br>or in `number` fields in the response from the<br>`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts` operation.|

## Update a Dependabot alert

<a id="opIddependabot/update-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/alerts/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "state": "dismissed",
    "dismissed_reason": "tolerable_risk",
    "dismissed_comment": "This alert is accurate but we use a sanitizer."
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts/{alert_number}`

The authenticated user must have access to security alerts for the repository to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[Granting access to security alerts](https://docs.github.com/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-security-and-analysis-settings-for-your-repository#granting-access-to-security-alerts)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts#update-a-dependabot-alert">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "dismissed",
  "dismissed_reason": "tolerable_risk",
  "dismissed_comment": "This alert is accurate but we use a sanitizer."
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dependabot-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies a Dependabot alert in its repository.<br>You can find this at the end of the URL for a Dependabot alert within GitHub,<br>or in `number` fields in the response from the<br>`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts` operation.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» state|body|string|false|The state of the Dependabot alert.<br>A `dismissed_reason` must be provided when setting the state to `dismissed`.|
|» dismissed_reason|body|string|false|**Required when `state` is `dismissed`.** A reason for dismissing the alert.|
|» dismissed_comment|body|string|false|An optional comment associated with dismissing the alert.|
|» assignees|body|[string]|false|Usernames to assign to this Dependabot Alert.<br>Pass one or more user logins to _replace_ the set of assignees on this alert.<br>Send an empty array (`[]`) to clear all assignees from the alert.<br>To assign an AI agent, include the bot login (for example, `copilot-swe-agent[bot]`).|
|» agent_assignment|body|object|false|Parameters for AI agent assignment. Only used when an agent bot login is<br>included in `assignees`. Ignored when no agent is being assigned.|
|» » custom_instructions|body|string|false|Custom instructions for the agent.|
|» » custom_agent|body|string|false|A custom agent identifier.|
|» » model|body|string|false|The model to use for the agent.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|dismissed|
|» state|open|
|» dismissed_reason|fix_started|
|» dismissed_reason|inaccurate|
|» dismissed_reason|no_bandwidth|
|» dismissed_reason|not_used|
|» dismissed_reason|tolerable_risk|

## List repository secrets

<a id="opIddependabot/list-repo-secrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/secrets`

Lists all secrets available in a repository without revealing their encrypted
values.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#list-repository-secrets">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 2,
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT",
      "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z"
    },
    {
      "name": "MY_ARTIFACTORY_PASSWORD",
      "created_at": "2020-01-10T10:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-11T11:59:22Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-1-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|
|secrets|[[dependabot-secret](#schemadependabot-secret)]|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

## Get a repository public key

<a id="opIddependabot/get-repo-public-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/secrets/public-key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/secrets/public-key`

Gets your public key, which you need to encrypt secrets. You need to
encrypt a secret before you can create or update secrets. Anyone with read access
to the repository can use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint if the repository is private.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#get-a-repository-public-key">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-repository-public-key-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-repository-public-key-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[dependabot-public-key](#schemadependabot-public-key)|

This operation does not require authentication

## Create or update a repository secret

<a id="opIddependabot/create-or-update-repo-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependabot/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates a repository secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#create-or-update-a-repository-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get a repository public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/secrets#get-a-repository-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a diff of the dependencies between commits

<a id="opIddependency-graph/diff-range"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependency-graph/compare/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/compare/{basehead}`

Gets the diff of the dependency changes between two commits of a repository, based on the changes to the dependency manifests made in those commits.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-review#get-a-diff-of-the-dependencies-between-commits">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-diff-of-the-dependencies-between-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|basehead|path|string|true|The base and head Git revisions to compare. The Git revisions will be resolved to commit SHAs. Named revisions will be resolved to their corresponding HEAD commits, and an appropriate merge base will be determined. This parameter expects the format `{base}...{head}`.|
|name|query|string|false|The full path, relative to the repository root, of the dependency manifest file.|

## Export a software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository.

<a id="opIddependency-graph/export-sbom"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependency-graph/sbom \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> [!WARNING]
> **Closing down notice:** This operation is closing down and will not be accessible after November 13, 2026. Please migrate to the asynchronous flow. Use "[Request generation of a software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/sboms#request-generation-of-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository)" to trigger the report, then "[Fetch a software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/sboms#fetch-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository)" to retrieve it. For more information, see the [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-12-synchronous-sbom-api-deprecated/).

Exports the software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository in SPDX JSON format.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/sboms#export-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Fetch a software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository.

<a id="opIddependency-graph/fetch-sbom-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/{sbom_uuid}`

Fetches a previously generated software bill of materials (SBOM) for a repository.
When the SBOM is ready, the response is a 302 redirect to a temporary download URL for the SBOM in SPDX JSON format.
The generated SBOM report may be retained for up to one week from the original request.
The temporary download URL returned by this endpoint expires separately, and its expiry is set when the fetch request is made.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/sboms#fetch-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="fetch-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|sbom_uuid|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the SBOM export.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-a-software-bill-of-materials-sbom-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|SBOM is still being processed, no content is returned.|None|
|302|Found|Redirects to a temporary download URL for the completed SBOM.|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|302|Location|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a snapshot of dependencies for a repository

<a id="opIddependency-graph/create-repository-snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dependency-graph/snapshots \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "version": 0,
    "sha": "ce587453ced02b1526dfb4cb910479d431683101",
    "ref": "refs/heads/main",
    "job": {
      "correlator": "yourworkflowname_youractionname",
      "id": "yourrunid"
    },
    "detector": {
      "name": "octo-detector",
      "version": "0.0.1",
      "url": "https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo"
    },
    "scanned": "2022-06-14T20:25:00Z",
    "manifests": {
      "package-lock.json": {
        "name": "package-lock.json",
        "file": {
          "source_location": "src/package-lock.json"
        },
        "resolved": {
          "@actions/core": {
            "package_url": "pkg:/npm/%40actions/core@1.1.9",
            "dependencies": [
              "@actions/http-client"
            ]
          },
          "@actions/http-client": {
            "package_url": "pkg:/npm/%40actions/http-client@1.0.7",
            "dependencies": [
              "tunnel"
            ]
          },
          "tunnel": {
            "package_url": "pkg:/npm/tunnel@0.0.6"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/snapshots`

Create a new snapshot of a repository's dependencies.

The authenticated user must have access to the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-submission#create-a-snapshot-of-dependencies-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": 0,
  "sha": "ce587453ced02b1526dfb4cb910479d431683101",
  "ref": "refs/heads/main",
  "job": {
    "correlator": "yourworkflowname_youractionname",
    "id": "yourrunid"
  },
  "detector": {
    "name": "octo-detector",
    "version": "0.0.1",
    "url": "https://github.com/octo-org/octo-repo"
  },
  "scanned": "2022-06-14T20:25:00Z",
  "manifests": {
    "package-lock.json": {
      "name": "package-lock.json",
      "file": {
        "source_location": "src/package-lock.json"
      },
      "resolved": {
        "@actions/core": {
          "package_url": "pkg:/npm/%40actions/core@1.1.9",
          "dependencies": [
            "@actions/http-client"
          ]
        },
        "@actions/http-client": {
          "package_url": "pkg:/npm/%40actions/http-client@1.0.7",
          "dependencies": [
            "tunnel"
          ]
        },
        "tunnel": {
          "package_url": "pkg:/npm/tunnel@0.0.6"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-snapshot-of-dependencies-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[snapshot](#schemasnapshot)|true|none|
|» version|body|integer|true|The version of the repository snapshot submission.|
|» job|body|object|true|none|
|» » id|body|string|true|The external ID of the job.|
|» » correlator|body|string|true|Correlator provides a key that is used to group snapshots submitted over time. Only the "latest" submitted snapshot for a given combination of `job.correlator` and `detector.name` will be considered when calculating a repository's current dependencies. Correlator should be as unique as it takes to distinguish all detection runs for a given "wave" of CI workflow you run. If you're using GitHub Actions, a good default value for this could be the environment variables GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_JOB concatenated together. If you're using a build matrix, then you'll also need to add additional key(s) to distinguish between each submission inside a matrix variation.|
|» » html_url|body|string|false|The url for the job.|
|» sha|body|string|true|The commit SHA associated with this dependency snapshot. Maximum length: 64 characters.|
|» ref|body|string|true|The repository branch that triggered this snapshot.|
|» detector|body|object|true|A description of the detector used.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the detector used.|
|» » version|body|string|true|The version of the detector used.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The url of the detector used.|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|User-defined metadata to store domain-specific information limited to 8 keys with scalar values.|
|» manifests|body|object|false|A collection of package manifests, which are a collection of related dependencies declared in a file or representing a logical group of dependencies.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[manifest](#schemamanifest)|false|none|
|» scanned|body|string(date-time)|true|The time at which the snapshot was scanned.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 12345,
  "created_at": "2018-05-04T01:14:52Z",
  "message": "Dependency results for the repo have been successfully updated.",
  "result": "SUCCESS"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-snapshot-of-dependencies-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-snapshot-of-dependencies-for-a-repository-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|true|none|ID of the created snapshot.|
|created_at|string|true|none|The time at which the snapshot was created.|
|result|string|true|none|Either "SUCCESS", "ACCEPTED", or "INVALID". "SUCCESS" indicates that the snapshot was successfully created and the repository's dependencies were updated. "ACCEPTED" indicates that the snapshot was successfully created, but the repository's dependencies were not updated. "INVALID" indicates that the snapshot was malformed.|
|message|string|true|none|A message providing further details about the result, such as why the dependencies were not updated.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a gist

<a id="opIdgists/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/gists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "description": "Example of a gist",
    "public": false,
    "files": {
      "README.md": {
        "content": "Hello World"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /gists`

Allows you to add a new gist with one or more files.

> [!NOTE]
> Don't name your files "gistfile" with a numerical suffix. This is the format of the automatic naming scheme that Gist uses internally.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/gists/gists#create-a-gist">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Example of a gist",
  "public": false,
  "files": {
    "README.md": {
      "content": "Hello World"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-gist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the gist|
|» files|body|object|true|Names and content for the files that make up the gist|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » » content|body|string|true|Content of the file|
|» public|body|boolean \| string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|Flag indicating whether the gist is public|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|true|
|» » *oneOf*|false|

## List public gists

<a id="opIdgists/list-public"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/gists/public \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /gists/public`

List public gists sorted by most recently updated to least recently updated.

Note: With [pagination](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api), you can fetch up to 3000 gists. For example, you can fetch 100 pages with 30 gists per page or 30 pages with 100 gists per page.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/gists/gists#list-public-gists">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-public-gists-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Update a gist

<a id="opIdgists/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/gists/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "description": "An updated gist description",
    "files": {
      "README.md": {
        "content": "Hello World from GitHub"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /gists/{gist_id}`

Allows you to update a gist's description and to update, delete, or rename gist files. Files
from the previous version of the gist that aren't explicitly changed during an edit
are unchanged.

At least one of `description` or `files` is required.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/gists/gists#update-a-gist">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "An updated gist description",
  "files": {
    "README.md": {
      "content": "Hello World from GitHub"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-gist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|gist_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the gist.|
|body|body|object \| null|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the gist.|
|» files|body|object|false|The gist files to be updated, renamed, or deleted. Each `key` must match the current filename<br>(including extension) of the targeted gist file. For example: `hello.py`.<br><br>To delete a file, set the whole file to null. For example: `hello.py : null`. The file will also be<br>deleted if the specified object does not contain at least one of `content` or `filename`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » » content|body|string|false|The new content of the file.|
|» » » filename|body|string \| null|false|The new filename for the file.|

## Get a gist revision

<a id="opIdgists/get-revision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/gists/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /gists/{gist_id}/{sha}`

Gets a specified gist revision.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/gists/gists#get-a-gist-revision">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-gist-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|gist_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the gist.|
|sha|path|string|true|none|

## Get a blob

<a id="opIdgit/get-blob"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/blobs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/blobs/{file_sha}`

The `content` in the response will always be Base64 encoded.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw blob data.
- **`application/vnd.github+json`**: Returns a JSON representation of the blob with `content` as a base64 encoded string. This is the default if no media type is specified.

**Note** This endpoint supports blobs up to 100 megabytes in size.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/blobs#get-a-blob">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|file_sha|path|string|true|none|

## Create a commit

<a id="opIdgit/create-commit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/commits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "message": "my commit message",
    "author": {
      "name": "Mona Octocat",
      "email": "octocat@github.com",
      "date": "2008-07-09T16:13:30+12:00"
    },
    "parents": [
      "7d1b31e74ee336d15cbd21741bc88a537ed063a0"
    ],
    "tree": "827efc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132",
    "signature": "-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----\n\niQIzBAABAQAdFiEESn/54jMNIrGSE6Tp6cQjvhfv7nAFAlnT71cACgkQ6cQjvhfv\n7nCWwA//XVqBKWO0zF+bZl6pggvky3Oc2j1pNFuRWZ29LXpNuD5WUGXGG209B0hI\nDkmcGk19ZKUTnEUJV2Xd0R7AW01S/YSub7OYcgBkI7qUE13FVHN5ln1KvH2all2n\n2+JCV1HcJLEoTjqIFZSSu/sMdhkLQ9/NsmMAzpf/iIM0nQOyU4YRex9eD1bYj6nA\nOQPIDdAuaTQj1gFPHYLzM4zJnCqGdRlg0sOM/zC5apBNzIwlgREatOYQSCfCKV7k\nnrU34X8b9BzQaUx48Qa+Dmfn5KQ8dl27RNeWAqlkuWyv3pUauH9UeYW+KyuJeMkU\n+NyHgAsWFaCFl23kCHThbLStMZOYEnGagrd0hnm1TPS4GJkV4wfYMwnI4KuSlHKB\njHl3Js9vNzEUQipQJbgCgTiWvRJoK3ENwBTMVkKHaqT4x9U4Jk/XZB6Q8MA09ezJ\n3QgiTjTAGcum9E9QiJqMYdWQPWkaBIRRz5cET6HPB48YNXAAUsfmuYsGrnVLYbG+\nUpC6I97VybYHTy2O9XSGoaLeMI9CsFn38ycAxxbWagk5mhclNTP5mezIq6wKSwmr\nX11FW3n1J23fWZn5HJMBsRnUCgzqzX3871IqLYHqRJ/bpZ4h20RhTyPj5c/z7QXp\neSakNQMfbbMcljkha+ZMuVQX1K9aRlVqbmv3ZMWh+OijLYVU2bc=\n=5Io4\n-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----\n"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits`

Creates a new Git [commit object](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-Objects).

**Signature verification object**

The response will include a `verification` object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the `verification` object:

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `verified` | `boolean` | Indicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified. |
| `reason` | `string` | The reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in the table below. |
| `signature` | `string` | The signature that was extracted from the commit. |
| `payload` | `string` | The value that was signed. |
| `verified_at` | `string` | The date the signature was verified by GitHub. |

These are the possible values for `reason` in the `verification` object:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `expired_key` | The key that made the signature is expired. |
| `not_signing_key` | The "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature. |
| `gpgverify_error` | There was an error communicating with the signature verification service. |
| `gpgverify_unavailable` | The signature verification service is currently unavailable. |
| `unsigned` | The object does not include a signature. |
| `unknown_signature_type` | A non-PGP signature was found in the commit. |
| `no_user` | No user was associated with the `committer` email address in the commit. |
| `unverified_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account. |
| `bad_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature. |
| `unknown_key` | The key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account. |
| `malformed_signature` | There was an error parsing the signature. |
| `invalid` | The signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature. |
| `valid` | None of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified. |

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/commits#create-a-commit">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "message": "my commit message",
  "author": {
    "name": "Mona Octocat",
    "email": "octocat@github.com",
    "date": "2008-07-09T16:13:30+12:00"
  },
  "parents": [
    "7d1b31e74ee336d15cbd21741bc88a537ed063a0"
  ],
  "tree": "827efc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132",
  "signature": "-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----\n\niQIzBAABAQAdFiEESn/54jMNIrGSE6Tp6cQjvhfv7nAFAlnT71cACgkQ6cQjvhfv\n7nCWwA//XVqBKWO0zF+bZl6pggvky3Oc2j1pNFuRWZ29LXpNuD5WUGXGG209B0hI\nDkmcGk19ZKUTnEUJV2Xd0R7AW01S/YSub7OYcgBkI7qUE13FVHN5ln1KvH2all2n\n2+JCV1HcJLEoTjqIFZSSu/sMdhkLQ9/NsmMAzpf/iIM0nQOyU4YRex9eD1bYj6nA\nOQPIDdAuaTQj1gFPHYLzM4zJnCqGdRlg0sOM/zC5apBNzIwlgREatOYQSCfCKV7k\nnrU34X8b9BzQaUx48Qa+Dmfn5KQ8dl27RNeWAqlkuWyv3pUauH9UeYW+KyuJeMkU\n+NyHgAsWFaCFl23kCHThbLStMZOYEnGagrd0hnm1TPS4GJkV4wfYMwnI4KuSlHKB\njHl3Js9vNzEUQipQJbgCgTiWvRJoK3ENwBTMVkKHaqT4x9U4Jk/XZB6Q8MA09ezJ\n3QgiTjTAGcum9E9QiJqMYdWQPWkaBIRRz5cET6HPB48YNXAAUsfmuYsGrnVLYbG+\nUpC6I97VybYHTy2O9XSGoaLeMI9CsFn38ycAxxbWagk5mhclNTP5mezIq6wKSwmr\nX11FW3n1J23fWZn5HJMBsRnUCgzqzX3871IqLYHqRJ/bpZ4h20RhTyPj5c/z7QXp\neSakNQMfbbMcljkha+ZMuVQX1K9aRlVqbmv3ZMWh+OijLYVU2bc=\n=5Io4\n-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----\n"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» message|body|string|true|The commit message|
|» tree|body|string|true|The SHA of the tree object this commit points to|
|» parents|body|[string]|false|The full SHAs of the commits that were the parents of this commit. If omitted or empty, the commit will be written as a root commit. For a single parent, an array of one SHA should be provided; for a merge commit, an array of more than one should be provided.|
|» author|body|object|false|Information about the author of the commit. By default, the `author` will be the authenticated user and the current date. See the `author` and `committer` object below for details.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » date|body|string(date-time)|false|Indicates when this commit was authored (or committed). This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» committer|body|object|false|Information about the person who is making the commit. By default, `committer` will use the information set in `author`. See the `author` and `committer` object below for details.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » date|body|string(date-time)|false|Indicates when this commit was authored (or committed). This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» signature|body|string|false|The [PGP signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Good_Privacy) of the commit. GitHub adds the signature to the `gpgsig` header of the created commit. For a commit signature to be verifiable by Git or GitHub, it must be an ASCII-armored detached PGP signature over the string commit as it would be written to the object database. To pass a `signature` parameter, you need to first manually create a valid PGP signature, which can be complicated. You may find it easier to [use the command line](https://git-scm.com/book/id/v2/Git-Tools-Signing-Your-Work) to create signed commits.|

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{commit_sha}`

Gets a Git [commit object](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-Objects).

To get the contents of a commit, see "[Get a commit](/rest/commits/commits#get-a-commit)."

**Signature verification object**

The response will include a `verification` object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the `verification` object:

| Name | Type | Description |

| `verified` | `boolean` | Indicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified. |
| `reason` | `string` | The reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in the table below. |
| `signature` | `string` | The signature that was extracted from the commit. |
| `payload` | `string` | The value that was signed. |
| `verified_at` | `string` | The date the signature was verified by GitHub. |

These are the possible values for `reason` in the `verification` object:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `expired_key` | The key that made the signature is expired. |
| `not_signing_key` | The "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature. |
| `gpgverify_error` | There was an error communicating with the signature verification service. |
| `gpgverify_unavailable` | The signature verification service is currently unavailable. |
| `unsigned` | The object does not include a signature. |
| `unknown_signature_type` | A non-PGP signature was found in the commit. |
| `no_user` | No user was associated with the `committer` email address in the commit. |
| `unverified_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account. |
| `bad_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature. |
| `unknown_key` | The key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account. |
| `malformed_signature` | There was an error parsing the signature. |
| `invalid` | The signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature. |
| `valid` | None of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified. |

## List matching references

<a id="opIdgit/list-matching-refs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/matching-refs/heads%2Ffeature-a \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/{ref}`

Returns an array of references from your Git database that match the supplied name. The `:ref` in the URL must be formatted as `heads/<branch name>` for branches and `tags/<tag name>` for tags. If the `:ref` doesn't exist in the repository, but existing refs start with `:ref`, they will be returned as an array.

When you use this endpoint without providing a `:ref`, it will return an array of all the references from your Git database, including notes and stashes if they exist on the server. Anything in the namespace is returned, not just `heads` and `tags`.

> [!NOTE]
> You need to explicitly [request a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-a-pull-request) to trigger a test merge commit, which checks the mergeability of pull requests. For more information, see "[Checking mergeability of pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-git-database-api#checking-mergeability-of-pull-requests)".

If you request matching references for a branch named `feature` but the branch `feature` doesn't exist, the response can still include other matching head refs that start with the word `feature`, such as `featureA` and `featureB`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#list-matching-references">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-matching-references-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|path|string|true|The Git reference. For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "ref": "refs/heads/feature-a",
    "node_id": "MDM6UmVmcmVmcy9oZWFkcy9mZWF0dXJlLWE=",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/refs/heads/feature-a",
    "object": {
      "type": "commit",
      "sha": "aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd",
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/commits/aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd"
    }
  },
  {
    "ref": "refs/heads/feature-b",
    "node_id": "MDM6UmVmcmVmcy9oZWFkcy9mZWF0dXJlLWI=",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/refs/heads/feature-b",
    "object": {
      "type": "commit",
      "sha": "612077ae6dffb4d2fbd8ce0cccaa58893b07b5ac",
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/commits/612077ae6dffb4d2fbd8ce0cccaa58893b07b5ac"
    }
  }
]
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-matching-references-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h3 id="list-matching-references-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[git-ref](#schemagit-ref)]|false|none|none|

## Create a reference

<a id="opIdgit/create-ref"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/refs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ref": "refs/heads/featureA",
    "sha": "aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs`

Creates a reference for your repository. You are unable to create new references for empty repositories, even if the commit SHA-1 hash used exists. Empty repositories are repositories without branches.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#create-a-reference">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "refs/heads/featureA",
  "sha": "aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ref|body|string|true|The name of the fully qualified reference (ie: `refs/heads/master`). If it doesn't start with 'refs' and have at least two slashes, it will be rejected.|
|» sha|body|string|true|The SHA1 value for this reference.|

```json
    "sha": "aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/commits/aa218f56b14c9653891f9e74264a383fa43fefbd"
  }
}
```

```json
  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```
