## Create a tag object

<a id="opIdgit/create-tag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "tag": "v0.0.1",
    "message": "initial version",
    "object": "c3d0be41ecbe669545ee3e94d31ed9a4bc91ee3c",
    "type": "commit",
    "tagger": {
      "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
      "email": "octocat@github.com",
      "date": "2011-06-17T14:53:35-07:00"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/tags`

Note that creating a tag object does not create the reference that makes a tag in Git. If you want to create an annotated tag in Git, you have to do this call to create the tag object, and then [create](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#create-a-reference) the `refs/tags/[tag]` reference. If you want to create a lightweight tag, you only have to [create](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#create-a-reference) the tag reference - this call would be unnecessary.

**Signature verification object**

The response will include a `verification` object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the `verification` object:

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `verified` | `boolean` | Indicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified. |
| `reason` | `string` | The reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in table below. |
| `signature` | `string` | The signature that was extracted from the commit. |
| `payload` | `string` | The value that was signed. |
| `verified_at` | `string` | The date the signature was verified by GitHub. |

These are the possible values for `reason` in the `verification` object:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `expired_key` | The key that made the signature is expired. |
| `not_signing_key` | The "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature. |
| `gpgverify_error` | There was an error communicating with the signature verification service. |
| `gpgverify_unavailable` | The signature verification service is currently unavailable. |
| `unsigned` | The object does not include a signature. |
| `unknown_signature_type` | A non-PGP signature was found in the commit. |
| `no_user` | No user was associated with the `committer` email address in the commit. |
| `unverified_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account. |
| `bad_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature. |
| `unknown_key` | The key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account. |
| `malformed_signature` | There was an error parsing the signature. |
| `invalid` | The signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature. |
| `valid` | None of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified. |

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/tags#create-a-tag-object">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tag": "v0.0.1",
  "message": "initial version",
  "object": "c3d0be41ecbe669545ee3e94d31ed9a4bc91ee3c",
  "type": "commit",
  "tagger": {
    "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
    "email": "octocat@github.com",
    "date": "2011-06-17T14:53:35-07:00"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tag-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» tag|body|string|true|The tag's name. This is typically a version (e.g., "v0.0.1").|
|» message|body|string|true|The tag message.|
|» object|body|string|true|The SHA of the git object this is tagging.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the object we're tagging. Normally this is a `commit` but it can also be a `tree` or a `blob`.|
|» tagger|body|object|false|An object with information about the individual creating the tag.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the author of the tag|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email of the author of the tag|
|» » date|body|string(date-time)|false|When this object was tagged. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|commit|
|» type|tree|
|» type|blob|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "node_id": "MDM6VGFnOTQwYmQzMzYyNDhlZmFlMGY5ZWU1YmM3YjJkNWM5ODU4ODdiMTZhYw==",
  "tag": "v0.0.1",
  "sha": "940bd336248efae0f9ee5bc7b2d5c985887b16ac",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/tags/940bd336248efae0f9ee5bc7b2d5c985887b16ac",
  "message": "initial version",
  "tagger": {
    "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
    "email": "octocat@github.com",
    "date": "2014-11-07T22:01:45Z"
  },
  "object": {
    "type": "commit",
    "sha": "c3d0be41ecbe669545ee3e94d31ed9a4bc91ee3c",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/commits/c3d0be41ecbe669545ee3e94d31ed9a4bc91ee3c"
  },
  "verification": {
    "verified": false,
    "reason": "unsigned",
    "signature": null,
    "payload": null,
    "verified_at": null
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tag-object-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[git-tag](#schemagit-tag)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||none|

This operation does not require authentication

## Create a tree

<a id="opIdgit/create-tree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/trees \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
    "tree": [
      {
        "path": "file.rb",
        "mode": "100644",
        "type": "blob",
        "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees`

The tree creation API accepts nested entries. If you specify both a tree and a nested path modifying that tree, this endpoint will overwrite the contents of the tree with the new path contents, and create a new tree structure.

If you use this endpoint to add, delete, or modify the file contents in a tree, you will need to commit the tree and then update a branch to point to the commit. For more information see "[Create a commit](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/commits#create-a-commit)" and "[Update a reference](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#update-a-reference)."

Returns an error if you try to delete a file that does not exist.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/trees#create-a-tree">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "base_tree": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
  "tree": [
    {
      "path": "file.rb",
      "mode": "100644",
      "type": "blob",
      "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-tree-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» tree|body|[object]|true|Objects (of `path`, `mode`, `type`, and `sha`) specifying a tree structure.|
|» » path|body|string|false|The file referenced in the tree.|
|» » mode|body|string|false|The file mode; one of `100644` for file (blob), `100755` for executable (blob), `040000` for subdirectory (tree), `160000` for submodule (commit), or `120000` for a blob that specifies the path of a symlink.|
|» » type|body|string|false|Either `blob`, `tree`, or `commit`.|
|» » sha|body|string \| null|false|The SHA1 checksum ID of the object in the tree. Also called `tree.sha`. If the value is `null` then the file will be deleted.  <br>  <br>**Note:** Use either `tree.sha` or `content` to specify the contents of the entry. Using both `tree.sha` and `content` will return an error.|
|» » content|body|string|false|The content you want this file to have. GitHub will write this blob out and use that SHA for this entry. Use either this, or `tree.sha`.  <br>  <br>**Note:** Use either `tree.sha` or `content` to specify the contents of the entry. Using both `tree.sha` and `content` will return an error.|
|» base_tree|body|string|false|The SHA1 of an existing Git tree object which will be used as the base for the new tree. If provided, a new Git tree object will be created from entries in the Git tree object pointed to by `base_tree` and entries defined in the `tree` parameter. Entries defined in the `tree` parameter will overwrite items from `base_tree` with the same `path`. If you're creating new changes on a branch, then normally you'd set `base_tree` to the SHA1 of the Git tree object of the current latest commit on the branch you're working on.<br>If not provided, GitHub will create a new Git tree object from only the entries defined in the `tree` parameter. If you create a new commit pointing to such a tree, then all files which were a part of the parent commit's tree and were not defined in the `tree` parameter will be listed as deleted by the new commit.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mode|100644|
|» » mode|100755|
|» » mode|040000|
|» » mode|160000|
|» » mode|120000|
|» » type|blob|
|» » type|tree|
|» » type|commit|

> Example responses

```json
    {

    }
  ],
```

## Get a tree

<a id="opIdgit/get-tree"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/git/trees/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree_sha}`

Returns a single tree using the SHA1 value or ref name for that tree.

If `truncated` is `true` in the response then the number of items in the `tree` array exceeded our maximum limit. If you need to fetch more items, use the non-recursive method of fetching trees, and fetch one sub-tree at a time.

> [!NOTE]
> The limit for the `tree` array is 100,000 entries with a maximum size of 7 MB when using the `recursive` parameter.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/git/trees#get-a-tree">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-tree-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|tree_sha|path|string|true|The SHA1 value or ref (branch or tag) name of the tree.|
|recursive|query|string|false|Setting this parameter to any value returns the objects or subtrees referenced by the tree specified in `:tree_sha`. For example, setting `recursive` to any of the following will enable returning objects or subtrees: `0`, `1`, `"true"`, and `"false"`. Omit this parameter to prevent recursively returning objects or subtrees.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sha": "9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/trees/9fb037999f264ba9a7fc6274d15fa3ae2ab98312",
  "tree": [
    {
      "path": "file.rb",
      "mode": "100644",
      "type": "blob",
      "size": 30,
      "sha": "44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132",
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/blobs/44b4fc6d56897b048c772eb4087f854f46256132"
    },
    {
      "path": "subdir",
      "mode": "040000",
      "type": "tree",
      "sha": "f484d249c660418515fb01c2b9662073663c242e",
      "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/git/blobs/f484d249c660418515fb01c2b9662073663c242e"
    },
    {
      "path": "exec_file",
      "mode": "100755",
      "type": "blob",
      "size": 75,
      "sha": "45b983be36b73c0788dc9cbcb76cbb80fc7bb057",

    }
```

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-issues">issues</h1>

Interact with GitHub Issues.

## List issues assigned to the authenticated user

<a id="opIdissues/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /issues`

List issues assigned to the authenticated user across all visible repositories including owned repositories, member
repositories, and organization repositories. You can use the `filter` query parameter to fetch issues that are not
necessarily assigned to you.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request` key. Be aware that the `id` of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an _issue id_. To find out the pull request id, use the "[List pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests)" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#list-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|string|false|Indicates which sorts of issues to return. `assigned` means issues assigned to you. `created` means issues created by you. `mentioned` means issues mentioning you. `subscribed` means issues you're subscribed to updates for. `all` or `repos` means all issues you can see, regardless of participation or creation.|
|state|query|string|false|Indicates the state of the issues to return.|
|labels|query|string|false|A list of comma separated label names. Example: `bug,ui,@high`|
|sort|query|string|false|What to sort results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|collab|query|boolean|false|none|
|orgs|query|boolean|false|none|
|owned|query|boolean|false|none|
|pulls|query|boolean|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|assigned|
|filter|created|
|filter|mentioned|
|filter|subscribed|
|filter|repos|
|filter|all|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|all|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|comments|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## List organization issues assigned to the authenticated user

<a id="opIdissues/list-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/issues`

List issues in an organization assigned to the authenticated user.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request` key. Be aware that the `id` of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an _issue id_. To find out the pull request id, use the "[List pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests)" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#list-organization-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|filter|query|string|false|Indicates which sorts of issues to return. `assigned` means issues assigned to you. `created` means issues created by you. `mentioned` means issues mentioning you. `subscribed` means issues you're subscribed to updates for. `all` or `repos` means all issues you can see, regardless of participation or creation.|
|state|query|string|false|Indicates the state of the issues to return.|
|labels|query|string|false|A list of comma separated label names. Example: `bug,ui,@high`|
|type|query|string|false|Can be the name of an issue type.|
|sort|query|string|false|What to sort results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|assigned|
|filter|created|
|filter|mentioned|
|filter|subscribed|
|filter|repos|
|filter|all|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|all|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|comments|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## List assignees

<a id="opIdissues/list-assignees"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/assignees \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/assignees`

Lists the [available assignees](https://docs.github.com/articles/assigning-issues-and-pull-requests-to-other-github-users/) for issues in a repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/assignees#list-assignees">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-assignees-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Check if a user can be assigned

<a id="opIdissues/check-user-can-be-assigned"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/assignees/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/assignees/{assignee}`

Checks if a user has permission to be assigned to an issue in this repository.

If the `assignee` can be assigned to issues in the repository, a `204` header with no content is returned.

Otherwise a `404` status code is returned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/assignees#check-if-a-user-can-be-assigned">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="check-if-a-user-can-be-assigned-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|assignee|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

```json
  "message": "string",
```

## List repository issues

<a id="opIdissues/list-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`

List issues in a repository. Only open issues will be listed.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request` key. Be aware that the `id` of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an _issue id_. To find out the pull request id, use the "[List pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests)" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#list-repository-issues">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|milestone|query|string|false|If an `integer` is passed, it should refer to a milestone by its `number` field. If the string `*` is passed, issues with any milestone are accepted. If the string `none` is passed, issues without milestones are returned.|
|state|query|string|false|Indicates the state of the issues to return.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Can be the name of a user. Pass in `none` for issues with no assigned user, and `*` for issues assigned to any user.|
|type|query|string|false|Can be the name of an issue type. If the string `*` is passed, issues with any type are accepted. If the string `none` is passed, issues without type are returned.|
|creator|query|string|false|The user that created the issue.|
|mentioned|query|string|false|A user that's mentioned in the issue.|
|issue_field_values|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of issue field filters in `field_slug:value` format.<br>Only issues matching all specified field values are returned.<br>Requires issue fields to be enabled for the repository. Issue fields are<br>not available for user-owned repositories, and field availability for<br>organization-owned public repositories depends on the organization's<br>visibility settings. For example, `priority:Urgent,severity:High` filters<br>issues where the `priority` field is `Urgent` AND the `severity` field is<br>`High`.|
|labels|query|string|false|A list of comma separated label names. Example: `bug,ui,@high`|
|sort|query|string|false|What to sort results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|all|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|comments|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Create an issue

<a id="opIdissues/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "Found a bug",
    "body": "I'\''m having a problem with this.",
    "assignees": [
      "octocat"
    ],
    "milestone": 1,
    "labels": [
      "bug"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`

Any user with pull access to a repository can create an issue. If [issues are disabled in the repository](https://docs.github.com/articles/disabling-issues/), the API returns a `410 Gone` status.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#create-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Found a bug",
  "body": "I'm having a problem with this.",
  "assignees": [
    "octocat"
  ],
  "milestone": 1,
  "labels": [
    "bug"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string \| integer|true|The title of the issue.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» body|body|string|false|The contents of the issue.|
|» assignee|body|string \| null|false|Login for the user that this issue should be assigned to. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set the assignee for new issues. The assignee is silently dropped otherwise. **This field is closing down.**_|
|» milestone|body|null \| string \| integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|The `number` of the milestone to associate this issue with. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set the milestone for new issues. The milestone is silently dropped otherwise._|
|» labels|body|[string \| object]|false|Labels to associate with this issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set labels for new issues. Labels are silently dropped otherwise._|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » description|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » color|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» assignees|body|[string]|false|Logins for Users to assign to this issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set assignees for new issues. Assignees are silently dropped otherwise._|
|» issue_field_values|body|[object]|false|An array of issue field values to set on this issue. Each field value must include the field ID and the value to set. Issue fields are only available for organization-owned repositories with the feature enabled. Field values are silently dropped otherwise.|
|» » field_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the issue field to set|
|» » value|body|string \| number \| [string]|true|The value to set for the field. For multi-select fields, provide an array of option names.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|The name of the issue type to associate with this issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can set the type for new issues. The type is silently dropped otherwise._|
|» parent_issue_id|body|integer|false|The id of the parent issue to add this issue to as a sub-issue. _NOTE: Only users with triage access to both the parent issue's repository and this repository can set the parent issue._|

## List issue comments for a repository

<a id="opIdissues/list-comments-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments`

You can use the REST API to list comments on issues and pull requests for a repository. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.

By default, issue comments are ordered by ascending ID.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#list-issue-comments-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issue-comments-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|Either `asc` or `desc`. Ignored without the `sort` parameter.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get an issue comment

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{comment_id}`

You can use the REST API to get comments on issues and pull requests. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#get-an-issue-comment">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-issue-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the comment.|

## Update an issue comment

<a id="opIdissues/update-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/comments/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "Me too"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{comment_id}`

You can use the REST API to update comments on issues and pull requests. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#update-an-issue-comment">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": "Me too"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-issue-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the comment.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» body|body|string|true|The contents of the comment.|

## Get an issue

<a id="opIdissues/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}`

The API returns a [`301 Moved Permanently` status](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api#follow-redirects) if the issue was
[transferred](https://docs.github.com/articles/transferring-an-issue-to-another-repository/) to another repository. If
the issue was transferred to or deleted from a repository where the authenticated user lacks read access, the API
returns a `404 Not Found` status. If the issue was deleted from a repository where the authenticated user has read
access, the API returns a `410 Gone` status. To receive webhook events for transferred and deleted issues, subscribe
to the [`issues`](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#issues) webhook.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request` key. Be aware that the `id` of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an _issue id_. To find out the pull request id, use the "[List pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests)" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/components/examples/issue"
}
```

> 301 Response

```json

  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 410 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[issue](#schemaissue)|
|301|Moved Permanently|Moved permanently|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|410|Gone|Gone|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Update an issue

<a id="opIdissues/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "Found a bug",
    "body": "I'\''m having a problem with this.",
    "assignees": [
      "octocat"
    ],
    "milestone": 1,
    "state": "open",
    "labels": [
      "bug"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}`

Issue owners and users with push access or Triage role can edit an issue.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#update-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Found a bug",
  "body": "I'm having a problem with this.",
  "assignees": [
    "octocat"
  ],
  "milestone": 1,
  "state": "open",
  "labels": [
    "bug"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|» assignee|body|string \| null|false|Username to assign to this issue. **This field is closing down.**|
|» state|body|string|false|The open or closed state of the issue.|
|» state_reason|body|string \| null|false|The reason for the state change. Ignored unless `state` is changed.|
|» duplicate_issue_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the issue that this issue duplicates, used when marking this issue as a duplicate with `status: Duplicate` or `state_reason: duplicate`. The issue must exist and be accessible to the authenticated user.|
|» milestone|body|null \| string \| integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|The `number` of the milestone to associate this issue with or use `null` to remove the current milestone. Only users with push access can set the milestone for issues. Without push access to the repository, milestone changes are silently dropped.|
|» labels|body|[string \| object]|false|Labels to associate with this issue. Pass one or more labels to _replace_ the set of labels on this issue. Send an empty array (`[]`) to clear all labels from the issue. Only users with push access can set labels for issues. Without push access to the repository, label changes are silently dropped.|

|» » rationale|body|string|false|Optional reasoning for selecting this label.|

|» » confidence|body|string|false|The confidence level for this label choice.|

Send an empty array (`[]`) to clear all assignees from the issue. Only users with push access can set assignees for new issues. Without push access to the repository, assignee changes are silently dropped.|

|» » confidence|body|string|false|The confidence level for this assignee choice.|

|» » field_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the issue field to set|

## List issue artifacts

<a id="opIdissues/list-issue-artifacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/artifacts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/artifacts`

Lists artifacts attached to an issue. Results are ordered by artifact number.

The `type` parameter filters the response to artifacts of one type.
Results can be requested by page. The page defaults to `1`; the page size
defaults to `30` and can be set from `1` to `100`.

The response is a bare array and does not include pagination metadata such as
a `Link` header, a total count, or the service's `has_next_page` signal.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/artifacts#list-issue-artifacts">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issue-artifacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|type|query|string|false|The artifact type to return.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|generic|
|type|link|
|type|plan|
|type|embedded_html|

## Create an issue artifact

<a id="opIdissues/create-issue-artifact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/artifacts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "type": "generic",
    "name": "Research notes",
    "body": "## Findings\n\nThe API supports issue artifacts."
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/artifacts`

Creates an artifact attached to an issue.

The artifact type defaults to `generic` when omitted. Creating an artifact
requires permission to update the issue.

The request can return `403` if the repository is read-only or locked, or a
GitHub App installation has only `issues: read` permission.

To create an HTML artifact, set `type` to `embedded_html` and provide the HTML source
in `body`. Open the returned `html_url` to inspect the source, then select
**Preview** to view the rendered artifact. Select **Show source** to return
to the HTML source.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/artifacts#create-an-issue-artifact">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "generic",
  "name": "Research notes",
  "body": "## Findings\n\nThe API supports issue artifacts."
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-issue-artifact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|false|The artifact type.|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the artifact.|
|» body|body|string|true|The artifact content. For `embedded_html` artifacts, provide the HTML source.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|generic|
|» type|link|
|» type|plan|
|» type|embedded_html|

## Add assignees to an issue

<a id="opIdissues/add-assignees"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/assignees \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "assignees": [
      "hubot",
      "other_user"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/assignees`

Adds up to 10 assignees to an issue. Users already assigned to an issue are not replaced.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/assignees#add-assignees-to-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignees": [
    "hubot",
    "other_user"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-assignees-to-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» assignees|body|[string \| object]|false|Usernames of people to assign this issue to. _NOTE: Only users with push access can add assignees to an issue. Assignees are silently ignored otherwise._|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » login|body|string|true|The login of the user to assign.|
|» » rationale|body|string|false|Optional reasoning for adding this assignee.|
|» » suggest|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the assignee is stored as a pending suggestion for human review rather than applied directly.|
|» » confidence|body|string|false|The confidence level for this assignee choice.|

## Remove assignees from an issue

<a id="opIdissues/remove-assignees"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/assignees \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "assignees": [
      "hubot",
      "other_user"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/assignees`

Removes one or more assignees from an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/assignees#remove-assignees-from-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignees": [
    "hubot",
    "other_user"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-assignees-from-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» assignees|body|[string]|false|Usernames of assignees to remove from an issue. _NOTE: Only users with push access can remove assignees from an issue. Assignees are silently ignored otherwise._|

## Check if a user can be assigned to a issue

<a id="opIdissues/check-user-can-be-assigned-to-issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/assignees/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/assignees/{assignee}`

Checks if a user has permission to be assigned to a specific issue.

If the `assignee` can be assigned to this issue, a `204` status code with no content is returned.

Otherwise a `404` status code is returned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/assignees#check-if-a-user-can-be-assigned-to-a-issue">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="check-if-a-user-can-be-assigned-to-a-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|assignee|path|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="check-if-a-user-can-be-assigned-to-a-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response if `assignee` can be assigned to `issue_number`|None|
|404|Not Found|Response if `assignee` can not be assigned to `issue_number`|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List issue comments

<a id="opIdissues/list-comments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments`

You can use the REST API to list comments on issues and pull requests. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.

Issue comments are ordered by ascending ID.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#list-issue-comments">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issue-comments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

## Create an issue comment

<a id="opIdissues/create-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/comments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "Me too"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments`

You can use the REST API to create comments on issues and pull requests. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications).
Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

## List dependencies an issue is blocked by

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/dependencies/blocked_by`

You can use the REST API to list the dependencies an issue is blocked by.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-dependencies#list-dependencies-an-issue-is-blocked-by">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Add a dependency an issue is blocked by

<a id="opIdissues/add-blocked-by-dependency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/dependencies/blocked_by \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "issue_id": 1
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/dependencies/blocked_by`

You can use the REST API to add a 'blocked by' relationship to an issue.

Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see [Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)
and [Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api).

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-dependencies#add-a-dependency-an-issue-is-blocked-by">API method documentation</a>

```json
{
  "issue_id": 1
}
```

## Remove dependency an issue is blocked by

<a id="opIdissues/remove-dependency-blocked-by"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/dependencies/blocked_by/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/dependencies/blocked_by/{issue_id}`

You can use the REST API to remove a dependency that an issue is blocked by.

Removing content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see [Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)
and [Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api).

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).
- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass a specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-dependencies#remove-dependency-an-issue-is-blocked-by">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-dependency-an-issue-is-blocked-by-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|issue_id|path|integer|true|The id of the blocking issue to remove as a dependency|

## List dependencies an issue is blocking

<a id="opIdissues/list-dependencies-blocking"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/dependencies/blocking \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/dependencies/blocking`

You can use the REST API to list the dependencies an issue is blocking.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-dependencies#list-dependencies-an-issue-is-blocking">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-dependencies-an-issue-is-blocking-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Set issue field values for an issue

<a id="opIdissues/set-issue-field-values"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/issue-field-values \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "issue_field_values": [
      {
        "field_id": 123,
        "value": "Critical"
      },
      {
        "field_id": 456,
        "value": 5
      },
      {
        "field_id": 789,
        "value": "2024-12-31"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/issue-field-values`

Set custom field values for an issue, replacing any existing values. You can set values for organization-level issue fields that have been defined for the repository's organization.

This endpoint supports the following field data types:
- **`text`**: String values for text fields
- **`single_select`**: Option names for single-select fields (must match an existing option name)
- **`number`**: Numeric values for number fields
- **`date`**: ISO 8601 date strings for date fields

This operation will replace all existing field values with the provided ones. If you want to add field values without replacing existing ones, use the `POST` endpoint instead.

Only users with push access to the repository can set issue field values. If you don't have the proper permissions, you'll receive a `403 Forbidden` response.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-field-values#set-issue-field-values-for-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issue_field_values": [
    {
      "field_id": 123,
      "value": "Critical"
    },
    {
      "field_id": 456,
      "value": 5
    },
    {
      "field_id": 789,
      "value": "2024-12-31"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-issue-field-values-for-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» issue_field_values|body|[object]|false|An array of issue field values to set for this issue. Each field value must include the field ID and the value to set. All existing field values will be replaced.|
|» » field_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the issue field to set|
|» » value|body|string \| number|true|The value to set for the field. The type depends on the field's data type:<br>- For text fields: provide a string value<br>- For single_select fields: provide the option name as a string (must match an existing option)<br>- For number fields: provide a numeric value<br>- For date fields: provide an ISO 8601 date string|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|The value to set for text, single_select, or date fields|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|The value to set for number fields|

## Add issue field values to an issue

<a id="opIdissues/add-issue-field-values"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/issue-field-values \
  -X POST \

```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/issue-field-values`

Add custom field values to an issue. You can set values for organization-level issue fields that have been defined for the repository's organization.
Adding an empty array will clear all existing field values for the issue.

This endpoint supports the following field data types:
- **`text`**: String values for text fields
- **`single_select`**: Option names for single-select fields (must match an existing option name)
- **`number`**: Numeric values for number fields
- **`date`**: ISO 8601 date strings for date fields

Only users with push access to the repository can add issue field values. If you don't have the proper permissions, you'll receive a `403 Forbidden` response.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-field-values#add-issue-field-values-to-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

```json
      "field_id": 456,
      "value": 5
    },
    {
      "field_id": 789,
      "value": "2024-12-31"

}
```

<h3 id="add-issue-field-values-to-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|

|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» issue_field_values|body|[object]|false|An array of issue field values to add to this issue. Each field value must include the field ID and the value to set.|
|» » field_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the issue field to set|
|» » value|body|string \| number \| [string]|true|The value to set for the field. The type depends on the field's data type:<br>- For text fields: provide a string value<br>- For single_select fields: provide the option name as a string (must match an existing option)<br>- For number fields: provide a numeric value<br>- For multi_select fields: provide an array of option names (must match existing options)<br>- For date fields: provide an ISO 8601 date string|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|The value to set for text, single_select, or date fields|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|The value to set for number fields|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|The value to set for multi_select fields (array of option names)|

## Delete an issue field value from an issue

<a id="opIdissues/delete-issue-field-value"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/issue-field-values/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/issue-field-values/{issue_field_id}`

Remove a specific custom field value from an issue.

Only users with push access to the repository can delete issue field values. If you don't have the proper permissions, you'll receive a `403 Forbidden` response.

If the specified field does not have a value set on the issue, this operation will return a `404` error.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issue-field-values#delete-an-issue-field-value-from-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-an-issue-field-value-from-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|issue_field_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the issue field.|

## Lock an issue

<a id="opIdissues/lock"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/lock \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "lock_reason": "off-topic"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/lock`

Users with push access can lock an issue or pull request's conversation.

Note that, if you choose not to pass any parameters, you'll need to set `Content-Length` to zero when calling out to this endpoint. For more information, see "[HTTP method](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#http-method)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#lock-an-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "lock_reason": "off-topic"
}
```

<h3 id="lock-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» lock_reason|body|string|false|The reason for locking the issue or pull request conversation. Lock will fail if you don't use one of these reasons:  <br> * `off-topic`  <br> * `too heated`  <br> * `resolved`  <br> * `spam`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» lock_reason|off-topic|
|» lock_reason|too heated|
|» lock_reason|resolved|
|» lock_reason|spam|

## Get parent issue

<a id="opIdissues/get-parent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/parent \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/parent`

You can use the REST API to get the parent issue of a sub-issue.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/sub-issues#get-parent-issue">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-parent-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|

## Add a related issue

<a id="opIdissues/add-relates-to"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/relates_to \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "issue_id": 1
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/relates_to`

You can use the REST API to mark an issue as related to another issue.

Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see [Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)
and [Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api).

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#add-a-related-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "issue_id": 1
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-related-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» issue_id|body|integer|true|The id of the issue to mark as related to the current issue|
