## Remove a related issue

<a id="opIdissues/remove-relates-to"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/relates_to/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/relates_to/{issue_id}`

You can use the REST API to remove a 'relates to' relationship between two issues.

Removing content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see [Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)
and [Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api).

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#remove-a-related-issue">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-a-related-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|issue_id|path|integer|true|The id of the related issue to remove|

## Remove sub-issue

<a id="opIdissues/remove-sub-issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/sub_issue \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "sub_issue_id": 6
  }'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issue`

You can use the REST API to remove a sub-issue from an issue.
Removing content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."
This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."
- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass a specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/sub-issues#remove-sub-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sub_issue_id": 6
}
```

<h3 id="remove-sub-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» sub_issue_id|body|integer|true|The id of the sub-issue to remove|

## List sub-issues

<a id="opIdissues/list-sub-issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/sub_issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues`

You can use the REST API to list the sub-issues on an issue.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see [Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types).

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw Markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the Markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's Markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/sub-issues#list-sub-issues">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-sub-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Add sub-issue

<a id="opIdissues/add-sub-issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/sub_issues \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "sub_issue_id": 1
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues`

You can use the REST API to add sub-issues to issues.

Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/sub-issues#add-sub-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sub_issue_id": 1
}
```

<h3 id="add-sub-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» sub_issue_id|body|integer|true|The id of the sub-issue to add. The sub-issue must belong to the same repository owner as the parent issue|
|» replace_parent|body|boolean|false|Option that, when true, instructs the operation to replace the sub-issues current parent issue|

## Reprioritize sub-issue

<a id="opIdissues/reprioritize-sub-issue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/sub_issues/priority \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "sub_issue_id": 6,
    "after_id": 5
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues/priority`

You can use the REST API to reprioritize a sub-issue to a different position in the parent list.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/sub-issues#reprioritize-sub-issue">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sub_issue_id": 6,
  "after_id": 5
}
```

<h3 id="reprioritize-sub-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» sub_issue_id|body|integer|true|The id of the sub-issue to reprioritize|
|» after_id|body|integer|false|The id of the sub-issue to be prioritized after (either positional argument after OR before should be specified).|
|» before_id|body|integer|false|The id of the sub-issue to be prioritized before (either positional argument after OR before should be specified).|

## List issue suggestions

<a id="opIdissues/list-suggestions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/suggestions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/suggestions`

Lists the suggestions on an issue. A suggestion is an agent-proposed change to an issue's type, labels, fields, assignees, or closed state that a maintainer can approve or dismiss.

By default only pending suggestions are returned. Use `state=all` to return suggestions in every state, or `state=<state>` to filter to a single state. Use `action=<action>` to return only suggestions for a specific change.

This endpoint is only available while the issue suggestions feature is enabled for the repository, and only supports issues, not pull requests.

Requires triage access to the repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#list-issue-suggestions">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issue-suggestions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|state|query|string|false|Filter suggestions by their state.|
|action|query|string|false|Filter suggestions by the change they propose.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|pending|
|state|applied|
|state|approved|
|state|dismissed|
|state|replaced|
|state|invalidated|
|state|all|
|action|set_type|
|action|add_label|
|action|add_field|
|action|add_assignee|
|action|close_issue|

## Approve an issue suggestion

<a id="opIdissues/approve-suggestion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/suggestions/0/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/suggestions/{suggestion_id}/approve`

Approves a pending suggestion on an issue. Applies the proposed change (creating the corresponding timeline event), transitions the suggestion to `approved`, and dismisses any competing pending suggestions for the same change.

Requires triage access to the repository. Approving a suggestion also requires permission to perform the change it applies (for example, setting the issue type, adding a label or assignee, or closing the issue); this only affects fine-grained access tokens and GitHub Apps whose permissions are narrower than the triage role. This endpoint only supports issues, not pull requests.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#approve-an-issue-suggestion">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="approve-an-issue-suggestion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|suggestion_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the suggestion.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": 12,
```

## Dismiss an issue suggestion

<a id="opIdissues/dismiss-suggestion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issues/0/suggestions/0/dismiss \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/suggestions/{suggestion_id}/dismiss`

Dismisses a pending suggestion on an issue. Transitions the suggestion to `dismissed` without applying any change or creating a timeline event.

Requires triage access to the repository. This endpoint only supports issues, not pull requests.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#dismiss-an-issue-suggestion">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="dismiss-an-issue-suggestion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|issue_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the issue.|
|suggestion_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the suggestion.|

## Create a label

<a id="opIdissues/create-label"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/labels \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "bug",
    "description": "Something isn'\''t working",
    "color": "f29513"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels`

Creates a label for the specified repository with the given name and color. The name and color parameters are required. The color must be a valid [hexadecimal color code](http://www.color-hex.com/).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels#create-a-label">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "bug",
  "description": "Something isn't working",
  "color": "f29513"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-label-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the label. Emoji can be added to label names, using either native emoji or colon-style markup. For example, typing `:strawberry:` will render the emoji ![:strawberry:](https://github.githubassets.com/images/icons/emoji/unicode/1f353.png ":strawberry:"). For a full list of available emoji and codes, see "[Emoji cheat sheet](https://github.com/ikatyang/emoji-cheat-sheet)."|
|» color|body|string|false|The [hexadecimal color code](http://www.color-hex.com/) for the label, without the leading `#`.|
|» description|body|string|false|A short description of the label. Must be 100 characters or fewer.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 208045946,
  "node_id": "MDU6TGFiZWwyMDgwNDU5NDY=",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/labels/bug",
  "name": "bug",
  "description": "Something isn't working",
  "color": "f29513",
  "default": true,
  "archived_at": null,
  "archived_by": null
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-label-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[label](#schemalabel)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

## Update a label

<a id="opIdissues/update-label"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/labels/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "new_name": "bug :bug:",
    "description": "Small bug fix required",
    "color": "b01f26"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{name}`

Updates a label using the given label name.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels#update-a-label">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "new_name": "bug :bug:",
  "description": "Small bug fix required",
  "color": "b01f26"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-label-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» new_name|body|string|false|The new name of the label. Emoji can be added to label names, using either native emoji or colon-style markup. For example, typing `:strawberry:` will render the emoji ![:strawberry:](https://github.githubassets.com/images/icons/emoji/unicode/1f353.png ":strawberry:"). For a full list of available emoji and codes, see "[Emoji cheat sheet](https://github.com/ikatyang/emoji-cheat-sheet)."|
|» color|body|string|false|The [hexadecimal color code](http://www.color-hex.com/) for the label, without the leading `#`.|
|» description|body|string|false|A short description of the label. Must be 100 characters or fewer.|
|» archived|body|boolean|false|Whether to archive or unarchive the label. Archived labels cannot be added to issues or pull requests. For more information, see "[Archiving labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-labels/managing-labels)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 208045946,
  "node_id": "MDU6TGFiZWwyMDgwNDU5NDY=",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/labels/bug%20:bug:",
  "name": "bug :bug:",
  "description": "Small bug fix required",
  "color": "b01f26",
  "default": true,
  "archived_at": null,
  "archived_by": null
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[label](#schemalabel)|

## Update a milestone

<a id="opIdissues/update-milestone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/milestones/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "v1.0",
    "state": "open",
    "description": "Tracking milestone for version 1.0",
    "due_on": "2012-10-09T23:39:01Z"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones/{milestone_number}`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones#update-a-milestone">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "v1.0",
  "state": "open",
  "description": "Tracking milestone for version 1.0",
  "due_on": "2012-10-09T23:39:01Z"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-milestone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|milestone_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the milestone.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the milestone.|
|» state|body|string|false|The state of the milestone. Either `open` or `closed`.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the milestone.|
|» due_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The milestone due date. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|open|
|» state|closed|

## List user account issues assigned to the authenticated user

<a id="opIdissues/list-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/issues \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/issues`

List issues across owned and member repositories assigned to the authenticated user.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the `pull_request` key. Be aware that the `id` of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an _issue id_. To find out the pull request id, use the "[List pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests)" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#list-user-account-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-user-account-issues-assigned-to-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter|query|string|false|Indicates which sorts of issues to return. `assigned` means issues assigned to you. `created` means issues created by you. `mentioned` means issues mentioning you. `subscribed` means issues you're subscribed to updates for. `all` or `repos` means all issues you can see, regardless of participation or creation.|
|state|query|string|false|Indicates the state of the issues to return.|
|labels|query|string|false|A list of comma separated label names. Example: `bug,ui,@high`|
|sort|query|string|false|What to sort results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|assigned|
|filter|created|
|filter|mentioned|
|filter|subscribed|
|filter|repos|
|filter|all|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|all|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|comments|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-licenses">licenses</h1>

View various OSS licenses.

## Get all commonly used licenses

<a id="opIdlicenses/get-all-commonly-used"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/licenses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /licenses`

Lists the most commonly used licenses on GitHub. For more information, see "[Licensing a repository ](https://docs.github.com/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/licenses/licenses#get-all-commonly-used-licenses">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-all-commonly-used-licenses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|featured|query|boolean|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /licenses/{license}`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/licenses/licenses#get-a-license">API method documentation</a>

## Get the license for a repository

<a id="opIdlicenses/get-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/license \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/license`

This method returns the contents of the repository's license file, if one is detected.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw contents of the license.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns the license contents in HTML. Markup languages are rendered to HTML using GitHub's open-source [Markup library](https://github.com/github/markup).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/licenses/licenses#get-the-license-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-license-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|query|[code-scanning-ref](#schemacode-scanning-ref)|false|The Git reference for the results you want to list. The `ref` for a branch can be formatted either as `refs/heads/<branch name>` or simply `<branch name>`. To reference a pull request use `refs/pull/<number>/merge`.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-markdown">markdown</h1>

Render GitHub flavored Markdown

## Render a Markdown document

<a id="opIdmarkdown/render"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/markdown \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "text": "Hello **world**"
  }'
```

`POST /markdown`

Depending on what is rendered in the Markdown, you may need to provide additional token scopes for labels, such as `issues:read` or `pull_requests:read`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/markdown/markdown#render-a-markdown-document">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "Hello **world**"
}
```

<h3 id="render-a-markdown-document-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|The Markdown text to render in HTML.|
|» mode|body|string|false|The rendering mode.|
|» context|body|string|false|The repository context to use when creating references in `gfm` mode.  For example, setting `context` to `octo-org/octo-repo` will change the text `#42` into an HTML link to issue 42 in the `octo-org/octo-repo` repository.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|markdown|
|» mode|gfm|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
<p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Content-Type|string||none|
|200|Content-Length|string||none|
|200|X-CommonMarker-Version|string||none|

## Render a Markdown document in raw mode

<a id="opIdmarkdown/render-raw"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/markdown/raw \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -d '{"text":"Hello **world**"}'
```

`POST /markdown/raw`

You must send Markdown as plain text (using a `Content-Type` header of `text/plain` or `text/x-markdown`) to this endpoint, rather than using JSON format. In raw mode, [GitHub Flavored Markdown](https://github.github.com/gfm/) is not supported and Markdown will be rendered in plain format like a README.md file. Markdown content must be 400 KB or less.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/markdown/markdown#render-a-markdown-document-in-raw-mode">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "Hello **world**"
}
```

<h3 id="render-a-markdown-document-in-raw-mode-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
<p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>
```

<h3 id="render-a-markdown-document-in-raw-mode-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-CommonMarker-Version|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get GitHub meta information

<a id="opIdmeta/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/meta \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /meta`

Returns meta information about GitHub, including a list of GitHub's IP addresses. For more information, see "[About GitHub's IP addresses](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-github-s-ip-addresses/)."

The API's response also includes a list of GitHub's domain names, and the public keys used by GitHub to sign commits made through the web UI.

The values shown in the documentation's response are example values. You must always query the API directly to get the latest values.

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint returns both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. However, not all features support IPv6. You should refer to the specific documentation for each feature to determine if IPv6 is supported.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/meta/meta#get-apiname-meta-information">API method documentation</a>

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-migrations">migrations</h1>

## List organization migrations

<a id="opIdmigrations/list-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/migrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/migrations`

Lists the most recent migrations, including both exports (which can be started through the REST API) and imports (which cannot be started using the REST API).

A list of `repositories` is only returned for export migrations.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/orgs#list-organization-migrations">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-migrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Exclude attributes from the API response to improve performance|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|exclude|repositories|

## Start an organization migration

<a id="opIdmigrations/start-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/migrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repositories": [
      "github/Hello-World"
    ],
    "lock_repositories": true
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/migrations`

Initiates the generation of a migration archive.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/orgs#start-an-organization-migration">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    "github/Hello-World"
  ],
  "lock_repositories": true
}
```

<h3 id="start-an-organization-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repositories|body|[string]|true|A list of arrays indicating which repositories should be migrated.|
|» lock_repositories|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether repositories should be locked (to prevent manipulation) while migrating data.|
|» exclude_metadata|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether metadata should be excluded and only git source should be included for the migration.|
|» exclude_git_data|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the repository git data should be excluded from the migration.|
|» exclude_attachments|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether attachments should be excluded from the migration (to reduce migration archive file size).|
|» exclude_releases|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether releases should be excluded from the migration (to reduce migration archive file size).|
|» exclude_owner_projects|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether projects owned by the organization or users should be excluded. from the migration.|
|» org_metadata_only|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether this should only include organization metadata (repositories array should be empty and will ignore other flags).|
|» exclude|body|[string]|false|Exclude related items from being returned in the response in order to improve performance of the request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» exclude|repositories|

## Get an organization migration status

<a id="opIdmigrations/get-status-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/migrations/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/migrations/{migration_id}`

Fetches the status of a migration.

The `state` of a migration can be one of the following values:

*   `pending`, which means the migration hasn't started yet.
*   `exporting`, which means the migration is in progress.
*   `exported`, which means the migration finished successfully.
*   `failed`, which means the migration failed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/orgs#get-an-organization-migration-status">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-organization-migration-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|migration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the migration.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|Exclude attributes from the API response to improve performance|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|exclude|repositories|

## Delete an organization migration archive

<a id="opIdmigrations/delete-archive-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/migrations/0/archive \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/migrations/{migration_id}/archive`

Deletes a previous migration archive. Migration archives are automatically deleted after seven days.

## Get an import status

<a id="opIdmigrations/get-import-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/import \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/import`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

View the progress of an import.

> [!WARNING]
> **Endpoint closing down notice:** Due to very low levels of usage and available alternatives, this endpoint is closing down and will no longer be available from 00:00 UTC on April 12, 2024. For more details and alternatives, see the [changelog](https://gh.io/source-imports-api-deprecation).

**Import status**

This section includes details about the possible values of the `status` field of the Import Progress response.

An import that does not have errors will progress through these steps:

*   `detecting` - the "detection" step of the import is in progress because the request did not include a `vcs` parameter. The import is identifying the type of source control present at the URL.
*   `importing` - the "raw" step of the import is in progress. This is where commit data is fetched from the original repository. The import progress response will include `commit_count` (the total number of raw commits that will be imported) and `percent` (0 - 100, the current progress through the import).
*   `mapping` - the "rewrite" step of the import is in progress. This is where SVN branches are converted to Git branches, and where author updates are applied. The import progress response does not include progress information.
*   `pushing` - the "push" step of the import is in progress. This is where the importer updates the repository on GitHub. The import progress response will include `push_percent`, which is the percent value reported by `git push` when it is "Writing objects".
*   `complete` - the import is complete, and the repository is ready on GitHub.

If there are problems, you will see one of these in the `status` field:

*   `auth_failed` - the import requires authentication in order to connect to the original repository. To update authentication for the import, please see the [Update an import](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#update-an-import) section.
*   `error` - the import encountered an error. The import progress response will include the `failed_step` and an error message. Contact [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/contact?tags=dotcom-rest-api) for more information.
*   `detection_needs_auth` - the importer requires authentication for the originating repository to continue detection. To update authentication for the import, please see the [Update an import](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#update-an-import) section.
*   `detection_found_nothing` - the importer didn't recognize any source control at the URL. To resolve, [Cancel the import](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#cancel-an-import) and [retry](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#start-an-import) with the correct URL.
*   `detection_found_multiple` - the importer found several projects or repositories at the provided URL. When this is the case, the Import Progress response will also include a `project_choices` field with the possible project choices as values. To update project choice, please see the [Update an import](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#update-an-import) section.

**The project_choices field**

When multiple projects are found at the provided URL, the response hash will include a `project_choices` field, the value of which is an array of hashes each representing a project choice. The exact key/value pairs of the project hashes will differ depending on the version control type.

**Git LFS related fields**

This section includes details about Git LFS related fields that may be present in the Import Progress response.

*   `use_lfs` - describes whether the import has been opted in or out of using Git LFS. The value can be `opt_in`, `opt_out`, or `undecided` if no action has been taken.
*   `has_large_files` - the boolean value describing whether files larger than 100MB were found during the `importing` step.
*   `large_files_size` - the total size in gigabytes of files larger than 100MB found in the originating repository.
*   `large_files_count` - the total number of files larger than 100MB found in the originating repository. To see a list of these files, make a "Get Large Files" request.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#get-an-import-status">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-import-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "vcs": "subversion",
  "use_lfs": true,
  "vcs_url": "http://svn.example.com/svn/myproject",
  "status": "complete",
  "status_text": "Done",
  "has_large_files": true,
  "large_files_size": 132331036,
  "large_files_count": 1,
  "authors_count": 4,
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/socm/import",
  "html_url": "https://import.github.com/octocat/socm/import",

  "repository_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/socm"
}
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/import`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

An import can be updated with credentials or a project choice by passing in the appropriate parameters in this API
request. If no parameters are provided, the import will be restarted.

Some servers (e.g. TFS servers) can have several projects at a single URL. In those cases the import progress will
have the status `detection_found_multiple` and the Import Progress response will include a `project_choices` array.
You can select the project to import by providing one of the objects in the `project_choices` array in the update request.

## Get commit authors

<a id="opIdmigrations/get-commit-authors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/import/authors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/import/authors`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Each type of source control system represents authors in a different way. For example, a Git commit author has a display name and an email address, but a Subversion commit author just has a username. The GitHub Importer will make the author information valid, but the author might not be correct. For example, it will change the bare Subversion username `hubot` into something like `hubot <hubot@12341234-abab-fefe-8787-fedcba987654>`.

This endpoint and the [Map a commit author](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#map-a-commit-author) endpoint allow you to provide correct Git author information.

> [!WARNING]
> **Endpoint closing down notice:** Due to very low levels of usage and available alternatives, this endpoint is closing down and will no longer be available from 00:00 UTC on April 12, 2024. For more details and alternatives, see the [changelog](https://gh.io/source-imports-api-deprecation).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/source-imports#get-commit-authors">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-commit-authors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|since|query|integer|false|A user ID. Only return users with an ID greater than this ID.|

## Start a user migration

<a id="opIdmigrations/start-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/migrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repositories": [
      "octocat/Hello-World"
    ],
    "lock_repositories": true
  }'
```

`POST /user/migrations`

Initiates the generation of a user migration archive.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#start-a-user-migration">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repositories": [
    "octocat/Hello-World"
  ],
  "lock_repositories": true
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-user-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» lock_repositories|body|boolean|false|Lock the repositories being migrated at the start of the migration|
|» exclude_metadata|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether metadata should be excluded and only git source should be included for the migration.|
|» exclude_git_data|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the repository git data should be excluded from the migration.|
|» exclude_attachments|body|boolean|false|Do not include attachments in the migration|
|» exclude_releases|body|boolean|false|Do not include releases in the migration|
|» exclude_owner_projects|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether projects owned by the organization or users should be excluded.|
|» org_metadata_only|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether this should only include organization metadata (repositories array should be empty and will ignore other flags).|
|» exclude|body|[string]|false|Exclude attributes from the API response to improve performance|
|» repositories|body|[string]|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» exclude|repositories|

## Get a user migration status

<a id="opIdmigrations/get-status-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/migrations/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/migrations/{migration_id}`

Fetches a single user migration. The response includes the `state` of the migration, which can be one of the following values:

*   `pending` - the migration hasn't started yet.
*   `exporting` - the migration is in progress.
*   `exported` - the migration finished successfully.
*   `failed` - the migration failed.

Once the migration has been `exported` you can [download the migration archive](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#download-a-user-migration-archive).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#get-a-user-migration-status">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-user-migration-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|migration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the migration.|
|exclude|query|[string]|false|none|

## Download a user migration archive

<a id="opIdmigrations/get-archive-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/migrations/0/archive \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/migrations/{migration_id}/archive`

Fetches the URL to download the migration archive as a `tar.gz` file. Depending on the resources your repository uses, the migration archive can contain JSON files with data for these objects:

*   attachments
*   bases
*   commit\_comments
*   issue\_comments
*   issue\_events
*   issues
*   milestones
*   organizations
*   projects
*   protected\_branches
*   pull\_request\_reviews
*   pull\_requests
*   releases
*   repositories
*   review\_comments
*   schema
*   users

The archive will also contain an `attachments` directory that includes all attachment files uploaded to GitHub.com and a `repositories` directory that contains the repository's Git data.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#download-a-user-migration-archive">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="download-a-user-migration-archive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|migration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the migration.|

```json
}
```

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Unlock a user repository

<a id="opIdmigrations/unlock-repo-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/migrations/0/repos/string/lock \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /user/migrations/{migration_id}/repos/{repo_name}/lock`

Unlocks a repository. You can lock repositories when you [start a user migration](https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#start-a-user-migration). Once the migration is complete you can unlock each repository to begin using it again or [delete the repository](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#delete-a-repository) if you no longer need the source data. Returns a status of `404 Not Found` if the repository is not locked.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/migrations/users#unlock-a-user-repository">API method documentation</a>

## List OIDC custom property inclusions for an enterprise

<a id="opIdoidc/list-oidc-custom-property-inclusions-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/actions/oidc/customization/properties/repo \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/actions/oidc/customization/properties/repo`

Lists the repository custom properties that are included in the OIDC token for repository actions in an enterprise.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> The "Enterprise administration" fine-grained permission is not available to callers. To use this API, you must use an OAuth app token or a personal access token (classic).

## Get an organization

<a id="opIdorgs/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}`

Gets information about an organization.

When the value of `two_factor_requirement_enabled` is `true`, the organization requires all members, billing managers, outside collaborators, guest collaborators, repository collaborators, or everyone with access to any repository within the organization to enable [two-factor authentication](https://docs.github.com/articles/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa/).

To see the full details about an organization, the authenticated user must be an organization owner.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to see the full details about an organization.

To see information about an organization's GitHub plan, GitHub Apps need the `Organization plan` permission.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/orgs#get-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Update an organization

<a id="opIdorgs/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "billing_email": "mona@github.com",
    "company": "GitHub",
    "email": "mona@github.com",
    "twitter_username": "github",
    "location": "San Francisco",
    "name": "github",
    "description": "GitHub, the company.",
    "default_repository_permission": "read",
    "members_can_create_repositories": true,
    "members_allowed_repository_creation_type": "all"
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}`

> [!WARNING]
> **Closing down notice:** GitHub will replace and discontinue `members_allowed_repository_creation_type` in favor of more granular permissions. The new input parameters are `members_can_create_public_repositories`, `members_can_create_private_repositories` for all organizations and `members_can_create_internal_repositories` for organizations associated with an enterprise account using GitHub Enterprise Cloud or GitHub Enterprise Server 2.20+. For more information, see the [blog post](https://developer.github.com/changes/2019-12-03-internal-visibility-changes).

> [!WARNING]
> **Closing down notice:** Code security product enablement for new repositories through the organization API is closing down. Please use [code security configurations](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#set-a-code-security-configuration-as-a-default-for-an-organization) to set defaults instead. For more information on setting a default security configuration, see the [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2024-07-09-sunsetting-security-settings-defaults-parameters-in-the-organizations-rest-api/).

Updates the organization's profile and member privileges.

The authenticated user must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` or `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/orgs#update-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "billing_email": "mona@github.com",
  "company": "GitHub",
  "email": "mona@github.com",
  "twitter_username": "github",
  "location": "San Francisco",
  "name": "github",
  "description": "GitHub, the company.",
  "default_repository_permission": "read",
  "members_can_create_repositories": true,
  "members_allowed_repository_creation_type": "all"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» billing_email|body|string|false|Billing email address. This address is not publicized.|
|» company|body|string|false|The company name.|
|» email|body|string|false|The publicly visible email address.|
|» twitter_username|body|string|false|The Twitter username of the company.|
|» location|body|string|false|The location.|
|» name|body|string|false|The shorthand name of the company.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the company. The maximum size is 160 characters.|
|» has_organization_projects|body|boolean|false|Whether an organization can use organization projects.|
|» has_repository_projects|body|boolean|false|Whether repositories that belong to the organization can use repository projects.|

## Create an artifact deployment record

<a id="opIdorgs/create-artifact-deployment-record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/artifacts/metadata/deployment-record \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "awesome-image",
    "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
    "status": "deployed",
    "logical_environment": "prod",
    "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
    "cluster": "moda-1",
    "deployment_name": "deployment-pod",
    "tags": {
      "data-access": "sensitive"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/artifacts/metadata/deployment-record`

Create or update deployment records for an artifact associated
with an organization.
This endpoint allows you to record information about a specific
artifact, such as its name, digest, environments, cluster, and
deployment.
The deployment name has to be uniqe within a cluster (i.e a
combination of logical, physical environment and cluster) as it
identifies unique deployment.
Multiple requests for the same combination of logical, physical
environment, cluster and deployment name will only create one
record, successive request will update the existing record.
This allows for a stable tracking of a deployment where the actual
deployed artifact can change over time.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata#create-an-artifact-deployment-record">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "awesome-image",
  "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
  "status": "deployed",
  "logical_environment": "prod",
  "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
  "cluster": "moda-1",
  "deployment_name": "deployment-pod",
  "tags": {
    "data-access": "sensitive"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-artifact-deployment-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the artifact.|
|» digest|body|string|true|The hex encoded digest of the artifact.|
|» version|body|string|false|The artifact version.|
|» status|body|string|true|The status of the artifact. Can be either deployed or decommissioned.|
|» logical_environment|body|string|true|The stage of the deployment.|
|» physical_environment|body|string|false|The physical region of the deployment.|
|» cluster|body|string|false|The deployment cluster.|
|» deployment_name|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the deployment represented by the new record. To accommodate differing<br>containers and namespaces within a cluster, the following format is recommended:<br>{namespaceName}-{deploymentName}-{containerName}.<br>|
|» tags|body|object|false|The tags associated with the deployment.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» runtime_risks|body|[string]|false|A list of runtime risks associated with the deployment.|
|» github_repository|body|string|false|The name of the GitHub repository associated with the artifact. This should be used<br>when there are no provenance attestations available for the artifact. The repository<br>must belong to the organization specified in the path parameter.<br><br>If a provenance attestation is available for the artifact, the API will use<br>the repository information from the attestation instead of this parameter.|
|» return_records|body|boolean|false|If true, the endpoint will return the created or updated record in the response body.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|deployed|
|» status|decommissioned|
|» runtime_risks|critical-resource|
|» runtime_risks|internet-exposed|
|» runtime_risks|lateral-movement|
|» runtime_risks|sensitive-data|

> Example responses

```json
  "total_count": 1,
  "deployment_records": [
    {
      "id": 123,
      "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
      "logical_environment": "prod",
      "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
      "cluster": "moda-1",
      "deployment_name": "prod-deployment",
      "tags": {
        "data": "sensitive"
      },
      "created": "2011-01-26T19:14:43Z",
      "updated_at": "2011-01-26T19:14:43Z",
      "attestation_id": 456
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

## Set cluster deployment records

<a id="opIdorgs/set-cluster-deployment-records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/artifacts/metadata/deployment-record/cluster/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "logical_environment": "prod",
    "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
    "deployments": [
      {
        "name": "awesome-image",
        "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
        "version": "2.1.0",
        "status": "deployed",
        "deployment_name": "deployment-pod",
        "tags": {
          "owning-team": "platform"
        },
        "runtime_risks": [
          "sensitive-data"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/artifacts/metadata/deployment-record/cluster/{cluster}`

Set deployment records for a given cluster.
If proposed records in the 'deployments' field have identical 'cluster', 'logical_environment',
'physical_environment', and 'deployment_name' values as existing records, the existing records will be updated.
If no existing records match, new records will be created.
Note: Artifacts are uniquely identified by the combination of their repository and digest fields. If two entries in the deployments
array resolve to the same repository and have identical digest fields but differing name and version fields, the endpoint will use
the artifact name and version from the record processed first, since a single artifact (identified by repository and digest) can
only have one name and version.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata#set-cluster-deployment-records">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "logical_environment": "prod",
  "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
  "deployments": [
    {
      "name": "awesome-image",
      "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
      "version": "2.1.0",
      "status": "deployed",
      "deployment_name": "deployment-pod",
      "tags": {
        "owning-team": "platform"
      },
      "runtime_risks": [
        "sensitive-data"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-cluster-deployment-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|cluster|path|string|true|The cluster name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» logical_environment|body|string|true|The stage of the deployment.|
|» physical_environment|body|string|false|The physical region of the deployment.|
|» deployments|body|[object]|true|The list of deployments to record.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the artifact.|
|» » digest|body|string|true|The hex encoded digest of the artifact.|
|» » version|body|string|false|The artifact version.|
|» » status|body|string|false|The deployment status of the artifact.|
|» » deployment_name|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the deployment represented by the new record. To accommodate differing<br>containers and namespaces within a record set, the following format is recommended:<br>{namespaceName}-{deploymentName}-{containerName}.<br>The deployment_name must be unique across all entries in the deployments array.<br>|
|» » github_repository|body|string|false|The name of the GitHub repository associated with the artifact. This should be used<br>when there are no provenance attestations available for the artifact. The repository<br>must belong to the organization specified in the path parameter.<br><br>If a provenance attestation is available for the artifact, the API will use<br>the repository information from the attestation instead of this parameter.|
|» » tags|body|object|false|Key-value pairs to tag the deployment record.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » runtime_risks|body|[string]|false|A list of runtime risks associated with the deployment.|
|» partial_success|body|boolean|false|When enabled, deployments associated with repositories the actor can write to are processed<br>while deployments associated with repositories that cannot be resolved or written to by the actor<br>are skipped and reported in the `errors` array. When false (the default), the endpoint returns<br>an error if any targeted repository cannot be resolved, the actor lacks write access, or no matching attestation can be found.<br>|
|» return_records|body|boolean|false|If true, the endpoint will return the set records in the response body<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » status|deployed|
|» » status|decommissioned|
|» » runtime_risks|critical-resource|
|» » runtime_risks|internet-exposed|
|» » runtime_risks|lateral-movement|
|» » runtime_risks|sensitive-data|

> Example responses

`POST /orgs/{org}/artifacts/metadata/deployment-record/cluster/{cluster}/jobs`

Create a background job to set deployment records for a given cluster.
Performs validation and permission checks synchronously, returning rejected
deployments immediately, then enqueues a background job for the actual
deployment updates. Use the companion GET endpoint to poll for job status.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata#create-a-cluster-deployment-records-job">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "logical_environment": "prod",
  "physical_environment": "pacific-east",
  "deployments": [
    {
      "name": "awesome-image",
      "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
      "version": "2.1.0",
      "status": "deployed",
      "deployment_name": "deployment-pod",
      "tags": {
        "owning-team": "platform"
      },
      "runtime_risks": [
        "sensitive-data"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-cluster-deployment-records-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|cluster|path|string|true|The cluster name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» logical_environment|body|string|true|The stage of the deployment.|
|» physical_environment|body|string|false|The physical region of the deployment.|
|» deployments|body|[object]|true|The list of deployments to record.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the artifact.|
|» » digest|body|string|true|The hex encoded digest of the artifact.|
|» » version|body|string|false|The artifact version.|
|» » status|body|string|false|The deployment status of the artifact.|
|» » deployment_name|body|string|true|The unique identifier for the deployment represented by the new record.<br>|
|» » github_repository|body|string|false|The name of the GitHub repository associated with the artifact.|
|» » tags|body|object|false|Key-value pairs to tag the deployment record.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » runtime_risks|body|[string]|false|A list of runtime risks associated with the deployment.|

## Create artifact metadata storage record

<a id="opIdorgs/create-artifact-storage-record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/artifacts/metadata/storage-record \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "libfoo",
    "version": "1.2.3",
    "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
    "artifact_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/bar/libfoo-1.2.3",
    "registry_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/",
    "repository": "bar",
    "status": "active"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/artifacts/metadata/storage-record`

Create metadata storage records for artifacts associated with an organization.
This endpoint will create a new artifact storage record on behalf of any artifact matching the provided digest and
associated with a repository owned by the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata#create-artifact-metadata-storage-record">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "libfoo",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
  "artifact_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/bar/libfoo-1.2.3",
  "registry_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/",
  "repository": "bar",
  "status": "active"
}
```

<h3 id="create-artifact-metadata-storage-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the artifact.|
|» digest|body|string|true|The digest of the artifact (algorithm:hex-encoded-digest).|
|» version|body|string|false|The artifact version.|
|» artifact_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL where the artifact is stored.|
|» path|body|string(uri)|false|The path of the artifact.|
|» registry_url|body|string(uri)|true|The base URL of the artifact registry.|
|» repository|body|string|false|The repository name within the registry.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the artifact (e.g., active, inactive).|
|» github_repository|body|string|false|The name of the GitHub repository associated with the artifact. This should be used<br>when there are no provenance attestations available for the artifact. The repository<br>must belong to the organization specified in the path parameter.<br><br>If a provenance attestation is available for the artifact, the API will use<br>the repository information from the attestation instead of this parameter.|
|» return_records|body|boolean|false|If true, the endpoint will return the created record in the response body.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|eol|
|» status|deleted|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 1,
  "storage_records": [
    {
      "name": "libfoo",
      "digest": "sha256:1bb1e949e55dcefc6353e7b36c8897d2a107d8e8dca49d4e3c0ea8493fc0bc72",
      "artifact_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/bar/libfoo-1.2.3",
      "registry_url": "https://reg.example.com/artifactory/",
      "repository": "bar",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "2023-10-01T12:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2023-10-01T12:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Artifact metadata storage record stored successfully.|Inline|

`GET /orgs/{org}/artifacts/{subject_digest}/metadata/storage-records`

List artifact storage records with a given subject digest for repositories owned by an organization.

Results are filtered by the authenticated user's permissions; records for repositories the user cannot read are omitted. Fine-grained access tokens require the `artifact-metadata:read` permission.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/artifact-metadata#list-artifact-storage-records">API method documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|subject_digest|path|string|true|The parameter should be set to the attestation's subject's SHA256 digest, in the form `sha256:HEX_DIGEST`.|

## List attestations by bulk subject digests

<a id="opIdorgs/list-attestations-bulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/attestations/bulk-list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "subject_digests": [
      "sha256:abc123",
      "sha512:def456"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/attestations/bulk-list`

List a collection of artifact attestations associated with any entry in a list of subject digests owned by an organization.

The collection of attestations returned by this endpoint is filtered according to the authenticated user's permissions; if the authenticated user cannot read a repository, the attestations associated with that repository will not be included in the response. In addition, when using a fine-grained access token the `attestations:read` permission is required.

**Please note:** in order to offer meaningful security benefits, an attestation's signature and timestamps **must** be cryptographically verified, and the identity of the attestation signer **must** be validated. Attestations can be verified using the [GitHub CLI `attestation verify` command](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify). For more information, see [our guide on how to use artifact attestations to establish a build's provenance](https://docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/attestations#list-attestations-by-bulk-subject-digests">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject_digests": [
    "sha256:abc123",
    "sha512:def456"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-attestations-by-bulk-subject-digests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» subject_digests|body|[string]|true|List of subject digests to fetch attestations for.|
|» predicate_type|body|string|false|Optional filter for fetching attestations with a given predicate type.<br>This option accepts `provenance`, `sbom`, `release`, or freeform text<br>for custom predicate types.|

## List attestations

<a id="opIdorgs/list-attestations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/attestations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/attestations/{subject_digest}`

List a collection of artifact attestations with a given subject digest that are associated with repositories owned by an organization.

The collection of attestations returned by this endpoint is filtered according to the authenticated user's permissions; if the authenticated user cannot read a repository, the attestations associated with that repository will not be included in the response. In addition, when using a fine-grained access token the `attestations:read` permission is required.

**Please note:** in order to offer meaningful security benefits, an attestation's signature and timestamps **must** be cryptographically verified, and the identity of the attestation signer **must** be validated. Attestations can be verified using the [GitHub CLI `attestation verify` command](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify). For more information, see [our guide on how to use artifact attestations to establish a build's provenance](https://docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/attestations#list-attestations">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-attestations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|subject_digest|path|string|true|The parameter should be set to the attestation's subject's SHA256 digest, in the form `sha256:HEX_DIGEST`.|
|predicate_type|query|string|false|Optional filter for fetching attestations with a given predicate type.<br>This option accepts `provenance`, `sbom`, `release`, or freeform text<br>for custom predicate types.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attestations": [
    {
      "repository_id": 1,
      "bundle_url": "https://tmastaging.blob.core.windows.net/attestations/1/2024/11/08/4.json.sn?se=2024-11-09T17%3A13%3A43Z&sig=jPSbbJnIEshUyCjBLU5Ykq0uuGc5UYxTZE1%2FhdBNMXk%3D&sp=r&spr=https%2Chttp&sr=b&st=2024-11-08T17%3A13%3A43Z&sv=2024-08-04",
      "initiator": "user"
    },
    {
      "repository_id": 1,
      "bundle_url": "https://tmastaging.blob.core.windows.net/attestations/1/2024/11/08/5.json.sn?se=2024-11-09T17%3A13%3A43Z&sig=jPSbbJnIEshUyCjBLU5Ykq0uuGc5UYxTZE1%2FhdBNMXk%3D&sp=r&spr=https%2Chttp&sr=b&st=2024-11-08T17%3A13%3A43Z&sv=2024-08-04",
      "initiator": "user"
    }
  ]
}
```

## List organization webhooks

<a id="opIdorgs/list-webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/hooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/hooks`

List webhooks for an organization.

The authenticated user must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit
webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/webhooks#list-organization-webhooks">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>
