## Create an organization webhook

<a id="opIdorgs/create-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/hooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "web",
    "active": true,
    "events": [
      "push",
      "pull_request"
    ],
    "config": {
      "url": "http://example.com/webhook",
      "content_type": "json"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/hooks`

Create a hook that posts payloads in JSON format.

You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or
edit webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/webhooks#create-an-organization-webhook">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "web",
  "active": true,
  "events": [
    "push",
    "pull_request"
  ],
  "config": {
    "url": "http://example.com/webhook",
    "content_type": "json"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Must be passed as "web".|
|» config|body|object|true|Key/value pairs to provide settings for this webhook.|
|» » url|body|[webhook-config-url](#schemawebhook-config-url)|true|The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.|
|» » content_type|body|[webhook-config-content-type](#schemawebhook-config-content-type)|false|The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.|
|» » secret|body|[webhook-config-secret](#schemawebhook-config-secret)|false|If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).|
|» » insecure_ssl|body|[webhook-config-insecure-ssl](#schemawebhook-config-insecure-ssl)|false|none|
|» » username|body|string|false|none|
|» » password|body|string|false|none|
|» events|body|[string]|false|Determines what [events](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads) the hook is triggered for. Set to `["*"]` to receive all possible events.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. Set to `true` to send notifications.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "url": "https://api.github.com/orgs/octocat/hooks/1",
  "ping_url": "https://api.github.com/orgs/octocat/hooks/1/pings",
  "deliveries_url": "https://api.github.com/orgs/octocat/hooks/1/deliveries",
  "name": "web",
  "events": [
    "push",
    "pull_request"

  "active": true,
  "config": {
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "content_type": "json"
  },
  "updated_at": "2011-09-06T20:39:23Z",
  "created_at": "2011-09-06T17:26:27Z",
  "type": "Organization"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
    {
```

## Update an organization webhook

<a id="opIdorgs/update-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/hooks/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "events": [
      "pull_request"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}`

Updates a webhook configured in an organization. When you update a webhook,
the `secret` will be overwritten. If you previously had a `secret` set, you must
provide the same `secret` or set a new `secret` or the secret will be removed. If
you are only updating individual webhook `config` properties, use "[Update a webhook
configuration for an organization](/rest/orgs/webhooks#update-a-webhook-configuration-for-an-organization)".

You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit
webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/webhooks#update-an-organization-webhook">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "events": [
    "pull_request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|hook_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» config|body|object|false|Key/value pairs to provide settings for this webhook.|
|» » url|body|[webhook-config-url](#schemawebhook-config-url)|true|The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.|
|» » content_type|body|[webhook-config-content-type](#schemawebhook-config-content-type)|false|The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.|
|» » secret|body|[webhook-config-secret](#schemawebhook-config-secret)|false|If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).|
|» » insecure_ssl|body|[webhook-config-insecure-ssl](#schemawebhook-config-insecure-ssl)|false|none|
|» events|body|[string]|false|Determines what [events](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads) the hook is triggered for.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. Set to `true` to send notifications.|
|» name|body|string|false|none|

## Redeliver a delivery for an organization webhook

<a id="opIdorgs/redeliver-webhook-delivery"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/hooks/0/deliveries/0/attempts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/attempts`

Redeliver a delivery for a webhook configured in an organization.

You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit
webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/webhooks#redeliver-a-delivery-for-an-organization-webhook">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="redeliver-a-delivery-for-an-organization-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|hook_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.|
|delivery_id|path|integer|true|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
null
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="redeliver-a-delivery-for-an-organization-webhook-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Ping an organization webhook

<a id="opIdorgs/ping-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/hooks/0/pings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook_id}/pings`

This will trigger a [ping event](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/#ping-event)
to be sent to the hook.

You must be an organization owner to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need `admin:org_hook` scope. OAuth apps cannot list, view, or edit
webhooks that they did not create and users cannot list, view, or edit webhooks that were created by OAuth apps.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/webhooks#ping-an-organization-webhook">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|hook_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
```

## Get route stats by actor

<a id="opIdapi-insights/get-route-stats-by-actor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.github.com/orgs/string/insights/api/route-stats/installation/0?min_timestamp=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/insights/api/route-stats/{actor_type}/{actor_id}`

Get API request count statistics for an actor broken down by route within a specified time frame.

Under normal conditions, you can expect API data to appear within 4–6 hours after making a request. During incidents or periods of unusually high volume, it may take longer to show up.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/api-insights#get-route-stats-by-actor">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-route-stats-by-actor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|actor_type|path|string|true|The type of the actor|
|actor_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the actor|
|min_timestamp|query|string|true|The minimum timestamp to query for stats. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|max_timestamp|query|string|false|The maximum timestamp to query for stats. Defaults to the time 30 days ago. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|api_route_substring|query|string|false|Providing a substring will filter results where the API route contains the substring. This is a case-insensitive search.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|actor_type|installation|
|actor_type|classic_pat|
|actor_type|fine_grained_pat|
|actor_type|oauth_app|
|actor_type|github_app_user_to_server|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
|sort|last_rate_limited_timestamp|
|sort|last_request_timestamp|
|sort|rate_limited_request_count|
|sort|http_method|
|sort|api_route|
|sort|total_request_count|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "http_method": "GET",
    "api_route": "/repositories/:repository_id",
    "total_request_count": 544665,
    "rate_limited_request_count": 13,
    "last_request_timestamp": "2024-09-18T15:43:03Z",
    "last_rate_limited_timestamp": "2024-09-18T06:30:09Z"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="get-route-stats-by-actor-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[api-insights-route-stats](#schemaapi-insights-route-stats)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|max_timestamp|query|string|false|The maximum timestamp to query for stats. Defaults to the time 30 days ago. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|

## Get user stats

<a id="opIdapi-insights/get-user-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.github.com/orgs/string/insights/api/user-stats/string?min_timestamp=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/insights/api/user-stats/{user_id}`

Get API usage statistics within an organization for a user broken down by the type of access.

Under normal conditions, you can expect API data to appear within 4–6 hours after making a request. During incidents or periods of unusually high volume, it may take longer to show up.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/api-insights#get-user-stats">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-user-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user to query for stats|
|min_timestamp|query|string|true|The minimum timestamp to query for stats. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|max_timestamp|query|string|false|The maximum timestamp to query for stats. Defaults to the time 30 days ago. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|actor_name_substring|query|string|false|Providing a substring will filter results where the actor name contains the substring. This is a case-insensitive search.|

|sort|total_request_count|

`GET /orgs/{org}/installations`

## Create an organization invitation

<a id="opIdorgs/create-invitation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/invitations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "octocat@github.com",
    "role": "direct_member",
    "team_ids": [
      12,
      26
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/invitations`

Invite people to an organization by using their GitHub user ID or their email address. In order to create invitations in an organization, the authenticated user must be an organization owner.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/members#create-an-organization-invitation">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "octocat@github.com",
  "role": "direct_member",
  "team_ids": [
    12,
    26
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» invitee_id|body|integer|false|**Required unless you provide `email`**. GitHub user ID for the person you are inviting.|
|» email|body|string|false|**Required unless you provide `invitee_id`**. Email address of the person you are inviting, which can be an existing GitHub user.|
|» role|body|string|false|The role for the new member. <br> * `admin` - Organization owners with full administrative rights to the organization and complete access to all repositories and teams.  <br> * `direct_member` - Non-owner organization members with ability to see other members and join teams by invitation.  <br> * `billing_manager` - Non-owner organization members with ability to manage the billing settings of your organization. <br> * `reinstate` - The previous role assigned to the invitee before they were removed from your organization. Can be one of the roles listed above. Only works if the invitee was previously part of your organization.|
|» team_ids|body|[integer]|false|Specify IDs for the teams you want to invite new members to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|admin|
|» role|direct_member|
|» role|billing_manager|
|» role|reinstate|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "login": "monalisa",
  "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjE=",
  "email": "octocat@github.com",
  "role": "direct_member",
  "created_at": "2016-11-30T06:46:10-08:00",
  "inviter": {
    "login": "other_user",
    "id": 1,
    "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjE=",
    "avatar_url": "https://github.com/images/error/other_user_happy.gif",

    "following_url": "https://api.github.com/users/other_user/following{/other_user}",
    "gists_url": "https://api.github.com/users/other_user/gists{/gist_id}",
    "starred_url": "https://api.github.com/users/other_user/starred{/owner}{/repo}",
    "subscriptions_url": "https://api.github.com/users/other_user/subscriptions",
    "organizations_url": "https://api.github.com/users/other_user/orgs",
```

## Set organization membership for a user

<a id="opIdorgs/set-membership-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/memberships/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "role": "member"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/memberships/{username}`

Only authenticated organization owners can add a member to the organization or update the member's role.

*   If the authenticated user is _adding_ a member to the organization, the invited user will receive an email inviting them to the organization. The user's [membership status](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/members#get-organization-membership-for-a-user) will be `pending` until they accept the invitation.
    
*   Authenticated users can _update_ a user's membership by passing the `role` parameter. If the authenticated user changes a member's role to `admin`, the affected user will receive an email notifying them that they've been made an organization owner. If the authenticated user changes an owner's role to `member`, no email will be sent.

**Rate limits**

To prevent abuse, organization owners are limited to creating 50 organization invitations for an organization within a 24 hour period. If the organization is more than one month old or on a paid plan, the limit is 500 invitations per 24 hour period.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/members#set-organization-membership-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role": "member"
}
```

<h3 id="set-organization-membership-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» role|body|string|false|The role to give the user in the organization. Can be one of:  <br> * `admin` - The user will become an owner of the organization.  <br> * `member` - The user will become a non-owner member of the organization.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|admin|
|» role|member|

## Remove organization membership for a user

<a id="opIdorgs/remove-membership-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/memberships/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/memberships/{username}`

In order to remove a user's membership with an organization, the authenticated user must be an organization owner.

If the specified user is an active member of the organization, this will remove them from the organization. If the specified user has been invited to the organization, this will cancel their invitation. The specified user will receive an email notification in both cases.

> [!NOTE]

## Get all organization roles for an organization

<a id="opIdorgs/list-org-roles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/organization-roles \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/organization-roles`

Lists the organization roles available in this organization. For more information on organization roles, see "[Using organization roles](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/using-organization-roles)."

To use this endpoint, the authenticated user must be one of:

- An administrator for the organization.
- An organization member (or a member of a team) assigned a custom organization role that includes the **View organization roles** (`read_organization_custom_org_role`) permission. For more information, see "[Permissions for organization access](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/permissions-of-custom-organization-roles#permissions-for-organization-access)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a id="opIdorgs/revoke-all-org-roles-team"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/organization-roles/teams/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/organization-roles/teams/{team_slug}`

Removes all assigned organization roles from a team. For more information on organization roles, see "[Using organization roles](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/using-organization-roles)."

## Get an organization role

<a id="opIdorgs/get-org-role"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/organization-roles/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/organization-roles/{role_id}`

Gets an organization role that is available to this organization. For more information on organization roles, see "[Using organization roles](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/using-organization-roles)."

To use this endpoint, the authenticated user must be one of:

For more information, see "[Permissions for organization access](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/permissions-of-custom-organization-roles#permissions-for-organization-access)."

## Convert an organization member to outside collaborator

<a id="opIdorgs/convert-member-to-outside-collaborator"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/outside_collaborators/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "async": true
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/outside_collaborators/{username}`

When an organization member is converted to an outside collaborator, they'll only have access to the repositories that their current team membership allows. The user will no longer be a member of the organization. For more information, see "[Converting an organization member to an outside collaborator](https://docs.github.com/articles/converting-an-organization-member-to-an-outside-collaborator/)". Converting an organization member to an outside collaborator may be restricted by enterprise administrators. For more information, see "[Enforcing repository management policies in your enterprise](https://docs.github.com/admin/policies/enforcing-policies-for-your-enterprise/enforcing-repository-management-policies-in-your-enterprise#enforcing-a-policy-for-inviting-outside-collaborators-to-repositories)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/outside-collaborators#convert-an-organization-member-to-outside-collaborator">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "async": true
}
```

<h3 id="convert-an-organization-member-to-outside-collaborator-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» async|body|boolean|false|When set to `true`, the request will be performed asynchronously. Returns a 202 status code when the job is successfully queued.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
null
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="convert-an-organization-member-to-outside-collaborator-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|User is getting converted asynchronously|Inline|
|204|No Content|User was converted|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden if user is the last owner of the organization, not a member of the organization, or if the enterprise enforces a policy for inviting outside collaborators. For more information, see "[Enforcing repository management policies in your enterprise](https://docs.github.com/admin/policies/enforcing-policies-for-your-enterprise/enforcing-repository-management-policies-in-your-enterprise#enforcing-a-policy-for-inviting-outside-collaborators-to-repositories)."|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List requests to access organization resources with fine-grained personal access tokens

<a id="opIdorgs/list-pat-grant-requests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/personal-access-token-requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/personal-access-token-requests`

Lists requests from organization members to access organization resources with a fine-grained personal access token.

Only GitHub Apps can use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/personal-access-tokens#list-requests-to-access-organization-resources-with-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-requests-to-access-organization-resources-with-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|owner|query|[string]|false|A list of owner usernames to use to filter the results.|
|repository|query|string|false|The name of the repository to use to filter the results.|
|permission|query|string|false|The permission to use to filter the results.|
|last_used_before|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show fine-grained personal access tokens used before the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|last_used_after|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show fine-grained personal access tokens used after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|token_id|query|[string]|false|The ID of the token|

## Review requests to access organization resources with fine-grained personal access tokens

<a id="opIdorgs/review-pat-grant-requests-in-bulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/personal-access-token-requests \

      42,
      73
    ],
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/personal-access-token-requests`

Approves or denies multiple pending requests to access organization resources via a fine-grained personal access token.

Only GitHub Apps can use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/personal-access-tokens#review-requests-to-access-organization-resources-with-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens">API method documentation</a>

```json
  "pat_request_ids": [

  ],
  "action": "deny",
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» pat_request_ids|body|[integer]|false|Unique identifiers of the requests for access via fine-grained personal access token. Must be formed of between 1 and 100 `pat_request_id` values.|

## Get registered app installations for external custom properties

<a id="opIdorgs/external-properties-for-repos-get-organization-app-installations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/properties/installations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/properties/installations`

Gets the registered GitHub App installations used to read and write external custom properties for an organization.

A GitHub App installation token will only be able to see its own registration info, whereas an authenticated user will be able to see all registrations for the organization.

To use this endpoint, the authenticated caller must have the `organization_external_properties_for_repos:admin` permission.

## Register an app installation for external custom properties

<a id="opIdorgs/external-properties-for-repos-register-organization-app-installation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/properties/installations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "installation_id": 67890,
    "display_name": "Acme"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/properties/installations`

Registers a GitHub App installation so it can read and write external custom properties for an organization, and assigns it a display name.

The display name must be 1 to 15 characters and contain only letters and numbers. Capitalization is preserved as entered.

An app installation can only be registered once, and its display name can't be changed afterward. Calling with an app installation that has already been registered returns a `422` response with an `already_exists` error code for `installation_id`. If the display name is already in use by another app installation in the organization, the response is `422` with an `already_exists` error code for `display_name`. An invalid display name also returns `422`.

The app installation being registered must have write or admin permission for organization external custom properties for repositories. If it doesn't, the response is `422`. This is the permission of the installation being registered, which isn't necessarily the caller.

Uninstalling the GitHub App unregisters it, and removes the external custom properties it created.

To use this endpoint, the authenticated caller must have the `organization_external_properties_for_repos:admin` permission.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/custom-properties#register-an-app-installation-for-external-custom-properties">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "installation_id": 67890,
  "display_name": "Acme"
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-app-installation-for-external-custom-properties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» installation_id|body|integer|false|The unique identifier of the GitHub App installation to register for managing external custom properties. When authenticating as a GitHub App installation, this defaults to the authenticated installation and can be omitted. It is required for all other callers (users and fine-grained personal access tokens).|
|» display_name|body|string|true|The display name for this app installation's external custom properties in the organization. Must be 1 to 15 characters and contain only letters and numbers. Capitalization is preserved as entered. This can't be changed after the app installation is registered.|

> Example responses

```json
  "display_name": "Acme",
  "installation": {
    "id": 1
  }
}
```

## Create or update external custom property values for organization repositories

<a id="opIdorgs/external-properties-for-repos-create-or-update-organization-values"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/properties/installations/values \

      }
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/properties/installations/values`

Create new or update existing external custom property values for repositories in a batch that belong to an organization.
Each target repository will have its external custom property values updated to match the values provided in the request.

A maximum of 30 repositories can be updated in a single request.

Using a value of `null` for an external custom property will remove or 'unset' the property value from the repository.

To use this endpoint, the authenticated GitHub App must have the `organization_external_properties_for_repos:write` permission.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/custom-properties#create-or-update-external-custom-property-values-for-organization-repositories">API method documentation</a>

```json
  "repository_names": [

      "value": "production"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "service",
      "value": "web"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "team",
      "value": "octocat"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create or update custom properties for an organization

<a id="opIdorgs/custom-properties-for-repos-create-or-update-organization-definitions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/properties/schema \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "properties": [
      {
        "property_name": "environment",
        "value_type": "single_select",
        "required": true,
        "default_value": "production",
        "description": "Prod or dev environment",
        "allowed_values": [
          "production",
          "development"
        ],
        "values_editable_by": "org_actors"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "service",
        "value_type": "string"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "team",
        "value_type": "string",
        "description": "Team owning the repository"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/properties/schema`

Creates new or updates existing custom properties defined for an organization in a batch.

If the property already exists, the existing property will be replaced with the new values.
Missing optional values will fall back to default values, previous values will be overwritten.
E.g. if a property exists with `values_editable_by: org_and_repo_actors` and it's updated without specifying `values_editable_by`, it will be updated to default value `org_actors`.

To use this endpoint, the authenticated user must be one of:
  - An administrator for the organization.
  - A user, or a user on a team, with the fine-grained permission of `custom_properties_org_definitions_manager` in the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/custom-properties#create-or-update-custom-properties-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

```json

  "properties": [
    {
      "property_name": "environment",
      "value_type": "single_select",
      "required": true,
      "default_value": "production",
      "description": "Prod or dev environment",
      "allowed_values": [
        "production",
        "development"
      ],
      "values_editable_by": "org_actors"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "service",
      "value_type": "string"

}
```

|» allowed_values|body|[string]|false|An ordered list of the allowed values of the property.<br>The property can have up to 200 allowed values.|

## Create or update custom property values for organization repositories

<a id="opIdorgs/custom-properties-for-repos-create-or-update-organization-values"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/properties/values \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository_names": [
      "Hello-World",
      "octo-repo"
    ],
    "properties": [
      {
        "property_name": "environment",
        "value": "production"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "service",
        "value": "web"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "team",
        "value": "octocat"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/properties/values`

Create new or update existing custom property values for repositories in a batch that belong to an organization.
Each target repository will have its custom property values updated to match the values provided in the request.

A maximum of 30 repositories can be updated in a single request.

Using a value of `null` for a custom property will remove or 'unset' the property value from the repository.

To use this endpoint, the authenticated user must be one of:
  - An administrator for the organization.
  - A user, or a user on a team, with the fine-grained permission of `custom_properties_org_values_editor` in the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/custom-properties#create-or-update-custom-property-values-for-organization-repositories">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository_names": [
    "Hello-World",
    "octo-repo"
  ],
  "properties": [
    {
      "property_name": "environment",
      "value": "production"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "service",
      "value": "web"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "team",
      "value": "octocat"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-custom-property-values-for-organization-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repository_names|body|[string]|true|The names of repositories that the custom property values will be applied to.|
|» properties|body|[[custom-property-value](#schemacustom-property-value)]|true|List of custom property names and associated values to apply to the repositories.|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-custom-property-values-for-organization-repositories-responses">Responses</h3>

> [!WARNING]
> **Closing down notice:** The ability to enable or disable a security feature for all eligible repositories in an organization is closing down. Please use [code security configurations](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations) instead. For more information, see the [changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2024-07-22-deprecation-of-api-endpoint-to-enable-or-disable-a-security-feature-for-an-organization/).

For more information, see "[Managing security managers in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/managing-security-managers-in-your-organization)."

The authenticated user must be an organization owner or be member of a team with the security manager role to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org`, `write:org`, or `repo` scopes to use this endpoint.

If you specify the `query_suite` parameter, the default setup will be configured with this query suite only on all repositories that didn't have default setup already configured. It will not change the query suite on repositories that already have default setup configured.<br>If you don't specify any `query_suite` in your request, the preferred query suite of the organization will be applied.|

## Get an organization membership for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdorgs/get-membership-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/memberships/orgs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/memberships/orgs/{org}`

If the authenticated user is an active or pending member of the organization, this endpoint will return the user's membership. If the authenticated user is not affiliated with the organization, a `404` is returned. This endpoint will return a `403` if the request is made by a GitHub App that is blocked by the organization.

## Update an organization membership for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdorgs/update-membership-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/memberships/orgs/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "state": "active"
  }'
```

`PATCH /user/memberships/orgs/{org}`

Converts the authenticated user to an active member of the organization, if that user has a pending invitation from the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/members#update-an-organization-membership-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "active"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» state|body|string|true|The state that the membership should be in. Only `"active"` will be accepted.|

## List organizations for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdorgs/list-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/orgs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/orgs`

List organizations for the authenticated user.

For OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic), this endpoint only lists organizations that your authorization allows you to operate on in some way (e.g., you can list teams with `read:org` scope, you can publicize your organization membership with `user` scope, etc.). Therefore, this API requires at least `user` or `read:org` scope for OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic). Requests with insufficient scope will receive a `403 Forbidden` response.

> [!NOTE]
> Requests using a fine-grained access token will receive a `200 Success` response with an empty list.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/orgs#list-organizations-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organizations-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

## List organizations for a user

<a id="opIdorgs/list-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/orgs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/orgs`

List [public organization memberships](https://docs.github.com/articles/publicizing-or-concealing-organization-membership) for the specified user.

This method only lists _public_ memberships, regardless of authentication. If you need to fetch all of the organization memberships (public and private) for the authenticated user, use the [List organizations for the authenticated user](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/orgs#list-organizations-for-the-authenticated-user) API instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/orgs#list-organizations-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Get list of conflicting packages during Docker migration for organization

<a id="opIdpackages/list-docker-migration-conflicting-packages-for-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/docker/conflicts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/docker/conflicts`

Lists all packages that are in a specific organization, are readable by the requesting user, and that encountered a conflict during a Docker migration.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#get-list-of-conflicting-packages-during-docker-migration-for-organization">API method documentation</a>

## List packages for an organization

<a id="opIdpackages/list-packages-for-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.github.com/orgs/string/packages?package_type=npm' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/packages`

Lists packages in an organization readable by the user.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` scope to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#list-packages-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-packages-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|query|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|visibility|query|string|false|The selected visibility of the packages.  This parameter is optional and only filters an existing result set.<br><br>The `internal` visibility is only supported for GitHub Packages registries that allow for granular permissions. For other ecosystems `internal` is synonymous with `private`.<br>For the list of GitHub Packages registries that support granular permissions, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Delete a package for an organization

<a id="opIdpackages/delete-package-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/packages/npm/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}`

Deletes an entire package in an organization. You cannot delete a public package if any version of the package has more than 5,000 downloads. In this scenario, contact GitHub support for further assistance.

The authenticated user must have admin permissions in the organization to use this endpoint. If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must also have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `delete:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#delete-a-package-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Restore a package for an organization

<a id="opIdpackages/restore-package-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/packages/npm/string/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/restore`

Restores an entire package in an organization.

You can restore a deleted package under the following conditions:
  - The package was deleted within the last 30 days.
  - The same package namespace and version is still available and not reused for a new package. If the same package namespace is not available, you will not be able to restore your package. In this scenario, to restore the deleted package, you must delete the new package that uses the deleted package's namespace first.

The authenticated user must have admin permissions in the organization to use this endpoint. If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must also have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `write:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#restore-a-package-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="restore-a-package-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|token|query|string|false|package token|

## Delete package version for an organization

<a id="opIdpackages/delete-package-version-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/packages/npm/string/versions/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions/{package_version_id}`

Deletes a specific package version in an organization. If the package is public and the package version has more than 5,000 downloads, you cannot delete the package version. In this scenario, contact GitHub support for further assistance.

The authenticated user must have admin permissions in the organization to use this endpoint. If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must also have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `delete:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#delete-package-version-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-package-version-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|package_version_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the package version.|

## Restore package version for an organization

<a id="opIdpackages/restore-package-version-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/packages/npm/string/versions/0/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions/{package_version_id}/restore`

Restores a specific package version in an organization.

You can restore a deleted package under the following conditions:
  - The package was deleted within the last 30 days.
  - The same package namespace and version is still available and not reused for a new package. If the same package namespace is not available, you will not be able to restore your package. In this scenario, to restore the deleted package, you must delete the new package that uses the deleted package's namespace first.

The authenticated user must have admin permissions in the organization to use this endpoint. If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must also have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `write:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#restore-package-version-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="restore-package-version-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|package_version_id|path|integer|true|Unique identifier of the package version.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|package_type|npm|
|package_type|maven|
|package_type|rubygems|
|package_type|docker|

|package_type|container|

Deletes a package owned by the authenticated user. You cannot delete a public package if any version of the package has more than 5,000 downloads. In this scenario, contact GitHub support for further assistance.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `delete:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|

## Restore a package for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdpackages/restore-package-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/packages/npm/string/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /user/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/restore`

Restores a package owned by the authenticated user.

You can restore a deleted package under the following conditions:
  - The package was deleted within the last 30 days.
  - The same package namespace and version is still available and not reused for a new package. If the same package namespace is not available, you will not be able to restore your package. In this scenario, to restore the deleted package, you must delete the new package that uses the deleted package's namespace first.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `write:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#restore-a-package-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|token|query|string|false|package token|

## List packages for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/list-packages-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.github.com/users/string/packages?package_type=npm' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/packages`

Lists all packages in a user's namespace for which the requesting user has access.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` scope to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#list-packages-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-packages-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|query|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|visibility|query|string|false|The selected visibility of the packages.  This parameter is optional and only filters an existing result set.<br><br>The `internal` visibility is only supported for GitHub Packages registries that allow for granular permissions. For other ecosystems `internal` is synonymous with `private`.<br>For the list of GitHub Packages registries that support granular permissions, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|package_type|npm|
|package_type|maven|
|package_type|rubygems|
|package_type|docker|
|package_type|nuget|
|package_type|container|
|visibility|public|
|visibility|private|
|visibility|internal|

## Get a package for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/get-package-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/packages/npm/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}`

Gets a specific package metadata for a public package owned by a user.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` scope to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#get-a-package-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|package_type|npm|
|package_type|maven|
|package_type|rubygems|
|package_type|docker|
|package_type|nuget|
|package_type|container|

## Delete a package for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/delete-package-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/packages/npm/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /users/{username}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}`

Deletes an entire package for a user. You cannot delete a public package if any version of the package has more than 5,000 downloads. In this scenario, contact GitHub support for further assistance.

If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `delete:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#delete-a-package-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-package-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|

## Restore a package for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/restore-package-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/packages/npm/string/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /users/{username}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/restore`

Restores an entire package for a user.

You can restore a deleted package under the following conditions:
  - The package was deleted within the last 30 days.
  - The same package namespace and version is still available and not reused for a new package. If the same package namespace is not available, you will not be able to restore your package. In this scenario, to restore the deleted package, you must delete the new package that uses the deleted package's namespace first.

If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `write:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#restore-a-package-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="restore-a-package-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|

## Delete package version for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/delete-package-version-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/packages/npm/string/versions/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /users/{username}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions/{package_version_id}`

Deletes a specific package version for a user. If the package is public and the package version has more than 5,000 downloads, you cannot delete the package version. In this scenario, contact GitHub support for further assistance.

If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `delete:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. ## Restore package version for a user

<a id="opIdpackages/restore-package-version-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/packages/npm/string/versions/0/restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /users/{username}/packages/{package_type}/{package_name}/versions/{package_version_id}/restore`

Restores a specific package version for a user.

You can restore a deleted package under the following conditions:
  - The package was deleted within the last 30 days.
  - The same package namespace and version is still available and not reused for a new package. If the same package namespace is not available, you will not be able to restore your package. In this scenario, to restore the deleted package, you must delete the new package that uses the deleted package's namespace first.

If the `package_type` belongs to a GitHub Packages registry that supports granular permissions, the authenticated user must have admin permissions to the package. For the list of these registries, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:packages` and `write:packages` scopes to use this endpoint. For more information, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#permissions-for-repository-scoped-packages)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/packages/packages#restore-package-version-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

|package_type|path|string|true|The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.|
|package_name|path|string|true|The name of the package.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-pulls">pulls</h1>

Interact with GitHub Pull Requests.

## List pull requests

<a id="opIdpulls/list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`

Lists pull requests in a specified repository.

Draft pull requests are available in public repositories with GitHub
Free and GitHub Free for organizations, GitHub Pro, and legacy per-repository billing
plans, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise
Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products)
in the GitHub Help documentation.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|state|query|string|false|Either `open`, `closed`, or `all` to filter by state.|
|head|query|string|false|Filter pulls by head user or head organization and branch name in the format of `user:ref-name` or `organization:ref-name`. For example: `github:new-script-format` or `octocat:test-branch`.|
|base|query|string|false|Filter pulls by base branch name. Example: `gh-pages`.|
|sort|query|string|false|What to sort results by. `popularity` will sort by the number of comments. `long-running` will sort by date created and will limit the results to pull requests that have been open for more than a month and have had activity within the past month.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction of the sort. Default: `desc` when sort is `created` or sort is not specified, otherwise `asc`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|state|all|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|popularity|
|sort|long-running|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
