<h3 id="list-pull-requests-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[pull-request-simple](#schemapull-request-simple)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "Amazing new feature",
    "body": "Please pull these awesome changes in!",
    "head": "octocat:new-feature",
    "base": "master"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`

Draft pull requests are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations, GitHub Pro, and legacy per-repository billing plans, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

To open or update a pull request in a public repository, you must have write access to the head or the source branch. For organization-owned repositories, you must be a member of the organization that owns the repository to open or update a pull request.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)" and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Amazing new feature",
  "body": "Please pull these awesome changes in!",
  "head": "octocat:new-feature",
  "base": "master"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is specified.|
|» head|body|string|true|The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. For cross-repository pull requests in the same network, namespace `head` with a user like this: `username:branch`.|
|» head_repo|body|string(repo.nwo)|false|The name of the repository where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both repositories are owned by the same organization.|
|» base|body|string|true|The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This should be an existing branch on the current repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base of another repository.|
|» body|body|string|false|The contents of the pull request.|
|» maintainer_can_modify|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether [maintainers can modify](https://docs.github.com/articles/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork/) the pull request.|
|» draft|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the pull request is a draft. See "[Draft Pull Requests](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-pull-requests#draft-pull-requests)" in the GitHub Help documentation to learn more.|
|» issue|body|integer(int64)|false|An issue in the repository to convert to a pull request. The issue title, body, and comments will become the title, body, and comments on the new pull request. Required unless `title` is specified.|

## List review comments in a repository

<a id="opIdpulls/list-review-comments-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments`

Lists review comments for all pull requests in a repository. By default,
review comments are in ascending order by ID.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#list-review-comments-in-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-review-comments-in-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|sort|query|string|false|none|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results. Ignored without `sort` parameter.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|created_at|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get a review comment for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/get-review-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/comments/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}`

Provides details for a specified review comment.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#get-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the comment.|

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/comments/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "I like this too!"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}`

Edits the content of a specified review comment.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#update-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": "I like this too!"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the comment.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» body|body|string|true|The text of the reply to the review comment.|

## Get a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}`

Draft pull requests are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations, GitHub Pro, and legacy per-repository billing plans, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

Lists details of a pull request by providing its number.

When you get, [create](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls/#create-a-pull-request), or [edit](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#update-a-pull-request) a pull request, GitHub creates a merge commit to test whether the pull request can be automatically merged into the base branch. This test commit is not added to the base branch or the head branch. You can review the status of the test commit using the `mergeable` key. For more information, see "[Checking mergeability of pull requests](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-git-database-api#checking-mergeability-of-pull-requests)".

The value of the `mergeable` attribute can be `true`, `false`, or `null`. If the value is `null`, then GitHub has started a background job to compute the mergeability. After giving the job time to complete, resubmit the request. When the job finishes, you will see a non-`null` value for the `mergeable` attribute in the response. If `mergeable` is `true`, then `merge_commit_sha` will be the SHA of the _test_ merge commit.

The value of the `merge_commit_sha` attribute changes depending on the state of the pull request. Before merging a pull request, the `merge_commit_sha` attribute holds the SHA of the _test_ merge commit. After merging a pull request, the `merge_commit_sha` attribute changes depending on how you merged the pull request:

*   If merged as a [merge commit](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-merge-methods-on-github/), `merge_commit_sha` represents the SHA of the merge commit.
*   If merged via a [squash](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-merge-methods-on-github/#squashing-your-merge-commits), `merge_commit_sha` represents the SHA of the squashed commit on the base branch.
*   If [rebased](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-merge-methods-on-github/#rebasing-and-merging-your-commits), `merge_commit_sha` represents the commit that the base branch was updated to.

Pass the appropriate [media type](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types) to fetch diff and patch formats.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.diff`**: For more information, see "[git-diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff)" in the Git documentation. If a diff is corrupt, contact us through the [GitHub Support portal](https://support.github.com/). Include the repository name and pull request ID in your message.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|

|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|

|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable|Inline|

## Update a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "new title",
    "body": "updated body",
    "state": "open",
    "base": "master"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}`

Draft pull requests are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations, GitHub Pro, and legacy per-repository billing plans, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

To open or update a pull request in a public repository, you must have write access to the head or the source branch. For organization-owned repositories, you must be a member of the organization that owns the repository to open or update a pull request.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#update-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "new title",
  "body": "updated body",
  "state": "open",
  "base": "master"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the pull request.|
|» body|body|string|false|The contents of the pull request.|
|» state|body|string|false|State of this Pull Request. Either `open` or `closed`.|
|» base|body|string|false|The name of the branch you want your changes pulled into. This should be an existing branch on the current repository. You cannot update the base branch on a pull request to point to another repository.|
|» maintainer_can_modify|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether [maintainers can modify](https://docs.github.com/articles/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork/) the pull request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|open|
|» state|closed|

## List review comments on a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/list-review-comments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments`

Lists all review comments for a specified pull request. By default, review comments
are in ascending order by ID.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#list-review-comments-on-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-review-comments-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results. Ignored without `sort` parameter.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Create a review comment for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/create-review-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/comments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "Great stuff!",
    "commit_id": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e",
    "path": "file1.txt",
    "start_line": 1,
    "start_side": "RIGHT",
    "line": 2,
    "side": "RIGHT"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments`

Creates a review comment on the diff of a specified pull request. To add a regular comment to a pull request timeline, see "[Create an issue comment](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#create-an-issue-comment)."

If your comment applies to more than one line in the pull request diff, you should use the parameters `line`, `side`, and optionally `start_line` and `start_side` in your request.

The `position` parameter is closing down. If you use `position`, the `line`, `side`, `start_line`, and `start_side` parameters are not required.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": "Great stuff!",
  "commit_id": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e",
  "path": "file1.txt",
  "start_line": 1,
  "start_side": "RIGHT",
  "line": 2,
  "side": "RIGHT"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» body|body|string|true|The text of the review comment.|
|» commit_id|body|string|true|The SHA of the commit needing a comment. Not using the latest commit SHA may render your comment outdated if a subsequent commit modifies the line you specify as the `position`.|
|» path|body|string|true|The relative path to the file that necessitates a comment.|
|» position|body|integer|false|**Deprecated.** **This parameter is closing down. Use `line` instead**. The position in the diff where you want to add a review comment. Note this value is not the same as the line number in the file. The position value equals the number of lines down from the first "@@" hunk header in the file you want to add a comment. The line just below the "@@" line is position 1, the next line is position 2, and so on. The position in the diff continues to increase through lines of whitespace and additional hunks until the beginning of a new file.|
|» side|body|string|false|In a split diff view, the side of the diff that the pull request's changes appear on. Can be `LEFT` or `RIGHT`. Use `LEFT` for deletions that appear in red. Use `RIGHT` for additions that appear in green or unchanged lines that appear in white and are shown for context. For a multi-line comment, side represents whether the last line of the comment range is a deletion or addition. For more information, see "[Diff view options](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-comparing-branches-in-pull-requests#diff-view-options)" in the GitHub Help documentation.|
|» line|body|integer|false|**Required unless using `subject_type:file`**. The line of the blob in the pull request diff that the comment applies to. For a multi-line comment, the last line of the range that your comment applies to.|
|» start_line|body|integer|false|**Required when using multi-line comments unless using `in_reply_to`**. The `start_line` is the first line in the pull request diff that your multi-line comment applies to. To learn more about multi-line comments, see "[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/articles/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request)" in the GitHub Help documentation.|
|» start_side|body|string|false|**Required when using multi-line comments unless using `in_reply_to`**. The `start_side` is the starting side of the diff that the comment applies to. Can be `LEFT` or `RIGHT`. To learn more about multi-line comments, see "[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/articles/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request)" in the GitHub Help documentation. See `side` in this table for additional context.|
|» in_reply_to|body|integer|false|The ID of the review comment to reply to. To find the ID of a review comment with ["List review comments on a pull request"](#list-review-comments-on-a-pull-request). When specified, all parameters other than `body` in the request body are ignored.|
|» subject_type|body|string|false|The level at which the comment is targeted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» side|LEFT|
|» side|RIGHT|
|» start_side|LEFT|
|» start_side|RIGHT|
|» start_side|side|
|» subject_type|line|
|» subject_type|file|

## Create a reply for a review comment

<a id="opIdpulls/create-reply-for-review-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/comments/0/replies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "Great stuff!"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies`

Creates a reply to a review comment for a pull request. For the `comment_id`, provide the ID of the review comment you are replying to. This must be the ID of a _top-level review comment_, not a reply to that comment. Replies to replies are not supported.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)"
and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-reply-for-a-review-comment">API method documentation</a>

## List commits on a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/list-commits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/commits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/commits`

Lists a maximum of 250 commits for a pull request. To receive a complete
commit list for pull requests with more than 250 commits, use the [List commits](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#list-commits)
endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-commits-on-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Merge a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/merge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/merge \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "commit_title": "Expand enum",
    "commit_message": "Add a new value to the merge_method enum"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge`

> [!NOTE]
> We recommend using the [asynchronous merge API](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#merge-a-pull-request-asynchronously) instead. This endpoint does not support stacked pull requests or merging with a merge queue.

Merges a pull request into the base branch.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications).
Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)" and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#merge-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

```json
  "commit_title": "Expand enum",
  "commit_message": "Add a new value to the merge_method enum"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» commit_title|body|string|false|Title for the automatic commit message.|
|» commit_message|body|string|false|Extra detail to append to automatic commit message.|
|» sha|body|string|false|SHA that pull request head must match to allow merge.|
|» merge_method|body|string|false|The merge method to use.|

## Merge a pull request asynchronously

<a id="opIdpulls/merge-async"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/merge-async \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "commit_title": "Fix race condition",
    "commit_message": "Avoids a race by trying to read the file and handling the exception if it does not exist.",
    "sha": "6358cd125586d9def8c3e5943f23506202da81cc",
    "merge_method": "squash",
    "merge_action": "direct_merge"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge-async`

Merges a pull request into the base branch in the background or adds it to a merge queue. Background processing allows certain types of errors to be retried and reduces the risk of timeouts for complex merges.

This is the required API for merging stacked pull requests. For a stacked pull request, the operation includes all open downstack pull requests.

A new asynchronous merge request returns a `202` response with a UUID that can be used to [fetch the result of the merge](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-the-result-of-an-asynchronous-merge). If another asynchronous merge request is already pending for this pull request, a `409` response returns that request's UUID and merge options instead.

If the pull request is already merged or already in a merge queue, a `200` response is returned immediately. A `merged` result includes the merge commit OID. An `enqueued` result means the pull request was added to the merge queue, not that it has merged.

If the pull request cannot be merged (e.g. because it is closed, or still a draft) this result will be returned immediately with a `400` response status. Branch protection rules and repository rules are not run at this stage, only basic pull request state checks are performed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#merge-a-pull-request-asynchronously">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commit_title": "Fix race condition",
  "commit_message": "Avoids a race by trying to read the file and handling the exception if it does not exist.",
  "sha": "6358cd125586d9def8c3e5943f23506202da81cc",
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "merge_action": "direct_merge"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-a-pull-request-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» commit_title|body|string|false|Title for the automatic commit message. Only supported for direct merges.|
|» commit_message|body|string|false|Extra detail to append to automatic commit message. Only supported for direct merges.|
|» sha|body|string|false|SHA that pull request head must match to allow merge. If not provided, the current head of the PR at the time of the request will be used; if the PR is pushed in between the merge being requested and being executed, the merge will be cancelled.|
|» merge_method|body|string|false|The merge method to use for a direct merge. Only supported for direct merges.|
|» merge_action|body|string|false|The action that will be taken to merge the pull request. `direct_merge` merges the pull request directly without using a merge queue; `merge_queue` adds the pull request to a merge queue; `default` uses a merge queue if one is configured for the target branch, or merges directly otherwise. If omitted, defaults to `default`.|
|» bypass_rules|body|boolean|false|Whether to bypass repository rules that the authenticated actor is permitted to bypass.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» merge_method|merge|
|» merge_method|squash|
|» merge_method|rebase|
|» merge_action|default|
|» merge_action|direct_merge|
|» merge_action|merge_queue|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "merged",
  "details": {
    "message": "Pull request is already merged.",
    "sha": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e"
  }
}
```

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "details": {
    "message": "Merge request enqueued.",
    "uuid": "630b9d5e-3f2a-4f7e-8b0c-2d5f9a8c1e42",
    "merge_method": "squash",
    "merge_action": "direct_merge",
    "expected_head_sha": "6358cd125586d9def8c3e5943f23506202da81cc"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "details": {
    "message": "Pull request is closed."
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "details": {
    "message": "A merge request already exists for this pull request.",
    "uuid": "630b9d5e-3f2a-4f7e-8b0c-2d5f9a8c1e42",
    "merge_method": "squash",
    "merge_action": "default",

  }
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="merge-a-pull-request-asynchronously-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|if the pull request was already merged, or is already in a merge queue|[pull-request-merge-async-result](#schemapull-request-merge-async-result)|
|202|Accepted|if the merge request was accepted and will run in the background|[pull-request-merge-async-result](#schemapull-request-merge-async-result)|
|400|Bad Request|if the pull request is not ready to be merged, e.g. because it is closed|[pull-request-merge-async-result](#schemapull-request-merge-async-result)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|409|Conflict|if there is an existing merge request already enqueued for this pull request|[pull-request-merge-async-result](#schemapull-request-merge-async-result)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get the result of an asynchronous merge

<a id="opIdpulls/get-merge-async-result"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/merge-async/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge-async/{uuid}`

Fetches the current result of an asynchronous merge request, identified by the UUID that was returned when the merge was requested.

While the request's status is `pending`, the response includes the UUID, merge method, merge action, and expected head SHA of the request. Once the asynchronous request completes, its status is one of:

- `merged`: The pull request was merged into the base branch. The response includes the merge commit OID.
- `enqueued`: The pull request was added to a merge queue.
- `failed`: The request failed. The response includes a message describing the failure.

An `enqueued` result is final for the merge queue requests and does not mean the pull request has merged. This result does not change when the merge queue later merges the pull request. To get the eventual merge status, [check if a pull request has been merged](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#check-if-a-pull-request-has-been-merged).

The result of an asynchronous merge request is retained for 24 hours after its most recent update. After this window the request expires and this endpoint returns a `404` response for its UUID.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-the-result-of-an-asynchronous-merge">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-result-of-an-asynchronous-merge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the asynchronous merge request, as returned when the merge was requested.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "details": {
    "message": "Merge request is in progress.",
    "uuid": "630b9d5e-3f2a-4f7e-8b0c-2d5f9a8c1e42",
    "merge_method": "merge",
    "merge_action": "default",
    "expected_head_sha": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e",
    "bypass_rules": false
  }
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-result-of-an-asynchronous-merge-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|the current result of the asynchronous merge request|[pull-request-merge-async-result](#schemapull-request-merge-async-result)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get all requested reviewers for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/list-requested-reviewers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/requested_reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/requested_reviewers`

Gets the users or teams whose review is requested for a pull request. Once a requested reviewer submits a review, they are no longer considered a requested reviewer. Their review will instead be returned by the [List reviews for a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request) operation.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/review-requests#get-all-requested-reviewers-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-all-requested-reviewers-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|

## Request reviewers for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/request-reviewers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/requested_reviewers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "reviewers": [
      "octocat",
      "hubot",
      "other_user"
    ],
    "team_reviewers": [
      "justice-league"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/requested_reviewers`

Requests reviews for a pull request from a given set of users and/or teams.
This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)" and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/review-requests#request-reviewers-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reviewers": [
    "octocat",
    "hubot",
    "other_user"
  ],
  "team_reviewers": [
    "justice-league"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="request-reviewers-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reviewers|body|[string]|false|An array of user `login`s that will be requested.|
|» team_reviewers|body|[string]|false|An array of team `slug`s that will be requested.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

Status Code **503**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|none|none|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove requested reviewers from a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/remove-requested-reviewers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/requested_reviewers \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "reviewers": [
      "octocat",
      "hubot",
      "other_user"
    ],
    "team_reviewers": [
      "justice-league"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/requested_reviewers`

Removes review requests from a pull request for a given set of users and/or teams.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/review-requests#remove-requested-reviewers-from-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reviewers": [
    "octocat",
    "hubot",
    "other_user"
  ],
  "team_reviewers": [
    "justice-league"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-requested-reviewers-from-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reviewers|body|[string]|true|An array of user `login`s that will be removed.|
|» team_reviewers|body|[string]|false|An array of team `slug`s that will be removed.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Rerequest reviewers for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/rerequest-reviewers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/requested_reviewers/rerequest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "reviewers": [
      "octocat",
      "hubot",
      "other_user"
    ],
    "team_reviewers": [
      "justice-league"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/requested_reviewers/rerequest`

Rerequests reviews for a pull request from a given set of users and/or teams.
This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)" and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/review-requests#rerequest-reviewers-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reviewers": [
    "octocat",
    "hubot",
    "other_user"
  ],
  "team_reviewers": [
    "justice-league"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="rerequest-reviewers-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reviewers|body|[string]|false|An array of user `login`s whose reviews will be rerequested.|
|» team_reviewers|body|[string]|false|An array of team `slug`s whose reviews will be rerequested.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## List reviews for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/list-reviews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/reviews \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews`

Lists all reviews for a specified pull request. The list of reviews returns in chronological order.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-reviews-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Create a review for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/create-review"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/reviews \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "commit_id": "ecdd80bb57125d7ba9641ffaa4d7d2c19d3f3091",
    "body": "This is close to perfect! Please address the suggested inline change.",
    "event": "REQUEST_CHANGES",
    "comments": [
      {
        "path": "file.md",
        "position": 6,
        "body": "Please add more information here, and fix this typo."
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews`

Creates a review on a specified pull request.

This endpoint triggers [notifications](https://docs.github.com/github/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/about-notifications). Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting. For more information, see "[Rate limits for the API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api#about-secondary-rate-limits)" and "[Best practices for using the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api)."

Pull request reviews created in the `PENDING` state are not submitted and therefore do not include the `submitted_at` property in the response. To create a pending review for a pull request, leave the `event` parameter blank. For more information about submitting a `PENDING` review, see "[Submit a review for a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#submit-a-review-for-a-pull-request)."

> [!NOTE]
> To comment on a specific line in a file, you need to first determine the position of that line in the diff. To see a pull request diff, add the `application/vnd.github.v3.diff` media type to the `Accept` header of a call to the [Get a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#get-a-pull-request) endpoint.

The `position` value equals the number of lines down from the first "@@" hunk header in the file you want to add a comment. The line just below the "@@" line is position 1, the next line is position 2, and so on. The position in the diff continues to increase through lines of whitespace and additional hunks until the beginning of a new file.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "commit_id": "ecdd80bb57125d7ba9641ffaa4d7d2c19d3f3091",
  "body": "This is close to perfect! Please address the suggested inline change.",
  "event": "REQUEST_CHANGES",
  "comments": [
    {
      "path": "file.md",
      "position": 6,
      "body": "Please add more information here, and fix this typo."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-review-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» commit_id|body|string|false|The SHA of the commit that needs a review. Not using the latest commit SHA may render your review comment outdated if a subsequent commit modifies the line you specify as the `position`. Defaults to the most recent commit in the pull request when you do not specify a value.|
|» body|body|string|false|**Required** when using `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `COMMENT` for the `event` parameter. The body text of the pull request review.|
|» event|body|string|false|The review action you want to perform. The review actions include: `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, or `COMMENT`. By leaving this blank, you set the review action state to `PENDING`, which means you will need to [submit the pull request review](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#submit-a-review-for-a-pull-request) when you are ready.|
|» comments|body|[object]|false|Use the following table to specify the location, destination, and contents of the draft review comment.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The relative path to the file that necessitates a review comment.|
|» » position|body|integer|false|The position in the diff where you want to add a review comment. Note this value is not the same as the line number in the file. The `position` value equals the number of lines down from the first "@@" hunk header in the file you want to add a comment. The line just below the "@@" line is position 1, the next line is position 2, and so on. The position in the diff continues to increase through lines of whitespace and additional hunks until the beginning of a new file.|
|» » body|body|string|true|Text of the review comment.|
|» » line|body|integer|false|none|
|» » side|body|string|false|none|
|» » start_line|body|integer|false|none|
|» » start_side|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|APPROVE|
|» event|REQUEST_CHANGES|
|» event|COMMENT|

## Submit a review for a pull request

<a id="opIdpulls/submit-review"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/reviews/0/events \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "body": "Here is the body for the review.",
    "event": "REQUEST_CHANGES"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}/events`

Submits a pending review for a pull request. For more information about creating a pending review for a pull request, see "[Create a review for a pull request](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request)."

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.raw+json`**: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include `body`. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.text+json`**: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include `body_text`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.html+json`**: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include `body_html`.
- **`application/vnd.github-commitcomment.full+json`**: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include `body`, `body_text`, and `body_html`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews#submit-a-review-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "body": "Here is the body for the review.",
  "event": "REQUEST_CHANGES"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-review-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|review_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the review.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» body|body|string|false|The body text of the pull request review|
|» event|body|string|true|The review action you want to perform. The review actions include: `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, or `COMMENT`. When you leave this blank, the API returns _HTTP 422 (Unrecognizable entity)_ and sets the review action state to `PENDING`, which means you will need to re-submit the pull request review using a review action.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|APPROVE|
|» event|REQUEST_CHANGES|
|» event|COMMENT|

## Update a pull request branch

<a id="opIdpulls/update-branch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/update-branch \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "expected_head_sha": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/update-branch`

Updates the pull request branch with the latest upstream changes by merging HEAD from the base branch into the pull request branch.
Note: If making a request on behalf of a GitHub App you must also have permissions to write the contents of the head repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#update-a-pull-request-branch">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expected_head_sha": "6dcb09b5b57875f334f61aebed695e2e4193db5e"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-pull-request-branch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» expected_head_sha|body|string|false|The expected SHA of the pull request's HEAD ref. This is the most recent commit on the pull request's branch. If the expected SHA does not match the pull request's HEAD, you will receive a `422 Unprocessable Entity` status. You can use the "[List commits](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#list-commits)" endpoint to find the most recent commit SHA. Default: SHA of the pull request's current HEAD ref.|

> Example responses

```json
  "message": "Updating pull request branch.",
  "url": "https://github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/pulls/53"
}
```

```json
    {
```
```json
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stacks`

Creates a stack from an ordered list of pull request numbers. Provide the pull
request numbers from the bottom of the stack to the top. Each pull request's
base ref must match the previous pull request's head ref.

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» pull_requests|body|[integer]|true|An ordered list of pull request numbers forming the stack from bottom to top.|

## Add pull requests to a pull request stack

<a id="opIdpull-request-stacks/add"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/stacks/0/add \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "pull_requests": [
      104,
      102
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stacks/{stack_number}/add`

Appends an ordered list of pull request numbers onto the top of an existing
stack. Provide only the pull requests you want to add, from the current top of
the stack upward. The first new pull request's base ref must match the current
top pull request's head ref.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/stacks#add-pull-requests-to-a-pull-request-stack">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "pull_requests": [
    104,
    102
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-pull-requests-to-a-pull-request-stack-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|stack_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request stack.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» pull_requests|body|[integer]|true|An ordered list of pull request numbers to append to the stack, from the current top upward.|

## Remove pull requests from a pull request stack

<a id="opIdpull-request-stacks/unstack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/stacks/0/unstack \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stacks/{stack_number}/unstack`

Removes the unmerged pull requests from a stack. Pull requests that cannot be
unstacked (for example, those that are queued for merge) are left in place. When pull requests remain in the stack, the updated
stack is returned with a `200`. When no pull requests remain, the stack is
dissolved and a `204` is returned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/stacks#remove-pull-requests-from-a-pull-request-stack">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-pull-requests-from-a-pull-request-stack-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|stack_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request stack.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-rate-limit">rate-limit</h1>

Check your current rate limit status.

## Get rate limit status for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdrate-limit/get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/rate_limit \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /rate_limit`

> [!NOTE]
> Accessing this endpoint does not count against your REST API rate limit.

Rate limit status reflects the applicable limits for the requester and resource category, not the hostname used for the request. Requests authenticated as a user share the user's rate limit across credentials. Requests without authentication use the requesting IP address. API requests routed through either an API hostname or a web hostname can count against the same applicable limit.

Some categories of endpoints have custom rate limits that are separate from the rate limit governing the other REST API endpoints. For this reason, the API response categorizes your rate limit. Under `resources`, you'll see objects relating to different categories:
* The `core` object provides your rate limit status for all non-search-related resources in the REST API.
* The `search` object provides your rate limit status for the REST API for searching (excluding code searches). For more information, see "[Search](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search)."
* The `code_search` object provides your rate limit status for the REST API for searching code. For more information, see "[Search code](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#search-code)."
* The `graphql` object provides your rate limit status for the GraphQL API. For more information, see "[Resource limitations](https://docs.github.com/graphql/overview/resource-limitations#rate-limit)."
* The `integration_manifest` object provides your rate limit status for the `POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions` operation. For more information, see "[Creating a GitHub App from a manifest](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/setting-up-a-github-app/creating-a-github-app-from-a-manifest#3-you-exchange-the-temporary-code-to-retrieve-the-app-configuration)."
* The `dependency_snapshots` object provides your rate limit status for submitting snapshots to the dependency graph. For more information, see "[Dependency graph](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph)."
* The `dependency_sbom` object provides your rate limit status for requesting SBOMs from the dependency graph. For more information, see "[Dependency graph](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependency-graph)."
* The `actions_runner_registration` object provides your rate limit status for registering self-hosted runners in GitHub Actions. For more information, see "[Self-hosted runners](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/self-hosted-runners)."
* The `source_import` object is no longer in use for any API endpoints, and it will be removed in the next API version. For more information about API versions, see "[API Versions](https://docs.github.com/rest/about-the-rest-api/api-versions)."

> [!NOTE]
> The `rate` object is closing down. If you're writing new API client code or updating existing code, you should use the `core` object instead of the `rate` object. The `core` object contains the same information that is present in the `rate` object.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/rate-limit/rate-limit#get-rate-limit-status-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/reactions/reactions#create-reaction-for-a-release">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content": "heart"
}
```

<h3 id="create-reaction-for-a-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|release_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the release.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» content|body|string|true|The [reaction type](https://docs.github.com/rest/reactions/reactions#about-reactions) to add to the release.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» content|+1|
|» content|laugh|
|» content|heart|
|» content|hooray|
|» content|rocket|
|» content|eyes|

## Delete a release reaction

<a id="opIdreactions/delete-for-release"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/releases/0/reactions/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{release_id}/reactions/{reaction_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a repository by `repository_id` using the route `DELETE delete /repositories/:repository_id/releases/:release_id/reactions/:reaction_id`.

Delete a reaction to a [release](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases/releases#get-a-release).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/reactions/reactions#delete-a-release-reaction">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-release-reaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|release_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the release.|
|reaction_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the reaction.|

<h3 id="delete-a-release-reaction-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

This operation does not require authentication

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-repos">repos</h1>

## List organization repositories

<a id="opIdrepos/list-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/repos \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/repos`

Lists repositories for the specified organization.

> [!NOTE]
> In order to see the `security_and_analysis` block for a repository you must have admin permissions for the repository or be an owner or security manager for the organization that owns the repository. For more information, see "[Managing security managers in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/managing-security-managers-in-your-organization)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#list-organization-repositories">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|type|query|string|false|Specifies the types of repositories you want returned.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The order to sort by. Default: `asc` when using `full_name`, otherwise `desc`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|all|
|type|public|
|type|private|
|type|forks|
|type|sources|
|type|member|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|pushed|
|sort|full_name|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
