## List pull requests associated with a commit

<a id="opIdrepos/list-pull-requests-associated-with-commit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string/pulls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{commit_sha}/pulls`

Lists the merged pull request that introduced the commit to the repository. If the commit is not present in the default branch, it will return merged and open pull requests associated with the commit.

To list the open or merged pull requests associated with a branch, you can set the `commit_sha` parameter to the branch name.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-associated-with-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|commit_sha|path|string|true|The SHA of the commit.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Get a commit

<a id="opIdrepos/get-commit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}`

Returns the contents of a single commit reference. You must have `read` access for the repository to use this endpoint.

> [!NOTE]
> If there are more than 300 files in the commit diff and the default JSON media type is requested, the response will include pagination link headers for the remaining files, up to a limit of 3000 files. Each page contains the static commit information, and the only changes are to the file listing.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)." Pagination query parameters are not supported for these media types.

- **`application/vnd.github.diff`**: Returns the diff of the commit. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
- **`application/vnd.github.patch`**: Returns the patch of the commit. Diffs with binary data will have no `patch` property. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
- **`application/vnd.github.sha`**: Returns the commit's SHA-1 hash. You can use this endpoint to check if a remote reference's SHA-1 hash is the same as your local reference's SHA-1 hash by providing the local SHA-1 reference as the ETag.

**Signature verification object**

The response will include a `verification` object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the `verification` object:

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `verified` | `boolean` | Indicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified. |
| `reason` | `string` | The reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in table below. |
| `signature` | `string` | The signature that was extracted from the commit. |
| `payload` | `string` | The value that was signed. |
| `verified_at` | `string` | The date the signature was verified by GitHub. |

These are the possible values for `reason` in the `verification` object:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `expired_key` | The key that made the signature is expired. |
| `not_signing_key` | The "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature. |
| `gpgverify_error` | There was an error communicating with the signature verification service. |
| `gpgverify_unavailable` | The signature verification service is currently unavailable. |
| `unsigned` | The object does not include a signature. |
| `unknown_signature_type` | A non-PGP signature was found in the commit. |
| `no_user` | No user was associated with the `committer` email address in the commit. |
| `unverified_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account. |
| `bad_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature. |
| `unknown_key` | The key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account. |
| `malformed_signature` | There was an error parsing the signature. |
| `invalid` | The signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature. |
| `valid` | None of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified. |

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#get-a-commit">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|ref|path|string|true|The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|

## Get the combined status for a specific reference

<a id="opIdrepos/get-combined-status-for-ref"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string/status \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/status`

Users with pull access in a repository can access a combined view of commit statuses for a given ref. The ref can be a SHA, a branch name, or a tag name.


Additionally, a combined `state` is returned. The `state` is one of:

*   **failure** if any of the contexts report as `error` or `failure`
*   **pending** if there are no statuses or a context is `pending`
*   **success** if the latest status for all contexts is `success`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/statuses#get-the-combined-status-for-a-specific-reference">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-combined-status-for-a-specific-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|path|string|true|The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List commit statuses for a reference

<a id="opIdrepos/list-commit-statuses-for-ref"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/commits/string/statuses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/statuses`

Users with pull access in a repository can view commit statuses for a given ref. The ref can be a SHA, a branch name, or a tag name. Statuses are returned in reverse chronological order. The first status in the list will be the latest one.

This resource is also available via a legacy route: `GET /repos/:owner/:repo/statuses/:ref`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/statuses#list-commit-statuses-for-a-reference">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-commit-statuses-for-a-reference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ref|path|string|true|The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Get community profile metrics

<a id="opIdrepos/get-community-profile-metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/community/profile \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/community/profile`

Returns all community profile metrics for a repository. The repository cannot be a fork.

The returned metrics include an overall health score, the repository description, the presence of documentation, the
detected code of conduct, the detected license, and the presence of ISSUE\_TEMPLATE, PULL\_REQUEST\_TEMPLATE,
README, and CONTRIBUTING files.

The `health_percentage` score is defined as a percentage of how many of
the recommended community health files are present. For more information, see
"[About community profiles for public repositories](https://docs.github.com/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/about-community-profiles-for-public-repositories)."

`content_reports_enabled` is only returned for organization-owned repositories.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/metrics/community#get-community-profile-metrics">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-community-profile-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Compare two commits

<a id="opIdrepos/compare-commits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/compare/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{basehead}`

Compares two commits against one another. You can compare refs (branches or tags) and commit SHAs in the same repository, or you can compare refs and commit SHAs that exist in different repositories within the same repository network, including fork branches. For more information about how to view a repository's network, see "[Understanding connections between repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/viewing-activity-and-data-for-your-repository/understanding-connections-between-repositories)."

This endpoint is equivalent to running the `git log BASE..HEAD` command, but it returns commits in a different order. The `git log BASE..HEAD` command returns commits in reverse chronological order, whereas the API returns commits in chronological order.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.diff`**: Returns the diff of the commit.
- **`application/vnd.github.patch`**: Returns the patch of the commit. Diffs with binary data will have no `patch` property.

The API response includes details about the files that were changed between the two commits. This includes the status of the change (if a file was added, removed, modified, or renamed), and details of the change itself. For example, files with a `renamed` status have a `previous_filename` field showing the previous filename of the file, and files with a `modified` status have a `patch` field showing the changes made to the file.

When calling this endpoint without any paging parameter (`per_page` or `page`), the returned list is limited to 250 commits, and the last commit in the list is the most recent of the entire comparison.

**Working with large comparisons**

To process a response with a large number of commits, use a query parameter (`per_page` or `page`) to paginate the results. When using pagination:

- The list of changed files is only shown on the first page of results, and it includes up to 300 changed files for the entire comparison.
- The results are returned in chronological order, but the last commit in the returned list may not be the most recent one in the entire set if there are more pages of results.

For more information on working with pagination, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

**Signature verification object**

The response will include a `verification` object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The `verification` object includes the following fields:

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| `verified` | `boolean` | Indicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified. |
| `reason` | `string` | The reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in table below. |
| `signature` | `string` | The signature that was extracted from the commit. |
| `payload` | `string` | The value that was signed. |
| `verified_at` | `string` | The date the signature was verified by GitHub. |

These are the possible values for `reason` in the `verification` object:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | ----------- |
| `expired_key` | The key that made the signature is expired. |
| `not_signing_key` | The "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature. |
| `gpgverify_error` | There was an error communicating with the signature verification service. |
| `gpgverify_unavailable` | The signature verification service is currently unavailable. |
| `unsigned` | The object does not include a signature. |
| `unknown_signature_type` | A non-PGP signature was found in the commit. |
| `no_user` | No user was associated with the `committer` email address in the commit. |
| `unverified_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account. |
| `bad_email` | The `committer` email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature. |
| `unknown_key` | The key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account. |
| `malformed_signature` | There was an error parsing the signature. |
| `invalid` | The signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature. |
| `valid` | None of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified. |

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/commits#compare-two-commits">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="compare-two-commits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|basehead|path|string|true|The base branch and head branch to compare. This parameter expects the format `BASE...HEAD`. Both must be branch names in `repo`. To compare with a branch that exists in a different repository in the same network as `repo`, the `basehead` parameter expects the format `USERNAME:BASE...USERNAME:HEAD`.|

## Get repository content

<a id="opIdrepos/get-content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/contents/string \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`

Gets the contents of a file or directory in a repository. Specify the file path or directory with the `path` parameter. If you omit the `path` parameter, you will receive the contents of the repository's root directory.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "[Media types](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types)."

- **`application/vnd.github.raw+json`**: Returns the raw file contents for files and symlinks.
- **`application/vnd.github.html+json`**: Returns the file contents in HTML. Markup languages are rendered to HTML using GitHub's open-source [Markup library](https://github.com/github/markup).
- **`application/vnd.github.object+json`**: Returns the contents in a consistent object format regardless of the content type. For example, instead of an array of objects for a directory, the response will be an object with an `entries` attribute containing the array of objects.

If the content is a directory, the response will be an array of objects, one object for each item in the directory. When listing the contents of a directory, submodules have their "type" specified as "file". Logically, the value _should_ be "submodule". This behavior exists [for backwards compatibility purposes](https://git.io/v1YCW). In the next major version of the API, the type will be returned as "submodule".

If the content is a symlink and the symlink's target is a normal file in the repository, then the API responds with the content of the file. Otherwise, the API responds with an object describing the symlink itself.

If the content is a submodule, the `submodule_git_url` field identifies the location of the submodule repository, and the `sha` identifies a specific commit within the submodule repository. Git uses the given URL when cloning the submodule repository, and checks out the submodule at that specific commit. If the submodule repository is not hosted on github.com, the Git URLs (`git_url` and `_links["git"]`) and the github.com URLs (`html_url` and `_links["html"]`) will have null values.

**Notes**:

- To get a repository's contents recursively, you can [recursively get the tree](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/trees#get-a-tree).
- This API has an upper limit of 1,000 files for a directory. If you need to retrieve
more files, use the [Git Trees API](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/trees#get-a-tree).
- Download URLs expire and are meant to be used just once. To ensure the download URL does not expire, please use the contents API to obtain a fresh download URL for each download.
- If the requested file's size is:
  - 1 MB or smaller: All features of this endpoint are supported.
  - Between 1-100 MB: Only the `raw` or `object` custom media types are supported. Both will work as normal, except that when using the `object` media type, the `content` field will be an empty
string and the `encoding` field will be `"none"`. To get the contents of these larger files, use the `raw` media type.
  - Greater than 100 MB: This endpoint is not supported.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents#get-repository-content">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-repository-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|path|path|string|true|path parameter|
|ref|query|string|false|The name of the commit/branch/tag. Default: the repository’s default branch.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "file",
  "encoding": "base64",
  "size": 5362,
```

## Create or update file contents

<a id="opIdrepos/create-or-update-file-contents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/contents/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "message": "my commit message",
    "committer": {
      "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
      "email": "octocat@github.com"
    },
    "content": "bXkgbmV3IGZpbGUgY29udGVudHM="
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`

Creates a new file or replaces an existing file in a repository.

> [!NOTE]
> If you use this endpoint and the "[Delete a file](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents/#delete-a-file)" endpoint in parallel, the concurrent requests will conflict and you will receive errors. You must use these endpoints serially instead.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint. The `workflow` scope is also required in order to modify files in the `.github/workflows` directory.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents#create-or-update-file-contents">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "message": "my commit message",
  "committer": {
    "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
    "email": "octocat@github.com"
  },
  "content": "bXkgbmV3IGZpbGUgY29udGVudHM="
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-file-contents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|path|path|string|true|path parameter|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» message|body|string|true|The commit message.|
|» content|body|string|true|The new file content, using Base64 encoding.|
|» sha|body|string|false|**Required if you are updating a file**. The blob SHA of the file being replaced.|
|» branch|body|string|false|The branch name. Default: the repository’s default branch.|
|» committer|body|object|false|The person that committed the file. Default: the authenticated user.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the author or committer of the commit. You'll receive a `422` status code if `name` is omitted.|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email of the author or committer of the commit. You'll receive a `422` status code if `email` is omitted.|
|» » date|body|string|false|none|
|» author|body|object|false|The author of the file. Default: The `committer` or the authenticated user if you omit `committer`.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the author or committer of the commit. You'll receive a `422` status code if `name` is omitted.|
|» » email|body|string|true|The email of the author or committer of the commit. You'll receive a `422` status code if `email` is omitted.|
|» » date|body|string|false|none|

## Delete a file

<a id="opIdrepos/delete-file"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/contents/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "message": "my commit message",
    "committer": {
      "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
      "email": "octocat@github.com"
    },
    "sha": "329688480d39049927147c162b9d2deaf885005f"
  }'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`

Deletes a file in a repository.

You can provide an additional `committer` parameter, which is an object containing information about the committer. Or, you can provide an `author` parameter, which is an object containing information about the author.

The `author` section is optional and is filled in with the `committer` information if omitted. If the `committer` information is omitted, the authenticated user's information is used.

You must provide values for both `name` and `email`, whether you choose to use `author` or `committer`. Otherwise, you'll receive a `422` status code.

> [!NOTE]
> If you use this endpoint and the "[Create or update file contents](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents/#create-or-update-file-contents)" endpoint in parallel, the concurrent requests will conflict and you will receive errors. You must use these endpoints serially instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/contents#delete-a-file">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "message": "my commit message",
  "committer": {
    "name": "Monalisa Octocat",
    "email": "octocat@github.com"
  },
  "sha": "329688480d39049927147c162b9d2deaf885005f"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|path|path|string|true|path parameter|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» message|body|string|true|The commit message.|
|» sha|body|string|true|The blob SHA of the file being deleted.|
|» branch|body|string|false|The branch name. Default: the repository’s default branch|
|» committer|body|object|false|object containing information about the committer.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» author|body|object|false|object containing information about the author.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the author (or committer) of the commit|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email of the author (or committer) of the commit|

> Example responses

## List repository contributors

<a id="opIdrepos/list-contributors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/contributors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contributors`

Lists contributors to the specified repository and sorts them by the number of commits per contributor in descending order. This endpoint may return information that is a few hours old because the GitHub REST API caches contributor data to improve performance.

GitHub identifies contributors by author email address. This endpoint groups contribution counts by GitHub user, which includes all associated email addresses. To improve performance, only the first 500 author email addresses in the repository link to GitHub users. The rest will appear as anonymous contributors without associated GitHub user information.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#list-repository-contributors">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-contributors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|anon|query|string|false|Set to `1` or `true` to include anonymous contributors in results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "login": "octocat",
    "id": 1,
    "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjE=",
    "avatar_url": "https://github.com/images/error/octocat_happy.gif",
    "gravatar_id": "",
    "url": "https://api.github.com/users/octocat",
    "html_url": "https://github.com/octocat",
    "followers_url": "https://api.github.com/users/octocat/followers",
```

## Create a deployment

<a id="opIdrepos/create-deployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/deployments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ref": "topic-branch",
    "payload": "{ \"deploy\": \"migrate\" }",
    "description": "Deploy request from hubot"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments`

Deployments offer a few configurable parameters with certain defaults.

The `ref` parameter can be any named branch, tag, or SHA. At GitHub we often deploy branches and verify them
before we merge a pull request.

The `environment` parameter allows deployments to be issued to different runtime environments. Teams often have
multiple environments for verifying their applications, such as `production`, `staging`, and `qa`. This parameter
makes it easier to track which environments have requested deployments. The default environment is `production`.

The `auto_merge` parameter is used to ensure that the requested ref is not behind the repository's default branch. If
the ref _is_ behind the default branch for the repository, we will attempt to merge it for you. If the merge succeeds,
the API will return a successful merge commit. If merge conflicts prevent the merge from succeeding, the API will
return a failure response.

By default, [commit statuses](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/statuses) for every submitted context must be in a `success`
state. The `required_contexts` parameter allows you to specify a subset of contexts that must be `success`, or to
specify contexts that have not yet been submitted. You are not required to use commit statuses to deploy. If you do
not require any contexts or create any commit statuses, the deployment will always succeed.

The `payload` parameter is available for any extra information that a deployment system might need. It is a JSON text
field that will be passed on when a deployment event is dispatched.

The `task` parameter is used by the deployment system to allow different execution paths. In the web world this might
be `deploy:migrations` to run schema changes on the system. In the compiled world this could be a flag to compile an
application with debugging enabled.

Merged branch response:

You will see this response when GitHub automatically merges the base branch into the topic branch instead of creating
a deployment. This auto-merge happens when:
*   Auto-merge option is enabled in the repository
*   Topic branch does not include the latest changes on the base branch, which is `master` in the response example
*   There are no merge conflicts

If there are no new commits in the base branch, a new request to create a deployment should give a successful
response.

Merge conflict response:

This error happens when the `auto_merge` option is enabled and when the default branch (in this case `master`), can't
be merged into the branch that's being deployed (in this case `topic-branch`), due to merge conflicts.

Failed commit status checks:

This error happens when the `required_contexts` parameter indicates that one or more contexts need to have a `success`
status for the commit to be deployed, but one or more of the required contexts do not have a state of `success`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repo_deployment` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments#create-a-deployment">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "topic-branch",
  "payload": "{ \"deploy\": \"migrate\" }",
  "description": "Deploy request from hubot"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ref|body|string|true|The ref to deploy. This can be a branch, tag, or SHA.|
|» task|body|string|false|Specifies a task to execute (e.g., `deploy` or `deploy:migrations`).|
|» auto_merge|body|boolean|false|Attempts to automatically merge the default branch into the requested ref, if it's behind the default branch.|
|» required_contexts|body|[string]|false|The [status](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/statuses) contexts to verify against commit status checks. If you omit this parameter, GitHub verifies all unique contexts before creating a deployment. To bypass checking entirely, pass an empty array. Defaults to all unique contexts.|
|» payload|body|object \| string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|JSON payload with extra information about the deployment.|
|» environment|body|string|false|Name for the target deployment environment (e.g., `production`, `staging`, `qa`).|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Short description of the deployment.|
|» transient_environment|body|boolean|false|Specifies if the given environment is specific to the deployment and will no longer exist at some point in the future. Default: `false`|
|» production_environment|body|boolean|false|Specifies if the given environment is one that end-users directly interact with. Default: `true` when `environment` is `production` and `false` otherwise.|

## Delete a deployment

<a id="opIdrepos/delete-deployment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/deployments/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments/{deployment_id}`

If the repository only has one deployment, you can delete the deployment regardless of its status. If the repository has more than one deployment, you can only delete inactive deployments. This ensures that repositories with multiple deployments will always have an active deployment.

To set a deployment as inactive, you must:

*   Create a new deployment that is active so that the system has a record of the current state, then delete the previously active deployment.
*   Mark the active deployment as inactive by adding any non-successful deployment status.

For more information, see "[Create a deployment](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments/#create-a-deployment)" and "[Create a deployment status](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/statuses#create-a-deployment-status)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repo_deployment` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments#delete-a-deployment">API method documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|deployment_id|path|integer|true|deployment_id parameter|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» state|body|string|true|The state of the status. When you set a transient deployment to `inactive`, the deployment will be shown as `destroyed` in GitHub.|
|» target_url|body|string|false|The target URL to associate with this status. This URL should contain output to keep the user updated while the task is running or serve as historical information for what happened in the deployment.<br><br>> [!NOTE]<br>> It's recommended to use the `log_url` parameter, which replaces `target_url`.|
|» log_url|body|string|false|The full URL of the deployment's output. This parameter replaces `target_url`. We will continue to accept `target_url` to support legacy uses, but we recommend replacing `target_url` with `log_url`. Setting `log_url` will automatically set `target_url` to the same value. Default: `""`|
|» description|body|string|false|A short description of the status. The maximum description length is 140 characters.|
|» environment|body|string|false|Name for the target deployment environment, which can be changed when setting a deploy status. For example, `production`, `staging`, or `qa`. If not defined, the environment of the previous status on the deployment will be used, if it exists. Otherwise, the environment of the deployment will be used.|
|» environment_url|body|string|false|Sets the URL for accessing your environment. Default: `""`|
|» auto_inactive|body|boolean|false|Adds a new `inactive` status to all prior non-transient, non-production environment deployments with the same repository and `environment` name as the created status's deployment. An `inactive` status is only added to deployments that had a `success` state. Default: `true`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|error|
|» state|failure|
|» state|inactive|
|» state|in_progress|
|» state|queued|
|» state|pending|
|» state|success|

## Create a repository dispatch event

<a id="opIdrepos/create-dispatch-event"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/dispatches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "event_type": "on-demand-test",
    "client_payload": {
      "unit": false,
      "integration": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches`

You can use this endpoint to trigger a webhook event called `repository_dispatch` when you want activity that happens outside of GitHub to trigger a GitHub Actions workflow or GitHub App webhook. You must configure your GitHub Actions workflow or GitHub App to run when the `repository_dispatch` event occurs. For an example `repository_dispatch` webhook payload, see "[RepositoryDispatchEvent](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#repository_dispatch)."

The `client_payload` parameter is available for any extra information that your workflow might need. This parameter is a JSON payload that will be passed on when the webhook event is dispatched. For example, the `client_payload` can include a message that a user would like to send using a GitHub Actions workflow. Or the `client_payload` can be used as a test to debug your workflow.

This input example shows how you can use the `client_payload` as a test to debug your workflow.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#create-a-repository-dispatch-event">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "on-demand-test",
  "client_payload": {
    "unit": false,
    "integration": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-dispatch-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» event_type|body|string|true|A custom webhook event name. Must be 100 characters or fewer.|
|» client_payload|body|object|false|JSON payload with extra information about the webhook event that your action or workflow may use. The maximum number of top-level properties is 10. The total size of the JSON payload must be less than 64KB.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Create or update an environment

<a id="opIdrepos/create-or-update-environment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "wait_timer": 30,
    "prevent_self_review": false,
    "reviewers": [
      {
        "type": "User",
        "id": 1
      },
      {
        "type": "Team",
        "id": 1
      }
    ],
    "deployment_branch_policy": {
      "protected_branches": false,
      "custom_branch_policies": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}`

Create or update an environment with protection rules, such as required reviewers. For more information about environment protection rules, see "[Environments](/actions/reference/environments#environment-protection-rules)."

> [!NOTE]
> To create or update name patterns that branches must match in order to deploy to this environment, see "[Deployment branch policies](/rest/deployments/branch-policies)."

> [!NOTE]
> To create or update secrets for an environment, see "[GitHub Actions secrets](/rest/actions/secrets)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/environments#create-or-update-an-environment">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "wait_timer": 30,
  "prevent_self_review": false,
  "reviewers": [
    {
      "type": "User",
      "id": 1
    },
    {
      "type": "Team",
      "id": 1
    }
  ],
  "deployment_branch_policy": {
    "protected_branches": false,
    "custom_branch_policies": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» wait_timer|body|[wait-timer](#schemawait-timer)|false|The amount of time to delay a job after the job is initially triggered. The time (in minutes) must be an integer between 0 and 43,200 (30 days).|
|» prevent_self_review|body|[prevent-self-review](#schemaprevent-self-review)|false|Whether or not a user who created the job is prevented from approving their own job.|
|» reviewers|body|[object]|false|The people or teams that may review jobs that reference the environment. You can list up to six users or teams as reviewers. The reviewers must have at least read access to the repository. Only one of the required reviewers needs to approve the job for it to proceed.|
|» » type|body|[deployment-reviewer-type](#schemadeployment-reviewer-type)|false|The type of reviewer.|
|» » id|body|integer|false|The id of the user or team who can review the deployment|
|» deployment_branch_policy|body|[deployment-branch-policy-settings](#schemadeployment-branch-policy-settings)|false|The type of deployment branch policy for this environment. To allow all branches to deploy, set to `null`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|User|
|» » type|Team|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 161088068,
  "node_id": "MDExOkVudmlyb25tZW50MTYxMDg4MDY4",
  "name": "staging",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/github/hello-world/environments/staging",
  "html_url": "https://github.com/github/hello-world/deployments/activity_log?environments_filter=staging",
  "created_at": "2020-11-23T22:00:40Z",
  "updated_at": "2020-11-23T22:00:40Z",
```

## Create a deployment branch policy

<a id="opIdrepos/create-deployment-branch-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string/deployment-branch-policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "release/*"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}/deployment-branch-policies`

Creates a deployment branch or tag policy for an environment.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/branch-policies#create-a-deployment-branch-policy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "release/*"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deployment-branch-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|body|body|[deployment-branch-policy-name-pattern-with-type](#schemadeployment-branch-policy-name-pattern-with-type)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name pattern that branches or tags must match in order to deploy to the environment.<br><br>Wildcard characters will not match `/`. For example, to match branches that begin with `release/` and contain an additional single slash, use `release/*/*`.<br>For more information about pattern matching syntax, see the [Ruby File.fnmatch documentation](https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.5.1/File.html#method-c-fnmatch).|
|» type|body|string|false|Whether this rule targets a branch or tag|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|branch|
|» type|tag|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 364662,
  "node_id": "MDE2OkdhdGVCcmFuY2hQb2xpY3kzNjQ2NjI=",
  "name": "release/*"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deployment-branch-policy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[deployment-branch-policy](#schemadeployment-branch-policy)|
|303|See Other|Response if the same branch name pattern already exists|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found or `deployment_branch_policy.custom_branch_policies` property for the environment is set to false|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint with a private repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/protection-rules#get-a-custom-deployment-protection-rule">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-custom-deployment-protection-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|protection_rule_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the protection rule.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 3,
  "node_id": "IEH37kRlcGxveW1lbnRTdGF0ddiv",
  "enabled": true,
  "app": {
    "id": 1,
    "node_id": "GHT58kRlcGxveW1lbnRTdTY!bbcy",
    "slug": "a-custom-app",
    "integration_url": "https://api.github.com/apps/a-custom-app"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-custom-deployment-protection-rule-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[deployment-protection-rule](#schemadeployment-protection-rule)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Disable a custom protection rule for an environment

<a id="opIdrepos/disable-deployment-protection-rule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/environments/string/deployment_protection_rules/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/{environment_name}/deployment_protection_rules/{protection_rule_id}`

Disables a custom deployment protection rule for an environment.

The authenticated user must have admin or owner permissions to the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/protection-rules#disable-a-custom-protection-rule-for-an-environment">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="disable-a-custom-protection-rule-for-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment_name|path|string|true|The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|protection_rule_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the protection rule.|

<h3 id="disable-a-custom-protection-rule-for-an-environment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a fork

<a id="opIdrepos/create-fork"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/forks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "organization": "octocat",
    "name": "Hello-World",
    "default_branch_only": true
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/forks`

Create a fork for the authenticated user.

> [!NOTE]
> Forking a Repository happens asynchronously. You may have to wait a short period of time before you can access the git objects. If this takes longer than 5 minutes, be sure to contact [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/contact?tags=dotcom-rest-api).

> [!NOTE]
> Although this endpoint works with GitHub Apps, the GitHub App must be installed on the destination account with access to all repositories and on the source account with access to the source repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/forks#create-a-fork">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization": "octocat",
  "name": "Hello-World",
  "default_branch_only": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-fork-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» organization|body|string|false|Optional parameter to specify the organization name if forking into an organization.|
|» name|body|string|false|When forking from an existing repository, a new name for the fork.|
|» default_branch_only|body|boolean|false|When forking from an existing repository, fork with only the default branch.|

## Get the hash algorithm for a repository

<a id="opIdrepos/get-hash-algorithm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/hash-algorithm \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hash-algorithm`

Returns the hash algorithm used to store repository objects.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#get-the-hash-algorithm-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-the-hash-algorithm-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "hash_algorithm": "sha1"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-hash-algorithm-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[repository-hash-algorithm](#schemarepository-hash-algorithm)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List repository webhooks

<a id="opIdrepos/list-webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/hooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks`

Lists webhooks for a repository. `last response` may return null if there have not been any deliveries within 30 days.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/webhooks#list-repository-webhooks">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Create a repository webhook

<a id="opIdrepos/create-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/hooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "web",
    "active": true,
    "events": [
      "push",
      "pull_request"
    ],
    "config": {
      "url": "https://example.com/webhook",
      "content_type": "json",
      "insecure_ssl": "0"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks`

Repositories can have multiple webhooks installed. Each webhook should have a unique `config`. Multiple webhooks can
share the same `config` as long as those webhooks do not have any `events` that overlap.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/webhooks#create-a-repository-webhook">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "web",
  "active": true,
  "events": [
    "push",
    "pull_request"
  ],
  "config": {
    "url": "https://example.com/webhook",
    "content_type": "json",
    "insecure_ssl": "0"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Use `web` to create a webhook. Default: `web`. This parameter only accepts the value `web`.|
|» config|body|object|false|Key/value pairs to provide settings for this webhook.|
|» » url|body|[webhook-config-url](#schemawebhook-config-url)|false|The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.|
|» » content_type|body|[webhook-config-content-type](#schemawebhook-config-content-type)|false|The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.|
|» » secret|body|[webhook-config-secret](#schemawebhook-config-secret)|false|If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).|
|» » insecure_ssl|body|[webhook-config-insecure-ssl](#schemawebhook-config-insecure-ssl)|false|none|
|» events|body|[string]|false|Determines what [events](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads) the hook is triggered for.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. Set to `true` to send notifications.|

> Example responses

```json
    "push",

    "content_type": "json",

  },

  }
}
```

## Update a repository webhook

<a id="opIdrepos/update-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/hooks/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "add_events": [
      "pull_request"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}`

Updates a webhook configured in a repository. If you previously had a `secret` set, you must provide the same `secret` or set a new `secret` or the secret will be removed. If you are only updating individual webhook `config` properties, use "[Update a webhook configuration for a repository](/rest/webhooks/repo-config#update-a-webhook-configuration-for-a-repository)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/webhooks#update-a-repository-webhook">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "add_events": [
    "pull_request"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-repository-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|hook_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» config|body|[webhook-config](#schemawebhook-config)|false|Configuration object of the webhook|
|» events|body|[string]|false|Determines what [events](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads) the hook is triggered for. This replaces the entire array of events.|
|» add_events|body|[string]|false|Determines a list of events to be added to the list of events that the Hook triggers for.|
|» remove_events|body|[string]|false|Determines a list of events to be removed from the list of events that the Hook triggers for.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. Set to `true` to send notifications.|

## Test the push repository webhook

<a id="opIdrepos/test-push-webhook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/hooks/0/tests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}/tests`

This will trigger the hook with the latest push to the current repository if the hook is subscribed to `push` events. If the hook is not subscribed to `push` events, the server will respond with 204 but no test POST will be generated.

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/invitations/{invitation_id}`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/collaborators/invitations#update-a-repository-invitation">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json

  "permissions": "write"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-repository-invitation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|invitation_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the invitation.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» permissions|body|string|false|The permissions that the associated user will have on the repository. Valid values are `read`, `write`, `maintain`, `triage`, and `admin`.|

|» permissions|triage|
|» permissions|admin|

## List issue types for a repository

<a id="opIdrepos/list-issue-types"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/issue-types \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issue-types`

Lists enabled issue types inherited from the repository owner.
OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.
Fine-grained access tokens require the "Metadata" repository permission (read).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/issue-types#list-issue-types-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-issue-types-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 410,
    "node_id": "IT_kwDNAd3NAZo",
    "name": "Task",
    "description": "A specific piece of work",
    "created_at": "2024-12-11T14:39:09Z",
    "updated_at": "2024-12-11T14:39:09Z"
  },
  {
    "id": 411,
    "node_id": "IT_kwDNAd3NAZs",
    "name": "Bug",
    "description": "An unexpected problem or behavior",
    "created_at": "2024-12-11T14:39:09Z",
    "updated_at": "2024-12-11T14:39:09Z"
  }
]
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-issue-types-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h3 id="list-issue-types-for-a-repository-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[issue-type](#schemaissue-type)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a deploy key

<a id="opIdrepos/create-deploy-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "octocat@octomac",
    "key": "ssh-rsa AAA...",
    "read_only": true
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys`

You can create a read-only deploy key.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deploy-keys/deploy-keys#create-a-deploy-key">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "octocat@octomac",
  "key": "ssh-rsa AAA...",
  "read_only": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deploy-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|A name for the key.|
|» key|body|string|true|The contents of the key.|
|» read_only|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the key will only be able to read repository contents. Otherwise, the key will be able to read and write.  <br>  <br>Deploy keys with write access can perform the same actions as an organization member with admin access, or a collaborator on a personal repository. For more information, see "[Repository permission levels for an organization](https://docs.github.com/articles/repository-permission-levels-for-an-organization/)" and "[Permission levels for a user account repository](https://docs.github.com/articles/permission-levels-for-a-user-account-repository/)."|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "key": "ssh-rsa AAA...",
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/keys/1",
  "title": "octocat@octomac",
  "verified": true,
  "created_at": "2014-12-10T15:53:42Z",
  "read_only": true,
  "added_by": "octocat",
  "last_used": "2022-01-10T15:53:42Z",
  "enabled": true
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-deploy-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[deploy-key](#schemadeploy-key)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete a deploy key

<a id="opIdrepos/delete-deploy-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/keys/0 \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys/{key_id}`

Deploy keys are immutable. If you need to update a key, remove the key and create a new one instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/deploy-keys/deploy-keys#delete-a-deploy-key">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-deploy-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|key_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the key.|

<h3 id="delete-a-deploy-key-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

This operation does not require authentication

## List repository languages

<a id="opIdrepos/list-languages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/languages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`

Lists languages for the specified repository. The value shown for each language is the number of bytes of code written in that language.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#list-repository-languages">API method documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "C": 78769,
  "Python": 7769
}
```

<h3 id="list-repository-languages-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[language](#schemalanguage)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Sync a fork branch with the upstream repository

<a id="opIdrepos/merge-upstream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/merge-upstream \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "branch": "main"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/merge-upstream`

Sync a branch of a forked repository to keep it up-to-date with the upstream repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branches#sync-a-fork-branch-with-the-upstream-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "branch": "main"
}
```

<h3 id="sync-a-fork-branch-with-the-upstream-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» branch|body|string|true|The name of the branch which should be updated to match upstream.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Successfully fetched and fast-forwarded from upstream defunkt:main",
  "merge_type": "fast-forward",
  "base_branch": "defunkt:main"
}
```

<h3 id="sync-a-fork-branch-with-the-upstream-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The branch has been successfully synced with the upstream repository|[merged-upstream](#schemamerged-upstream)|
|409|Conflict|The branch could not be synced because of a merge conflict|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The branch could not be synced for some other reason|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Merge a branch

<a id="opIdrepos/merge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/merges \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "base": "master",
    "head": "cool_feature",
    "commit_message": "Shipped cool_feature!"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/merges`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branches#merge-a-branch">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "base": "master",
  "head": "cool_feature",
  "commit_message": "Shipped cool_feature!"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-a-branch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» base|body|string|true|The name of the base branch that the head will be merged into.|
|» head|body|string|true|The head to merge. This can be a branch name or a commit SHA1.|
|» commit_message|body|string|false|Commit message to use for the merge commit. If omitted, a default message will be used.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response


## Update information about a GitHub Pages site

<a id="opIdrepos/update-information-about-pages-site"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pages \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "cname": "octocatblog.com",
    "source": {
      "branch": "main",
      "path": "/"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages`

Updates information for a GitHub Pages site. For more information, see "[About GitHub Pages](/github/working-with-github-pages/about-github-pages).

The authenticated user must be a repository administrator, maintainer, or have the 'manage GitHub Pages settings' permission.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pages/pages#update-information-about-a-apiname-pages-site">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cname": "octocatblog.com",
  "source": {
    "branch": "main",
    "path": "/"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-information-about-a-github-pages-site-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» cname|body|string \| null|false|Specify a custom domain for the repository. Sending a `null` value will remove the custom domain. For more about custom domains, see "[Using a custom domain with GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site)."|
|» https_enforced|body|boolean|false|Specify whether HTTPS should be enforced for the repository.|
|» build_type|body|string|false|The process by which the GitHub Pages site will be built. `workflow` means that the site is built by a custom GitHub Actions workflow. `legacy` means that the site is built by GitHub when changes are pushed to a specific branch.|
|» source|body|string \| object|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|Update the source for the repository. Must include the branch name, and may optionally specify the subdirectory `/docs`. Possible values are `"gh-pages"`, `"master"`, and `"master /docs"`.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|object|false|Update the source for the repository. Must include the branch name and path.|
|» » branch|body|string|true|The repository branch used to publish your site's source files.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The repository directory that includes the source files for the Pages site. Allowed paths are `/` or `/docs`.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» » *anyOf*|gh-pages|

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages`

Configures a GitHub Pages site. For more information, see "[About GitHub Pages](/github/working-with-github-pages/about-github-pages)."

The authenticated user must be a repository administrator, maintainer, or have the 'manage GitHub Pages settings' permission.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pages/pages#create-a-apiname-pages-site">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object \| null|true|none|
|» build_type|body|string|false|The process in which the Page will be built. Possible values are `"legacy"` and `"workflow"`.|
|» source|body|object|false|The source branch and directory used to publish your Pages site.|

|» » path|body|string|false|The repository directory that includes the source files for the Pages site. Allowed paths are `/` or `/docs`. Default: `/`|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Request a GitHub Pages build

<a id="opIdrepos/request-pages-build"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pages/builds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages/builds`

You can request that your site be built from the latest revision on the default branch. This has the same effect as pushing a commit to your default branch, but does not require an additional commit. Manually triggering page builds can be helpful when diagnosing build warnings and failures.

Build requests are limited to one concurrent build per repository and one concurrent build per requester. If you request a build while another is still in progress, the second request will be queued until the first completes.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pages/pages#request-a-apiname-pages-build">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="request-a-github-pages-build-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/github/developer.github.com/pages/builds/latest",
  "status": "queued"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-github-pages-build-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[page-build-status](#schemapage-build-status)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a DNS health check for GitHub Pages

<a id="opIdrepos/get-pages-health-check"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pages/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages/health`

Gets a health check of the DNS settings for the `CNAME` record configured for a repository's GitHub Pages.

The first request to this endpoint returns a `202 Accepted` status and starts an asynchronous background task to get the results for the domain. After the background task completes, subsequent requests to this endpoint return a `200 OK` status with the health check results in the response.

The authenticated user must be a repository administrator, maintainer, or have the 'manage GitHub Pages settings' permission to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pages/pages#get-a-dns-health-check-for-github-pages">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-dns-health-check-for-github-pages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Create or update custom property values for a repository

<a id="opIdrepos/custom-properties-for-repos-create-or-update-repository-values"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/properties/values \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "properties": [
      {
        "property_name": "environment",
        "value": "production"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "service",
        "value": "web"
      },
      {
        "property_name": "team",
        "value": "octocat"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/properties/values`

Create new or update existing custom property values for a repository.
Using a value of `null` for a custom property will remove or 'unset' the property value from the repository.

Repository admins and other users with the repository-level "edit custom property values" fine-grained permission can use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/custom-properties#create-or-update-custom-property-values-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "properties": [
    {
      "property_name": "environment",
      "value": "production"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "service",
      "value": "web"
    },
    {
      "property_name": "team",
      "value": "octocat"
    }
  ]
}
```

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» properties|body|[[custom-property-value](#schemacustom-property-value)]|true|A list of custom property names and associated values to apply to the repositories.|
