<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-secret-scanning">secret-scanning</h1>

Retrieve secret scanning alerts from a repository.

## List secret scanning alerts for an organization

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/list-alerts-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/secret-scanning/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/secret-scanning/alerts`

Lists secret scanning alerts for eligible repositories in an organization, from newest to oldest.

The authenticated user must be an administrator or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#list-secret-scanning-alerts-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-secret-scanning-alerts-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|state|query|string|false|Set to `open` or `resolved` to only list secret scanning alerts in a specific state.|
|secret_type|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of secret types to return. All default secret patterns are returned. To return generic patterns, pass the token name(s) in the parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.|
|exclude_secret_types|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of secret types to exclude from the results. All default secret patterns are returned except those matching the specified types. Cannot be combined with the `secret_type` parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.|
|exclude_providers|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of provider slugs to exclude from the results.<br>Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).<br>You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.<br>Cannot be combined with the `providers` parameter.|
|providers|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of provider slugs to filter by.<br>Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).<br>You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.<br>Cannot be combined with the `exclude_providers` parameter.|
|resolution|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of resolutions. Only secret scanning alerts with one of these resolutions are listed. Valid resolutions are `false_positive`, `wont_fix`, `revoked`, `pattern_edited`, `pattern_deleted` or `used_in_tests`.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Filters alerts by assignee. Use `*` to get all assigned alerts, `none` to get all unassigned alerts, or a GitHub username to get alerts assigned to a specific user.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by. `created` means when the alert was created. `updated` means when the alert was updated or resolved.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events before this cursor. To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "before" query string.|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events after this cursor.  To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "after" query string.|
|validity|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of validities that, when present, will return alerts that match the validities in this list. Valid options are `active`, `inactive`, and `unknown`.|
|is_publicly_leaked|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the publicly-leaked tag being present.|
|is_multi_repo|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the multi-repo tag being present.|
|hide_secret|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to hide literal secrets in the results.|
|is_bypassed|query|boolean|false|A boolean value (`true` or `false`) indicating whether to filter alerts by their push protection bypass status. When set to `true`, only alerts that were created because a push protection rule was bypassed will be returned. When set to `false`, only alerts that were not caused by a push protection bypass will be returned.|
|included_metadata|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of metadata fields to filter alerts by. Only alerts that have all of the<br>specified metadata fields attached will be returned. Possible values are: `owner-email`, `owner-id`,<br>`owner-name`, `secret-id`, `secret-name`, `secret-issued-date`, `secret-expiration-date`, `organization-name`,<br>`organization-id`, `last-used-date`, and `has-organization-access`.|
|owner_email_hash|query|string|false|Filters alerts to only those whose attached `owner_email` metadata field matches the<br>provided value. The value must be the lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the email<br>address to match (for example, the SHA-256 of `user@example.com`). Only alerts that<br>have an `owner_email` metadata value whose SHA-256 hash equals this parameter are<br>returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|resolved|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## List organization custom patterns

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/list-org-custom-patterns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/secret-scanning/custom-patterns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/secret-scanning/custom-patterns`

Lists secret scanning custom patterns for an organization.

Personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/custom-patterns#list-organization-custom-patterns">API method documentation</a>

## List secret scanning alerts for a repository

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/list-alerts-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts`

Lists secret scanning alerts for an eligible repository, from newest to oldest.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the repository or for the organization that owns the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#list-secret-scanning-alerts-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-secret-scanning-alerts-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|state|query|string|false|Set to `open` or `resolved` to only list secret scanning alerts in a specific state.|
|secret_type|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of secret types to return. All default secret patterns are returned. To return generic patterns, pass the token name(s) in the parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.|
|exclude_secret_types|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of secret types to exclude from the results. All default secret patterns are returned except those matching the specified types. Cannot be combined with the `secret_type` parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.|
|exclude_providers|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of provider slugs to exclude from the results.<br>Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).<br>You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.<br>Cannot be combined with the `providers` parameter.|
|providers|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of provider slugs to filter by.<br>Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).<br>You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.<br>Cannot be combined with the `exclude_providers` parameter.|
|resolution|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of resolutions. Only secret scanning alerts with one of these resolutions are listed. Valid resolutions are `false_positive`, `wont_fix`, `revoked`, `pattern_edited`, `pattern_deleted` or `used_in_tests`.|
|assignee|query|string|false|Filters alerts by assignee. Use `*` to get all assigned alerts, `none` to get all unassigned alerts, or a GitHub username to get alerts assigned to a specific user.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by. `created` means when the alert was created. `updated` means when the alert was updated or resolved.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events before this cursor. To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "before" query string.|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events after this cursor.  To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "after" query string.|
|validity|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of validities that, when present, will return alerts that match the validities in this list. Valid options are `active`, `inactive`, and `unknown`.|
|is_publicly_leaked|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the publicly-leaked tag being present.|
|is_multi_repo|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the multi-repo tag being present.|
|hide_secret|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to hide literal secrets in the results.|
|is_bypassed|query|boolean|false|A boolean value (`true` or `false`) indicating whether to filter alerts by their push protection bypass status. When set to `true`, only alerts that were created because a push protection rule was bypassed will be returned. When set to `false`, only alerts that were not caused by a push protection bypass will be returned.|
|included_metadata|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of metadata fields to filter alerts by. Only alerts that have all of the<br>specified metadata fields attached will be returned. Possible values are: `owner-email`, `owner-id`,<br>`owner-name`, `secret-id`, `secret-name`, `secret-issued-date`, `secret-expiration-date`, `organization-name`,<br>`organization-id`, `last-used-date`, and `has-organization-access`.|
|owner_email_hash|query|string|false|Filters alerts to only those whose attached `owner_email` metadata field matches the<br>provided value. The value must be the lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 hash of the email<br>address to match (for example, the SHA-256 of `user@example.com`). Only alerts that<br>have an `owner_email` metadata value whose SHA-256 hash equals this parameter are<br>returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|open|
|state|resolved|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get a secret scanning alert

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/get-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/alerts/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}`

Gets a single secret scanning alert detected in an eligible repository.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the repository or for the organization that owns the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#get-a-secret-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-secret-scanning-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|
|hide_secret|query|boolean|false|A boolean value representing whether or not to hide literal secrets in the results.|

## Update a secret scanning alert

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/update-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/alerts/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "state": "resolved",
    "resolution": "false_positive"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}`

Updates the status of a secret scanning alert in an eligible repository.

You can also use this endpoint to assign or unassign an alert to a user who has write access to the repository.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the repository or for the organization that owns the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#update-a-secret-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "state": "resolved",
  "resolution": "false_positive"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-secret-scanning-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» state|body|[secret-scanning-alert-state](#schemasecret-scanning-alert-state)|false|Sets the state of the secret scanning alert. You must provide `resolution` when you set the state to `resolved`.|
|» resolution|body|[secret-scanning-alert-resolution](#schemasecret-scanning-alert-resolution)|false|**Required when the `state` is `resolved`.** The reason for resolving the alert.|
|» resolution_comment|body|[secret-scanning-alert-resolution-comment](#schemasecret-scanning-alert-resolution-comment)|false|An optional comment when closing or reopening an alert. Cannot be updated or deleted.|
|» assignee|body|[secret-scanning-alert-assignee](#schemasecret-scanning-alert-assignee)|false|The username of the user to assign to the alert. Set to `null` to unassign the alert.|
|» validity|body|string \| null|false|Sets the validity of the secret scanning alert. Can be `active`, `inactive`, or `null` to clear the override.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|open|
|» state|resolved|
|» resolution|false_positive|
|» resolution|wont_fix|
|» resolution|revoked|
|» resolution|used_in_tests|
|» resolution|null|
|» validity|active|
|» validity|inactive|
|» validity|null|

## List locations for a secret scanning alert

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/list-locations-for-alert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/alerts/0/locations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts/{alert_number}/locations`

Lists all locations for a given secret scanning alert for an eligible repository.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the repository or for the organization that owns the repository to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#list-locations-for-a-secret-scanning-alert">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|alert_number|path|[alert-number](#schemaalert-number)|true|The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List repository custom patterns

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/list-repo-custom-patterns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/custom-patterns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/custom-patterns`

Lists secret scanning custom patterns for a repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

Fine-grained access tokens require the `administration:write` repository permission.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/custom-patterns#list-repository-custom-patterns">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-custom-patterns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|state|query|string|false|Filter custom patterns by state. When absent, returns patterns in all states.|
|push_protection|query|string|false|Filter custom patterns by whether push protection is enabled. When absent, returns patterns regardless of push protection status.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|published|
|state|unpublished|
|push_protection|enabled|
|push_protection|disabled|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|name|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Update a repository custom pattern

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/update-repo-custom-pattern"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/custom-patterns/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "pattern": "updated_secret_[0-9A-Z]{16}",
    "start_delimiter": "[^0-9A-Za-z]",
    "end_delimiter": "[^0-9A-Za-z]",
    "must_match": [
      "updated_secret_[0-9]{2}*"
    ],
    "must_not_match": [
      "updated_secret_1234567890ABCDEF"
    ],
    "custom_pattern_version": "0ujsswThIGTUYm2K8FjOOfXtY1K"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/custom-patterns/{pattern_id}`

Updates a secret scanning custom pattern for a repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

Fine-grained access tokens require the `administration:write` repository permission.

```json
    "updated_secret_[0-9]{2}*"
  ],
  "must_not_match": [

}
```

<h3 id="update-a-repository-custom-pattern-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

|» must_match|body|[string]|false|Updated list of regexes that the secret must match.|
|» must_not_match|body|[string]|false|Updated list of regexes that the secret must not match.|
|» custom_pattern_version|body|[secret-scanning-row-version](#schemasecret-scanning-row-version)|true|The version of the entity. This is used to confirm you're updating the current version of the entity and mitigate unintentionally overriding someone else's update.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Create a push protection bypass

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/create-push-protection-bypass"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/push-protection-bypasses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "reason": "will_fix_later",
    "placeholder_id": "2k4dM4tseyC5lPIsjl5emX9sPNk"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/push-protection-bypasses`

Creates a bypass for a previously push protected secret.

The authenticated user must be the original author of the committed secret.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#create-a-push-protection-bypass">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "will_fix_later",
  "placeholder_id": "2k4dM4tseyC5lPIsjl5emX9sPNk"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-push-protection-bypass-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reason|body|[secret-scanning-push-protection-bypass-reason](#schemasecret-scanning-push-protection-bypass-reason)|true|The reason for bypassing push protection.|
|» placeholder_id|body|[secret-scanning-push-protection-bypass-placeholder-id](#schemasecret-scanning-push-protection-bypass-placeholder-id)|true|The ID of the push protection bypass placeholder. This value is returned on any push protected routes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» reason|false_positive|
|» reason|used_in_tests|
|» reason|will_fix_later|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "reason": "will_fix_later",
  "expire_at": "2020-11-06T18:18:30Z",
  "token_type": "mailchimp_api_key"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string"
}
```

## Get secret scanning scan history for a repository

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning/get-scan-history"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/secret-scanning/scan-history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/scan-history`

Lists the latest default incremental and backfill scans by type for a repository.

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint requires [GitHub Advanced Security](https://docs.github.com/get-started/learning-about-github/about-github-advanced-security).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `security_events` scope to use this endpoint. If this endpoint is only used with public repositories, the token can use the `public_repo` scope instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#get-secret-scanning-scan-history-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Create a team

<a id="opIdteams/create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Justice League",
    "description": "A great team",
    "permission": "push",
    "notification_setting": "notifications_enabled",
    "privacy": "closed"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/teams`

To create a team, the authenticated user must be a member or owner of `{org}`. By default, organization members can create teams. Organization owners can limit team creation to organization owners. For more information, see "[Setting team creation permissions](https://docs.github.com/articles/setting-team-creation-permissions-in-your-organization)."

When you create a new team, you automatically become a team maintainer without explicitly adding yourself to the optional array of `maintainers`. For more information, see "[About teams](https://docs.github.com/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/about-teams)".

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#create-a-team">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Justice League",
  "description": "A great team",
  "permission": "push",
  "notification_setting": "notifications_enabled",
  "privacy": "closed"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the team.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the team.|
|» maintainers|body|[string]|false|List GitHub usernames for organization members who will become team maintainers.|
|» repo_names|body|[string]|false|The full name (e.g., "organization-name/repository-name") of repositories to add the team to.|
|» privacy|body|string|false|The level of privacy this team should have. The options are:  <br>**For a non-nested team:**  <br> * `secret` - only visible to organization owners and members of this team.  <br> * `closed` - visible to all members of this organization.  <br>Default: `secret`  <br>**For a parent or child team:**  <br> * `closed` - visible to all members of this organization.  <br>Default for child team: `closed`|
|» notification_setting|body|string|false|The notification setting the team has chosen. The options are:  <br> * `notifications_enabled` - team members receive notifications when the team is @mentioned.  <br> * `notifications_disabled` - no one receives notifications.  <br>Default: `notifications_enabled`|
|» permission|body|string|false|**Closing down notice**. The permission that new repositories will be added to the team with when none is specified.|
|» parent_team_id|body|integer|false|The ID of a team to set as the parent team.|
|» parent_team_slug|body|string|false|The slug of a team to set as the parent team. Ignored when `parent_team_id` is also provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» privacy|secret|
|» privacy|closed|
|» notification_setting|notifications_enabled|
|» notification_setting|notifications_disabled|
|» permission|pull|
|» permission|push|

> Example responses

```json
  "node_id": "MDQ6VGVhbTE=",
```

## Get a team by name

<a id="opIdteams/get-by-name"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}`

Gets a team using the team's `slug`. To create the `slug`, GitHub replaces special characters in the `name` string, changes all words to lowercase, and replaces spaces with a `-` separator. For example, `"My TEam Näme"` would become `my-team-name`.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `GET /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}`.

## Delete a team

<a id="opIdteams/delete-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}`

To delete a team, the authenticated user must be an organization owner or team maintainer.

If you are an organization owner, deleting a parent team will delete all of its child teams as well.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#delete-a-team">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Update a team

<a id="opIdteams/update-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "new team name",
    "description": "new team description",
    "privacy": "closed",
    "notification_setting": "notifications_enabled"
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}`

To edit a team, the authenticated user must either be an organization owner or a team maintainer.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `PATCH /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#update-a-team">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "new team name",
  "description": "new team description",
  "privacy": "closed",
  "notification_setting": "notifications_enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the team.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the team.|
|» privacy|body|string|false|The level of privacy this team should have. Editing teams without specifying this parameter leaves `privacy` intact. When a team is nested, the `privacy` for parent teams cannot be `secret`. The options are:  <br>**For a non-nested team:**  <br> * `secret` - only visible to organization owners and members of this team.  <br> * `closed` - visible to all members of this organization.  <br>**For a parent or child team:**  <br> * `closed` - visible to all members of this organization.|
|» notification_setting|body|string|false|The notification setting the team has chosen. Editing teams without specifying this parameter leaves `notification_setting` intact. The options are: <br> * `notifications_enabled` - team members receive notifications when the team is @mentioned.  <br> * `notifications_disabled` - no one receives notifications.|
|» permission|body|string|false|**Closing down notice**. The permission that new repositories will be added to the team with when none is specified.|
|» parent_team_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of a team to set as the parent team.|
|» parent_team_slug|body|string \| null|false|The slug of a team to set as the parent team. Ignored when `parent_team_id` is also provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» privacy|secret|
|» privacy|closed|
|» notification_setting|notifications_enabled|
|» notification_setting|notifications_disabled|
|» permission|pull|
|» permission|push|
|» permission|admin|

## List pending team invitations

<a id="opIdteams/list-pending-invitations-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/invitations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/invitations`

The return hash contains a `role` field which refers to the Organization Invitation role and will be one of the following values: `direct_member`, `admin`, `billing_manager`, `hiring_manager`, or `reinstate`. If the invitee is not a GitHub member, the `login` field in the return hash will be `null`.

> [!NOTE]

## List team members

<a id="opIdteams/list-members-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/members`

Team members will include the members of child teams.

Each member includes their `role` on the team (`member` or `maintainer`) and an `inherited` flag indicating whether the membership is inherited from a child team (`true`) or is a direct membership (`false`). These fields let you read a member's role and direct/inherited status without additional requests.

To list members in a team, the team must be visible to the authenticated user.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `GET /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/members`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#list-team-members">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-team-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|role|query|string|false|Filters members returned by their role in the team.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|role|member|
|role|maintainer|
|role|all|

## Get team membership for a user

<a id="opIdteams/get-membership-for-user-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/memberships/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/memberships/{username}`

Team members will include the members of child teams.

To get a user's membership with a team, the team must be visible to the authenticated user.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `GET /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/memberships/{username}`.

> [!NOTE]
> The response contains the `state` of the membership and the member's `role`.

The `role` for organization owners is set to `maintainer`. For more information about `maintainer` roles, see [Create a team](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#create-a-team).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#get-team-membership-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|

> Example responses

```json
  "url": "https://api.github.com/teams/1/memberships/octocat",
```

## Add or update team membership for a user

<a id="opIdteams/add-or-update-membership-for-user-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/memberships/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "role": "maintainer"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/memberships/{username}`

Adds an organization member to a team. An authenticated organization owner or team maintainer can add organization members to a team.

Team synchronization is available for organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

> [!NOTE]
> When you have team synchronization set up for a team with your organization's identity provider (IdP), you will see an error if you attempt to use the API for making changes to the team's membership. If you have access to manage group membership in your IdP, you can manage GitHub team membership through your identity provider, which automatically adds and removes team members in an organization. For more information, see "[Synchronizing teams between your identity provider and GitHub](https://docs.github.com/articles/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github/)."

An organization owner can add someone who is not part of the team's organization to a team. When an organization owner adds someone to a team who is not an organization member, this endpoint will send an invitation to the person via email. This newly-created membership will be in the "pending" state until the person accepts the invitation, at which point the membership will transition to the "active" state and the user will be added as a member of the team.

If the user is already a member of the team, this endpoint will update the role of the team member's role. To update the membership of a team member, the authenticated user must be an organization owner or a team maintainer.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `PUT /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/memberships/{username}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role": "maintainer"
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» role|body|string|false|The role that this user should have in the team.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|member|
|» role|maintainer|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "url": "https://api.github.com/teams/1/memberships/octocat",
  "role": "member",
  "state": "pending"
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[team-membership](#schemateam-membership)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden if team synchronization is set up|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity if you attempt to add an organization to a team|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove team membership for a user

<a id="opIdteams/remove-membership-for-user-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/memberships/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/memberships/{username}`

To remove a membership between a user and a team, the authenticated user must have 'admin' permissions to the team or be an owner of the organization that the team is associated with. Removing team membership does not delete the user, it just removes their membership from the team.

Team synchronization is available for organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

> [!NOTE]
> When you have team synchronization set up for a team with your organization's identity provider (IdP), you will see an error if you attempt to use the API for making changes to the team's membership. If you have access to manage group membership in your IdP, you can manage GitHub team membership through your identity provider, which automatically adds and removes team members in an organization. For more information, see "[Synchronizing teams between your identity provider and GitHub](https://docs.github.com/articles/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github/)."

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/memberships/{username}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#remove-team-membership-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

## Check team permissions for a repository

<a id="opIdteams/check-permissions-for-repo-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/repos/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`

Checks whether a team has `admin`, `push`, `maintain`, `triage`, or `pull` permission for a repository. Repositories inherited through a parent team will also be checked.

You can also get information about the specified repository, including what permissions the team grants on it, by passing the following custom [media type](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#media-types/) via the `application/vnd.github.v3.repository+json` accept header.

If a team doesn't have permission for the repository, you will receive a `404 Not Found` response status.

If the repository is private, you must have at least `read` permission for that repository, and your token must have the `repo` or `admin:org` scope. Otherwise, you will receive a `404 Not Found` response status.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `GET /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#check-team-permissions-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="check-team-permissions-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Add or update team repository permissions

<a id="opIdteams/add-or-update-repo-permissions-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/repos/string/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "permission": "push"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`

To add a repository to a team or update the team's permission on a repository, the authenticated user must have admin access to the repository, and must be able to see the team. The repository must be owned by the organization, or a direct fork of a repository owned by the organization. You will get a `422 Unprocessable Entity` status if you attempt to add a repository to a team that is not owned by the organization. Note that, if you choose not to pass any parameters, you'll need to set `Content-Length` to zero when calling out to this endpoint. For more information, see "[HTTP method](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#http-method)."

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `PUT /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`.

For more information about the permission levels, see "[Repository permission levels for an organization](https://docs.github.com/github/setting-up-and-managing-organizations-and-teams/repository-permission-levels-for-an-organization#permission-levels-for-repositories-owned-by-an-organization)".

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#add-or-update-team-repository-permissions">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permission": "push"
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-team-repository-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» permission|body|string|false|The permission to grant the team on this repository. We accept the following permissions to be set: `pull`, `triage`, `push`, `maintain`, `admin` and you can also specify a custom repository role name, if the owning organization has defined any. If no permission is specified, the team's `permission` attribute will be used to determine what permission to grant the team on this repository.|

<h3 id="add-or-update-team-repository-permissions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove a repository from a team

<a id="opIdteams/remove-repo-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/repos/string/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`

If the authenticated user is an organization owner or a team maintainer, they can remove any repositories from the team. To remove a repository from a team as an organization member, the authenticated user must have admin access to the repository and must be able to see the team. This does not delete the repository, it just removes it from the team.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#remove-a-repository-from-a-team">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-a-repository-from-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

<h3 id="remove-a-repository-from-a-team-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List child teams

<a id="opIdteams/list-child-in-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/teams/string/teams \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team_slug}/teams`

Lists the child teams of the team specified by `{team_slug}`.

> [!NOTE]
> You can also specify a team by `org_id` and `team_id` using the route `GET /organizations/{org_id}/team/{team_id}/teams`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#list-child-teams">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-child-teams-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|team_slug|path|string|true|The slug of the team name.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Get a team (Legacy)

<aside class="warning">

The return hash contains a `role` field which refers to the Organization Invitation role and will be one of the following values: `direct_member`, `admin`, `billing_manager`, `hiring_manager`, or `reinstate`. ## Add team member (Legacy)

<a id="opIdteams/add-member-legacy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/teams/0/members/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /teams/{team_id}/members/{username}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

The "Add team member" endpoint (described below) is closing down.

We recommend using the [Add or update team membership for a user](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user) endpoint instead. It allows you to invite new organization members to your teams.

Team synchronization is available for organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

To add someone to a team, the authenticated user must be an organization owner or a team maintainer in the team they're changing. The person being added to the team must be a member of the team's organization.

> [!NOTE]
> When you have team synchronization set up for a team with your organization's identity provider (IdP), you will see an error if you attempt to use the API for making changes to the team's membership. If you have access to manage group membership in your IdP, you can manage GitHub team membership through your identity provider, which automatically adds and removes team members in an organization. For more information, see "[Synchronizing teams between your identity provider and GitHub](https://docs.github.com/articles/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github/)."

Note that you'll need to set `Content-Length` to zero when calling out to this endpoint. For more information, see "[HTTP method](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#http-method)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#add-team-member-legacy">API method documentation</a>

We recommend using the [Remove team membership for a user](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#remove-team-membership-for-a-user) endpoint instead. It allows you to remove both active and pending memberships.

Team synchronization is available for organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

To remove a team member, the authenticated user must have 'admin' permissions to the team or be an owner of the org that the team is associated with. Removing a team member does not delete the user, it just removes them from the team.

> [!NOTE]
> When you have team synchronization set up for a team with your organization's identity provider (IdP), you will see an error if you attempt to use the API for making changes to the team's membership. If you have access to manage group membership in your IdP, you can manage GitHub team membership through your identity provider, which automatically adds and removes team members in an organization. For more information, see "[Synchronizing teams between your identity provider and GitHub](https://docs.github.com/articles/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github/)."

Team members will include the members of child teams.

To get a user's membership with a team, the team must be visible to the authenticated user.

**Note:**
The response contains the `state` of the membership and the member's `role`.

The `role` for organization owners is set to `maintainer`. For more information about `maintainer` roles, see [Create a team](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#create-a-team).

<a id="opIdteams/add-or-update-membership-for-user-legacy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/teams/0/memberships/string \
  -X PUT \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "role": "member"
  }'
```

`PUT /teams/{team_id}/memberships/{username}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> [!WARNING]
> **Endpoint closing down notice:** This endpoint route is closing down and will be removed from the Teams API. We recommend migrating your existing code to use the new [Add or update team membership for a user](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user) endpoint.

Team synchronization is available for organizations using GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see [GitHub's products](https://docs.github.com/github/getting-started-with-github/githubs-products) in the GitHub Help documentation.

If the user is already a member of the team's organization, this endpoint will add the user to the team. To add a membership between an organization member and a team, the authenticated user must be an organization owner or a team maintainer.

> [!NOTE]
> When you have team synchronization set up for a team with your organization's identity provider (IdP), you will see an error if you attempt to use the API for making changes to the team's membership. If you have access to manage group membership in your IdP, you can manage GitHub team membership through your identity provider, which automatically adds and removes team members in an organization. For more information, see "[Synchronizing teams between your identity provider and GitHub](https://docs.github.com/articles/synchronizing-teams-between-your-identity-provider-and-github/)."

If the user is unaffiliated with the team's organization, this endpoint will send an invitation to the user via email. This newly-created membership will be in the "pending" state until the user accepts the invitation, at which point the membership will transition to the "active" state and the user will be added as a member of the team. To add a membership between an unaffiliated user and a team, the authenticated user must be an organization owner.

If the user is already a member of the team, this endpoint will update the role of the team member's role. To update the membership of a team member, the authenticated user must be an organization owner or a team maintainer.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members#add-or-update-team-membership-for-a-user-legacy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role": "member"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» role|body|string|false|The role that this user should have in the team.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» role|member|
|» role|maintainer|

```json
}
```

## Add or update team repository permissions (Legacy)

<a id="opIdteams/add-or-update-repo-permissions-legacy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/teams/0/repos/string/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "permission": "push"
  }'
```

`PUT /teams/{team_id}/repos/{owner}/{repo}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

> [!WARNING]
> **Endpoint closing down notice:** This endpoint route is closing down and will be removed from the Teams API. We recommend migrating your existing code to use the new "[Add or update team repository permissions](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#add-or-update-team-repository-permissions)" endpoint.

To add a repository to a team or update the team's permission on a repository, the authenticated user must have admin access to the repository, and must be able to see the team. The repository must be owned by the organization, or a direct fork of a repository owned by the organization. You will get a `422 Unprocessable Entity` status if you attempt to add a repository to a team that is not owned by the organization.

Note that, if you choose not to pass any parameters, you'll need to set `Content-Length` to zero when calling out to this endpoint. For more information, see "[HTTP method](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#http-method)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#add-or-update-team-repository-permissions-legacy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permission": "push"
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-team-repository-permissions-legacy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the team.|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» permission|body|string|false|The permission to grant the team on this repository. If no permission is specified, the team's `permission` attribute will be used to determine what permission to grant the team on this repository.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» permission|pull|
|» permission|push|
|» permission|admin|

```json
}
```

## List teams for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdteams/list-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/teams \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/teams`

List all of the teams across all of the organizations to which the authenticated
user belongs.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `user`, `repo`, or `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

When using a fine-grained personal access token, the resource owner of the token must be a single organization, and the response will only include the teams from that organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/teams#list-teams-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-users">users</h1>

Interact with and view information about users and also current user.

## Get the authenticated user

<a id="opIdusers/get-authenticated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user`

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:user` scope, or the broader `user` scope, for this endpoint to return the private user response. The private user response includes additional fields such as `private_gists`, `total_private_repos`, `owned_private_repos`, `disk_usage`, `collaborators`, and `two_factor_authentication`. Tokens without these scopes receive the public user response.

The private and public user response types are unrelated to the [private profile](https://docs.github.com/account-and-profile/concepts/personal-profile#private-profiles) setting. A token without scopes still authenticates as the token's owner, so values subject to private profile visibility, such as `followers` and `following`, may differ from an unauthenticated response.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/users#get-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

## Update the authenticated user

<a id="opIdusers/update-authenticated"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "blog": "https://github.com/blog",
    "name": "monalisa octocat"
  }'
```

`PATCH /user`

**Note:** If your email is set to private and you send an `email` parameter as part of this request to update your profile, your privacy settings are still enforced: the email address will not be displayed on your public profile or via the API.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/users#update-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
  "blog": "https://github.com/blog",
  "name": "monalisa octocat"
}
```

|» name|body|string|false|The new name of the user.|

|» blog|body|string|false|The new blog URL of the user.|
|» twitter_username|body|string \| null|false|The new Twitter username of the user.|

## Create a GPG key for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdusers/create-gpg-key-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/gpg_keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Octocat'\''s GPG Key",
    "armored_public_key": "-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----\nVersion: GnuPG v1\n\nmQINBFnZ2ZIBEADQ2Z7Z7\n-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----"
  }'
```

`POST /user/gpg_keys`

Adds a GPG key to the authenticated user's GitHub account.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:gpg_key` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/gpg-keys#create-a-gpg-key-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Octocat's GPG Key",
  "armored_public_key": "-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----\nVersion: GnuPG v1\n\nmQINBFnZ2ZIBEADQ2Z7Z7\n-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-gpg-key-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A descriptive name for the new key.|

## Delete a GPG key for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdusers/delete-gpg-key-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/gpg_keys/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /user/gpg_keys/{gpg_key_id}`

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:gpg_key` scope to use this endpoint.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:public_key` scope to use this endpoint.

## Create a public SSH key for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdusers/create-public-ssh-key-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAA",
    "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
  }'
```

`POST /user/keys`

Adds a public SSH key to the authenticated user's GitHub account.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:public_key` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/keys#create-a-public-ssh-key-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAA",
  "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-public-ssh-key-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Get a user using their ID

<a id="opIdusers/get-by-id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/{account_id}`

Provides publicly available information about someone with a GitHub account. This method takes their durable user `ID` instead of their `login`, which can change over time.

If you are requesting information about an [Enterprise Managed User](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/managing-iam/understanding-iam-for-enterprises/about-enterprise-managed-users), or a GitHub App bot that is installed in an organization that uses Enterprise Managed Users, your requests must be authenticated as a user or GitHub App that has access to the organization to view that account's information. If you are not authorized, the request will return a `404 Not Found` status.

The `email` key in the following response is the publicly visible email address from your GitHub [profile page](https://github.com/settings/profile). When setting up your profile, you can select a primary email address to be public which provides an email entry for this endpoint. If you do not set a public email address for `email`, then it will have a value of `null`. You only see publicly visible email addresses when authenticated with GitHub. For more information, see [Authentication](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#authentication).

The Emails API enables you to list all of your email addresses, and toggle a primary email to be visible publicly. For more information, see [Emails API](https://docs.github.com/rest/users/emails).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/users#get-a-user-using-their-id">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-user-using-their-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|integer|true|account_id parameter|

Note: Pagination is powered exclusively by the `since` parameter. Use the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers) to get the URL for the next page of users.

## Get a user

<a id="opIdusers/get-by-username"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}`

Provides publicly available information about someone with a GitHub account.

If the specified user has a [private profile](https://docs.github.com/account-and-profile/concepts/personal-profile#private-profiles), the `followers` and `following` values are `0` unless the request is authenticated as that user. A request authenticated as the specified user returns the actual values even if the token has no OAuth scopes.

The `events_url` value is a URI template. Replace `{/privacy}` with `/public` to retrieve only public events. Omit it to retrieve public events and, when authenticated as the user, private events. For more information, see "[List events for the authenticated user](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/events#list-events-for-the-authenticated-user)."

If you are requesting information about an [Enterprise Managed User](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/managing-iam/understanding-iam-for-enterprises/about-enterprise-managed-users), or a GitHub App bot that is installed in an organization that uses Enterprise Managed Users, your requests must be authenticated as a user or GitHub App that has access to the organization to view that account's information. If you are not authorized, the request will return a `404 Not Found` status.

The `email` key in the following response is the publicly visible email address from your GitHub [profile page](https://github.com/settings/profile). When setting up your profile, you can select a primary email address to be public which provides an email entry for this endpoint. If you do not set a public email address for `email`, then it will have a value of `null`. You only see publicly visible email addresses when authenticated with GitHub. For more information, see [Authentication](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-rest-api#authentication).

The Emails API enables you to list all of your email addresses, and toggle a primary email to be visible publicly. For more information, see [Emails API](https://docs.github.com/rest/users/emails).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/users#get-a-user">API method documentation</a>

## List attestations by bulk subject digests

<a id="opIdusers/list-attestations-bulk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/attestations/bulk-list \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "subject_digests": [
      "sha256:abc123",
      "sha512:def456"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/{username}/attestations/bulk-list`

List a collection of artifact attestations associated with any entry in a list of subject digests owned by a user.

The collection of attestations returned by this endpoint is filtered according to the authenticated user's permissions; if the authenticated user cannot read a repository, the attestations associated with that repository will not be included in the response. In addition, when using a fine-grained access token the `attestations:read` permission is required.

**Please note:** in order to offer meaningful security benefits, an attestation's signature and timestamps **must** be cryptographically verified, and the identity of the attestation signer **must** be validated. Attestations can be verified using the [GitHub CLI `attestation verify` command](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify). For more information, see [our guide on how to use artifact attestations to establish a build's provenance](https://docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/attestations#list-attestations-by-bulk-subject-digests">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "subject_digests": [
    "sha256:abc123",
    "sha512:def456"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-attestations-by-bulk-subject-digests-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» subject_digests|body|[string]|true|List of subject digests to fetch attestations for.|
|» predicate_type|body|string|false|Optional filter for fetching attestations with a given predicate type.<br>This option accepts `provenance`, `sbom`, `release`, or freeform text<br>for custom predicate types.|

## List attestations

<a id="opIdusers/list-attestations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/attestations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/attestations/{subject_digest}`

List a collection of artifact attestations with a given subject digest that are associated with repositories owned by a user.

The collection of attestations returned by this endpoint is filtered according to the authenticated user's permissions; if the authenticated user cannot read a repository, the attestations associated with that repository will not be included in the response. In addition, when using a fine-grained access token the `attestations:read` permission is required.

**Please note:** in order to offer meaningful security benefits, an attestation's signature and timestamps **must** be cryptographically verified, and the identity of the attestation signer **must** be validated. Attestations can be verified using the [GitHub CLI `attestation verify` command](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify). For more information, see [our guide on how to use artifact attestations to establish a build's provenance](https://docs.github.com/actions/security-guides/using-artifact-attestations-to-establish-provenance-for-builds).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/attestations#list-attestations">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-attestations-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|subject_digest|path|string|true|Subject Digest|
|predicate_type|query|string|false|Optional filter for fetching attestations with a given predicate type.<br>This option accepts `provenance`, `sbom`, `release`, or freeform text<br>for custom predicate types.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "attestations": [
    {
      "repository_id": 1,
      "bundle_url": "https://tmastaging.blob.core.windows.net/attestations/1/2024/11/08/4.json.sn?se=2024-11-09T17%3A13%3A43Z&sig=jPSbbJnIEshUyCjBLU5Ykq0uuGc5UYxTZE1%2FhdBNMXk%3D&sp=r&spr=https%2Chttp&sr=b&st=2024-11-08T17%3A13%3A43Z&sv=2024-08-04",
      "initiator": "user"
    },
    {

      "bundle_url": "https://tmastaging.blob.core.windows.net/attestations/1/2024/11/08/5.json.sn?se=2024-11-09T17%3A13%3A43Z&sig=jPSbbJnIEshUyCjBLU5Ykq0uuGc5UYxTZE1%2FhdBNMXk%3D&sp=r&spr=https%2Chttp&sr=b&st=2024-11-08T17%3A13%3A43Z&sv=2024-08-04",
      "initiator": "user"
    }
  ]
}
```
