## Get contextual information for a user

<a id="opIdusers/get-context-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/hovercard \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/hovercard`

Provides hovercard information. You can find out more about someone in relation to their pull requests, issues, repositories, and organizations.

  The `subject_type` and `subject_id` parameters provide context for the person's hovercard, which returns more information than without the parameters. For example, if you wanted to find out more about `octocat` who owns the `Spoon-Knife` repository, you would use a `subject_type` value of `repository` and a `subject_id` value of `1300192` (the ID of the `Spoon-Knife` repository).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/users/users#get-contextual-information-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-contextual-information-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|subject_type|query|string|false|Identifies which additional information you'd like to receive about the person's hovercard. Can be `organization`, `repository`, `issue`, `pull_request`. **Required** when using `subject_id`.|
|subject_id|query|string|false|Uses the ID for the `subject_type` you specified. **Required** when using `subject_type`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|subject_type|organization|
|subject_type|repository|
|subject_type|issue|
|subject_type|pull_request|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "contexts": [
    {
      "message": "Owns this repository",
      "octicon": "repo"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
```

|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Manage access control for organization codespaces

<a id="opIdcodespaces/set-codespaces-access"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/codespaces/access \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "visibility": "selected_members",
    "selected_usernames": [
      "johnDoe",
      "atomIO"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/codespaces/access`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Sets which users can access codespaces in an organization. This is synonymous with granting or revoking codespaces access permissions for users according to the visibility.
OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organizations#manage-access-control-for-organization-codespaces">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "visibility": "selected_members",
  "selected_usernames": [
    "johnDoe",
    "atomIO"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="manage-access-control-for-organization-codespaces-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Which users can access codespaces in the organization. `disabled` means that no users can access codespaces in the organization.|
|» selected_usernames|body|[string]|false|The usernames of the organization members who should have access to codespaces in the organization. Required when `visibility` is `selected_members`. The provided list of usernames will replace any existing value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|disabled|
|» visibility|selected_members|
|» visibility|all_members|
|» visibility|all_members_and_outside_collaborators|

## Create or update an organization secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-or-update-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "visibility": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      1296269,
      1296280
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates an organization development environment secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    1296269,
    1296280
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-organization-secret-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|The value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get an organization public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#get-an-organization-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|The ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Which type of organization repositories have access to the organization secret. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the secret.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository IDs that can access the organization secret. You can only provide a list of repository IDs when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#list-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|

```json
null
```

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Set selected repositories for an organization secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/set-selected-repos-for-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/codespaces/secrets/string/repositories \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      64780797
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}/repositories`

Replaces all repositories for an organization development environment secret when the `visibility`
for repository access is set to `selected`. The visibility is set when you [Create
or update an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    64780797
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array of repository ids that can access the organization secret. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can add and remove individual repositories using the [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret) and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organization-secrets#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|409|Conflict|Conflict when visibility type not set to selected|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete a codespace from the organization

<a id="opIdcodespaces/delete-from-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/members/string/codespaces/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/members/{username}/codespaces/{codespace_name}`

Deletes a user's codespace.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organizations#delete-a-codespace-from-the-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-codespace-from-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|codespace_name|path|string|true|The name of the codespace.|

> Example responses

```json
null
```

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/members/string/codespaces/string/stop \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/members/{username}/codespaces/{codespace_name}/stop`

Stops a user's codespace.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/organizations#stop-a-codespace-for-an-organization-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="stop-a-codespace-for-an-organization-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|codespace_name|path|string|true|The name of the codespace.|

## List codespaces in a repository for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/list-in-repository-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces`

Lists the codespaces associated to a specified repository and the authenticated user.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#list-codespaces-in-a-repository-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-codespaces-in-a-repository-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Create a codespace in a repository

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-with-repo-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "ref": "main",
    "machine": "standardLinux32gb"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces`

Creates a codespace owned by the authenticated user in the specified repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#create-a-codespace-in-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "main",
  "machine": "standardLinux32gb"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codespace-in-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object \| null|true|none|
|» ref|body|string|false|Git ref (typically a branch name) for this codespace|
|» location|body|string|false|The requested location for a new codespace. Best efforts are made to respect this upon creation. Assigned by IP if not provided.|
|» geo|body|string|false|The geographic area for this codespace. If not specified, the value is assigned by IP. This property replaces `location`, which is closing down.|
|» client_ip|body|string|false|IP for location auto-detection when proxying a request|
|» machine|body|string|false|Machine type to use for this codespace|
|» devcontainer_path|body|string|false|Path to devcontainer.json config to use for this codespace|
|» multi_repo_permissions_opt_out|body|boolean|false|Whether to authorize requested permissions from devcontainer.json|
|» working_directory|body|string|false|Working directory for this codespace|
|» idle_timeout_minutes|body|integer|false|Time in minutes before codespace stops from inactivity|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Display name for this codespace|
|» retention_period_minutes|body|integer|false|Duration in minutes after codespace has gone idle in which it will be deleted. Must be integer minutes between 0 and 43200 (30 days).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» geo|EuropeWest|
|» geo|SoutheastAsia|
|» geo|UsEast|
|» geo|UsWest|

## List devcontainer configurations in a repository for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/list-devcontainers-in-repository-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces/devcontainers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/devcontainers`

Lists the devcontainer.json files associated with a specified repository and the authenticated user. These files
specify launchpoint configurations for codespaces created within the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#list-devcontainer-configurations-in-a-repository-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-devcontainer-configurations-in-a-repository-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "devcontainers": [
    {
      "path": ".devcontainer/foobar/devcontainer.json",
      "name": "foobar",
      "display_name": "foobar"
```

## Check if permissions defined by a devcontainer have been accepted by the authenticated user

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/permissions_check`

Checks whether the permissions defined by a given devcontainer configuration have been accepted by the authenticated user.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

The value of `ref` will typically be a branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.|

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/secrets`

Lists all development environment secrets available in a repository without revealing their encrypted
values.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/repository-secrets#list-repository-secrets">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 2,
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "GH_TOKEN",
      "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "all"
    },
    {
      "name": "GIST_ID",
      "created_at": "2020-01-10T10:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-11T11:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "all"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-repository-secrets-2-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|
|secrets|[[repo-codespaces-secret](#schemarepo-codespaces-secret)]|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a repository public key

<a id="opIdcodespaces/get-repo-public-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces/secrets/public-key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/secrets/public-key`

Gets your public key, which you need to encrypt secrets. You need to
encrypt a secret before you can create or update secrets.

If the repository is private, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/repository-secrets#get-a-repository-public-key">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-repository-public-key-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-repository-public-key-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[codespaces-public-key](#schemacodespaces-public-key)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a repository secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/get-repo-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Gets a single repository development environment secret without revealing its encrypted value.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/repository-secrets#get-a-repository-secret">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-repository-secret-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

## Create or update a repository secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-or-update-repo-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates a repository development environment secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint. The associated user must be a repository admin.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/repository-secrets#create-or-update-a-repository-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get a repository public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/repository-secrets#get-a-repository-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

## Create a codespace from a pull request

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-with-pr-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/pulls/0/codespaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository_id": 1,
    "ref": "main"
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/codespaces`

Creates a codespace owned by the authenticated user for the specified pull request.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#create-a-codespace-from-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository_id": 1,
  "ref": "main"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codespace-from-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object \| null|true|none|
|» location|body|string|false|The requested location for a new codespace. Best efforts are made to respect this upon creation. Assigned by IP if not provided.|
|» geo|body|string|false|The geographic area for this codespace. If not specified, the value is assigned by IP. This property replaces `location`, which is closing down.|
|» client_ip|body|string|false|IP for location auto-detection when proxying a request|
|» machine|body|string|false|Machine type to use for this codespace|
|» devcontainer_path|body|string|false|Path to devcontainer.json config to use for this codespace|
|» multi_repo_permissions_opt_out|body|boolean|false|Whether to authorize requested permissions from devcontainer.json|
|» working_directory|body|string|false|Working directory for this codespace|
|» idle_timeout_minutes|body|integer|false|Time in minutes before codespace stops from inactivity|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Display name for this codespace|
|» retention_period_minutes|body|integer|false|Duration in minutes after codespace has gone idle in which it will be deleted. Must be integer minutes between 0 and 43200 (30 days).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» geo|EuropeWest|
|» geo|SoutheastAsia|
|» geo|UsEast|
|» geo|UsWest|

<h3 id="create-a-codespace-from-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when the codespace was successfully created|[codespace](#schemacodespace)|
|202|Accepted|Response when the codespace creation partially failed but is being retried in the background|[codespace](#schemacodespace)|
|401|Unauthorized|Requires authentication|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-codespace-from-a-pull-request-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **503**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|none|none|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|documentation_url|string|false|none|none|

This operation does not require authentication

## List codespaces for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/list-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/codespaces`

Lists the authenticated user's codespaces.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#list-codespaces-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-codespaces-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|repository_id|query|integer|false|ID of the Repository to filter on|

## Create a codespace for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository_id": 1,
    "ref": "main",
    "geo": "UsWest"
  }'
```

`POST /user/codespaces`

Creates a new codespace, owned by the authenticated user.

This endpoint requires either a `repository_id` OR a `pull_request` but not both.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#create-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository_id": 1,
  "ref": "main",
  "geo": "UsWest"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» repository_id|body|integer|true|Repository id for this codespace|
|» ref|body|string|false|Git ref (typically a branch name) for this codespace|
|» location|body|string|false|The requested location for a new codespace. Best efforts are made to respect this upon creation. Assigned by IP if not provided.|
|» geo|body|string|false|The geographic area for this codespace. If not specified, the value is assigned by IP. This property replaces `location`, which is closing down.|
|» client_ip|body|string|false|IP for location auto-detection when proxying a request|
|» machine|body|string|false|Machine type to use for this codespace|
|» devcontainer_path|body|string|false|Path to devcontainer.json config to use for this codespace|
|» multi_repo_permissions_opt_out|body|boolean|false|Whether to authorize requested permissions from devcontainer.json|
|» working_directory|body|string|false|Working directory for this codespace|
|» idle_timeout_minutes|body|integer|false|Time in minutes before codespace stops from inactivity|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Display name for this codespace|
|» retention_period_minutes|body|integer|false|Duration in minutes after codespace has gone idle in which it will be deleted. Must be integer minutes between 0 and 43200 (30 days).|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» pull_request|body|object|true|Pull request number for this codespace|
|» » pull_request_number|body|integer|true|Pull request number|
|» » repository_id|body|integer|true|Repository id for this codespace|
|» location|body|string|false|The requested location for a new codespace. Best efforts are made to respect this upon creation. Assigned by IP if not provided.|
|» geo|body|string|false|The geographic area for this codespace. If not specified, the value is assigned by IP. This property replaces `location`, which is closing down.|
|» machine|body|string|false|Machine type to use for this codespace|
|» devcontainer_path|body|string|false|Path to devcontainer.json config to use for this codespace|
|» working_directory|body|string|false|Working directory for this codespace|
|» idle_timeout_minutes|body|integer|false|Time in minutes before codespace stops from inactivity|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» geo|EuropeWest|
|» geo|SoutheastAsia|
|» geo|UsEast|
|» geo|UsWest|
|» geo|EuropeWest|
|» geo|SoutheastAsia|
|» geo|UsEast|
|» geo|UsWest|

## List secrets for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/list-secrets-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/codespaces/secrets`

Lists all development environment secrets available for a user's codespaces without revealing their
encrypted values.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#list-secrets-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-secrets-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "total_count": 2,
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "GH_TOKEN",
      "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "all"
    },
    {
      "name": "GIST_ID",
      "created_at": "2020-01-10T10:59:22Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-11T11:59:22Z",
      "visibility": "all"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-secrets-for-the-authenticated-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="list-secrets-for-the-authenticated-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|total_count|integer|true|none|none|
|secrets|[[codespaces-secret](#schemacodespaces-secret)]|true|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get public key for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/get-public-key-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/public-key \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/codespaces/secrets/public-key`

Gets your public key, which you need to encrypt secrets. You need to encrypt a secret before you can create or update secrets.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#get-public-key-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "key": "2Sg8iYjAxxmI2LvUXpJjkYrMxURPc8r+dB7TJyvv1234"
}
```

<h3 id="get-public-key-for-the-authenticated-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[codespaces-user-public-key](#schemacodespaces-user-public-key)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a secret for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/get-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Gets a development environment secret available to a user's codespaces without revealing its encrypted value.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#get-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "CODESPACE_GH_SECRET",
  "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
  "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repositories_url": "https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/CODESPACE_GH_SECRET/repositories"
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[codespaces-secret](#schemacodespaces-secret)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a secret for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/create-or-update-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      "1234567",
      "2345678"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates a development environment secret for a user's codespace with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#create-or-update-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    "1234567",
    "2345678"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get the public key for the authenticated user](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#get-public-key-for-the-authenticated-user) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer \| string]|false|An array of repository ids that can access the user secret. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#list-selected-repositories-for-a-user-secret), [Set selected repositories for a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-a-user-secret), and [Remove a selected repository from a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#remove-a-selected-repository-from-a-user-secret) endpoints.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response after successfully creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response after successfully updating a secret|None|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Delete a secret for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/delete-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}`

Deletes a development environment secret from a user's codespaces using the secret name. Deleting the secret will remove access from all codespaces that were allowed to access the secret.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#delete-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

<h3 id="delete-a-secret-for-the-authenticated-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List selected repositories for a user secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/list-repositories-for-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}/repositories`

List the repositories that have been granted the ability to use a user's development environment secret.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<h3 id="list-selected-repositories-for-a-user-secret-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|

## Set selected repositories for a user secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/set-repositories-for-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/string/repositories \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      "1296269",
      "1296280"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}/repositories`

Select the repositories that will use a user's development environment secret.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` or `codespace:secrets` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-a-user-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    "1296269",
    "1296280"
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array of repository ids for which a codespace can access the secret. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#list-selected-repositories-for-a-user-secret), [Add a selected repository to a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#add-a-selected-repository-to-a-user-secret), and [Remove a selected repository from a user secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/secrets#remove-a-selected-repository-from-a-user-secret) endpoints.|

## Remove a selected repository from a user secret

<a id="opIdcodespaces/remove-repository-for-secret-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/secrets/string/repositories/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /user/codespaces/secrets/{secret_name}/repositories/{repository_id}`

Removes a repository from the selected repositories for a user's development environment secret.

The authenticated user must have Codespaces access to use this endpoint.

## Update a codespace for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/update-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "machine": "standardLinux"
  }'
```

`PATCH /user/codespaces/{codespace_name}`

Updates a codespace owned by the authenticated user. Currently only the codespace's machine type and recent folders can be modified using this endpoint.

If you specify a new machine type it will be applied the next time your codespace is started.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#update-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "machine": "standardLinux"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|codespace_name|path|string|true|The name of the codespace.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» machine|body|string|false|A valid machine to transition this codespace to.|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Display name for this codespace|
|» recent_folders|body|[string]|false|Recently opened folders inside the codespace. It is currently used by the clients to determine the folder path to load the codespace in.|

## Export a codespace for the authenticated user

<a id="opIdcodespaces/export-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/string/exports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /user/codespaces/{codespace_name}/exports`

Triggers an export of the specified codespace and returns a URL and ID where the status of the export can be monitored.

If changes cannot be pushed to the codespace's repository, they will be pushed to a new or previously-existing fork instead.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#export-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="export-a-codespace-for-the-authenticated-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|codespace_name|path|string|true|The name of the codespace.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "state": "succeeded",
  "completed_at": "2022-01-01T14:59:22Z",

}
```

## Create a repository from an unpublished codespace

<a id="opIdcodespaces/publish-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/codespaces/string/publish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repository": "monalisa-octocat-hello-world-g4wpq6h95q",
    "private": false
  }'
```

`POST /user/codespaces/{codespace_name}/publish`

Publishes an unpublished codespace, creating a new repository and assigning it to the codespace.

The codespace's token is granted write permissions to the repository, allowing the user to push their changes.

This will fail for a codespace that is already published, meaning it has an associated repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `codespace` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/codespaces/codespaces#create-a-repository-from-an-unpublished-codespace">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repository": "monalisa-octocat-hello-world-g4wpq6h95q",
  "private": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-from-an-unpublished-codespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|codespace_name|path|string|true|The name of the codespace.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A name for the new repository.|
|» private|body|boolean|false|Whether the new repository should be private.|

## Get Copilot enterprise usage metrics for a specific day

<a id="opIdcopilot/copilot-enterprise-one-day-usage-metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/copilot/metrics/reports/enterprise-1-day`

Use this endpoint to retrieve download links for the Copilot enterprise usage metrics report for a specific day. The report provides comprehensive usage data for Copilot features across the enterprise.

The report contains aggregated metrics for the specified day, including usage statistics for various Copilot features, user engagement data, and feature adoption metrics. Reports are generated daily and made available for download through signed URLs with a limited expiration time.

The response includes download links to the report files, along with the specific date of the report. The report covers a complete day for which data has been processed. Reports are available starting from October 10, 2025, and historical data can be accessed for up to 1 year from the current date.

Enterprise owners, billing managers, and authorized users with fine-grained "View Enterprise Copilot Metrics" permission can retrieve Copilot metrics reports for the enterprise. ## Set the coding agent policy for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcopilot/set-enterprise-coding-agent-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/copilot/policies/coding_agent \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "policy_state": "enabled_for_all_orgs"
  }'
```

`PUT /enterprises/{enterprise}/copilot/policies/coding_agent`

Sets the policy for Copilot cloud agent usage across an enterprise.

Enterprise owners can configure whether Copilot cloud agent is enabled for all
organizations, disabled for all organizations, configured by individual organization
admins, or enabled for selected organizations only.

Only enterprise owners can set the coding agent policy for their enterprise.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:enterprise` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-coding-agent-management#set-the-coding-agent-policy-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "policy_state": "enabled_for_all_orgs"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-coding-agent-policy-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|The coding agent policy configuration|
|» policy_state|body|string|true|The policy state for Copilot cloud agent in the enterprise. Can be one of `enabled_for_all_orgs`, `disabled_for_all_orgs`, `enabled_for_selected_orgs`, or `configured_by_org_admins`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» policy_state|enabled_for_all_orgs|
|» policy_state|disabled_for_all_orgs|
|» policy_state|enabled_for_selected_orgs|
|» policy_state|configured_by_org_admins|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="set-the-coding-agent-policy-for-an-enterprise-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|A header with no content is returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add organizations to the enterprise coding agent policy

<a id="opIdcopilot/add-organizations-to-enterprise-coding-agent-policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/copilot/policies/coding_agent/organizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "organizations": [
      "my-org-1",
      "my-org-2"
    ],
    "custom_properties": [
      {
        "property_name": "department",
        "values": [
          "engineering",
          "security"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise}/copilot/policies/coding_agent/organizations`

Enables Copilot cloud agent for the specified organizations within the enterprise.

The enterprise's coding agent policy must be set to `enabled_for_selected_orgs` before
using this endpoint. Organizations can be specified by login or matched via custom properties.

Only organizations that have Copilot enabled and belong to the enterprise will be affected.

Only enterprise owners can add organizations to the coding agent policy.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:enterprise` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-coding-agent-management#add-organizations-to-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organizations": [
    "my-org-1",
    "my-org-2"
  ],
  "custom_properties": [
    {
      "property_name": "department",
      "values": [
        "engineering",
        "security"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-organizations-to-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|The organizations to enable Copilot cloud agent for|
|» organizations|body|[string]|false|List of organization logins within the enterprise to enable Copilot cloud agent for.|
|» custom_properties|body|[object]|false|List of custom property filters to match organizations. Organizations matching any of the specified property name/value pairs will be included. This is a one-time operation, setting the property on an organization in the future will not automatically update its coding agent policy.|
|» » property_name|body|string|true|The name of the custom property to filter by.|
|» » values|body|[string]|true|The values of the custom property to match.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-organizations-to-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|A header with no content is returned.|None|

using this endpoint. Organizations can be specified by login or matched via custom properties.

Only organizations that have Copilot enabled and belong to the enterprise will be affected.

Only enterprise owners can remove organizations from the coding agent policy.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:enterprise` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-coding-agent-management#remove-organizations-from-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organizations": [
    "my-org-1",
    "my-org-2"
  ],
  "custom_properties": [
    {
      "property_name": "department",
      "values": [
        "engineering",
        "security"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-organizations-from-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|The organizations to disable Copilot cloud agent for|
|» organizations|body|[string]|false|List of organization logins within the enterprise to disable Copilot cloud agent for.|
|» custom_properties|body|[object]|false|List of custom property filters to match organizations. Organizations matching any of the specified property name/value pairs will be included. This is a one-time operation, setting the property on an organization in the future will not automatically update its coding agent policy.|
|» » property_name|body|string|true|The name of the custom property to filter by.|
|» » values|body|[string]|true|The values of the custom property to match.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-organizations-from-the-enterprise-coding-agent-policy-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|A header with no content is returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List all Copilot seat assignments for an organization

<a id="opIdcopilot/list-copilot-seats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/billing/seats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/billing/seats`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists all Copilot seats for which an organization with a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise subscription is currently being billed.
Only organization owners can view assigned seats.

Each seat object contains information about the assigned user's most recent Copilot activity. Users must have telemetry enabled in their IDE for Copilot in the IDE activity to be reflected in `last_activity_at`.
For more information about activity data, see [Metrics data properties for GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot/reference/metrics-data).

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `read:org` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-user-management#list-all-copilot-seat-assignments-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-all-copilot-seat-assignments-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Add teams to the Copilot subscription for an organization

<a id="opIdcopilot/add-copilot-seats-for-teams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/billing/selected_teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_teams": [
      "engteam1",
      "engteam2",
      "engteam3"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/copilot/billing/selected_teams`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Purchases a GitHub Copilot seat for all users within each specified team.
The organization will be billed for each seat based on the organization's Copilot plan. For more information about Copilot pricing, see "[About billing for GitHub Copilot in your organization](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-the-copilot-subscription-for-your-organization/about-billing-for-github-copilot-in-your-organization)."

Only organization owners can purchase Copilot seats for their organization members. The organization must have a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise subscription and a configured suggestion matching policy.
For more information about setting up a Copilot subscription, see "[Subscribing to Copilot for your organization](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-the-copilot-subscription-for-your-organization/subscribing-to-copilot-for-your-organization)."
For more information about setting a suggestion matching policy, see "[Managing policies for Copilot in your organization](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/setting-policies-for-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-policies-for-copilot-in-your-organization#policies-for-suggestion-matching)."

The response contains the total number of new seats that were created and existing seats that were refreshed.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:org` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-user-management#add-teams-to-the-copilot-subscription-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_teams": [
    "engteam1",
    "engteam2",
    "engteam3"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-teams-to-the-copilot-subscription-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_teams|body|[string]|true|List of team names within the organization to which to grant access to GitHub Copilot.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "seats_created": 5
}
```

```json
  "documentation_url": "string",

  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

  "url": "string",
```

## Remove teams from the Copilot subscription for an organization

<a id="opIdcopilot/cancel-copilot-seat-assignment-for-teams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/billing/selected_teams \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_teams": [
      "engteam1",
      "engteam2",
      "engteam3"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/copilot/billing/selected_teams`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Sets seats for all members of each team specified to "pending cancellation".
This will cause the members of the specified team(s) to lose access to GitHub Copilot at the end of the current billing cycle unless they retain access through another team.
For more information about disabling access to Copilot, see "[Revoking access to Copilot for members of your organization](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-access-to-github-copilot-in-your-organization/revoking-access-to-copilot-for-members-of-your-organization)."

Only organization owners can cancel Copilot seats for their organization members.

The response contains the total number of seats set to "pending cancellation".

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:org` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-user-management#remove-teams-from-the-copilot-subscription-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_teams": [

}
```

## Remove users from the Copilot subscription for an organization

<a id="opIdcopilot/cancel-copilot-seat-assignment-for-users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/billing/selected_users \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_usernames": [
      "cooluser1",
      "hacker2",
      "octocat"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/copilot/billing/selected_users`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Sets seats for all users specified to "pending cancellation".
This will cause the specified users to lose access to GitHub Copilot at the end of the current billing cycle unless they retain access through team membership.
For more information about disabling access to Copilot, see "[Revoking access to Copilot for members of your organization](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/managing-github-copilot-in-your-organization/managing-access-to-github-copilot-in-your-organization/revoking-access-to-copilot-for-members-of-your-organization)."

Only organization owners can cancel Copilot seats for their organization members.

The response contains the total number of seats set to "pending cancellation".

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `manage_billing:copilot` or `admin:org` scopes to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-user-management#remove-users-from-the-copilot-subscription-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_usernames": [
    "cooluser1",
    "hacker2",
    "octocat"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-users-from-the-copilot-subscription-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_usernames|body|[string]|true|The usernames of the organization members for which to revoke access to GitHub Copilot.|

## Get Copilot content exclusion rules for an organization

<a id="opIdcopilot/copilot-content-exclusion-for-organization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/content_exclusion \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/content_exclusion`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Gets information about an organization's Copilot content exclusion path rules.
To configure these settings, go to the organization's settings on GitHub.
For more information, see "[Excluding content from GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/configuring-and-auditing-content-exclusion/excluding-content-from-github-copilot#configuring-content-exclusions-for-your-organization)."

Organization owners can view details about Copilot content exclusion rules for the organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need either the `copilot` or `read:org` scopes to use this endpoint.

> [!CAUTION]
> * At this time, the API does not support comments. This endpoint will not return any comments in the existing rules.
> * At this time, the API does not support duplicate keys. If your content exclusion configuration contains duplicate keys, the API will return only the last occurrence of that key. For example, if duplicate entries are present, only the final value will be included in the response.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-content-exclusion-management#get-copilot-content-exclusion-rules-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

## Set Copilot content exclusion rules for an organization

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/content_exclusion \
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/copilot/content_exclusion`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Sets Copilot content exclusion path rules for an organization.
To configure these settings, go to the organization's settings on GitHub.
For more information, see "[Excluding content from GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot/managing-copilot/configuring-and-auditing-content-exclusion/excluding-content-from-github-copilot#configuring-content-exclusions-for-your-organization)."

Organization owners can set Copilot content exclusion rules for the organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `copilot` scope to use this endpoint.

> [!CAUTION]
> * At this time, the API does not support comments. When using this endpoint, any existing comments in your rules will be deleted.
> * At this time, the API does not support duplicate keys. If you submit content exclusions through the API with duplicate keys, only the last occurrence will be saved. Earlier entries with the same key will be overwritten.

## Get Copilot organization usage metrics for a specific day

<a id="opIdcopilot/copilot-organization-one-day-usage-metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/metrics/reports/organization-1-day?day=2025-10-13' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/organization-1-day`

Use this endpoint to retrieve download links for the Copilot organization usage metrics report for a specific day. The report provides comprehensive usage data for Copilot features across the organization.

The report contains aggregated metrics for the specified day, including usage statistics for various Copilot features, user engagement data, and feature adoption metrics. Reports are generated daily and made available for download through signed URLs with a limited expiration time.

The response includes download links to the report files, along with the specific date of the report. The report covers a complete day for which data has been processed.

Organization owners and authorized users with fine-grained "View Organization Copilot Metrics" permission can retrieve Copilot metrics reports for the organization. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

For more information about organization metrics attribution, see [How are metrics attributed across organizations](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/copilot-metrics#how-are-metrics-attributed-across-organizations).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-usage-metrics#get-copilot-organization-usage-metrics-for-a-specific-day">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-copilot-organization-usage-metrics-for-a-specific-day-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|day|query|string(date)|true|The day to request data for, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "download_links": [
    "https://example.com/copilot-usage-report-1.ndjson",
    "https://example.com/copilot-usage-report-2.ndjson"

  "report_day": "2025-07-01"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

## Get Copilot organization usage metrics

<a id="opIdcopilot/copilot-organization-usage-metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot/metrics/reports/organization-28-day/latest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/organization-28-day/latest`

Use this endpoint to retrieve download links for the latest 28-day organization Copilot usage metrics report. The report provides comprehensive usage data for Copilot features across the organization.

The report contains aggregated metrics for the previous 28 days, including usage statistics for various Copilot features, user engagement data, and feature adoption metrics. Reports are generated daily and made available for download through signed URLs with a limited expiration time.

The response includes download links to the report files, along with the specific date range covered by the report. The report covers a complete 28-day period ending on the most recent day for which data has been processed.

Organization owners and authorized users with fine-grained "View Organization Copilot Metrics" permission can retrieve Copilot metrics reports for the organization. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

For more information about organization metrics attribution, see [How are metrics attributed across organizations](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/copilot-metrics#how-are-metrics-attributed-across-organizations).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot/copilot-usage-metrics#get-copilot-organization-usage-metrics">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-copilot-organization-usage-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Get Copilot organization repository report for a specific day

<a id="opIdcopilot/copilot-organization-repos-one-day-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/repos-1-day`

Use this endpoint to retrieve download links for the Copilot organization repository report for a specific day. The report provides per-repository pull request metrics for Copilot across the organization, with one entry per repository.

The report contains repository-level pull request activity for the specified day, including the Copilot Coding Agent (CCA) and Copilot Code Review (CCR) breakdowns. Only repositories that had activity on the specified day are included. Reports are generated daily and made available for download through signed URLs with a limited expiration time.

The response includes download links to the report files, along with the specific date of the report. The report covers a complete day for which data has been processed.

Organization owners and authorized users with fine-grained "View Organization Copilot Metrics" permission can retrieve Copilot metrics reports for the organization. OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

For more information about organization metrics attribution, see [How are metrics attributed across organizations](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/copilot-metrics#how-are-metrics-attributed-across-organizations).

`GET /orgs/{org}/members/{username}/copilot`

Gets the GitHub Copilot seat details for a member of an organization who currently has access to GitHub Copilot.

The seat object contains information about the user's most recent Copilot activity. Users must have telemetry enabled in their IDE for Copilot in the IDE activity to be reflected in `last_activity_at`.

Only organization owners can view Copilot seat assignment details for members of their organization.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|» copilot_code_review|boolean|true|none|Whether the Copilot code review tool is enabled for the Copilot cloud agent.|
|» secret_scanning|boolean|true|none|Whether the secret scanning tool is enabled for the Copilot cloud agent.|
|» dependency_vulnerability_checks|boolean|true|none|Whether the dependency vulnerability checks tool is enabled for the Copilot cloud agent.|
|require_actions_workflow_approval|boolean|true|none|Whether Actions workflow approval is required for Copilot cloud agent pull requests.|
|is_firewall_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the firewall is enabled.|
|is_firewall_recommended_allowlist_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the firewall recommended allowlist is enabled.|
|custom_allowlist|[string]|true|none|A list of custom allowlist entries, as hosts or URLs, that the firewall will allow the Copilot cloud agent to access.|
|is_automations_enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether automations are enabled in this repository. When true, users can create automations that automatically run agents on a schedule or in response to events like new issues or updated pull requests.|
|require_write_access_for_automation_triggers|boolean|true|none|Whether write access is required for automation triggers. When true, automations will only run if the user triggering the event has write access to the repository. When false, users can create automations that listen for events triggered by users without write access.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-copilot-spaces">copilot-spaces</h1>

Endpoints to manage Copilot Spaces using the REST API.

## List organization Copilot Spaces

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/list-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces`

Lists Copilot Spaces owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have read access to the organization's Copilot Spaces.

Only Spaces that are readable by the authenticated user are returned. This includes public Spaces and internal Spaces if the user is a member of the organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in a space; spaces with inaccessible resources are omitted from the response.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#list-organization-copilot-spaces">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-organization-copilot-spaces-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
