## Create an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/create-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Team Planning Space",
    "description": "Organization space for team planning and coordination",
    "general_instructions": "Help the team with planning and coordination tasks",
    "resources_attributes": [
      {
        "resource_type": "github_file",
        "metadata": {
          "repository_id": 123456,
          "file_path": "docs/planning.md"
        }
      },
      {
        "resource_type": "free_text",
        "metadata": {
          "name": "Team Guidelines",
          "text": "Our team follows agile methodology and holds daily standups"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces`

Creates a new Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have permissions to create spaces in the organization.

Organization members with appropriate permissions can create Copilot Spaces to be shared within their organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by the submitted resources.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#create-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Team Planning Space",
  "description": "Organization space for team planning and coordination",
  "general_instructions": "Help the team with planning and coordination tasks",
  "resources_attributes": [
    {
      "resource_type": "github_file",
      "metadata": {
        "repository_id": 123456,
        "file_path": "docs/planning.md"
      }
    },
    {
      "resource_type": "free_text",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "Team Guidelines",
        "text": "Our team follows agile methodology and holds daily standups"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the Copilot Space.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the Copilot Space.|
|» general_instructions|body|string|false|General instructions for the Copilot Space.|
|» base_role|body|string|false|The base role that determines default permissions for organization members.<br>- `no_access`: No default access (default)<br>- `reader`: Organization members can read the space<br>- `writer`: Organization members can read and edit the space<br>- `admin`: Organization members have full admin access to the space|
|» resources_attributes|body|[object]|false|Resources to attach to the space.|
|» » resource_type|body|string|false|The type of resource.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Metadata specific to the resource type.|
|» » » repository_id|body|integer|false|Repository ID for repository or file resources.|
|» » » file_path|body|string|false|File path for file resources.|
|» » » text|body|string|false|Text content for free text resources.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|Name for the resource.|
|» » » number|body|integer|false|Issue or PR number.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» base_role|reader|
|» base_role|writer|
|» base_role|admin|
|» base_role|no_access|
|» » resource_type|repository|
|» » resource_type|github_file|
|» » resource_type|free_text|
|» » resource_type|github_issue|
|» » resource_type|github_pull_request|
|» » resource_type|media_content|
|» » resource_type|uploaded_text_file|

## Get an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/get-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}`

Gets details about a specific Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have read access to the Space.

Internal Spaces require the authenticated user to be a member of the organization or have been granted read permissions.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#get-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|

## Set an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/update-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Updated Team Planning Space",
    "description": "Updated organization space for team planning and coordination",
    "general_instructions": "Updated instructions to help the team with planning and coordination tasks",
    "resources_attributes": [
      {
        "resource_type": "github_file",
        "metadata": {
          "repository_id": 123456,
          "file_path": "docs/updated-planning.md"
        }
      },
      {
        "id": 789,
        "_destroy": true
      },
      {
        "id": 456,
        "resource_type": "free_text",
        "metadata": {
          "name": "Updated Team Guidelines",
          "text": "Our updated team follows agile methodology and holds daily standups"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}`

Updates a Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have permissions to update spaces in the organization.

Organization members with appropriate permissions can update Copilot Spaces owned by their organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space, including any being added or updated.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#set-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Updated Team Planning Space",
  "description": "Updated organization space for team planning and coordination",
  "general_instructions": "Updated instructions to help the team with planning and coordination tasks",
  "resources_attributes": [
    {
      "resource_type": "github_file",
      "metadata": {
        "repository_id": 123456,
        "file_path": "docs/updated-planning.md"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": 789,
      "_destroy": true
    },
    {
      "id": 456,
      "resource_type": "free_text",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "Updated Team Guidelines",
        "text": "Our updated team follows agile methodology and holds daily standups"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the Copilot Space.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the Copilot Space.|
|» general_instructions|body|string|false|General instructions for the Copilot Space.|
|» base_role|body|string|false|The base role that determines default permissions for organization members. Changing this field requires admin permissions.<br>- `no_access`: No default access (default)<br>- `reader`: Organization members can read the space<br>- `writer`: Organization members can read and edit the space<br>- `admin`: Organization members have full admin access to the space|
|» resources_attributes|body|[object]|false|Resources to attach to the space.|
|» » resource_type|body|string|false|The type of resource.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Metadata specific to the resource type.|

|» » » text|body|string|false|Text content for free text resources.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|Name for the resource.|
|» » » number|body|integer|false|Issue or PR number.|

## Delete an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/delete-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}`

Deletes a Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have permissions to delete spaces in the organization.

**Warning:** This action is permanent and cannot be undone. Deleting a Copilot Space will remove all associated resources and configurations.

Organization members with appropriate permissions can delete Copilot Spaces owned by their organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need both the `read:org` and `repo` scopes to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#delete-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|

> Example responses

```json
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",

}
```

## List collaborators for an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/list-collaborators-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0/collaborators \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/collaborators`

Lists all collaborators for a specific Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to view collaborators.

Each collaborator entry specifies which user or team has access to the space and at what level (reader, writer, or admin). The space owner (organization) is excluded from this list.

**Note:** Team collaborators listed here are teams that are defined in the organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/collaborators#list-collaborators-for-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-collaborators-for-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|

## Add a collaborator to an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/add-collaborator-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0/collaborators \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "actor_type": "User",
    "actor_identifier": "octocat",
    "role": "writer"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/collaborators`

Adds a collaborator (user or team) to a specific Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to manage collaborators.

**Note:** When adding users as collaborators, they must already be members of the organization.
When adding teams as collaborators, they must be defined in the organization.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/collaborators#add-a-collaborator-to-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actor_type": "User",
  "actor_identifier": "octocat",
  "role": "writer"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-collaborator-to-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» actor_type|body|string|true|The type of actor (user or team).|
|» actor_identifier|body|string|true|The username (for users) or team slug (for teams). The numeric ID of a user or team is also accepted.|
|» role|body|string|true|The role to grant to the collaborator.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» actor_type|User|
|» actor_type|Team|

## Remove a collaborator from an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/remove-collaborator-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0/collaborators/User/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/collaborators/{actor_type}/{actor_identifier}`

Removes a collaborator from a specific Copilot Space owned by an organization. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to manage collaborators.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/collaborators#remove-a-collaborator-from-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-a-collaborator-from-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|actor_type|path|string|true|The type of actor (user or team).|
|actor_identifier|path|string|true|The username (for users) or team slug (for teams). The numeric ID of a user or team is also accepted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|actor_type|User|
|actor_type|Team|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-a-collaborator-from-an-organization-copilot-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

This operation does not require authentication

## Create a resource for an organization Copilot Space

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/create-resource-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/copilot-spaces/0/resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "resource_type": "free_text",
    "metadata": {
      "name": "notes.txt",
      "text": "Some helpful notes"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/resources`

Creates a new resource in a specific Copilot Space owned by an organization.
The authenticated user must have write permissions on the space.

The following resource types are supported: `repository`, `github_file`, `free_text`, `github_issue`, `github_pull_request`.
The `uploaded_text_file` and `media_content` types are not supported via this endpoint.

For `github_file` resources, if a resource with the same repository, file path, and SHA already exists, the existing resource is returned with a `200` status.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens and GitHub App user access tokens must have been granted access to the organization that owns the space. They must also have been granted access to every repository referenced by resources in the space, including the resource being created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/resources#create-a-resource-for-an-organization-copilot-space">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resource_type": "free_text",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "notes.txt",
    "text": "Some helpful notes"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-resource-for-an-organization-copilot-space-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» resource_type|body|string|true|The type of resource to create.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|Resource-specific metadata.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» resource_type|repository|
|» resource_type|github_file|
|» resource_type|free_text|
|» resource_type|github_issue|
|» resource_type|github_pull_request|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "resource_type": "github_file",
  "copilot_chat_attachment_id": null,
  "metadata": {
    "repository_id": 42,
    "file_path": "README.md",
    "sha": "abc123"
  },
  "created_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "resource_type": "free_text",
  "copilot_chat_attachment_id": null,
  "metadata": {
    "name": "notes.txt",
    "text": "Some helpful notes"
  },
  "created_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-resource-for-an-organization-copilot-space-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Duplicate github_file resource already exists|[copilot-space-resource](#schemacopilot-space-resource)|
|201|Created|Resource created|[copilot-space-resource](#schemacopilot-space-resource)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

This operation does not require authentication

## List Copilot Spaces for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/list-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/copilot-spaces`

Lists Copilot Spaces owned by a user. The authenticated user must have read access to the user's Copilot Spaces.

Only Spaces that are readable by the authenticated user are returned. This includes the user's own spaces, and public user spaces when accessing another user's spaces.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:user` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#list-copilot-spaces-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-copilot-spaces-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor.|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor.|

## Create a Copilot Space for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/create-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Development Space",
    "description": "Personal space for development assistance",
    "general_instructions": "Help me with React development patterns and best practices",
    "resources_attributes": [
      {
        "resource_type": "github_file",
        "metadata": {
          "repository_id": 789012,
          "file_path": "src/components/App.js"
        }
      },
      {
        "resource_type": "free_text",
        "metadata": {
          "name": "Development Notes",
          "text": "Focus on clean code principles and modern React patterns"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/{username}/copilot-spaces`

Creates a new Copilot Space owned by a user. Only the authenticated user can create spaces for their own account.

Users can create personal Copilot Spaces for their individual use.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:user` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#create-a-copilot-space-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My Development Space",
  "description": "Personal space for development assistance",
  "general_instructions": "Help me with React development patterns and best practices",
  "resources_attributes": [
    {
      "resource_type": "github_file",
      "metadata": {
        "repository_id": 789012,
        "file_path": "src/components/App.js"
      }
    },
    {
      "resource_type": "free_text",
      "metadata": {
        "name": "Development Notes",
        "text": "Focus on clean code principles and modern React patterns"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-copilot-space-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the Copilot Space.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the Copilot Space.|
|» general_instructions|body|string|false|General instructions for the Copilot Space.|
|» base_role|body|string|false|The base role that determines default permissions for the space.<br>- `no_access`: No default access (default)<br>- `reader`: Makes the space publicly readable<br>Note: User spaces do not support writer or admin base roles.|
|» resources_attributes|body|[object]|false|Resources to attach to the space.|
|» » resource_type|body|string|false|The type of resource.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Metadata specific to the resource type.|
|» » » repository_id|body|integer|false|Repository ID for repository or file resources.|
|» » » file_path|body|string|false|File path for file resources.|
|» » » text|body|string|false|Text content for free text resources.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|Name for the resource.|
|» » » number|body|integer|false|Issue or PR number.|

## Get a Copilot Space for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/get-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}`

Gets details about a specific Copilot Space owned by a user. The authenticated user must have read access to the Space.

Private user spaces require the authenticated user to be the owner of the space.
Public user spaces are accessible to any authenticated user.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#get-a-copilot-space-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|

## Delete a Copilot Space for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/delete-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /users/{username}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}`

Deletes a Copilot Space owned by a user. The authenticated user must be the owner of the space.

**Warning:** This action is permanent and cannot be undone. Deleting a space will remove all associated resources and configurations.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `user` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/copilot-spaces#delete-a-copilot-space-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces/0/collaborators \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/collaborators`

Lists all collaborators for a specific Copilot Space owned by a user. The authenticated user must be the owner of the space or have admin access to the space.

Each collaborator entry specifies which user has access to the space and at what level (reader, writer, or admin). The space owner is excluded from this list.

Team collaborators are not supported for user-owned Copilot Spaces.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `user` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/collaborators#list-collaborators-for-a-copilot-space-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-collaborators-for-a-copilot-space-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|

## Set a collaborator role for a Copilot Space for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/update-collaborator-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces/0/collaborators/User/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "role": "admin"
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{username}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/collaborators/{actor_type}/{actor_identifier}`

Updates the role of a collaborator for a specific Copilot Space owned by a user. The authenticated user must be the owner of the space or have admin access to the space.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `user` scope to use this endpoint.

|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|actor_type|path|string|true|The type of actor (must be `User` for user-owned spaces; `Team` will be rejected).|
|actor_identifier|path|string|true|The username of the collaborator. The numeric user ID is also accepted.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Create a resource for a Copilot Space for a user

<a id="opIdcopilot-spaces/create-resource-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/copilot-spaces/0/resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "resource_type": "free_text",
    "metadata": {
      "name": "notes.txt",
      "text": "Some helpful notes"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /users/{username}/copilot-spaces/{space_number}/resources`

Creates a new resource in a specific Copilot Space owned by a user.
The authenticated user must have write permissions on the space.

The following resource types are supported: `repository`, `github_file`, `free_text`, `github_issue`, `github_pull_request`.
The `uploaded_text_file` and `media_content` types are not supported via this endpoint.

For `github_file` resources, if a resource with the same repository, file path, and SHA already exists, the existing resource is returned with a `200` status.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:user` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/copilot-spaces/resources#create-a-resource-for-a-copilot-space-for-a-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resource_type": "free_text",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "notes.txt",
    "text": "Some helpful notes"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-resource-for-a-copilot-space-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|space_number|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the Copilot Space.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» resource_type|body|string|true|The type of resource to create.|
|» metadata|body|object|true|Resource-specific metadata.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» resource_type|repository|
|» resource_type|github_file|
|» resource_type|free_text|
|» resource_type|github_issue|
|» resource_type|github_pull_request|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "resource_type": "github_file",
  "copilot_chat_attachment_id": null,
  "metadata": {
    "repository_id": 42,
    "file_path": "README.md",
    "sha": "abc123"
  },
  "created_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
  },

  "updated_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "url": "string",

```

```json
      "resource": "string",

    }
```

<h3 id="create-a-resource-for-a-copilot-space-for-a-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Duplicate github_file resource already exists|[copilot-space-resource](#schemacopilot-space-resource)|
|201|Created|Resource created|[copilot-space-resource](#schemacopilot-space-resource)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-security-advisories">security-advisories</h1>

Manage security advisories.

## List global security advisories

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/list-global-advisories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/advisories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /advisories`

Lists all global security advisories that match the specified parameters. If no other parameters are defined, the request will return only GitHub-reviewed advisories that are not malware.

By default, all responses will exclude advisories for malware, because malware are not standard vulnerabilities. To list advisories for malware, you must include the `type` parameter in your request, with the value `malware`. For more information about the different types of security advisories, see "[About the GitHub Advisory database](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/global-security-advisories/about-the-github-advisory-database#about-types-of-security-advisories)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/global-advisories#list-global-security-advisories">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-global-security-advisories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ghsa_id|query|string|false|If specified, only advisories with this GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier will be returned.|
|type|query|string|false|If specified, only advisories of this type will be returned. By default, a request with no other parameters defined will only return reviewed advisories that are not malware.|
|cve_id|query|string|false|If specified, only advisories with this CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) identifier will be returned.|
|ecosystem|query|[security-advisory-ecosystems](#schemasecurity-advisory-ecosystems)|false|If specified, only advisories for these ecosystems will be returned.|
|severity|query|string|false|If specified, only advisories with these severities will be returned.|
|cwes|query|string \| [string]|false|If specified, only advisories with these Common Weakness Enumerations (CWEs) will be returned.<br><br>Example: `cwes=79,284,22` or `cwes[]=79&cwes[]=284&cwes[]=22`|
|is_withdrawn|query|boolean|false|Whether to only return advisories that have been withdrawn.|
|affects|query|string \| [string]|false|If specified, only return advisories that affect any of `package` or `package@version`. A maximum of 1000 packages can be specified.<br>If the query parameter causes the URL to exceed the maximum URL length supported by your client, you must specify fewer packages.<br><br>Example: `affects=package1,package2@1.0.0,package3@2.0.0` or `affects[]=package1&affects[]=package2@1.0.0`|
|published|query|string|false|If specified, only return advisories that were published on a date or date range.<br><br>For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."|
|updated|query|string|false|If specified, only return advisories that were updated on a date or date range.<br><br>For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."|
|modified|query|string|false|If specified, only show advisories that were updated or published on a date or date range.<br><br>For more information on the syntax of the date range, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."|
|epss_percentage|query|string|false|If specified, only return advisories that have an EPSS percentage score that matches the provided value.<br>The EPSS percentage represents the likelihood of a CVE being exploited.|
|epss_percentile|query|string|false|If specified, only return advisories that have an EPSS percentile score that matches the provided value.<br>The EPSS percentile represents the relative rank of the CVE's likelihood of being exploited compared to other CVEs.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|reviewed|
|type|malware|
|type|unreviewed|
|ecosystem|rubygems|
|ecosystem|npm|
|ecosystem|pip|
|ecosystem|maven|
|ecosystem|nuget|
|ecosystem|composer|
|ecosystem|go|
|ecosystem|rust|
|ecosystem|erlang|
|ecosystem|actions|
|ecosystem|pub|
|ecosystem|other|
|ecosystem|swift|
|severity|unknown|
|severity|low|
|severity|medium|
|severity|high|
|severity|critical|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
|sort|updated|
|sort|published|
|sort|epss_percentage|
|sort|epss_percentile|

## List repository security advisories for an organization

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/list-org-repository-advisories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/security-advisories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/security-advisories`

Lists repository security advisories for an organization.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:write` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#list-repository-security-advisories-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## List repository security advisories

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/list-repository-advisories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories`

Lists security advisories in a repository.

The authenticated user can access unpublished security advisories from a repository if they are a security manager or administrator of that repository, or if they are a collaborator on any security advisory.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:read` scope to to get a published security advisory in a private repository, or any unpublished security advisory that the authenticated user has access to.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#list-repository-security-advisories">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-repository-security-advisories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort the results by.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of advisories to return per page. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|state|query|string|false|Filter by state of the repository advisories. Only advisories of this state will be returned.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|published|
|state|triage|
|state|draft|
|state|published|
|state|closed|

## Create a repository security advisory

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/create-repository-advisory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "summary": "A new important advisory",
    "description": "A more in-depth description of what the problem is.",
    "severity": "high",
    "cve_id": null,
    "vulnerabilities": [
      {
        "package": {
          "name": "a-package",
          "ecosystem": "npm"
        },
        "vulnerable_version_range": "< 1.0.0",
        "patched_versions": "1.0.0",
        "vulnerable_functions": [
          "important_function"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "cwe_ids": [
      "CWE-1101",
      "CWE-20"
    ],
    "credits": [
      {
        "login": "monalisa",
        "type": "reporter"
      },
      {
        "login": "octocat",
        "type": "analyst"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories`

Creates a new repository security advisory.

In order to create a draft repository security advisory, the authenticated user must be a security manager or administrator of that repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:write` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#create-a-repository-security-advisory">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "summary": "A new important advisory",
  "description": "A more in-depth description of what the problem is.",
  "severity": "high",
  "cve_id": null,
  "vulnerabilities": [
    {
      "package": {
        "name": "a-package",
        "ecosystem": "npm"
      },
      "vulnerable_version_range": "< 1.0.0",
      "patched_versions": "1.0.0",
      "vulnerable_functions": [
        "important_function"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "cwe_ids": [
    "CWE-1101",
    "CWE-20"
  ],
  "credits": [
    {
      "login": "monalisa",
      "type": "reporter"
    },
    {
      "login": "octocat",
      "type": "analyst"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-repository-security-advisory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[repository-advisory-create](#schemarepository-advisory-create)|true|none|
|» summary|body|string|true|A short summary of the advisory.|
|» description|body|string|true|A detailed description of what the advisory impacts.|
|» cve_id|body|string \| null|false|The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) ID.|
|» vulnerabilities|body|[object]|true|A product affected by the vulnerability detailed in a repository security advisory.|
|» » package|body|object|true|The name of the package affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » » ecosystem|body|[security-advisory-ecosystems](#schemasecurity-advisory-ecosystems)|true|The package's language or package management ecosystem.|
|» » » name|body|string \| null|false|The unique package name within its ecosystem.|
|» » vulnerable_version_range|body|string \| null|false|The range of the package versions affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » patched_versions|body|string \| null|false|The package version(s) that resolve the vulnerability.|
|» » vulnerable_functions|body|[string]|false|The functions in the package that are affected.|
|» cwe_ids|body|[string]|false|A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) IDs.|
|» credits|body|[object]|false|A list of users receiving credit for their participation in the security advisory.|
|» » login|body|string|true|The username of the user credited.|
|» » type|body|[security-advisory-credit-types](#schemasecurity-advisory-credit-types)|true|The type of credit the user is receiving.|
|» severity|body|string \| null|false|The severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `cvss_vector_string`.|
|» cvss_vector_string|body|string \| null|false|The CVSS vector that calculates the severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `severity`.|
|» start_private_fork|body|boolean|false|Whether to create a temporary private fork of the repository to collaborate on a fix.|

## Privately report a security vulnerability

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/create-private-vulnerability-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "summary": "A newly discovered vulnerability",
    "description": "A more in-depth description of what the problem is.",
    "severity": "high",
    "vulnerabilities": [
      {
        "package": {
          "name": "a-package",
          "ecosystem": "npm"
        },
        "vulnerable_version_range": "< 1.0.0",
        "patched_versions": "1.0.0",
        "vulnerable_functions": [
          "important_function"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "cwe_ids": [
      "CWE-123"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/reports`

Report a security vulnerability to the maintainers of the repository.
See "[Privately reporting a security vulnerability](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/guidance-on-reporting-and-writing/privately-reporting-a-security-vulnerability)" for more information about private vulnerability reporting.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#privately-report-a-security-vulnerability">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "summary": "A newly discovered vulnerability",
  "description": "A more in-depth description of what the problem is.",
  "severity": "high",
  "vulnerabilities": [
    {
      "package": {
        "name": "a-package",
        "ecosystem": "npm"
      },
      "vulnerable_version_range": "< 1.0.0",
      "patched_versions": "1.0.0",
      "vulnerable_functions": [
        "important_function"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "cwe_ids": [
    "CWE-123"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="privately-report-a-security-vulnerability-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[private-vulnerability-report-create](#schemaprivate-vulnerability-report-create)|true|none|
|» summary|body|string|true|A short summary of the advisory.|
|» description|body|string|true|A detailed description of what the advisory impacts.|
|» vulnerabilities|body|[object]|false|An array of products affected by the vulnerability detailed in a repository security advisory.|
|» » package|body|object|true|The name of the package affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » » ecosystem|body|[security-advisory-ecosystems](#schemasecurity-advisory-ecosystems)|true|The package's language or package management ecosystem.|
|» » » name|body|string \| null|false|The unique package name within its ecosystem.|
|» » vulnerable_version_range|body|string \| null|false|The range of the package versions affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » patched_versions|body|string \| null|false|The package version(s) that resolve the vulnerability.|
|» » vulnerable_functions|body|[string]|false|The functions in the package that are affected.|
|» cwe_ids|body|[string]|false|A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) IDs.|
|» severity|body|string \| null|false|The severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `cvss_vector_string`.|
|» cvss_vector_string|body|string \| null|false|The CVSS vector that calculates the severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `severity`.|
|» start_private_fork|body|boolean|false|Whether to create a temporary private fork of the repository to collaborate on a fix. The fork is created only if you are permitted to create one; otherwise, this parameter is ignored and the report is still created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » ecosystem|rubygems|
|» » » ecosystem|npm|
|» » » ecosystem|pip|
|» » » ecosystem|maven|
|» » » ecosystem|nuget|
|» » » ecosystem|composer|
|» » » ecosystem|go|
|» » » ecosystem|rust|
|» » » ecosystem|erlang|
|» » » ecosystem|actions|
|» » » ecosystem|pub|
|» » » ecosystem|other|
|» » » ecosystem|swift|
|» severity|critical|
|» severity|high|
|» severity|medium|
|» severity|low|
|» severity|null|

## Get a repository security advisory

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/get-repository-advisory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}`

Get a repository security advisory using its GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) identifier.

Anyone can access any published security advisory on a public repository.

The authenticated user can access an unpublished security advisory from a repository if they are a security manager or administrator of that repository, or if they are a
collaborator on the security advisory.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:read` scope to to get a published security advisory in a private repository, or any unpublished security advisory that the authenticated user has access to.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#get-a-repository-security-advisory">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-repository-security-advisory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|

This operation does not require authentication

## Update a repository security advisory

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/update-repository-advisory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "severity": "critical",
    "state": "published"
  }'
```

`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}`

Update a repository security advisory using its GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) identifier.

In order to update any security advisory, the authenticated user must be a security manager or administrator of that repository,
or a collaborator on the repository security advisory.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:write` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#update-a-repository-security-advisory">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "severity": "critical",
  "state": "published"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-repository-security-advisory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|
|body|body|[repository-advisory-update](#schemarepository-advisory-update)|true|none|
|» summary|body|string|false|A short summary of the advisory.|
|» description|body|string|false|A detailed description of what the advisory impacts.|
|» cve_id|body|string \| null|false|The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) ID.|
|» vulnerabilities|body|[object]|false|A product affected by the vulnerability detailed in a repository security advisory.|
|» » package|body|object|true|The name of the package affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » » ecosystem|body|[security-advisory-ecosystems](#schemasecurity-advisory-ecosystems)|true|The package's language or package management ecosystem.|
|» » » name|body|string \| null|false|The unique package name within its ecosystem.|
|» » vulnerable_version_range|body|string \| null|false|The range of the package versions affected by the vulnerability.|
|» » patched_versions|body|string \| null|false|The package version(s) that resolve the vulnerability.|
|» » vulnerable_functions|body|[string]|false|The functions in the package that are affected.|
|» cwe_ids|body|[string]|false|A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) IDs.|
|» credits|body|[object]|false|A list of users receiving credit for their participation in the security advisory.|
|» » login|body|string|true|The username of the user credited.|
|» » type|body|[security-advisory-credit-types](#schemasecurity-advisory-credit-types)|true|The type of credit the user is receiving.|
|» severity|body|string \| null|false|The severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `cvss_vector_string`.|
|» cvss_vector_string|body|string \| null|false|The CVSS vector that calculates the severity of the advisory. You must choose between setting this field or `severity`.|
|» state|body|string|false|The state of the advisory.|
|» collaborating_users|body|[string]|false|A list of usernames who have been granted write access to the advisory.|
|» collaborating_teams|body|[string]|false|A list of team slugs which have been granted write access to the advisory.|

## List repository security advisory comments

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/list-repository-advisory-comments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}/comments`

Lists comments on a repository security advisory.

Accessing internal comments requires write access to the advisory.

Callers with read-only access to the advisory receive only eligible post-publication comments. For unpublished advisories, these callers receive an empty list.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#list-repository-security-advisory-comments">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Get a repository advisory comment

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/get-repository-advisory-comment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string/comments/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Get a comment on a repository security advisory using the comment's ID.

Advisory collaborators can view all non-confidential comments on advisories they have access to.
Other users can only view comments that are not considered internal.

GitHub Apps and fine-grained personal access tokens with the `repository_advisories: read` permission can view all non-confidential comments, including internal comments.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:read` scope to get a comment on a security advisory in a private repository, or any unpublished security advisory that the authenticated user has access to.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#get-a-repository-advisory-comment">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-a-repository-advisory-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|
|comment_id|path|integer(int64)|true|The unique identifier of the comment.|

## Request a CVE for a repository security advisory

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/create-repository-advisory-cve-request"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string/cve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}/cve`

If you want a CVE identification number for the security vulnerability in your project, and don't already have one, you can request a CVE identification number from GitHub. For more information see "[Requesting a CVE identification number](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/repository-security-advisories/publishing-a-repository-security-advisory#requesting-a-cve-identification-number-optional)."

You may request a CVE for public repositories, but cannot do so for private repositories.

In order to request a CVE for a repository security advisory, the authenticated user must be a security manager or administrator of that repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` or `repository_advisories:write` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#request-a-cve-for-a-repository-security-advisory">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="request-a-cve-for-a-repository-security-advisory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|

<h3 id="request-a-cve-for-a-repository-security-advisory-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error](#schemavalidation-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create a temporary private fork

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisories/create-fork"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/security-advisories/string/forks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa_id}/forks`

Create a temporary private fork to collaborate on fixing a security vulnerability in a repository.

Repository administrators, organization owners, and security managers can create a temporary private fork. The original reporter of a privately reported vulnerability can also create one while they remain a collaborator on the security advisory.

> [!NOTE]
> Forking a repository happens asynchronously. You may have to wait up to 5 minutes before you can access the fork.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/repository-advisories#create-a-temporary-private-fork">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="create-a-temporary-private-fork-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|ghsa_id|path|string|true|The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-interactions">interactions</h1>

Owner or admin management of users interactions.

## Get interaction restrictions for an organization

<a id="opIdinteractions/get-restrictions-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/interaction-limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/interaction-limits`

Shows which type of GitHub user can interact with this organization and when the restriction expires. If there is no restrictions, you will see an empty response.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/orgs#get-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "origin": "organization",
  "expires_at": "2018-08-17T04:18:39Z"
}
```

<h3 id="get-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|

<h3 id="get-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[interaction-limit-response](#schemainteraction-limit-response)|false|none|Interaction limit settings.|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Set interaction restrictions for an organization

<a id="opIdinteractions/set-restrictions-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/interaction-limits \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "limit": "collaborators_only",
    "expiry": "one_month"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/interaction-limits`

Temporarily restricts interactions to a certain type of GitHub user in any public repository in the given organization. You must be an organization owner to set these restrictions. Setting the interaction limit at the organization level will overwrite any interaction limits that are set for individual repositories owned by the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/orgs#set-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "expiry": "one_month"
}
```

<h3 id="set-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[interaction-limit](#schemainteraction-limit)|true|none|
|» limit|body|[interaction-group](#schemainteraction-group)|true|The type of GitHub user that can comment, open issues, or create pull requests while the interaction limit is in effect.|
|» expiry|body|[interaction-expiry](#schemainteraction-expiry)|false|The duration of the interaction restriction. Default: `one_day`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» limit|existing_users|
|» limit|contributors_only|
|» limit|collaborators_only|
|» expiry|one_day|
|» expiry|three_days|
|» expiry|one_week|
|» expiry|one_month|
|» expiry|six_months|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "origin": "organization",
  "expires_at": "2018-08-17T04:18:39Z"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

## Remove interaction restrictions for an organization

<a id="opIdinteractions/remove-restrictions-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/interaction-limits \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/interaction-limits`

Removes all interaction restrictions from public repositories in the given organization. You must be an organization owner to remove restrictions.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/orgs#remove-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="remove-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

<h3 id="remove-interaction-restrictions-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Response|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get pull request creation cap for an org

<a id="opIdinteractions/get-pull-request-creation-cap-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/interaction-limits/pulls/creation-cap \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/interaction-limits/pulls/creation-cap`

Gets the pull request creation cap configuration for an organization.
The cap limits the total number of open pull requests a user can have across all public
repositories in the organization at one time.

Only users with admin access to the organization can view the cap configuration.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/orgs#get-pull-request-creation-cap-for-an-org">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-pull-request-creation-cap-for-an-org-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "max_open_pull_requests": 1
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-pull-request-creation-cap-for-an-org-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method Not Allowed|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h3 id="get-pull-request-creation-cap-for-an-org-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Whether the pull request creation cap is enabled|
|max_open_pull_requests|integer|true|none|The maximum number of open pull requests a user can have at one time|
|include_drafts|boolean|false|none|Whether draft pull requests count toward the pull request creation cap|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

## Set interaction restrictions for a repository

<a id="opIdinteractions/set-restrictions-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/interaction-limits \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "limit": "collaborators_only",
    "expiry": "one_day"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/interaction-limits`

Temporarily restricts interactions to a certain type of GitHub user within the given repository. You must have owner or admin access to set these restrictions. If an interaction limit is set for the user or organization that owns this repository, you will receive a `409 Conflict` response and will not be able to use this endpoint to change the interaction limit for a single repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/repos#set-interaction-restrictions-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "expiry": "one_day"
}
```

<h3 id="set-interaction-restrictions-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|[interaction-limit](#schemainteraction-limit)|true|none|
|» limit|body|[interaction-group](#schemainteraction-group)|true|The type of GitHub user that can comment, open issues, or create pull requests while the interaction limit is in effect.|
|» expiry|body|[interaction-expiry](#schemainteraction-expiry)|false|The duration of the interaction restriction. Default: `one_day`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» limit|existing_users|
|» limit|contributors_only|
|» limit|collaborators_only|

```bash
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/interaction-limits`

Removes all interaction restrictions from the given repository. You must have owner or admin access to remove restrictions. If the interaction limit is set for the user or organization that owns this repository, you will receive a `409 Conflict` response and will not be able to use this endpoint to change the interaction limit for a single repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/repos#remove-interaction-restrictions-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|

## Set interaction restrictions for your public repositories

<a id="opIdinteractions/set-restrictions-for-authenticated-user"></a>

`PUT /user/interaction-limits`

Temporarily restricts which type of GitHub user can interact with your public repositories. Setting the interaction limit at the user level will overwrite any interaction limits that are set for individual repositories owned by the user.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/interactions/user#set-interaction-restrictions-for-your-public-repositories">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json

  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "expiry": "one_month"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[interaction-limit](#schemainteraction-limit)|true|none|
|» limit|body|[interaction-group](#schemainteraction-group)|true|The type of GitHub user that can comment, open issues, or create pull requests while the interaction limit is in effect.|
|» expiry|body|[interaction-expiry](#schemainteraction-expiry)|false|The duration of the interaction restriction. Default: `one_day`.|

## Get code security configurations for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcode-security/get-configurations-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations`

Lists all code security configurations available in an enterprise.

The authenticated user must be an administrator of the enterprise in order to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#get-code-security-configurations-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
