## Create a code security configuration for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcode-security/create-configuration-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "High rish settings",
    "description": "This is a code security configuration for octo-enterprise",
    "advanced_security": "enabled",
    "dependabot_alerts": "enabled",
    "dependabot_security_updates": "not_set",
    "secret_scanning": "enabled"
  }'
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations`

Creates a code security configuration in an enterprise.

The authenticated user must be an administrator of the enterprise in order to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#create-a-code-security-configuration-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "High rish settings",
  "description": "This is a code security configuration for octo-enterprise",
  "advanced_security": "enabled",
  "dependabot_alerts": "enabled",
  "dependabot_security_updates": "not_set",
  "secret_scanning": "enabled"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-code-security-configuration-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the code security configuration. Must be unique within the enterprise.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the code security configuration|
|» advanced_security|body|string|false|The enablement status of GitHub Advanced Security features. `enabled` will enable both Code Security and Secret Protection features.<br><br>> [!WARNING]<br>> `code_security` and `secret_protection` are deprecated values for this field. Prefer the individual `code_security` and `secret_protection` fields to set the status of these features.<br>|
|» code_security|body|string|false|The enablement status of GitHub Code Security features.|
|» dependency_graph|body|string|false|The enablement status of Dependency Graph|
|» dependency_graph_autosubmit_action|body|string|false|The enablement status of Automatic dependency submission|
|» dependency_graph_autosubmit_action_options|body|object|false|Feature options for Automatic dependency submission|
|» » labeled_runners|body|boolean|false|Whether to use runners labeled with 'dependency-submission' or standard GitHub runners.|
|» dependabot_alerts|body|string|false|The enablement status of Dependabot alerts|
|» dependabot_reachability|body|string|false|The enablement status of reachability analysis for Dependabot. Only available for enterprises with access to reachability analysis.<br>Requires Dependabot alerts to be enabled when set to `enabled`. Must be `disabled` when Dependabot alerts is `disabled`.<br>`not_set` leaves existing repository settings unchanged.|
|» dependabot_security_updates|body|string|false|The enablement status of Dependabot security updates|
|» code_scanning_options|body|[code-scanning-options](#schemacode-scanning-options)|false|Security Configuration feature options for code scanning|
|» code_scanning_default_setup|body|string|false|The enablement status of code scanning default setup|
|» code_scanning_default_setup_options|body|[code-scanning-default-setup-options](#schemacode-scanning-default-setup-options)|false|Feature options for code scanning default setup|
|» code_scanning_delegated_alert_dismissal|body|string|false|The enablement status of code scanning delegated alert dismissal|
|» secret_protection|body|string|false|The enablement status of GitHub Secret Protection features.|
|» secret_scanning|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning|
|» secret_scanning_push_protection|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning push protection|
|» secret_scanning_validity_checks|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning validity checks|
|» secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning non provider patterns|
|» secret_scanning_generic_secrets|body|string|false|The enablement status of Copilot secret scanning|
|» secret_scanning_generic_secrets_push_protection|body|string|false|The enablement status of generic secrets push protection|
|» secret_scanning_delegated_alert_dismissal|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning delegated alert dismissal|
|» secret_scanning_extended_metadata|body|string|false|The enablement status of secret scanning extended metadata|
|» private_vulnerability_reporting|body|string|false|The enablement status of private vulnerability reporting|
|» enforcement|body|string|false|The enforcement status for a security configuration|

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}`

## Delete a code security configuration for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcode-security/delete-configuration-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}`

Deletes a code security configuration from an enterprise.
Repositories attached to the configuration will retain their settings but will no longer be associated with
the configuration.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the enterprise to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

## Update a custom code security configuration for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcode-security/update-enterprise-configuration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "octo-enterprise recommended settings v2",
    "secret_scanning": "disabled",
    "code_scanning_default_setup": "enabled"
  }'
```

`PATCH /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}`

Updates a code security configuration in an enterprise.

The authenticated user must be an administrator of the enterprise in order to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#update-a-custom-code-security-configuration-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

```json

  "name": "octo-enterprise recommended settings v2",
  "secret_scanning": "disabled",
  "code_scanning_default_setup": "enabled"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|configuration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the code security configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

|» description|body|string|false|A description of the code security configuration|
|» advanced_security|body|string|false|The enablement status of GitHub Advanced Security features. `enabled` will enable both Code Security and Secret Protection features.<br><br>> [!WARNING]<br>> `code_security` and `secret_protection` are deprecated values for this field. Prefer the individual `code_security` and `secret_protection` fields to set the status of these features.<br>|
|» code_security|body|string|false|The enablement status of GitHub Code Security features.|

|» dependency_graph_autosubmit_action_options|body|object|false|Feature options for Automatic dependency submission|
|» » labeled_runners|body|boolean|false|Whether to use runners labeled with 'dependency-submission' or standard GitHub runners.|
|» dependabot_alerts|body|string|false|The enablement status of Dependabot alerts|
|» dependabot_reachability|body|string|false|The enablement status of reachability analysis for Dependabot. |» dependabot_security_updates|body|string|false|The enablement status of Dependabot security updates|
|» code_scanning_default_setup|body|string|false|The enablement status of code scanning default setup|
|» code_scanning_default_setup_options|body|[code-scanning-default-setup-options](#schemacode-scanning-default-setup-options)|false|Feature options for code scanning default setup|
|» code_scanning_options|body|[code-scanning-options](#schemacode-scanning-options)|false|Security Configuration feature options for code scanning|

## Attach an enterprise configuration to repositories

<a id="opIdcode-security/attach-enterprise-configuration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations/0/attach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "scope": "all"
  }'
```

`POST /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}/attach`

Attaches an enterprise code security configuration to repositories. If the repositories specified are already attached to a configuration, they will be re-attached to the provided configuration.

If insufficient GHAS licenses are available to attach the configuration to a repository, only free features will be enabled.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the enterprise to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#attach-an-enterprise-configuration-to-repositories">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scope": "all"
}
```

<h3 id="attach-an-enterprise-configuration-to-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|configuration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the code security configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scope|body|string|true|The type of repositories to attach the configuration to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» scope|all_without_configurations|

## Set a code security configuration as a default for an enterprise

<a id="opIdcode-security/set-configuration-as-default-for-enterprise"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/enterprises/string/code-security/configurations/0/defaults \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "default_for_new_repos": "all"
  }'
```

`PUT /enterprises/{enterprise}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}/defaults`

Sets a code security configuration as a default to be applied to new repositories in your enterprise.

This configuration will be applied by default to the matching repository type when created, but only for organizations within the enterprise that do not already have a default code security configuration set.

The authenticated user must be an administrator for the enterprise to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:enterprise` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#set-a-code-security-configuration-as-a-default-for-an-enterprise">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_for_new_repos": "all"
}
```

<h3 id="set-a-code-security-configuration-as-a-default-for-an-enterprise-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|path|string|true|The slug version of the enterprise name.|
|configuration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the code security configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» default_for_new_repos|body|string|false|Specify which types of repository this security configuration should be applied to by default.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» default_for_new_repos|all|
|» default_for_new_repos|none|

## Create a code security configuration

<a id="opIdcode-security/create-configuration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-security/configurations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "octo-org recommended settings",

    "advanced_security": "enabled",

    "dependabot_security_updates": "not_set",
    "secret_scanning": "enabled"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/code-security/configurations`

Creates a code security configuration in an organization.

The authenticated user must be an administrator or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `write:org` scope to use this endpoint.

```json
  "dependabot_security_updates": "not_set",
  "secret_scanning": "enabled"
}
```

## Detach configurations from repositories

<a id="opIdcode-security/detach-configuration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-security/configurations/detach \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      32,
      91
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/code-security/configurations/detach`

Detach code security configuration(s) from a set of repositories.
Repositories will retain their settings but will no longer be associated with the configuration.

The authenticated user must be an administrator or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

Repositories with active enterprise-enforced attachments are skipped unless the authenticated user can manage the enterprise's code security settings; the rest are detached. Inactive enterprise-enforced attachments, such as failed attachments, are detached. The request still returns `204` if every repository is skipped.

OAuth app tokens and classic PATs require the `write:org` scope. Managing enterprise-enforced configurations also requires `admin:enterprise` and is not supported by fine-grained PATs or GitHub App access tokens.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#detach-configurations-from-repositories">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    32,
    91
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="detach-configurations-from-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array of repository IDs to detach from configurations. Up to 250 IDs can be provided.|

## Attach a configuration to repositories

<a id="opIdcode-security/attach-configuration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-security/configurations/0/attach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "scope": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      32,
      91
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}/attach`

Attach a code security configuration to a set of repositories. If the repositories specified are already attached to a configuration, they will be re-attached to the provided configuration.

If insufficient GHAS licenses are available to attach the configuration to a repository, only free features will be enabled.

The authenticated user must be an administrator or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

Directly applying an enterprise-enforced configuration also requires permission to manage the enterprise's code security settings. Without it, the request returns `403` and no repositories change.

When applying a different configuration, repositories with active enterprise-enforced attachments are skipped unless the authenticated user can manage the enterprise's code security settings; the remaining repositories are updated. The request still returns `202` if every repository is skipped.

OAuth app tokens and classic PATs require the `write:org` scope. Directly applying an enterprise-enforced configuration also requires `admin:enterprise` and is not supported by fine-grained PATs or GitHub App access tokens.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#attach-a-configuration-to-repositories">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scope": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    32,
    91
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="attach-a-configuration-to-repositories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|configuration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the code security configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» scope|body|string|true|The type of repositories to attach the configuration to. `selected` means the configuration will be attached to only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids`|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository IDs to attach the configuration to. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `scope` is set to `selected`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» scope|all|
|» scope|all_without_configurations|
|» scope|public|
|» scope|private_or_internal|
|» scope|selected|

## Set a code security configuration as a default for an organization

<a id="opIdcode-security/set-configuration-as-default"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/code-security/configurations/0/defaults \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "default_for_new_repos": "all"
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/code-security/configurations/{configuration_id}/defaults`

Sets a code security configuration as a default to be applied to new repositories in your organization.

This configuration will be applied to the matching repository type (all, none, public, private and internal) by default when they are created.

The authenticated user must be an administrator or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint. Setting an enterprise-enforced configuration as the default also requires permission to manage the enterprise's code security settings.

A default set with this endpoint is an organization default, even if the configuration is owned or enforced by the enterprise. An enterprise-enforced configuration set as an enterprise-level default for the same repository visibility takes precedence.

OAuth app tokens and classic PATs require the `write:org` scope; setting an enterprise-enforced configuration as the default also requires `admin:enterprise`. Fine-grained PATs and GitHub App access tokens cannot perform that action.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/code-security/configurations#set-a-code-security-configuration-as-a-default-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default_for_new_repos": "all"
}
```

<h3 id="set-a-code-security-configuration-as-a-default-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|configuration_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the code security configuration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» default_for_new_repos|body|string|false|Specify which types of repository this security configuration should be applied to by default.|

## Create a private registry for an organization

<a id="opIdprivate-registries/create-org-private-registry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/private-registries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "registry_type": "maven_repository",
    "url": "https://maven.pkg.github.com/organization/",
    "username": "monalisa",
    "replaces_base": true,
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "visibility": "private"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/private-registries`


Creates a private registry configuration with an encrypted value for an organization. Encrypt your secret using [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."
For OIDC-based registries (`oidc_azure`, `oidc_aws`, `oidc_jfrog`, `oidc_cloudsmith`, or `oidc_gcp`), the `encrypted_value` and `key_id` fields should be omitted.
For anonymous registries (`anonymous`), the `username`, `encrypted_value`, and `key_id` fields must be omitted.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/private-registries/organization-configurations#create-a-private-registry-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "registry_type": "maven_repository",
  "url": "https://maven.pkg.github.com/organization/",
  "username": "monalisa",
  "replaces_base": true,
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "visibility": "private"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-private-registry-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» registry_type|body|string|true|The registry type.|
|» url|body|string(uri)|true|The URL of the private registry.|
|» username|body|string \| null|false|The username to use when authenticating with the private registry. This field should be omitted if the private registry does not require a username for authentication.|
|» replaces_base|body|boolean|false|Whether this private registry should replace the base registry (e.g., npmjs.org for npm, rubygems.org for rubygems). When set to `true`, Dependabot will only use this registry and will not fall back to the public registry. When set to `false` (default), Dependabot will use this registry for scoped packages but may fall back to the public registry for other packages.|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|The value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get private registries public key for an organization](https://docs.github.com/rest/private-registries/organization-configurations#get-private-registries-public-key-for-an-organization) endpoint. Required when `auth_type` is `token` or `username_password`. Should be omitted for OIDC auth types.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|The ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret. Required when `auth_type` is `token` or `username_password`. Should be omitted for OIDC auth types.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Which type of organization repositories have access to the private registry. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the private registry.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository IDs that can access the organization private registry. You can only provide a list of repository IDs when `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [Update a private registry for an organization](https://docs.github.com/rest/private-registries/organization-configurations#update-a-private-registry-for-an-organization) endpoint. This field should be omitted if `visibility` is set to `all` or `private`.|
|» auth_type|body|string|false|The authentication type for the private registry. Defaults to `token` if not specified. Use `oidc_azure`, `oidc_aws`, `oidc_jfrog`, `oidc_cloudsmith`, or `oidc_gcp` for OIDC authentication. Use `anonymous` for registries that do not require authentication; `username`, `encrypted_value`, and `key_id` must be omitted.|
|» tenant_id|body|string|false|The tenant ID of the Azure AD application. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_azure`.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The client ID of the Azure AD application. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_azure`.|
|» aws_region|body|string|false|The AWS region. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» account_id|body|string|false|The AWS account ID. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» role_name|body|string|false|The AWS IAM role name. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» domain|body|string|false|The CodeArtifact domain. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» domain_owner|body|string|false|The CodeArtifact domain owner (AWS account ID). Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» jfrog_oidc_provider_name|body|string|false|The JFrog OIDC provider name. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_jfrog`.|
|» audience|body|string|false|The OIDC audience. Optional for `oidc_aws`, `oidc_jfrog`, and `oidc_gcp`, and required for `oidc_cloudsmith` auth types.|
|» identity_mapping_name|body|string|false|The JFrog identity mapping name. Optional for `oidc_jfrog` auth type.|
|» namespace|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith organization namespace. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_cloudsmith`.|
|» service_slug|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith service account slug. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_cloudsmith`.|
|» api_host|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith API host. Optional for `oidc_cloudsmith` auth type. If omitted, `api.cloudsmith.io` is used by default.|
|» workload_identity_provider|body|string|false|The full resource name of the GCP Workload Identity Provider (e.g. `projects/<NUM>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/<POOL>/providers/<PROVIDER>`). Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_gcp`.|
|» service_account|body|string|false|The GCP service account email to impersonate. Optional for `oidc_gcp` auth type. If omitted, the federated token is used directly (direct WIF).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» registry_type|maven_repository|
|» registry_type|nuget_feed|
|» registry_type|goproxy_server|
|» registry_type|npm_registry|
|» registry_type|rubygems_server|
|» registry_type|cargo_registry|
|» registry_type|composer_repository|
|» registry_type|docker_registry|
|» registry_type|git_source|
|» registry_type|helm_registry|
|» registry_type|hex_organization|
|» registry_type|hex_repository|
|» registry_type|pub_repository|
|» registry_type|python_index|
|» registry_type|terraform_registry|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|
|» auth_type|token|
|» auth_type|username_password|
|» auth_type|oidc_azure|
|» auth_type|oidc_aws|
|» auth_type|oidc_jfrog|
|» auth_type|oidc_cloudsmith|
|» auth_type|oidc_gcp|
|» auth_type|anonymous|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "name": "MAVEN_REPOSITORY_SECRET",
  "registry_type": "maven_repository",
  "username": "monalisa",
  "visibility": "private",
  "created_at": "2019-08-10T14:59:22Z",
  "updated_at": "2020-01-10T14:59:22Z"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "resource": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "code": "string",
      "index": 0,
      "value": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-private-registry-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The organization private registry configuration|[org-private-registry-configuration-with-selected-repositories](#schemaorg-private-registry-configuration-with-selected-repositories)|

## Update a private registry for an organization

<a id="opIdprivate-registries/update-org-private-registry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/private-registries/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "username": "monalisa",
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/private-registries/{secret_name}`


Updates a private registry configuration with an encrypted value for an organization. Encrypt your secret using [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."
For OIDC-based registries (`oidc_azure`, `oidc_aws`, `oidc_jfrog`, `oidc_cloudsmith`, or `oidc_gcp`), the `encrypted_value` and `key_id` fields should be omitted.
For anonymous registries (`anonymous`), the `username`, `encrypted_value`, and `key_id` fields must be omitted, and `auth_type` cannot be changed to or from `anonymous`.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/private-registries/organization-configurations#update-a-private-registry-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "username": "monalisa",
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-private-registry-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» registry_type|body|string|false|The registry type.|
|» url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL of the private registry.|
|» username|body|string \| null|false|The username to use when authenticating with the private registry. This field should be omitted if the private registry does not require a username for authentication.|
|» replaces_base|body|boolean|false|Whether this private registry should replace the base registry (e.g., npmjs.org for npm, rubygems.org for rubygems). When set to `true`, Dependabot will only use this registry and will not fall back to the public registry. When set to `false` (default), Dependabot will use this registry for scoped packages but may fall back to the public registry for other packages.|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|false|The value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get private registries public key for an organization](https://docs.github.com/rest/private-registries/organization-configurations#get-private-registries-public-key-for-an-organization) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|false|The ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|
|» visibility|body|string|false|Which type of organization repositories have access to the private registry. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the private registry.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository IDs that can access the organization private registry. You can only provide a list of repository IDs when `visibility` is set to `selected`. This field should be omitted if `visibility` is set to `all` or `private`.|
|» auth_type|body|string|false|The authentication type for the private registry. This field cannot be changed after creation. If provided, it must match the existing `auth_type` of the configuration. To change the authentication type, delete and recreate the configuration.|
|» tenant_id|body|string|false|The tenant ID of the Azure AD application. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_azure`.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The client ID of the Azure AD application. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_azure`.|
|» aws_region|body|string|false|The AWS region. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» account_id|body|string|false|The AWS account ID. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» role_name|body|string|false|The AWS IAM role name. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» domain|body|string|false|The CodeArtifact domain. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» domain_owner|body|string|false|The CodeArtifact domain owner (AWS account ID). Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_aws`.|
|» jfrog_oidc_provider_name|body|string|false|The JFrog OIDC provider name. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_jfrog`.|
|» audience|body|string|false|The OIDC audience. Optional for `oidc_aws`, `oidc_jfrog`, and `oidc_gcp`, and required for `oidc_cloudsmith` auth types.|
|» identity_mapping_name|body|string|false|The JFrog identity mapping name. Optional for `oidc_jfrog` auth type.|
|» namespace|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith organization namespace. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_cloudsmith`.|
|» service_slug|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith service account slug. Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_cloudsmith`.|
|» api_host|body|string|false|The Cloudsmith API host. Optional for `oidc_cloudsmith` auth type. If omitted, `api.cloudsmith.io` is used by default.|
|» workload_identity_provider|body|string|false|The full resource name of the GCP Workload Identity Provider (e.g. `projects/<NUM>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/<POOL>/providers/<PROVIDER>`). Required when `auth_type` is `oidc_gcp`.|
|» service_account|body|string|false|The GCP service account email to impersonate. Optional for `oidc_gcp` auth type. If omitted, the federated token is used directly (direct WIF).|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-credentials">credentials</h1>

Revoke compromised or leaked GitHub credentials.

## Revoke a list of credentials

<a id="opIdcredentials/revoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/credentials/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "credentials": [
      "ghp_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
      "github_pat_0A1B2C3D4E5F6G7H8I9J0K_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456",
      "gho_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
      "ghu_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
      "ghr_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /credentials/revoke`

Submit a list of credentials to be revoked. This endpoint is intended to revoke credentials the caller does not own and may have found exposed on GitHub.com or elsewhere. It can also be used for credentials associated with an old user account that you no longer have access to. Credential owners will be notified of the revocation.

This endpoint currently accepts the following credential types:
- Personal access tokens (classic) (`ghp_`)
- Fine-grained personal access tokens (`github_pat_`)
- OAuth app access tokens (`gho_`)
- User-to-server tokens from GitHub Apps (`ghu_`)
- Refresh tokens from GitHub Apps (`ghr_`)


Revoked credentials may impact users on GitHub Free, Pro, & Team and GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users.
GitHub cannot reactivate any credentials that have been revoked; new credentials will need to be generated.

To prevent abuse, this API is limited to only 60 unauthenticated requests per hour and a max of 1000 tokens per API request.

> [!NOTE]
> Any authenticated requests will return a 403.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/credentials/revoke#revoke-a-list-of-credentials">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    "ghp_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
    "github_pat_0A1B2C3D4E5F6G7H8I9J0K_ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456",
    "gho_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
    "ghu_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
    "ghr_1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-list-of-credentials-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» credentials|body|[string]|true|A list of credentials to be revoked, up to 1000 per request.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
null
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "errors": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-list-of-credentials-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.|[validation-error-simple](#schemavalidation-error-simple)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Error|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-campaigns">campaigns</h1>

Endpoints to manage campaigns via the REST API.

## List campaigns for an organization

<a id="opIdcampaigns/list-org-campaigns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/campaigns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/campaigns`

Lists campaigns in an organization.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/campaigns/campaigns#list-campaigns-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-campaigns-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results by.|
|state|query|[campaign-state](#schemacampaign-state)|false|If specified, only campaigns with this state will be returned.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property by which to sort the results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|
|state|open|
|state|closed|
|sort|created|
|sort|updated|
|sort|ends_at|
|sort|published|

## Create a campaign for an organization

<a id="opIdcampaigns/create-campaign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/campaigns \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Critical CodeQL alerts",
    "description": "Address critical alerts before they are exploited to prevent breaches, protect sensitive data, and mitigate financial and reputational damage.",
    "managers": [
      "octocat"
    ],
    "ends_at": "2024-03-14T00:00:00Z",
    "code_scanning_alerts": [
      {
        "repository_id": 1296269,
        "alert_numbers": [
          1,
          2
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/campaigns`

Create a campaign for an organization.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint.

Fine-grained tokens must have the "Code scanning alerts" repository permissions (read) on all repositories included
in the campaign.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/campaigns/campaigns#create-a-campaign-for-an-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Critical CodeQL alerts",
  "description": "Address critical alerts before they are exploited to prevent breaches, protect sensitive data, and mitigate financial and reputational damage.",
  "managers": [
    "octocat"
  ],
  "ends_at": "2024-03-14T00:00:00Z",
  "code_scanning_alerts": [
    {
      "repository_id": 1296269,
      "alert_numbers": [
        1,
        2
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-campaign-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the campaign|
|» description|body|string|true|A description for the campaign|
|» managers|body|[string]|false|The logins of the users to set as the campaign managers. At this time, only a single manager can be supplied.|
|» team_managers|body|[string]|false|The slugs of the teams to set as the campaign managers.|
|» ends_at|body|string(date-time)|true|The end date and time of the campaign. The date must be in the future.|
|» contact_link|body|string \| null(uri)|false|The contact link of the campaign. Must be a URI.|
|» code_scanning_alerts|body|[object]|false|The code scanning alerts to include in this campaign|
|» » repository_id|body|integer|true|The repository id|
|» » alert_numbers|body|[integer]|true|The alert numbers|
|» generate_issues|body|boolean|false|If true, will automatically generate issues for the campaign. The default is false.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Update a campaign

<a id="opIdcampaigns/update-campaign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/campaigns/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Critical CodeQL alerts"
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/campaigns/{campaign_number}`

Updates a campaign in an organization.

The authenticated user must be an owner or security manager for the organization to use this endpoint.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `security_events` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/campaigns/campaigns#update-a-campaign">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Critical CodeQL alerts"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|campaign_number|path|integer|true|The campaign number.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the campaign|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the campaign|
|» managers|body|[string]|false|The logins of the users to set as the campaign managers. At this time, only a single manager can be supplied.|
|» team_managers|body|[string]|false|The slugs of the teams to set as the campaign managers.|
|» ends_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The end date and time of the campaign, in ISO 8601 format':' YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.|
|» contact_link|body|string \| null(uri)|false|The contact link of the campaign. Must be a URI.|
|» state|body|[campaign-state](#schemacampaign-state)|false|Indicates whether a campaign is open or closed|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|open|
|» state|closed|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-projects">projects</h1>

Endpoints to manage Projects using the REST API.

## List projects for organization

<a id="opIdprojects/list-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/projectsV2`

List all projects owned by a specific organization accessible by the authenticated user.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/projects#list-projects-for-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-projects-for-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|q|query|string|false|Limit results to projects of the specified type.|

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/drafts`

## Add a field to an organization-owned project.

<a id="opIdprojects/add-field-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/fields \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Team notes",
    "data_type": "text"
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/fields`

Add a field to an organization-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/fields#add-a-field-to-an-organization-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Team notes",
  "data_type": "text"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-field-to-an-organization-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» issue_field_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the IssueField to create the field for.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» single_select_options|body|[[projects-v2-field-single-select-option](#schemaprojects-v2-field-single-select-option)]|true|The options available for single select fields. At least one option must be provided when creating a single select field.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» iteration_configuration|body|[projects-v2-field-iteration-configuration](#schemaprojects-v2-field-iteration-configuration)|true|The configuration for iteration fields.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» data_type|text|
|» data_type|number|
|» data_type|date|
|» data_type|single_select|
|» data_type|iteration|

<a id="opIdprojects/list-items-for-org"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items`

List all items for a specific organization-owned project accessible by the authenticated user.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#list-items-for-an-organization-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-items-for-an-organization-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|q|query|string|false|Search query to filter items, see [Filtering projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects) for more information.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: `fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789` or `fields=123,456,789`|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

## Add item to organization owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/add-item-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "type": "Issue",
    "id": 3
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items`

Add an issue or pull request item to the specified organization owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#add-item-to-organization-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "Issue",
  "id": 3
}
```

<h3 id="add-item-to-organization-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|Details of the item to add to the project. You can specify either the unique ID or the repository owner, name, and issue/PR number.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of item to add to the project. Must be either Issue or PullRequest.|
|» id|body|integer|false|The unique identifier of the issue or pull request to add to the project.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The repository owner login.|
|» repo|body|string|false|The repository name.|
|» number|body|integer|false|The issue or pull request number.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|Issue|
|» type|PullRequest|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/components/examples/projects-v2-item-simple"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-item-to-organization-owned-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[projects-v2-item-simple](#schemaprojects-v2-item-simple)|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Requires authentication|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Get an item for an organization owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/get-org-item"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/items/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Get a specific item from an organization-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#get-an-item-for-an-organization-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-item-for-an-organization-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789 or fields=123,456,789|

## Delete project item for organization

<a id="opIdprojects/delete-item-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/items/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Delete a specific item from an organization-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#delete-project-item-for-organization">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-project-item-for-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-project-item-for-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|401|Unauthorized|Requires authentication|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

## Update project item for organization

<a id="opIdprojects/update-item-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/items/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "id": 123,
        "value": "Updated text value"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Update a specific item in an organization-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#update-project-item-for-organization">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "id": 123,
      "value": "Updated text value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-project-item-for-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|
|body|body|object|true|Field updates to apply to the project item. Only text, number, date, single select, and iteration fields are supported.|
|» fields|body|[object]|true|A list of field updates to apply.|
|» » id|body|integer|true|The ID of the project field to update.|
|» » value|body|null \| string \| number|true|The new value for the field:<br>- For text, number, and date fields, provide the new value directly.<br>- For single select and iteration fields, provide the ID of the option or iteration.<br>- To clear the field, set this to null.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|

## Create a view for an organization-owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/create-view-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/views \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "All Issues",
    "layout": "table",
    "filter": "is:issue",
    "visible_fields": [
      123,
      456,
      789
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/views`

Create a new view in an organization-owned project. Views allow you to customize how items in a project are displayed and filtered.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/views#create-a-view-for-an-organization-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "All Issues",
  "layout": "table",
  "filter": "is:issue",
  "visible_fields": [
    123,
    456,
    789
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-view-for-an-organization-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the view.|
|» layout|body|string|true|The layout of the view.|
|» filter|body|string|false|The filter query for the view. See [Filtering projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects) for more information.|
|» visible_fields|body|[integer]|false|`visible_fields` is not applicable to `roadmap` layout views.<br>For `table` and `board` layouts, this represents the field IDs that should be visible in the view. If not provided, the default visible fields will be used.|
|» sort_by|body|[[integer \| string]]|false|Sorting configuration for the view. Each element is a two-element array of `[field_id, direction]` where `direction` is `"asc"` or `"desc"`. Supports multiple sort criteria applied in order.|
|» group_by|body|[integer]|false|The field IDs to group items by (horizontal grouping). Supports a single field. The field must support grouping; fields such as `Title`, `Reviewers`, `Linked pull requests`, `Sub-issues progress`, `Tracked by`, and `Tracks` cannot be grouped on.|
|» vertical_group_by|body|[integer]|false|The field IDs to use as columns in `board` layout (vertical grouping). Supports a single field. The field must support grouping; fields such as `Title`, `Reviewers`, `Linked pull requests`, `Sub-issues progress`, `Tracked by`, and `Tracks` cannot be grouped on.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» layout|table|
|» layout|board|
|» layout|roadmap|

```json
  "$ref": "#/components/examples/projects-v2-view"
}
```

## List items for an organization project view

<a id="opIdprojects/list-view-items-for-org"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/projectsV2/0/views/0/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/projectsV2/{project_number}/views/{view_number}/items`

List items in an organization project with the saved view's filter applied.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#list-items-for-an-organization-project-view">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-items-for-an-organization-project-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|view_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the project view.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the<br>title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: `fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789` or `fields=123,456,789`|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. ## Create draft item for user owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/create-draft-item-for-authenticated-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/user/string/projectsV2/0/drafts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "title": "Sample Draft Issue Title"
  }'
```

`POST /user/{user_id}/projectsV2/{project_number}/drafts`

Create draft issue item for the specified user owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/drafts#create-draft-item-for-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "title": "Sample Draft Issue Title"
}
```

<h3 id="create-draft-item-for-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the user.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|Details of the draft item to create in the project.|
|» title|body|string|true|The title of the draft issue item to create in the project.|
|» body|body|string|false|The body content of the draft issue item to create in the project.|

## Create a view for a user-owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/create-view-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/views \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "All Issues",
    "layout": "table",
    "filter": "is:issue",
    "visible_fields": [
      123,
      456,
      789
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /users/{user_id}/projectsV2/{project_number}/views`

Create a new view in a user-owned project. Views allow you to customize how items in a project are displayed and filtered.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/views#create-a-view-for-a-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "All Issues",
  "layout": "table",
  "filter": "is:issue",
  "visible_fields": [
    123,
    456,
    789
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-view-for-a-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the user.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the view.|
|» layout|body|string|true|The layout of the view.|
|» filter|body|string|false|The filter query for the view. See [Filtering projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects) for more information.|
|» visible_fields|body|[integer]|false|`visible_fields` is not applicable to `roadmap` layout views.<br>For `table` and `board` layouts, this represents the field IDs that should be visible in the view. If not provided, the default visible fields will be used.|
|» sort_by|body|[[integer \| string]]|false|Sorting configuration for the view. Each element is a two-element array of `[field_id, direction]` where `direction` is `"asc"` or `"desc"`. Supports multiple sort criteria applied in order.|
|» group_by|body|[integer]|false|The field IDs to group items by (horizontal grouping). Supports a single field. The field must support grouping; fields such as `Title`, `Reviewers`, `Linked pull requests`, `Sub-issues progress`, `Tracked by`, and `Tracks` cannot be grouped on.|
|» vertical_group_by|body|[integer]|false|The field IDs to use as columns in `board` layout (vertical grouping). Supports a single field. The field must support grouping; fields such as `Title`, `Reviewers`, `Linked pull requests`, `Sub-issues progress`, `Tracked by`, and `Tracks` cannot be grouped on.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» layout|table|
|» layout|board|
|» layout|roadmap|

`POST /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/fields`

Add a field to a specified user owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/fields#add-field-to-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Team notes",
  "data_type": "text"
}
```

<h3 id="add-field-to-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» single_select_options|body|[[projects-v2-field-single-select-option](#schemaprojects-v2-field-single-select-option)]|true|The options available for single select fields. At least one option must be provided when creating a single select field.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the field.|
|» data_type|body|string|true|The field's data type.|
|» iteration_configuration|body|[projects-v2-field-iteration-configuration](#schemaprojects-v2-field-iteration-configuration)|true|The configuration for iteration fields.|

|Parameter|Value|

## List items for a user owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/list-items-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items`

List all items for a specific user-owned project accessible by the authenticated user.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#list-items-for-a-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-items-for-a-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|q|query|string|false|Search query to filter items, see [Filtering projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/filtering-projects) for more information.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: `fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789` or `fields=123,456,789`|

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<h3 id="list-items-for-a-user-owned-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[projects-v2-item-with-content](#schemaprojects-v2-item-with-content)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add item to user owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/add-item-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "type": "Issue",
    "id": 3
  }'
```

`POST /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items`

Add an issue or pull request item to the specified user owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#add-item-to-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "Issue",
  "id": 3
}
```

<h3 id="add-item-to-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|body|body|object|true|Details of the item to add to the project. You can specify either the unique ID or the repository owner, name, and issue/PR number.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of item to add to the project. Must be either Issue or PullRequest.|
|» id|body|integer|false|The unique identifier of the issue or pull request to add to the project.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The repository owner login.|
|» repo|body|string|false|The repository name.|
|» number|body|integer|false|The issue or pull request number.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|Issue|
|» type|PullRequest|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/components/examples/projects-v2-item-simple"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "documentation_url": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-item-to-user-owned-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response|[projects-v2-item-simple](#schemaprojects-v2-item-simple)|
|304|Not Modified|Not modified|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Requires authentication|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[basic-error](#schemabasic-error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get an item for a user owned project

<a id="opIdprojects/get-user-item"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/items/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Get a specific item from a user-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#get-an-item-for-a-user-owned-project">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-item-for-a-user-owned-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789 or fields=123,456,789|

`DELETE /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Delete a specific item from a user-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#delete-project-item-for-user">API method documentation</a>

|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|

## Update project item for user

<a id="opIdprojects/update-item-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/items/0 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "id": 123,
        "value": "Updated text value"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/items/{item_id}`

Update a specific item in a user-owned project.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#update-project-item-for-user">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "id": 123,
      "value": "Updated text value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-project-item-for-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|item_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the project item.|
|body|body|object|true|Field updates to apply to the project item. Only text, number, date, single select, and iteration fields are supported.|
|» fields|body|[object]|true|A list of field updates to apply.|
|» » id|body|integer|true|The ID of the project field to update.|
|» » value|body|null \| string \| number|true|The new value for the field:<br>- For text, number, and date fields, provide the new value directly.<br>- For single select and iteration fields, provide the ID of the option or iteration.<br>- To clear the field, set this to null.|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|

> Example responses

## List items for a user project view

<a id="opIdprojects/list-view-items-for-user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/users/string/projectsV2/0/views/0/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{username}/projectsV2/{project_number}/views/{view_number}/items`

List items in a user project with the saved view's filter applied.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/projects/items#list-items-for-a-user-project-view">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-items-for-a-user-project-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_number|path|integer|true|The project's number.|
|username|path|string|true|The handle for the GitHub user account.|
|view_number|path|integer|true|The number that identifies the project view.|
|fields|query|string \| [string]|false|Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the<br>title field will be returned.<br><br>Example: `fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789` or `fields=123,456,789`|
|before|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|after|query|string|false|A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-agent-automations">agent-automations</h1>

Endpoints to manage and interact with agent automations.

## List automations for user

<a id="opIdagent-automations/list-automations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/automations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/automations`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists automations created by the authenticated user across repositories they can read.
This includes both personal and shared automations created by the caller, but excludes
shared automations created by another user.

Use the repository-scoped list operation for those automations. The `type` filter
only narrows this creator-scoped collection.

To call this endpoint, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List automations for user"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#list-automations-for-user">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-automations-for-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|type|query|string|false|Filter automations by type. `personal` returns automations owned by their creator, `shared` returns automations owned by the repository. Omit to return both.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|personal|
|type|shared|

## List automations for a repository

<a id="opIdagent-automations/list-repo-automations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a paginated list of automations for a repository, including shared
automations and personal automations created by the caller.
`total_count` is the number of caller-visible automations matching the supplied
filters across all pages. Use the `type` field to distinguish personal and shared
automations.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (read). Personal automations require a user token.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List automations for a repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#list-automations-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-automations-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|type|query|string|false|Filter automations by type. `personal` returns automations owned by their creator, `shared` returns automations owned by the repository. Omit to return both.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|personal|
|type|shared|
