<h3 id="list-automations-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Automations retrieved successfully|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication required|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|Inline|

<h3 id="list-automations-for-a-repository-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automations|[object]|true|none|List of automations in the repository|
|» id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the automation.|
|» enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the automation is currently enabled.|
|» type|string|false|read-only|The type of automation. `personal` keeps it private to its creator and its runs act as that user. `shared` makes it belong to the repository, visible to anyone with read access to the repository, and its runs act as the Copilot app rather than as a person.|
|» require_actor_write_permission|boolean|false|none|When true, event-triggered runs require the event actor to have repo write permission, even when the org's allow_read_access_triggers policy is enabled. Does not apply to interval-scheduled runs, which always run as the automation owner.|
|» model|string|false|none|The model override for sessions triggered by this automation. Absent when the platform selects the model.|
|» reasoning_effort|string|false|none|The reasoning effort override for sessions triggered by this automation. Absent when the model's default is used.|
|» triggers|object|false|none|Trigger configuration for the automation.|
|» » interval|object|false|none|none|
|» » » cadence|[string]|true|none|One or more schedules on which the Automation runs.|
|» » » hour_utc|integer|false|none|UTC hour anchor (0 through 23) for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0` (midnight UTC).|
|» » » day_of_week|integer|false|none|UTC weekday anchor for weekly schedules, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday. Omitted weekly values default to Monday (`1`).|
|» » » minute_utc|integer|false|none|UTC minute anchor for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0`. Must be omitted whenever `cadence` includes `hourly`.|
|» » » write_scope|string|false|none|Has no effect: scheduled runs can change any resource in the repository, and an organization or repository policy requiring trigger-scoped writes does not apply to them.|
|» » » allow_copilot_triggers|boolean|false|none|When true, events Copilot creates, including from other automations and Copilot sessions, can start this automation through this trigger. Defaults to false. The Copilot coding agent app cannot turn it on: creating a trigger with true, or changing it from false to true, returns 422.|

## Create an automation for a repository

<a id="opIdagent-automations/create-repo-automation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Issue triage",
    "type": "personal",
    "triggers": {
      "issue_opened": {
        "query": "is:open"
      }
    },
    "prompt": "Inspect the new issue and suggest labels, priority, and next steps.",
    "tools": [
      "github/get_file_contents",
      "github/issue_read"
    ],
    "model": "gpt-6-sol",
    "reasoning_effort": "high"
  }'
```

`POST /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Creates a new automation in a repository. Personal automations are private to
their creator. Shared automations are visible to anyone with read access to
the repository and manageable by anyone with write access to the repository.

GitHub App installation access tokens can create shared automations by setting
`type` to `shared`. The installation must belong to the repository owner and
the token must have "Agent tasks"
repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.
For installation tokens, `created_by` identifies the App's bot account.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the
"Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Create an automation for a repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#create-an-automation-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Issue triage",
  "type": "personal",
  "triggers": {
    "issue_opened": {
      "query": "is:open"
    }
  },
  "prompt": "Inspect the new issue and suggest labels, priority, and next steps.",
  "tools": [
    "github/get_file_contents",
    "github/issue_read"
  ],
  "model": "gpt-6-sol",
  "reasoning_effort": "high"
}
```

```json
  "name": "Issue triage",
  "enabled": true,
  "type": "personal",
  "require_actor_write_permission": false,
  "triggers": {
    "issue_opened": {
      "query": "is:open"
    }
  },
  "prompt": "Inspect the new issue and suggest labels, priority, and next steps.",
  "tools": [
    "github/get_file_contents",
    "github/issue_read"
  ],
  "model": "gpt-6-sol",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "created_at": "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-05-01T12:00:00Z",

    "id": 123
  }
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-automation-for-a-repository-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Automation created successfully|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication required|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Insufficient permissions|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Failed|Inline|

<h3 id="create-an-automation-for-a-repository-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the automation.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the automation is currently enabled.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of automation. `personal` keeps it private to its creator and its runs act as that user. `shared` makes it belong to the repository, visible to anyone with read access to the repository, and its runs act as the Copilot app rather than as a person.|
|require_actor_write_permission|boolean|false|none|When true, event-triggered runs require the event actor to have repo write permission, even when the org's allow_read_access_triggers policy is enabled. Does not apply to interval-scheduled runs, which always run as the automation owner.|
|continuous_history|boolean|false|none|When true, runs of this automation build on the session history of its previous runs, and runs of the same automation are serialized. Not tracked in revision history.|
|triggers|object|false|none|Trigger configuration for the automation.|
|» interval|object|false|none|none|
|» » cadence|[string]|true|none|One or more schedules on which the Automation runs.|
|» » hour_utc|integer|false|none|UTC hour anchor (0 through 23) for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0` (midnight UTC).|
|» » day_of_week|integer|false|none|UTC weekday anchor for weekly schedules, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday. Omitted weekly values default to Monday (`1`).|
|» » minute_utc|integer|false|none|UTC minute anchor for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0`. Must be omitted whenever `cadence` includes `hourly`.|
|» » write_scope|string|false|none|Has no effect: scheduled runs can change any resource in the repository, and an organization or repository policy requiring trigger-scoped writes does not apply to them.|

## List available automation tools for a repository

<a id="opIdagent-automations/list-available-repo-automation-tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/available-tools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/available-tools`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists available tools for automations in a repository, including both
GitHub-provided tools and tools provided by custom MCP servers.

GitHub-provided tools are returned in named groups, with a name and
description provided for each tool.

MCP entries describe configured tool selection, not live discovery or runtime
availability. An explicit allowlist is returned in `tools`, with each `id` in
`<server-name>/<tool-name>` format, for example `sentry/list_issues`. An allowlist of
`["*"]` is returned as `supports_wildcard: true` with an empty `tools` array. Server URLs,
authentication headers, environment variables, and credentials are never returned.

For MCP tools, a list of configured MCP servers is provided, along with
the tools allowlisted for each server. Where `supports_wildcard` is true,
any tool that exists on the server can be used.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list available automation tools.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (read).

To call this endpoint, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List available automation tools for a repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#list-available-automation-tools-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-available-automation-tools-for-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|

```json
        }
      ],

    },

      "tools": [],
      "supports_wildcard": true
    }

}
```

## List available automation triggers for a repository

<a id="opIdagent-automations/list-available-repo-automation-triggers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/available-triggers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/available-triggers`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Lists available triggers for automations in a repository.

Each available trigger includes a title and description that can be presented
in user interfaces, plus a machine-readable schema of filters supported by the
trigger.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list available automation triggers.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (read).

To call this endpoint, OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List available automation triggers for a repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#list-available-automation-triggers-for-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

## Get an automation

<a id="opIdagent-automations/get-repo-automation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/{automation_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Fetches a repository automation by ID. The automation must be a personal
automation belonging to you or a shared automation.

Shared automations are visible to anyone with read access to the repository.
The `created_by` field identifies the creator and is distinct from the automation's
`type`.

GitHub App installation access tokens can access shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (read). Personal automations require a user token.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Get an automation"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#get-an-automation">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="get-an-automation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|automation_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the automation.|

<h3 id="get-an-automation-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the automation.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the automation is currently enabled.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of automation. `personal` keeps it private to its creator and its runs act as that user. `shared` makes it belong to the repository, visible to anyone with read access to the repository, and its runs act as the Copilot app rather than as a person.|
|require_actor_write_permission|boolean|false|none|When true, event-triggered runs require the event actor to have repo write permission, even when the org's allow_read_access_triggers policy is enabled. Does not apply to interval-scheduled runs, which always run as the automation owner.|
|continuous_history|boolean|false|none|When true, runs of this automation build on the session history of its previous runs, and runs of the same automation are serialized. Not tracked in revision history.|
|triggers|object|false|none|Trigger configuration for the automation.|
|» interval|object|false|none|none|
|» » cadence|[string]|true|none|One or more schedules on which the Automation runs.|
|» » hour_utc|integer|false|none|UTC hour anchor (0 through 23) for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0` (midnight UTC).|
|» » day_of_week|integer|false|none|UTC weekday anchor for weekly schedules, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday. Omitted weekly values default to Monday (`1`).|
|» » minute_utc|integer|false|none|UTC minute anchor for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0`. Must be omitted whenever `cadence` includes `hourly`.|

## Delete an automation

<a id="opIdagent-automations/delete-repo-automation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/{automation_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Deletes an automation in a repository. The automation must be a personal
automation belonging to you or a shared automation.

GitHub App installation access tokens can delete shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the
"Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Delete an automation"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#delete-an-automation">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="delete-an-automation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|automation_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the automation.|

```json
    }
  ],
```

```json
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "message": "string",

      "code": "missing",

    }
  ],

}
```

## Update an automation

<a id="opIdagent-automations/edit-repo-automation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "Issue triage and prioritization",
    "enabled": true,
    "model": "gpt-5.4",
    "reasoning_effort": "high",
    "triggers": {
      "issue_opened": {
        "query": "is:open label:auto-triage"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/{automation_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Updates an existing automation in a repository. The automation
must be a personal automation belonging to you or a shared automation.
Omitted fields are left unchanged. The automation's `type` is immutable.

GitHub App installation access tokens can update shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository and the
"Allow automations" setting must be enabled for the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Update an automation"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#update-an-automation">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Issue triage and prioritization",
  "enabled": true,
  "model": "gpt-5.4",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "triggers": {
    "issue_opened": {
      "query": "is:open label:auto-triage"
    }
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|automation_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|body|body|object|true|The automation fields to update. Omitted fields are left unchanged.|

<h3 id="update-an-automation-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Automation updated successfully|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication required|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Resource not found|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Validation Failed|Inline|

<h3 id="update-an-automation-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the automation.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the automation is currently enabled.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of automation. `personal` keeps it private to its creator and its runs act as that user. `shared` makes it belong to the repository, visible to anyone with read access to the repository, and its runs act as the Copilot app rather than as a person.|
|require_actor_write_permission|boolean|false|none|When true, event-triggered runs require the event actor to have repo write permission, even when the org's allow_read_access_triggers policy is enabled. Does not apply to interval-scheduled runs, which always run as the automation owner.|
|continuous_history|boolean|false|none|When true, runs of this automation build on the session history of its previous runs, and runs of the same automation are serialized. Not tracked in revision history.|
|triggers|object|false|none|Trigger configuration for the automation.|
|» interval|object|false|none|none|
|» » cadence|[string]|true|none|One or more schedules on which the Automation runs.|
|» » hour_utc|integer|false|none|UTC hour anchor (0 through 23) for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0` (midnight UTC).|
|» » day_of_week|integer|false|none|UTC weekday anchor for weekly schedules, where `0` is Sunday and `6` is Saturday. Omitted weekly values default to Monday (`1`).|
|» » minute_utc|integer|false|none|UTC minute anchor for daily and weekly schedules. Omitted daily and weekly values default to `0`. Must be omitted whenever `cadence` includes `hourly`.|
|» » write_scope|string|false|none|Has no effect: scheduled runs can change any resource in the repository, and an organization or repository policy requiring trigger-scoped writes does not apply to them.|

## List tasks for an automation in a repository

<a id="opIdagent-automations/list-repo-automation-tasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/string/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/{automation_id}/tasks`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a paginated list of tasks created by an automation in the specified
repository. The automation must belong to that exact repository.

User-owned automation history is visible only to the automation's creator.
Repository-owned automation history is visible to callers with read access to
repository automations. Deleted and unlisted tasks are excluded. Tasks produced
by private-session agents are excluded unless the caller created the task, is a
task collaborator, or the task is shared.

A missing repository, an inaccessible repository, or an automation that does not
belong to the specified repository returns `404` without revealing which condition
occurred.

GitHub App installation access tokens can list tasks for shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (read). Personal automations require a user token.

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List tasks for an automation in a repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#list-tasks-for-an-automation-in-a-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-tasks-for-an-automation-in-a-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|automation_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort results by. Can be `updated_at` or `created_at`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results. Can be `asc` or `desc`.|
|state|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of task states to filter by. Can be any combination of: `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `idle`, `waiting_for_user`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`.|
|is_archived|query|boolean|false|Filter by archived status. When `true`, returns only archived tasks. When `false` or omitted, returns only non-archived tasks. Defaults to `false`.|

## Run an automation

<a id="opIdagent-automations/create-repo-automation-task"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/automations/string/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "event": "manual",
    "context": "New Sentry issue detected: https://contoso.sentry.io/issues/7796648726"
  }'
```

`POST /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/automations/{automation_id}/tasks`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Runs an automation in a repository. Set `event` to `manual` and optionally include
`context` of up to 10,000 characters, which will be injected into the automation's
prompt.

The repository must have the "Allow automations" setting enabled, and the automation
must be a personal automation belonging to you or a shared automation.

GitHub App installation access tokens can run shared automations.
The installation must belong to the repository owner and the token must have
"Agent tasks" repository permissions (write). Personal automations require a user token.

A successful response accepts the run request and includes a preallocated
`task_id`, which can be fetched with the "Get a task by repo" Agent tasks API.
It does not confirm execution or task creation. Task creation is asynchronous,
so fetching the task immediately may return `404 Not Found`, and downstream
skips or failures can prevent its creation.

To call this endpoint, you must have write access to the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need:

* the `repo` scope for private or internal repositories
* the `repo` scope or `public_repo` scope for public repositories

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Run an automation"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [GitHub App installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (write)


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-automations/agent-automations#run-an-automation">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event": "manual",
  "context": "New Sentry issue detected: https://contoso.sentry.io/issues/7796648726"
}
```

<h3 id="run-an-automation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|automation_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the automation.|
|body|body|object|true|Configuration for the automation run.|
|» event|body|string|true|The event to trigger. Only `manual` is supported.|
|» context|body|string|false|Additional context for this automation run, up to 10,000 characters. Supported only when `event` is `manual`. The context supplements the automation's configured instructions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event|manual|

```json
  "event": "manual"
```

## Get Agent Merge configuration for a pull request

<a id="opIdagent-merge/get-agent-merge-enrollment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/pulls/42/agent-merge \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/agent-merge`

Gets the Agent Merge configuration for a pull request.

You must have write access to the repository.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the repo scope for private or internal repositories, or the public_repo scope for public repositories.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/agent-merge#get-agent-merge-configuration-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

## Update Agent Merge configuration for a pull request

<a id="opIdagent-merge/put-agent-merge-enrollment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/pulls/42/agent-merge \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "allowed_actions": [
      "fix_ci"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/agent-merge`

Updates the Agent Merge configuration for a pull request, enabling Agent Merge
or changing the allowed actions that Copilot is allowed to take on the pull
request.

If Agent Merge is currently enabled for the pull request, only the user
who most recently enabled it may change its allowed actions.

If enrollment eligibility cannot be determined, the operation returns `503`.

This endpoint is only available to users with a Copilot subscription,
excluding Copilot Free users. You must have write access to the repository,
the pull request must not be from a fork or part of a stack, and the repository
must have the "Allow automations" setting enabled.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the repo scope for private or internal repositories, or the public_repo scope for public repositories.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/agent-merge#update-agent-merge-configuration-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allowed_actions": [
    "fix_ci"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-agent-merge-configuration-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer(int64)|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|
|body|body|object|true|The Agent Merge enrollment configuration|
|» allowed_actions|body|[string]|true|The set of actions that Copilot may perform on the pull request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» allowed_actions|fix_ci|
|» allowed_actions|resolve_merge_conflicts|

## Disable Agent Merge for a pull request

<a id="opIdagent-merge/delete-agent-merge-enrollment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/pulls/42/agent-merge \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/agent-merge`

Disables Agent Merge for a pull request.

You must have write access to the repository. Disabling does not require
enrollment eligibility: your Copilot subscription, coding-agent and Automations
policies, the Agent Merge execution flag, pull request state, stack membership,
and repository archive state do not prevent cleanup. Authentication, token
repository selection, and "Agent tasks" write permission remain required.

OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the repo scope for private or internal repositories, or the public_repo scope for public repositories.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/agent-merge#disable-agent-merge-for-a-pull-request">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="disable-agent-merge-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|pull_number|path|integer(int64)|true|The number that identifies the pull request.|

<h1 id="github-v3-rest-api-agent-tasks">agent-tasks</h1>

Endpoints to manage and interact with agent tasks.

## List tasks for repository

<a id="opIdagent-tasks/list-tasks-for-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tasks`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a list of tasks for a specific repository

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List tasks for repository"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-tasks/agent-tasks#list-tasks-for-repository">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-tasks-for-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort results by. Can be `updated_at` or `created_at`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results. Can be `asc` or `desc`.|
|state|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of task states to filter by. Can be any combination of: `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `idle`, `waiting_for_user`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`.|
|is_archived|query|boolean|false|Filter by archived status. When `true`, returns only archived tasks. When `false` or omitted, returns only non-archived tasks. Defaults to `false`.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show tasks updated at or after this time (ISO 8601 timestamp)|
|creator_id|query|[integer]|false|Filter tasks by creator user ID. Accepts one or more user IDs.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|updated_at|
|sort|created_at|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Start a task

<a id="opIdagent-tasks/create-task-in-repo"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "Fix the login button on the homepage",
    "base_ref": "main"
  }'
```

`POST /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tasks`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Starts a new Copilot cloud agent task for a repository.

This endpoint is only available to users with a Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise subscription.

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Start a task"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read and write)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-tasks/agent-tasks#start-a-task">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "prompt": "Fix the login button on the homepage",
  "base_ref": "main"
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|The task creation parameters, including the user's prompt and optional agent settings.|
|» prompt|body|string|true|The user's prompt for the agent|
|» model|body|string|false|The model to use for this task. The allowed models may change over time and depend on the user's GitHub Copilot plan and organization policies. Currently supported values: `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6`, `gpt-5.2-codex`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, `gpt-5.4`, `claude-sonnet-4.5`, `claude-opus-4.5`|
|» custom_agent|body|string|false|Optional identifier for a custom agent to use for this task. Use the custom agent's filename without the extension - for example, for a `.github/agents/performance-optimizer.agent.md` custom agent, use `performance-optimizer`.|
|» create_pull_request|body|boolean|false|Whether to create a PR.|
|» base_ref|body|string|false|Base ref for new branch/PR|
|» head_ref|body|string|false|Head ref for existing branch/PR. If provided with `base_ref`, the agent looks up open PR context for `head_ref` targeting `base_ref` and commits to `head_ref` instead of creating a new branch.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
```

## Get a task by repo

<a id="opIdagent-tasks/get-task-by-repo-and-id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/repos/string/string/tasks/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tasks/{task_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a task by ID scoped to an owner/repo path

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Get a task by repo"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-tasks/agent-tasks#get-a-task-by-repo">API method documentation</a>

|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|task_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the task.|

## List tasks

<a id="opIdagent-tasks/list-tasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/tasks`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a list of tasks for the authenticated user

**Fine-grained access tokens for "List tasks"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)
* [Fine-grained personal access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens#creating-a-fine-grained-personal-access-token)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agent-tasks/agent-tasks#list-tasks">API method documentation</a>

<h3 id="list-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of results per page (max 100).|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the results to fetch.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort results by. Can be `updated_at` or `created_at`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results. Can be `asc` or `desc`.|
|state|query|string|false|Comma-separated list of task states to filter by. Can be any combination of: `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `idle`, `waiting_for_user`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`.|
|is_archived|query|boolean|false|Filter by archived status. When `true`, returns only archived tasks. When `false` or omitted, returns only non-archived tasks. Defaults to `false`.|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Only show tasks updated at or after this time (ISO 8601 timestamp)|

|---|---|
|sort|updated_at|
|sort|created_at|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

## Get a task by ID

<a id="opIdagent-tasks/get-task-by-id"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/agents/tasks/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /agents/tasks/{task_id}`

> [!NOTE]
> This endpoint is in public preview and is subject to change.

Returns a task by ID with its associated sessions

**Fine-grained access tokens for "Get a task by ID"**

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

* [GitHub App user access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-a-user-access-token-for-a-github-app)

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

* "Agent tasks" repository permissions (read)

GitHub App installation access tokens are not supported for this endpoint.

## List organization secrets

<a id="opIdagents/list-org-secrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/agents/secrets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets`

Lists all secrets available in an organization without revealing their
encrypted values.

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

## Create or update an organization secret

<a id="opIdagents/create-or-update-org-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/agents/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678",
    "visibility": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      1296269,
      1296280
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates an organization secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint. If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#create-or-update-an-organization-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    1296269,
    1296280
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-organization-secret-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|true|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get an organization public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#get-an-organization-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|Which type of organization repositories have access to the organization secret. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the secret.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository ids that can access the organization secret. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#list-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-an-organization-secret-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create an organization variable

<a id="opIdagents/create-org-variable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/orgs/string/agents/variables \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "USERNAME",
    "value": "octocat",
    "visibility": "selected",
    "selected_repository_ids": [
      1296269,
      1296280
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /orgs/{org}/agents/variables`

Creates an organization agent variable that you can reference in a GitHub Actions workflow.

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read variables.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `admin:org` scope to use this endpoint. If the repository is private, OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/variables#create-an-organization-variable">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "USERNAME",
  "value": "octocat",
  "visibility": "selected",
  "selected_repository_ids": [
    1296269,
    1296280
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-variable-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|org|path|string|true|The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the variable.|
|» value|body|string|true|The value of the variable.|
|» visibility|body|string|true|The type of repositories in the organization that can access the variable. `selected` means only the repositories specified by `selected_repository_ids` can access the variable.|
|» selected_repository_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of repository ids that can access the organization variable. You can only provide a list of repository ids when the `visibility` is set to `selected`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility|all|
|» visibility|private|
|» visibility|selected|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-variable-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a variable|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Create or update a repository secret

<a id="opIdagents/create-or-update-repo-secret"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.github.com/repos/string/string/agents/secrets/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
    "key_id": "012345678912345678"
  }'
```

`PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/agents/secrets/{secret_name}`

Creates or updates a repository secret with an encrypted value. Encrypt your secret using
[LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages). For more information, see "[Encrypting secrets for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/encrypting-secrets-for-the-rest-api)."

Authenticated users must have collaborator access to a repository to create, update, or read secrets.

OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `repo` scope to use this endpoint.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#create-or-update-a-repository-secret">API method documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "encrypted_value": "c2VjcmV0",
  "key_id": "012345678912345678"
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|owner|path|string|true|The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.|
|repo|path|string|true|The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.|
|secret_name|path|string|true|The name of the secret.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_value|body|string|true|Value for your secret, encrypted with [LibSodium](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc/bindings_for_other_languages) using the public key retrieved from the [Get a repository public key](https://docs.github.com/rest/agents/secrets#get-a-repository-public-key) endpoint.|
|» key_id|body|string|true|ID of the key you used to encrypt the secret.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
null
```

<h3 id="create-or-update-a-repository-secret-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Response when creating a secret|[empty-object](#schemaempty-object)|
|204|No Content|Response when updating a secret|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is a change to branch protection configurations for a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About protected branches](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/about-protected-branches).&quot; For information about using the APIs to manage branch protection rules, see &quot;[Branch protection rule](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#branchprotectionrule)&quot; in the GraphQL documentation or &quot;[Branch protection](https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branch-protection)&quot; in the REST API documentation. </aside>

## This event occurs when there is a change to branch protection configurations for a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About protected branches](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/about-protected-branches).&quot; For information about using the APIs to manage branch protection rules, see &quot;[Branch protection rule](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#branchprotectionrule)&quot; in the GraphQL documentation or &quot;[Branch protection](https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branch-protection)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdbranch-protection-configuration/enabled"></a>

`POST branch-protection-configuration-enabled`

All branch protections were enabled for a repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#branch_protection_configuration">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to branch protection rules. For more information, see &quot;[About protected branches](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/about-protected-branches).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage branch protection rules, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#branchprotectionrule) or &quot;[Branch protection](https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branch-protection)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdbranch-protection-rule/created"></a>

`POST branch-protection-rule-created`

A branch protection rule was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#branch_protection_rule">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to branch protection rules. For more information, see &quot;[About protected branches](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/about-protected-branches).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage branch protection rules, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#branchprotectionrule) or &quot;[Branch protection](https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branch-protection)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdbranch-protection-rule/deleted"></a>

`POST branch-protection-rule-deleted`

A branch protection rule was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#branch_protection_rule">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to branch protection rules. For more information, see &quot;[About protected branches](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/defining-the-mergeability-of-pull-requests/about-protected-branches).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage branch protection rules, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#branchprotectionrule) or &quot;[Branch protection](https://docs.github.com/rest/branches/branch-protection)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdbranch-protection-rule/edited"></a>

`POST branch-protection-rule-edited`

A branch protection rule was edited.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check run. For information about check runs, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check runs, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checkrun) or &quot;[Check Runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check suites, use the `check-suite` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; repository permission. To receive the `rerequested` and `requested_action` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `created` and `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check run was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-run/completed"></a>

`POST check-run-completed`

A check run was completed, and a conclusion is available.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_run">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check run. For information about check runs, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check runs, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checkrun) or &quot;[Check Runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check suites, use the `check-suite` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; repository permission. To receive the `rerequested` and `requested_action` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `created` and `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check run was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-run/created"></a>

`POST check-run-created`

A new check run was created.

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check run. For information about check runs, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check runs, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checkrun) or &quot;[Check Runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check suites, use the `check-suite` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; repository permission. To receive the `rerequested` and `requested_action` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `created` and `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check run was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-run/requested-action"></a>

`POST check-run-requested-action`

A check run completed, and someone requested a followup action that your app provides. Only the GitHub App someone requests to perform an action will receive the `requested_action` payload. For more information, see "[Creating CI tests with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/guides/creating-ci-tests-with-the-checks-api)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_run">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check run. For information about check runs, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check runs, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checkrun) or &quot;[Check Runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check suites, use the `check-suite` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; repository permission. To receive the `rerequested` and `requested_action` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `created` and `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check run was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-run/rerequested"></a>

`POST check-run-rerequested`

Someone requested to re-run a check run. Only the GitHub App that someone requests to re-run the check will receive the `rerequested` payload.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_run">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check suite. For information about check suites, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check suites, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checksuite) or &quot;[Check Suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check runs, use the `check_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. To receive the `requested` and `rerequested` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-suite/completed"></a>

`POST check-suite-completed`

All check runs in a check suite have completed, and a conclusion is available.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_suite">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-check-suite-for-information-about-check-suites-see-getting-started-with-the-checks-apihttpsdocsgithubcomrestguidesgetting-started-with-the-checks-api-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-check-suites-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectschecksuite-or-check-suiteshttpsdocsgithubcomrestcheckssuites-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-check-runs-use-the-checkrun-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-to-receive-the-requested-and-rerequested-event-types-the-app-must-have-at-least-write-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-github-apps-with-write-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-are-automatically-subscribed-to-this-webhook-event-repository-and-organization-webhooks-only-receive-payloads-for-the-completed-event-types-in-repositories-note-the-api-only-looks-for-pushes-in-the-repository-where-the-check-suite-was-created-pushes-to-a-branch-in-a-forked-repository-are-not-detected-and-return-an-empty-pullrequests-array-and-a-null-value-for-headbranch-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check suite. For information about check suites, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check suites, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checksuite) or &quot;[Check Suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check runs, use the `check_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. To receive the `requested` and `rerequested` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-suite/requested"></a>

`POST check-suite-requested`

Someone requested to run a check suite. By default, check suites are automatically created when you create a check run. For more information, see [the GraphQL API documentation for creating a check run](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/mutations#createcheckrun) or "[Create a check run](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/runs#create-a-check-run)" in the REST API documentation.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_suite">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-check-suite-for-information-about-check-suites-see-getting-started-with-the-checks-apihttpsdocsgithubcomrestguidesgetting-started-with-the-checks-api-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-check-suites-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectschecksuite-or-check-suiteshttpsdocsgithubcomrestcheckssuites-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-check-runs-use-the-checkrun-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-to-receive-the-requested-and-rerequested-event-types-the-app-must-have-at-least-write-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-github-apps-with-write-level-access-for-the-checks-permission-are-automatically-subscribed-to-this-webhook-event-repository-and-organization-webhooks-only-receive-payloads-for-the-completed-event-types-in-repositories-note-the-api-only-looks-for-pushes-in-the-repository-where-the-check-suite-was-created-pushes-to-a-branch-in-a-forked-repository-are-not-detected-and-return-an-empty-pullrequests-array-and-a-null-value-for-headbranch-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a check suite. For information about check suites, see &quot;[Getting started with the Checks API](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/getting-started-with-the-checks-api).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage check suites, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#checksuite) or &quot;[Check Suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to check runs, use the `check_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. To receive the `requested` and `rerequested` event types, the app must have at least write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission. GitHub Apps with write-level access for the &quot;Checks&quot; permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event. Repository and organization webhooks only receive payloads for the `completed` event types in repositories. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; The API only looks for pushes in the repository where the check suite was created. Pushes to a branch in a forked repository are not detected and return an empty `pull_requests` array and a `null` value for `head_branch`.

<a id="opIdcheck-suite/rerequested"></a>

`POST check-suite-rerequested`

Someone requested to re-run the check runs in a check suite. For more information, see [the GraphQL API documentation for creating a check suite](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/mutations#createchecksuite) or "[Create a check suite](https://docs.github.com/rest/checks/suites#create-a-check-suite)" in the REST API documentation.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#check_suite">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/appeared-in-branch"></a>

`POST code-scanning-alert-appeared-in-branch`

A previously created code scanning alert appeared in another branch. This can happen when a branch is merged into or created from a branch with a pre-existing code scanning alert.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#code_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/closed-by-user"></a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-code-scanning-alerts-in-a-repository-for-more-information-see-about-code-scanninghttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitycode-scanningautomatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errorsabout-code-scanning-and-about-code-scanning-alertshttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitycode-scanningautomatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errorsabout-code-scanning-alerts-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-code-scanning-see-code-scanninghttpsdocsgithubcomrestcode-scanning-in-the-rest-api-documentation-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-code-scanning-alerts-repository-permission-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/created"></a>
