<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-code-scanning-alerts-in-a-repository-for-more-information-see-about-code-scanninghttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitycode-scanningautomatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errorsabout-code-scanning-and-about-code-scanning-alertshttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitycode-scanningautomatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errorsabout-code-scanning-alerts-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-code-scanning-see-code-scanninghttpsdocsgithubcomrestcode-scanning-in-the-rest-api-documentation-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-code-scanning-alerts-repository-permission-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/fixed"></a>

`POST code-scanning-alert-fixed`

A code scanning alert was fixed in a branch by a commit.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#code_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/reopened"></a>

`POST code-scanning-alert-reopened`

A previously fixed code scanning alert reappeared in a branch.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#code_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

|» » state|body|string \| null|true|State of a code scanning alert. Events for alerts found outside the default branch will return a `null` value until they are dismissed or fixed.|

|» » » guid|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|true|The name of the tool used to generate the code scanning analysis alert.|
|» » » version|body|string \| null|true|The version of the tool used to detect the alert.|
|» » updated_at|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » url|body|string(uri)|true|none|
|» » dismissal_approved_by|body|null|false|none|
|» commit_oid|body|string \| null|true|The commit SHA of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» ref|body|string \| null|true|The Git reference of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcode-scanning-alert/reopened-by-user"></a>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to code scanning alerts in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[About code scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning)&quot; and &quot;[About code scanning alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/about-code-scanning-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage code scanning, see &quot;[Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/code-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Code scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to commit comments. For more information about commit comments, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage commit comments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#commitcomment) or &quot;[Commit comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to comments on pull request reviews, use the `pull_request_review_comment` event. For activity relating to issue comments, use the `issue_comment` event. For activity relating to discussion comments, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdcommit-comment/created"></a>

`POST commit-comment-created`

Someone commented on a commit.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#commit_comment">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when a Git branch or tag is created. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission. **Notes**: - This event will not occur when more than three tags are created at once. - Payloads are capped at 25 MB. If an event generates a larger payload, GitHub will not deliver a payload for that webhook event. This may happen, for example, if many branches or tags are pushed at once. We suggest monitoring your payload size to ensure delivery.

<a id="opIdcreate"></a>

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#create">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-a-git-branch-or-tag-is-created-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-contents-repository-permission-notes---this-event-will-not-occur-when-more-than-three-tags-are-created-at-once---payloads-are-capped-at-25-mb-if-an-event-generates-a-larger-payload-github-will-not-deliver-a-payload-for-that-webhook-event-this-may-happen-for-example-if-many-branches-or-tags-are-pushed-at-once-we-suggest-monitoring-your-payload-size-to-ensure-delivery-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-create](#schemawebhook-create)|true|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|true|The repository's current description.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» master_branch|body|string|true|The name of the repository's default branch (usually `main`).|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» pusher_type|body|[webhooks_deploy_pusher_type](#schemawebhooks_deploy_pusher_type)|true|The pusher type for the event. Can be either `user` or a deploy key.|
|» ref|body|[webhooks_ref_0](#schemawebhooks_ref_0)|true|The [`git ref`](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#get-a-reference) resource.|
|» ref_type|body|string|true|The type of Git ref object created in the repository.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ref_type|tag|
|» ref_type|branch|

For more information, see &quot;[Managing custom properties for repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-custom-properties-for-repositories-in-your-organization)&quot;. For information about the APIs to manage custom properties, see &quot;[Custom properties](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/custom-properties)&quot; in the REST API documentation. ## This event occurs when a Git branch or tag is deleted. To subscribe to all pushes to a repository, including branch and tag deletions, use the [`push`](#push) webhook event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; This event will not occur when more than three tags are deleted at once.

<a id="opIddelete"></a>

`POST delete`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#delete">External documentation</a>

|body|body|[webhook-delete](#schemawebhook-delete)|true|none|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/assignees-changed"></a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/auto-dismissed"></a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/auto-reopened"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-auto-reopened`

A Dependabot alert, that had been automatically closed by a Dependabot auto-triage rule, was automatically reopened because the alert metadata or rule changed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/created"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-created`

A manifest file change introduced a vulnerable dependency, or a GitHub Security Advisory was published and an existing dependency was found to be vulnerable.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#dependabot_alert">External documentation</a>

Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|

|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/dismissed"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-dismissed`

A Dependabot alert was manually closed.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-dependabot-alert-dismissed](#schemawebhook-dependabot-alert-dismissed)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» alert|body|[dependabot-alert](#schemadependabot-alert)|true|A Dependabot alert.|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|dismissed|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/fixed"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-fixed`

A manifest file change removed a vulnerability.

|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|

|body|body|[webhook-dependabot-alert-fixed](#schemawebhook-dependabot-alert-fixed)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|

|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/reintroduced"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-reintroduced`

A manifest file change introduced a vulnerable dependency that had previously been fixed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#dependabot_alert">External documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-dependabot-alert-reintroduced](#schemawebhook-dependabot-alert-reintroduced)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|

|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|reintroduced|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/reopened"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-reopened`

A Dependabot alert was manually reopened.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to Dependabot alerts. For more information about Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot; For information about the API to manage Dependabot alerts, see &quot;[Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/rest/dependabot/alerts)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Dependabot alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddependabot-alert/withdrawn"></a>

`POST dependabot-alert-withdrawn`

A Dependabot alert was withdrawn because the advisory or the vulnerable version
range that produced it is no longer valid. The alert contains identifiers
captured before deletion for matching external records, rather than the full
alert payload used by other actions. Its alert URLs identify the deleted alert
and may no longer resolve.


<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#dependabot_alert">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-dependabot-alert-withdrawn](#schemawebhook-dependabot-alert-withdrawn)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» alert|body|[dependabot-alert-withdrawn-webhook](#schemadependabot-alert-withdrawn-webhook)|true|Identifiers for a withdrawn Dependabot alert, captured before deletion so that<br>consumers can reconcile external records. This is not a full alert representation.<br>|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|withdrawn|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deploy keys. For more information, see &quot;[Managing deploy keys](https://docs.github.com/developers/overview/managing-deploy-keys).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deploy keys, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deploykey) or &quot;[Deploy keys](https://docs.github.com/rest/deploy-keys)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeploy-key/created"></a>

A deploy key was created.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deploy keys. For more information, see &quot;[Managing deploy keys](https://docs.github.com/developers/overview/managing-deploy-keys).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deploy keys, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deploykey) or &quot;[Deploy keys](https://docs.github.com/rest/deploy-keys)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeploy-key/deleted"></a>

`POST deploy-key-deleted`

A deploy key was deleted.

|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|deleted|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployments. For more information, see &quot;[About deployments](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/about-deployments).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deployments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deployment) or &quot;[Deployments](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to deployment status, use the `deployment_status` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeployment/created"></a>

`POST deployment-created`

A deployment was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployment protection rules. For more information, see &quot;[Using environments for deployment](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/targeting-different-environments/using-environments-for-deployment#environment-protection-rules).&quot; For information about the API to manage deployment protection rules, see [the REST API documentation](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/environments). To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeployment-protection-rule/requested"></a>

`POST deployment-protection-rule-requested`

A deployment protection rule was requested for an environment.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment_protection_rule">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-deployment-protection-rule-requested](#schemawebhook-deployment-protection-rule-requested)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|false|none|
|» environment|body|string|false|The name of the environment that has the deployment protection rule.|
|» event|body|string|false|The event that triggered the deployment protection rule.|
|» sha|body|string|false|The commit SHA that triggered the workflow. Always populated from the check suite, regardless of whether a deployment is created.|
|» ref|body|string|false|The ref (branch or tag) that triggered the workflow. Always populated from the check suite, regardless of whether a deployment is created.|
|» deployment_callback_url|body|string(uri)|false|The URL to review the deployment protection rule.|
|» deployment|body|null \| [deployment](#schemadeployment)|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|[deployment](#schemadeployment)|false|A request for a specific ref(branch,sha,tag) to be deployed|
|» pull_requests|body|[[pull-request](#schemapull-request)]|false|none|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|requested|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployment reviews. For more information, see &quot;[About deployments](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/about-deployments).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deployments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deployment) or &quot;[Deployments](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to deployment creation or deployment status, use the `deployment` or `deployment_status` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeployment-review/approved"></a>

`POST deployment-review-approved`

A deployment review was approved.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment_review">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployment reviews. For more information, see &quot;[About deployments](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/about-deployments).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deployments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deployment) or &quot;[Deployments](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to deployment creation or deployment status, use the `deployment` or `deployment_status` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeployment-review/rejected"></a>

`POST deployment-review-rejected`

A deployment review was rejected.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment_review">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployment reviews. For more information, see &quot;[About deployments](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/about-deployments).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deployments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deployment) or &quot;[Deployments](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to deployment creation or deployment status, use the `deployment` or `deployment_status` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIddeployment-review/requested"></a>

`POST deployment-review-requested`

A deployment review was requested.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment_review">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-deployment-reviews-for-more-information-see-about-deploymentshttpsdocsgithubcomactionsdeploymentabout-deployments-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-deployments-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsdeployment-or-deploymentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestdeploymentsdeployments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-deployment-creation-or-deployment-status-use-the-deployment-or-deploymentstatus-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-deployments-repository-permission-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to deployment statuses. For more information, see &quot;[About deployments](https://docs.github.com/actions/deployment/about-deployments).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage deployments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#deployment) or &quot;[Deployments](https://docs.github.com/rest/deployments/deployments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to deployment creation, use the `deployment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Deployments&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; A webhook event is not fired for deployment statuses with an `inactive` state.

<a id="opIddeployment-status/created"></a>

`POST deployment-status-created`

A new deployment status was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#deployment_status">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-deployment-statuses-for-more-information-see-about-deploymentshttpsdocsgithubcomactionsdeploymentabout-deployments-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-deployments-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsdeployment-or-deploymentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestdeploymentsdeployments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-deployment-creation-use-the-deployment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-deployments-repository-permission-note-a-webhook-event-is-not-fired-for-deployment-statuses-with-an-inactive-state-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/answered"></a>

`POST discussion-answered`

A comment on the discussion was marked as the answer.

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/category-changed"></a>

`POST discussion-category-changed`

The category of a discussion was changed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/closed"></a>

`POST discussion-closed`

A discussion was closed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a discussion as opposed to comments on a discussion, use the `discussion` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion-comment/created"></a>

`POST discussion-comment-created`

A comment on a discussion was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion_comment">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a discussion as opposed to comments on a discussion, use the `discussion` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion-comment/deleted"></a>

`POST discussion-comment-deleted`

A comment on a discussion was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion_comment">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a discussion as opposed to comments on a discussion, use the `discussion` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion-comment/edited"></a>

`POST discussion-comment-edited`

A comment on a discussion was edited.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion_comment">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-a-discussion-for-more-information-about-discussions-see-github-discussionshttpsdocsgithubcomdiscussions-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-discussions-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsdiscussion-for-activity-relating-to-a-discussion-as-opposed-to-comments-on-a-discussion-use-the-discussion-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-discussions-repository-permission-note-webhook-events-for-github-discussions-are-currently-in-public-preview-and-subject-to-change-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-discussion-comment-edited](#schemawebhook-discussion-comment-edited)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» changes|body|object|true|none|
|» » body|body|object|true|none|
|» » » from|body|string|true|none|
|» comment|body|[webhooks_comment](#schemawebhooks_comment)|true|none|
|» discussion|body|[discussion](#schemadiscussion)|true|A Discussion in a repository.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/created"></a>

`POST discussion-created`

A discussion was created.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/deleted"></a>

`POST discussion-deleted`

A discussion was deleted.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/edited"></a>

`POST discussion-edited`

The title or body on a discussion was edited, or the category of the discussion was changed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/labeled"></a>

`POST discussion-labeled`

A label was added to a discussion.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/locked"></a>

`POST discussion-locked`

A discussion was locked.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/pinned"></a>

`POST discussion-pinned`

A discussion was pinned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/reopened"></a>

`POST discussion-reopened`

A discussion was reopened.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/transferred"></a>

`POST discussion-transferred`

A discussion was transferred to another repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/unanswered"></a>

`POST discussion-unanswered`

A comment on the discussion was unmarked as the answer.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/unlabeled"></a>

`POST discussion-unlabeled`

A label was removed from a discussion.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/unlocked"></a>

`POST discussion-unlocked`

A discussion was unlocked.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a discussion. For more information about discussions, see &quot;[GitHub Discussions](https://docs.github.com/discussions).&quot; For information about the API to manage discussions, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#discussion). For activity relating to a comment on a discussion, use the `discussion_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Discussions&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for GitHub Discussions are currently in public preview and subject to change.

<a id="opIddiscussion/unpinned"></a>

`POST discussion-unpinned`

A discussion was unpinned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#discussion">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-discussion-unpinned](#schemawebhook-discussion-unpinned)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» discussion|body|[discussion](#schemadiscussion)|true|A Discussion in a repository.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|unpinned|

## This event occurs when someone forks a repository. For more information, see &quot;[Fork a repo](https://docs.github.com/get-started/quickstart/fork-a-repo).&quot; For information about the API to manage forks, see &quot;[Forks](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/forks)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

## This event occurs when a user revokes their authorization of a GitHub App. For more information, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the API to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation. A GitHub App receives this webhook by default and cannot unsubscribe from this event. Anyone can revoke their authorization of a GitHub App from their [GitHub account settings page](https://github.com/settings/apps/authorizations). Revoking the authorization of a GitHub App does not uninstall the GitHub App. You should program your GitHub App so that when it receives this webhook, it stops calling the API on behalf of the person who revoked the token. If your GitHub App continues to use a revoked access token, it will receive the `401 Bad Credentials` error. For details about requests with a user access token, which require GitHub App authorization, see &quot;[Authenticating with a GitHub App on behalf of a user](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/authenticating-with-a-github-app-on-behalf-of-a-user).&quot;

<a id="opIdgithub-app-authorization/revoked"></a>

`POST github-app-authorization-revoked`

Someone revoked their authorization of a GitHub App.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#github_app_authorization">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-someone-creates-or-updates-a-wiki-page-for-more-information-see-about-wikishttpsdocsgithubcomcommunitiesdocumenting-your-project-with-wikisabout-wikis-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-contents-repository-permission-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-gollum](#schemawebhook-gollum)|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» pages|body|[object]|true|The pages that were updated.|
|» » action|body|string|true|The action that was performed on the page. Can be `created` or `edited`.|
|» » html_url|body|string(uri)|true|Points to the HTML wiki page.|
|» » page_name|body|string|true|The name of the page.|
|» » sha|body|string|true|The latest commit SHA of the page.|
|» » summary|body|string \| null|true|none|
|» » title|body|string|true|The current page title.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub App installation. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-github-app-installation-all-github-apps-receive-this-event-by-default-you-cannot-manually-subscribe-to-this-event-for-more-information-about-github-apps-see-about-appshttpsdocsgithubcomdevelopersappsgetting-started-with-appsabout-appsabout-github-apps-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-github-apps-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsapp-or-appshttpsdocsgithubcomrestapps-in-the-rest-api-documentation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-installation-created](#schemawebhook-installation-created)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[installation](#schemainstallation)|true|Installation|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repositories|body|[webhooks_repositories](#schemawebhooks_repositories)|false|An array of repository objects that the installation can access.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» requester|body|[webhooks_user](#schemawebhooks_user)|false|none|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub App installation. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

|» requester|body|null|false|none|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|---|---|

|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» requester|body|null|false|none|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|new_permissions_accepted|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to which repositories a GitHub App installation can access. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to which repositories a GitHub App installation can access. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdinstallation-repositories/removed"></a>

`POST installation-repositories-removed`

Access to one or more repositories was revoked for a GitHub App installation.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#installation_repositories">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub App installation. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdinstallation/suspend"></a>

`POST installation-suspend`

Someone blocked access by a GitHub App to their user or organization account.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub App installation. All GitHub Apps receive this event by default. You cannot manually subscribe to this event. For more information about GitHub Apps, see &quot;[About apps](https://docs.github.com/developers/apps/getting-started-with-apps/about-apps#about-github-apps).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Apps, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#app) or &quot;[Apps](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdinstallation/unsuspend"></a>

`POST installation-unsuspend`

A GitHub App that was blocked from accessing a user or organization account was given access the account again.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#installation">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on an issue or pull request. For more information about issues and pull requests, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues)&quot; and &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issue comments, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issuecomment) or &quot;[Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to an issue as opposed to comments on an issue, use the `issue` event. For activity related to pull request reviews or pull request review comments, use the `pull_request_review` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. For more information about the different types of pull request comments, see &quot;[Working with comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/working-with-comments).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissue-comment/created"></a>

`POST issue-comment-created`

A comment on an issue or pull request was created.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on an issue or pull request. For more information about issues and pull requests, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues)&quot; and &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issue comments, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issuecomment) or &quot;[Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to an issue as opposed to comments on an issue, use the `issue` event. For activity related to pull request reviews or pull request review comments, use the `pull_request_review` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. For more information about the different types of pull request comments, see &quot;[Working with comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/working-with-comments).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissue-comment/deleted"></a>

`POST issue-comment-deleted`

A comment on an issue or pull request was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue_comment">External documentation</a>

This operation does not require authentication

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on an issue or pull request. For more information about issues and pull requests, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues)&quot; and &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issue comments, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issuecomment) or &quot;[Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to an issue as opposed to comments on an issue, use the `issue` event. For activity related to pull request reviews or pull request review comments, use the `pull_request_review` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. For more information about the different types of pull request comments, see &quot;[Working with comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/working-with-comments).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissue-comment/edited"></a>

`POST issue-comment-edited`

A comment on an issue or pull request was edited.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-or-pull-request-for-more-information-about-issues-and-pull-requests-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-and-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issue-comments-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissuecomment-or-issue-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissuescomments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-an-issue-as-opposed-to-comments-on-an-issue-use-the-issue-event-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-or-pull-request-review-comments-use-the-pullrequestreview-or-pullrequestreviewcomment-events-for-more-information-about-the-different-types-of-pull-request-comments-see-working-with-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestguidesworking-with-comments-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-issue-comment-edited](#schemawebhook-issue-comment-edited)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» changes|body|[webhooks_changes](#schemawebhooks_changes)|true|The changes to the comment.|
|» comment|body|[webhooks_issue_comment](#schemawebhooks_issue_comment)|true|The [comment](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#get-an-issue-comment) itself.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub.
