## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on an issue or pull request. For more information about issues and pull requests, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues)&quot; and &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issue comments, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issuecomment) or &quot;[Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to an issue as opposed to comments on an issue, use the `issue` event. For activity related to pull request reviews or pull request review comments, use the `pull_request_review` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. For more information about the different types of pull request comments, see &quot;[Working with comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/working-with-comments).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissue-comment/pinned"></a>

`POST issue-comment-pinned`

A comment on an issue was pinned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue_comment">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-or-pull-request-for-more-information-about-issues-and-pull-requests-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-and-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issue-comments-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissuecomment-or-issue-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissuescomments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-an-issue-as-opposed-to-comments-on-an-issue-use-the-issue-event-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-or-pull-request-review-comments-use-the-pullrequestreview-or-pullrequestreviewcomment-events-for-more-information-about-the-different-types-of-pull-request-comments-see-working-with-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestguidesworking-with-comments-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-3-responses">Responses</h3>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment on an issue or pull request. For more information about issues and pull requests, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues)&quot; and &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issue comments, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issuecomment) or &quot;[Issue comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to an issue as opposed to comments on an issue, use the `issue` event. For activity related to pull request reviews or pull request review comments, use the `pull_request_review` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. For more information about the different types of pull request comments, see &quot;[Working with comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/working-with-comments).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissue-comment/unpinned"></a>

`POST issue-comment-unpinned`

A comment on an issue was unpinned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue_comment">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to issue dependencies, such as blocking or blocked-by relationships. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-dependencies/blocked-by-added"></a>

`POST issue-dependencies-blocked-by-added`

An issue was marked as blocked by another issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue-dependencies">External documentation</a>

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to issue dependencies, such as blocking or blocked-by relationships. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-dependencies/blocked-by-removed"></a>

`POST issue-dependencies-blocked-by-removed`

The blocked by relationship between an issue and another issue was removed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to issue dependencies, such as blocking or blocked-by relationships. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-dependencies/blocking-added"></a>

`POST issue-dependencies-blocking-added`

An issue was marked as blocking another issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue-dependencies">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to issue dependencies, such as blocking or blocked-by relationships. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-dependencies/blocking-removed"></a>

`POST issue-dependencies-blocking-removed`

The blocking relationship between an issue and another issue was removed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue-dependencies">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a &quot;relates to&quot; relationship between two issues. For relationships between issues in the same repository, GitHub sends one delivery containing both issues. For relationships between issues in different repositories, GitHub sends one delivery for each repository. Each cross-repository delivery contains only the issue in the repository receiving the delivery and omits the related issue, its ID, and its repository details. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-relates-to/relates-to-added"></a>

`POST issue-relates-to-added`

An issue was marked as related to another issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue-relates-to">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a &quot;relates to&quot; relationship between two issues. For relationships between issues in the same repository, GitHub sends one delivery containing both issues. For relationships between issues in different repositories, GitHub sends one delivery for each repository. Each cross-repository delivery contains only the issue in the repository receiving the delivery and omits the related issue, its ID, and its repository details. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdissue-relates-to/relates-to-removed"></a>

`POST issue-relates-to-removed`

An issue's relationship to another issue was removed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue-relates-to">External documentation</a>

|body|body|[webhook-issue-relates-to-removed](#schemawebhook-issue-relates-to-removed)|true|none|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/assigned"></a>

An issue was assigned to a user.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-issues-assigned](#schemawebhook-issues-assigned)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|The action that was performed.|
|» assignee|body|[webhooks_user](#schemawebhooks_user)|false|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» issue|body|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|assigned|

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/closed"></a>

`POST issues-closed`

An issue was closed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/deleted"></a>

`POST issues-deleted`

An issue was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/demilestoned"></a>

`POST issues-demilestoned`

An issue was removed from a milestone.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/edited"></a>

`POST issues-edited`

The title or body on an issue was edited.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-4-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/field-added"></a>

`POST issues-field-added`

An issue field value was set or updated on an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-5-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/field-removed"></a>

`POST issues-field-removed`

An issue field value was cleared from an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-6-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/labeled"></a>

`POST issues-labeled`

A label was added to an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/locked"></a>

`POST issues-locked`

Conversation on an issue was locked. For more information, see "[Locking conversations](https://docs.github.com/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/locking-conversations)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-8-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/milestoned"></a>

`POST issues-milestoned`

An issue was added to a milestone.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-9-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/opened"></a>

`POST issues-opened`

An issue was created. When a closed issue is reopened, the action will be `reopened` instead.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-10-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/pinned"></a>

`POST issues-pinned`

An issue was pinned to a repository. For more information, see "[Pinning an issue to your repository](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/pinning-an-issue-to-your-repository)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

|body|body|[webhook-issues-pinned](#schemawebhook-issues-pinned)|true|none|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/reopened"></a>

`POST issues-reopened`

A closed issue was reopened.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-12-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/transferred"></a>

`POST issues-transferred`

An issue was transferred to another repository. For more information, see "[Transferring an issue to another repository](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/transferring-an-issue-to-another-repository)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-13-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/typed"></a>

`POST issues-typed`

An issue type was added to an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/unassigned"></a>

`POST issues-unassigned`

A user was unassigned from an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-issues-unassigned](#schemawebhook-issues-unassigned)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|The action that was performed.|
|» assignee|body|[webhooks_user_mannequin](#schemawebhooks_user_mannequin)|false|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» issue|body|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|unassigned|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/unlabeled"></a>

`POST issues-unlabeled`

A label was removed from an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/unlocked"></a>

`POST issues-unlocked`

Conversation on an issue was locked. For more information, see "[Locking conversations](https://docs.github.com/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/locking-conversations)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-17-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/unpinned"></a>

`POST issues-unpinned`

An issue was unpinned from a repository. For more information, see "[Pinning an issue to your repository](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/pinning-an-issue-to-your-repository)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-an-issue-for-more-information-about-issues-see-about-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomissuestracking-your-work-with-issuesabout-issues-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-issues-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsissue-or-issueshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissues-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-comment-on-an-issue-use-the-issuecomment-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permission-18-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an issue. For more information about issues, see &quot;[About issues](https://docs.github.com/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage issues, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#issue) or &quot;[Issues](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a comment on an issue, use the `issue_comment` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdissues/untyped"></a>

`POST issues-untyped`

An issue type was removed from an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issues">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "untyped",
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-issues-untyped](#schemawebhook-issues-untyped)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» issue|body|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|» type|body|[issue-type](#schemaissue-type)|true|The type assigned to the issue. This is only present for issues in repositories where issue types are supported.|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to labels. For more information, see &quot;[Managing labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage labels, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#label) or &quot;[Labels](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a label is added to or removed from an issue, pull request, or discussion, use the `labeled` or `unlabeled` action type for the `issues`, `pull_request`, or `discussion` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdlabel/archived"></a>

`POST label-archived`

A label was archived.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#label">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to labels. For more information, see &quot;[Managing labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage labels, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#label) or &quot;[Labels](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a label is added to or removed from an issue, pull request, or discussion, use the `labeled` or `unlabeled` action type for the `issues`, `pull_request`, or `discussion` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdlabel/created"></a>

`POST label-created`

A label was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#label">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to labels. For more information, see &quot;[Managing labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage labels, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#label) or &quot;[Labels](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a label is added to or removed from an issue, pull request, or discussion, use the `labeled` or `unlabeled` action type for the `issues`, `pull_request`, or `discussion` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdlabel/deleted"></a>

`POST label-deleted`

A label was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#label">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to labels. For more information, see &quot;[Managing labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage labels, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#label) or &quot;[Labels](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a label is added to or removed from an issue, pull request, or discussion, use the `labeled` or `unlabeled` action type for the `issues`, `pull_request`, or `discussion` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to labels. For more information, see &quot;[Managing labels](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage labels, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#label) or &quot;[Labels](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/labels)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a label is added to or removed from an issue, pull request, or discussion, use the `labeled` or `unlabeled` action type for the `issues`, `pull_request`, or `discussion` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdlabel/unarchived"></a>

`POST label-unarchived`

A label was unarchived.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub Marketplace purchase. For more information, see &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/marketplace).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Marketplace listings, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#marketplacelisting) or &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdmarketplace-purchase/cancelled"></a>

`POST marketplace-purchase-cancelled`

Someone cancelled a GitHub Marketplace plan, and the last billing cycle has ended. The change will take effect on the account immediately.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#marketplace_purchase">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub Marketplace purchase. For more information, see &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/marketplace).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Marketplace listings, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#marketplacelisting) or &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdmarketplace-purchase/changed"></a>

`POST marketplace-purchase-changed`

Someone upgraded or downgraded a GitHub Marketplace plan, and the last billing cycle has ended. The change will take effect on the account immediately.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#marketplace_purchase">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub Marketplace purchase. For more information, see &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/marketplace).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Marketplace listings, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#marketplacelisting) or &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdmarketplace-purchase/pending-change"></a>

`POST marketplace-purchase-pending-change`

Someone downgraded or cancelled a GitHub Marketplace plan. The new plan or cancellation will take effect at the end of the current billing cycle. When the change takes effect, the `changed` or `cancelled` event will be sent.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#marketplace_purchase">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub Marketplace purchase. For more information, see &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/marketplace).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Marketplace listings, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#marketplacelisting) or &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdmarketplace-purchase/pending-change-cancelled"></a>

`POST marketplace-purchase-pending-change-cancelled`

Someone cancelled a pending change to a GitHub Marketplace plan. Pending changes include plan cancellations and downgrades that will take effect at the end of a billing cycle.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#marketplace_purchase">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-github-marketplace-purchase-for-more-information-see-github-marketplacehttpsdocsgithubcommarketplace-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-github-marketplace-listings-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsmarketplacelisting-or-github-marketplacehttpsdocsgithubcomrestappsmarketplace-in-the-rest-api-documentation-3-responses">Responses</h3>

<aside class="success">

</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a GitHub Marketplace purchase. For more information, see &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/marketplace).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Marketplace listings, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#marketplacelisting) or &quot;[GitHub Marketplace](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/marketplace)&quot; in the REST API documentation.

<a id="opIdmarketplace-purchase/purchased"></a>

`POST marketplace-purchase-purchased`

Someone purchased a GitHub Marketplace plan. The change will take effect on the account immediately.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#marketplace_purchase">External documentation</a>

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to collaborators in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[Adding outside collaborators to repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/adding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organization).&quot; For more information about the API to manage repository collaborators, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositorycollaboratorconnection) or &quot;[Collaborators](https://docs.github.com/rest/collaborators/collaborators)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-collaborators-in-a-repository-for-more-information-see-adding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organizationhttpsdocsgithubcomorganizationsmanaging-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositoriesadding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organization-for-more-information-about-the-api-to-manage-repository-collaborators-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsrepositorycollaboratorconnection-or-collaboratorshttpsdocsgithubcomrestcollaboratorscollaborators-in-the-rest-api-documentation-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-members-organization-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to collaborators in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[Adding outside collaborators to repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/adding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organization).&quot; For more information about the API to manage repository collaborators, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositorycollaboratorconnection) or &quot;[Collaborators](https://docs.github.com/rest/collaborators/collaborators)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdmember/edited"></a>

Permissions were changed for a collaborator on a repository.

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to collaborators in a repository. For more information, see &quot;[Adding outside collaborators to repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/adding-outside-collaborators-to-repositories-in-your-organization).&quot; For more information about the API to manage repository collaborators, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositorycollaboratorconnection) or &quot;[Collaborators](https://docs.github.com/rest/collaborators/collaborators)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdmember/removed"></a>

`POST member-removed`

A collaborator was removed from a repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#member">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to team membership. For more information, see &quot;[About teams](https://docs.github.com/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams).&quot; For more information about the APIs to manage team memberships, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#team) or &quot;[Team members](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdmembership/added"></a>

`POST membership-added`

An organization member was added to a team.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#membership">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-team-membership-for-more-information-see-about-teamshttpsdocsgithubcomorganizationsorganizing-members-into-teamsabout-teams-for-more-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-team-memberships-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsteam-or-team-membershttpsdocsgithubcomrestteamsmembers-in-the-rest-api-documentation-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-members-organization-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to team membership. For more information, see &quot;[About teams](https://docs.github.com/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams).&quot; For more information about the APIs to manage team memberships, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#team) or &quot;[Team members](https://docs.github.com/rest/teams/members)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdmembership/removed"></a>

`POST membership-removed`

An organization member was removed from a team.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#membership">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a merge group in a merge queue. For more information, see &quot;[Managing a merge queue](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Merge queues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdmerge-group/checks-requested"></a>

`POST merge-group-checks-requested`

Status checks were requested for a merge group. This happens when a merge group is created or added to by the merge queue because a pull request was queued.

When you receive this event, you should perform checks on the head SHA and report status back using check runs or commit statuses.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#merge_group">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-merge-group-in-a-merge-queue-for-more-information-see-managing-a-merge-queuehttpsdocsgithubcomrepositoriesconfiguring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repositoryconfiguring-pull-request-mergesmanaging-a-merge-queue-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-merge-queues-repository-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a merge group in a merge queue. For more information, see &quot;[Managing a merge queue](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Merge queues&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdmerge-group/destroyed"></a>

`POST merge-group-destroyed`

The merge queue groups pull requests together to be merged. This event indicates that one of those merge groups was destroyed. This happens when a pull request is removed from the queue: any group containing that pull request is also destroyed.

When you receive this event, you may want to cancel any checks that are running on the head SHA to avoid wasting computing resources on a merge group that will not be used.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#merge_group">External documentation</a>

|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to milestones. For more information, see &quot;[About milestones](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/about-milestones).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage milestones, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#milestone) or &quot;[Milestones](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when an issue or pull request is added to or removed from a milestone, use the `milestoned` or `demilestoned` action type for the `issues` or `pull_request` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; or &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdmilestone/closed"></a>

`POST milestone-closed`

A milestone was closed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#milestone">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to milestones. For more information, see &quot;[About milestones](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/about-milestones).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage milestones, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#milestone) or &quot;[Milestones](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when an issue or pull request is added to or removed from a milestone, use the `milestoned` or `demilestoned` action type for the `issues` or `pull_request` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; or &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permissions.

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to milestones. For more information, see &quot;[About milestones](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/about-milestones).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage milestones, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#milestone) or &quot;[Milestones](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when an issue or pull request is added to or removed from a milestone, use the `milestoned` or `demilestoned` action type for the `issues` or `pull_request` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; or &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdmilestone/deleted"></a>

`POST milestone-deleted`

A milestone was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#milestone">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to milestones. For more information, see &quot;[About milestones](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/about-milestones).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage milestones, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#milestone) or &quot;[Milestones](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when an issue or pull request is added to or removed from a milestone, use the `milestoned` or `demilestoned` action type for the `issues` or `pull_request` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; or &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdmilestone/edited"></a>

`POST milestone-edited`

A milestone was edited.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#milestone">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-milestones-for-more-information-see-about-milestoneshttpsdocsgithubcomissuesusing-labels-and-milestones-to-track-workabout-milestones-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-milestones-see-the-graphql-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsmilestone-or-milestoneshttpsdocsgithubcomrestissuesmilestones-in-the-rest-api-documentation-if-you-want-to-receive-an-event-when-an-issue-or-pull-request-is-added-to-or-removed-from-a-milestone-use-the-milestoned-or-demilestoned-action-type-for-the-issues-or-pullrequest-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-or-pull-requests-repository-permissions-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to milestones. For more information, see &quot;[About milestones](https://docs.github.com/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/about-milestones).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage milestones, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#milestone) or &quot;[Milestones](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/milestones)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when an issue or pull request is added to or removed from a milestone, use the `milestoned` or `demilestoned` action type for the `issues` or `pull_request` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; or &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdmilestone/opened"></a>

`POST milestone-opened`

A milestone was opened.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#milestone">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when organization owners or moderators block or unblock a non-member from collaborating on the organization's repositories. For more information, see &quot;[Blocking a user from your organization](https://docs.github.com/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/blocking-a-user-from-your-organization).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage blocked users, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#userblockedevent) or &quot;[Blocking users](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/blocking)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when members are added or removed from an organization, use the `organization` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorg-block/blocked"></a>

`POST org-block-blocked`

A user was blocked from the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#org_block">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when organization owners or moderators block or unblock a non-member from collaborating on the organization's repositories. For more information, see &quot;[Blocking a user from your organization](https://docs.github.com/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/blocking-a-user-from-your-organization).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage blocked users, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#userblockedevent) or &quot;[Blocking users](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/blocking)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when members are added or removed from an organization, use the `organization` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorg-block/unblocked"></a>

`POST org-block-unblocked`

A previously blocked user was unblocked from the organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#org_block">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization and its members. For more information, see &quot;[About organizations](https://docs.github.com/organizations/collaborating-with-groups-in-organizations/about-organizations).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage organizations, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#organization) or &quot;[Organizations](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a non-member is blocked or unblocked from an organization, use the `org_block` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorganization/deleted"></a>

`POST organization-deleted`

An organization was deleted.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization and its members. For more information, see &quot;[About organizations](https://docs.github.com/organizations/collaborating-with-groups-in-organizations/about-organizations).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage organizations, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#organization) or &quot;[Organizations](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a non-member is blocked or unblocked from an organization, use the `org_block` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorganization/member-added"></a>

`POST organization-member-added`

A member accepted an invitation to join an organization.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#organization">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization and its members. For more information, see &quot;[About organizations](https://docs.github.com/organizations/collaborating-with-groups-in-organizations/about-organizations).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage organizations, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#organization) or &quot;[Organizations](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a non-member is blocked or unblocked from an organization, use the `org_block` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorganization/member-invited"></a>

A member was invited to join the organization.

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization and its members. For more information, see &quot;[About organizations](https://docs.github.com/organizations/collaborating-with-groups-in-organizations/about-organizations).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage organizations, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#organization) or &quot;[Organizations](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a non-member is blocked or unblocked from an organization, use the `org_block` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorganization/member-removed"></a>

`POST organization-member-removed`

A member was removed from the organization.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization and its members. For more information, see &quot;[About organizations](https://docs.github.com/organizations/collaborating-with-groups-in-organizations/about-organizations).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage organizations, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#organization) or &quot;[Organizations](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. If you want to receive an event when a non-member is blocked or unblocked from an organization, use the `org_block` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdorganization/renamed"></a>

`POST organization-renamed`

The name of an organization was changed.

## This event occurs when there is an attempted build of a GitHub Pages site. This event occurs regardless of whether the build is successful. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring a publishing source for your GitHub Pages site](https://docs.github.com/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site).&quot; For information about the API to manage GitHub Pages, see &quot;[Pages](https://docs.github.com/rest/pages)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pages&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpage-build"></a>

`POST page-build`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#page_build">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a request for a fine-grained personal access token to access resources that belong to a resource owner that requires approval for token access. For more information, see &quot;[Creating a personal access token](https://docs.github.com/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/creating-a-personal-access-token).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Personal access token requests&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdpersonal-access-token-request/approved"></a>

`POST personal-access-token-request-approved`

A fine-grained personal access token request was approved.
