<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-you-create-a-new-webhook-the-ping-event-is-a-confirmation-from-github-that-you-configured-the-webhook-correctly-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-ping](#schemawebhook-ping)|true|none|
|» hook|body|object|false|The webhook that is being pinged|
|» » active|body|boolean|true|Determines whether the hook is actually triggered for the events it subscribes to.|
|» » app_id|body|integer|false|Only included for GitHub Apps. When you register a new GitHub App, GitHub sends a ping event to the webhook URL you specified during registration. The GitHub App ID sent in this field is required for authenticating an app.|
|» » config|body|object|true|none|
|» » » content_type|body|[webhook-config-content-type](#schemawebhook-config-content-type)|false|The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.|
|» » » insecure_ssl|body|[webhook-config-insecure-ssl](#schemawebhook-config-insecure-ssl)|false|none|
|» » » secret|body|[webhook-config-secret](#schemawebhook-config-secret)|false|If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).|
|» » » url|body|[webhook-config-url](#schemawebhook-config-url)|false|The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.|
|» » created_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » deliveries_url|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » events|body|[string]|true|Determines what events the hook is triggered for. Default: ['push'].|
|» » id|body|integer|true|Unique identifier of the webhook.|
|» » last_response|body|[hook-response](#schemahook-response)|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|The type of webhook. The only valid value is 'web'.|
|» » ping_url|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » test_url|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » updated_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » url|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» hook_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the webhook that triggered the ping.|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|
|» zen|body|string|false|Random string of GitHub zen.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a card on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a column on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a card on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a column on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-card/created"></a>

`POST project-card-created`

A card was added to a project (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_card">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "created",
  "enterprise": {
    "description": "string",
    "html_url": "https://github.com/enterprises/octo-business",
```

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a card on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a column on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-card/deleted"></a>

`POST project-card-deleted`

A card on a project (classic) was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_card">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-card-on-a-project-classic-for-more-information-see-about-projects-classichttpsdocsgithubcomissuesorganizing-your-work-with-project-boardsmanaging-project-boardsabout-project-boards-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-classic-projects-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsproject-or-projects-classichttpsdocsgithubcomrestprojects-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-project-classic-or-a-column-on-a-project-classic-use-the-project-and-projectcolumn-event-this-event-relates-to-projects-classic-only-for-activity-relating-to-the-new-projects-experience-use-the-projectsv2-event-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-projects-repository-or-organization-permission-2-responses">Responses</h3>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a card on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a column on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-card/edited"></a>

`POST project-card-edited`

A note on a project (classic) was edited.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a card on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a column on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-card/moved"></a>

`POST project-card-moved`

A card on a project (classic) was moved to another column or to another position in its column.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_card">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-card-on-a-project-classic-for-more-information-see-about-projects-classichttpsdocsgithubcomissuesorganizing-your-work-with-project-boardsmanaging-project-boardsabout-project-boards-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-classic-projects-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectsproject-or-projects-classichttpsdocsgithubcomrestprojects-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-project-classic-or-a-column-on-a-project-classic-use-the-project-and-projectcolumn-event-this-event-relates-to-projects-classic-only-for-activity-relating-to-the-new-projects-experience-use-the-projectsv2-event-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-projects-repository-or-organization-permission-4-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a card or column on a project (classic), use the `project_card` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject/closed"></a>

`POST project-closed`

A project (classic) was closed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a column on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a card on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_card` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-column/created"></a>

`POST project-column-created`

A column was added to a project (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_column">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a column on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a card on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_card` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-column/deleted"></a>

`POST project-column-deleted`

A column was deleted from a project (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_column">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a column on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a card on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_card` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-column/edited"></a>

`POST project-column-edited`

The name of a column on a project (classic) was changed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_column">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a column on a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a project (classic) or a card on a project (classic), use the `project` and `project_card` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject-column/moved"></a>

`POST project-column-moved`

A column was moved to a new position on a project (classic).

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project_column">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a card or column on a project (classic), use the `project_card` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject/created"></a>

`POST project-created`

A project (classic) was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a card or column on a project (classic), use the `project_card` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject/deleted"></a>

`POST project-deleted`

A project (classic) was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#project">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a card or column on a project (classic), use the `project_card` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject/edited"></a>

`POST project-edited`

The name or description of a project (classic) was changed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a project (classic). For more information, see &quot;[About projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/issues/organizing-your-work-with-project-boards/managing-project-boards/about-project-boards).&quot; For information about the API to manage classic projects, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#project) or &quot;[Projects (classic)](https://docs.github.com/rest/projects)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a card or column on a project (classic), use the `project_card` and `project_column` event. This event relates to projects (classic) only. For activity relating to the new Projects experience, use the `projects_v2` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdproject/reopened"></a>

`POST project-reopened`

A project (classic) was closed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization-level project. For more information, see &quot;[About Projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects).&quot; For information about the Projects API, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#projectv2). For activity relating to a item on a project, use the `projects_v2_item` event. For activity relating to Projects (classic), use the `project`, `project_card`, and `project_column` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; organization permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for projects are currently in public preview and subject to change. To share feedback about projects webhooks with GitHub, see the [Projects webhook feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/17405).

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an item on an organization-level project. For more information, see &quot;[About Projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects).&quot; For information about the Projects API, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#projectv2item). For activity relating to a project (instead of an item on a project), use the `projects_v2` event. For activity relating to Projects (classic), use the `project`, `project_card`, and `project_column` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; organization permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for projects are currently in public preview and subject to change. To share feedback about projects webhooks with GitHub, see the [Projects webhook feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/17405).

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an item on an organization-level project. For more information, see &quot;[About Projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects).&quot; For information about the Projects API, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#projectv2item). For activity relating to a project (instead of an item on a project), use the `projects_v2` event. For activity relating to Projects (classic), use the `project`, `project_card`, and `project_column` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; organization permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for projects are currently in public preview and subject to change. To share feedback about projects webhooks with GitHub, see the [Projects webhook feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/17405).

<a id="opIdprojects-v2-item/reordered"></a>

`POST projects-v2-item-reordered`

The position of an item in an organization project was changed. For example, an item was moved above or below another item in the table or board layout.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to an organization-level project. For more information, see &quot;[About Projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects).&quot; For information about the Projects API, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#projectv2). For activity relating to a item on a project, use the `projects_v2_item` event. For activity relating to Projects (classic), use the `project`, `project_card`, and `project_column` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; organization permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Webhook events for projects are currently in public preview and subject to change. To share feedback about projects webhooks with GitHub, see the [Projects webhook feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/17405).

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a status update on an organization-level project. For more information, see &quot;[About Projects](https://docs.github.com/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/learning-about-projects/about-projects).&quot; For activity relating to a project, use the `projects_v2` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Projects&quot; organization permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; To share feedback about projects webhooks with GitHub, see the [Projects webhook feedback discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/17405).

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/assigned"></a>

`POST pull-request-assigned`

A pull request was assigned to a user.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/auto-merge-disabled"></a>

`POST pull-request-auto-merge-disabled`

Auto merge was disabled for a pull request. For more information, see "[Automatically merging a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/automatically-merging-a-pull-request)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/auto-merge-enabled"></a>

`POST pull-request-auto-merge-enabled`

Auto merge was enabled for a pull request. For more information, see "[Automatically merging a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/automatically-merging-a-pull-request)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-2-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/closed"></a>

`POST pull-request-closed`

A pull request was closed. If `merged` is false in the webhook payload, the pull request was closed with unmerged commits. If `merged` is true in the webhook payload, the pull request was merged.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/converted-to-draft"></a>

`POST pull-request-converted-to-draft`

A pull request was converted to a draft. For more information, see "[Changing the stage of a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/changing-the-stage-of-a-pull-request)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">

</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/demilestoned"></a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/dequeued"></a>

`POST pull-request-dequeued`

A pull request was removed from the merge queue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-6-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/edited"></a>

`POST pull-request-edited`

The title or body of a pull request was edited, or the base branch of a pull request was changed.

<aside class="success">

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/enqueued"></a>

`POST pull-request-enqueued`

A pull request was added to the merge queue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-8-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/labeled"></a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/locked"></a>

`POST pull-request-locked`

Conversation on a pull request was locked. For more information, see "[Locking conversations](https://docs.github.com/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/locking-conversations)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-10-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/milestoned"></a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/opened"></a>

`POST pull-request-opened`

A pull request was created

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/ready-for-review"></a>

`POST pull-request-ready-for-review`

A draft pull request was marked as ready for review. For more information, see "[Changing the stage of a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/changing-the-stage-of-a-pull-request)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/reopened"></a>

`POST pull-request-reopened`

A previously closed pull request was reopened.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review comment. A pull request review comment is a comment on a pull request's diff. For more information, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request review comments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreviewcomment) or &quot;[Pull request review comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review-comment/created"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-comment-created`

A comment on a pull request diff was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review_comment">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-pull-request-review-comment-a-pull-request-review-comment-is-a-comment-on-a-pull-requests-diff-for-more-information-see-commenting-on-a-pull-requesthttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsreviewing-changes-in-pull-requestscommenting-on-a-pull-requestadding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-request-review-comments-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequestreviewcomment-or-pull-request-review-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullscomments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review comment. A pull request review comment is a comment on a pull request's diff. For more information, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request review comments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreviewcomment) or &quot;[Pull request review comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review-comment/deleted"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-comment-deleted`

A comment on a pull request diff was deleted.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-pull-request-review-comment-deleted](#schemawebhook-pull-request-review-comment-deleted)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» comment|body|[webhooks_review_comment](#schemawebhooks_review_comment)|true|The [comment](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#get-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request) itself.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. <aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review comment. A pull request review comment is a comment on a pull request's diff. For more information, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request review comments, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreviewcomment) or &quot;[Pull request review comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review-comment/edited"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-comment-edited`

The content of a comment on a pull request diff was changed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review_comment">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review. A pull request review is a group of pull request review comments in addition to a body comment and a state. For more information, see &quot;[About pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request reviews, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreview) or &quot;[Pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review/dismissed"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-dismissed`

A review on a pull request was dismissed.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-pull-request-review-a-pull-request-review-is-a-group-of-pull-request-review-comments-in-addition-to-a-body-comment-and-a-state-for-more-information-see-about-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsreviewing-changes-in-pull-requestsabout-pull-request-reviews-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-request-reviews-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequestreview-or-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullsreviews-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review. A pull request review is a group of pull request review comments in addition to a body comment and a state. For more information, see &quot;[About pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request reviews, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreview) or &quot;[Pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review/edited"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-edited`

The body comment on a pull request review was edited.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-pull-request-review-a-pull-request-review-is-a-group-of-pull-request-review-comments-in-addition-to-a-body-comment-and-a-state-for-more-information-see-about-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsreviewing-changes-in-pull-requestsabout-pull-request-reviews-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-request-reviews-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequestreview-or-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullsreviews-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/review-request-removed"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-request-removed`

A request for review by a person or team was removed from a pull request.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/review-requested"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-requested`

Review by a person or team was requested for a pull request. For more information, see "[Requesting a pull request review](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/requesting-a-pull-request-review)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-16-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a pull request review. A pull request review is a group of pull request review comments in addition to a body comment and a state. For more information, see &quot;[About pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request reviews, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreview) or &quot;[Pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/reviews)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review/submitted"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-submitted`

A review on a pull request was submitted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment thread on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request reviews, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreviewthread) or &quot;[Pull request review comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request reviews, use the `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review-thread/resolved"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-thread-resolved`

A comment thread on a pull request was marked as resolved.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review_thread">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-comment-thread-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsreviewing-changes-in-pull-requestsabout-pull-request-reviews-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-request-reviews-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequestreviewthread-or-pull-request-review-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullscomments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-reviews-use-the-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreview-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a comment thread on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull request reviews](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull request reviews, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequestreviewthread) or &quot;[Pull request review comments](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request reviews, use the `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request-review-thread/unresolved"></a>

`POST pull-request-review-thread-unresolved`

A previously resolved comment thread on a pull request was marked as unresolved.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request_review_thread">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-comment-thread-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-request-reviewshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsreviewing-changes-in-pull-requestsabout-pull-request-reviews-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-request-reviews-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequestreviewthread-or-pull-request-review-commentshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullscomments-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-reviews-use-the-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreview-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-17-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/synchronize"></a>

`POST pull-request-synchronize`

A pull request's head branch was updated. For example, the head branch was updated from the base branch or new commits were pushed to the head branch.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/unassigned"></a>

`POST pull-request-unassigned`

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-19-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/unlabeled"></a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-on-a-pull-request-for-more-information-see-about-pull-requestshttpsdocsgithubcompull-requestscollaborating-with-pull-requestsproposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requestsabout-pull-requests-for-information-about-the-apis-to-manage-pull-requests-see-the-graphql-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomgraphqlreferenceobjectspullrequest-or-pullshttpsdocsgithubcomrestpullspulls-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-related-to-pull-request-reviews-pull-request-review-comments-pull-request-comments-or-pull-request-review-threads-use-the-pullrequestreview-pullrequestreviewcomment-issuecomment-or-pullrequestreviewthread-events-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-pull-requests-repository-permission-20-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity on a pull request. For more information, see &quot;[About pull requests](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage pull requests, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#pullrequest) or &quot;[Pulls](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity related to pull request reviews, pull request review comments, pull request comments, or pull request review threads, use the `pull_request_review`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `issue_comment`, or `pull_request_review_thread` events instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Pull requests&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdpull-request/unlocked"></a>

`POST pull-request-unlocked`

Conversation on a pull request was unlocked. For more information, see "[Locking conversations](https://docs.github.com/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/locking-conversations)."

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request">External documentation</a>

|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is a push to a repository branch. This includes when a commit is pushed, when a commit tag is pushed, when a branch is deleted, when a tag is deleted, or when a repository is created from a template. To subscribe to only branch and tag deletions, use the [`delete`](#delete) webhook event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; Events will not be created if more than 5000 branches are pushed at once. Events will not be created for tags when more than three tags are pushed at once.

<a id="opIdpush"></a>

`POST push`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#push">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to GitHub Packages. For more information, see &quot;[Introduction to GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/introduction-to-github-packages).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Packages, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#package) or &quot;[Packages](https://docs.github.com/rest/packages)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To install this event on a GitHub App, the app must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Packages&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; GitHub recommends that you use the newer `package` event instead.
