## This event occurs when there is activity relating to GitHub Packages. For more information, see &quot;[Introduction to GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/introduction-to-github-packages).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage GitHub Packages, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#package) or &quot;[Packages](https://docs.github.com/rest/packages)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To install this event on a GitHub App, the app must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Packages&quot; repository permission. &gt; [!NOTE] &gt; GitHub recommends that you use the newer `package` event instead.

<a id="opIdregistry-package/updated"></a>

`POST registry-package-updated`

A package that was previously published to a registry was updated.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#registry_package">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/created"></a>

`POST release-created`

A draft was saved, or a release or pre-release was published without previously being saved as a draft.

|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|

|body|body|[webhook-release-created](#schemawebhook-release-created)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. |» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/deleted"></a>

`POST release-deleted`

A release, pre-release, or draft release was deleted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#release">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-release-deleted](#schemawebhook-release-deleted)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» release|body|[webhooks_release](#schemawebhooks_release)|true|The [release](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases/releases/#get-a-release) object.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|deleted|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/edited"></a>

`POST release-edited`

The details of a release, pre-release, or draft release were edited. For more information, see "[Managing releases in a repository](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository#editing-a-release)."

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/prereleased"></a>

`POST release-prereleased`

A release was created and identified as a pre-release. A pre-release is a release that is not ready for production and may be unstable.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#release">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/published"></a>

`POST release-published`

A release, pre-release, or draft of a release was published.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#release">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-release-published](#schemawebhook-release-published)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» release|body|[webhooks_release_1](#schemawebhooks_release_1)|true|The [release](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases/releases/#get-a-release) object.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/released"></a>

`POST release-released`

A release was published, or a pre-release was changed to a release.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#release">External documentation</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|

|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-release-released](#schemawebhook-release-released)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» release|body|[webhooks_release](#schemawebhooks_release)|true|The [release](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases/releases/#get-a-release) object.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to releases. For more information, see &quot;[About releases](https://docs.github.com/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage releases, see [the GraphQL API documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#release) or &quot;[Releases](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrelease/unpublished"></a>

`POST release-unpublished`

A release or pre-release was unpublished.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#release">External documentation</a>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-release-unpublished](#schemawebhook-release-unpublished)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» release|body|[webhooks_release_1](#schemawebhooks_release_1)|true|The [release](https://docs.github.com/rest/releases/releases/#get-a-release) object.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a repository security advisory. For more information about repository security advisories, see &quot;[About GitHub Security Advisories for repositories](https://docs.github.com/code-security/repository-security-advisories/about-github-security-advisories-for-repositories).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Repository security advisories&quot; permission.

<a id="opIdrepository-advisory/published"></a>

`POST repository-advisory-published`

A repository security advisory was published.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_advisory">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a repository security advisory. For more information about repository security advisories, see &quot;[About GitHub Security Advisories for repositories](https://docs.github.com/code-security/repository-security-advisories/about-github-security-advisories-for-repositories).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Repository security advisories&quot; permission.

<a id="opIdrepository-advisory/reported"></a>

`POST repository-advisory-reported`

A private vulnerability report was submitted.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_advisory">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/archived"></a>

`POST repository-archived`

A repository was archived.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/created"></a>

`POST repository-created`

A repository was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/deleted"></a>

`POST repository-deleted`

A repository was deleted. GitHub Apps and repository webhooks will not receive this event.

## This event occurs when a GitHub App sends a `POST` request to `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches`. For more information, see [the REST API documentation for creating a repository dispatch event](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#create-a-repository-dispatch-event). In the payload, the `action` will be the `event_type` that was specified in the `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` request body. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Contents&quot; repository permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-a-repository-is-imported-to-github-for-more-information-see-importing-a-repository-with-github-importerhttpsdocsgithubcomget-startedimporting-your-projects-to-githubimporting-source-code-to-githubimporting-a-repository-with-github-importer-for-more-information-about-the-api-to-manage-imports-see-the-rest-api-documentationhttpsdocsgithubcomrestmigrationssource-imports-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-repository-import](#schemawebhook-repository-import)|true|none|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|
|» status|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|success|
|» status|cancelled|
|» status|failure|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/privatized"></a>

`POST repository-privatized`

The visibility of a repository was changed to `private`.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/publicized"></a>

`POST repository-publicized`

The visibility of a repository was changed to `public`.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

For more information about repository rulesets, see &quot;[Managing rulesets](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets).&quot; For more information on managing rulesets via the APIs, see [Repository ruleset](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositoryruleset) in the GraphQL documentation or &quot;[Repository rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/rules)&quot; and &quot;[Organization rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/rules) in the REST API documentation.&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdrepository-ruleset/created"></a>

`POST repository-ruleset-created`

A repository ruleset was created.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repository rulesets. For more information about repository rulesets, see &quot;[Managing rulesets](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets).&quot; For more information on managing rulesets via the APIs, see [Repository ruleset](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositoryruleset) in the GraphQL documentation or &quot;[Repository rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/rules)&quot; and &quot;[Organization rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/rules) in the REST API documentation.&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository or organization permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repository rulesets. For more information about repository rulesets, see &quot;[Managing rulesets](https://docs.github.com/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets).&quot; For more information on managing rulesets via the APIs, see [Repository ruleset](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repositoryruleset) in the GraphQL documentation or &quot;[Repository rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/rules)&quot; and &quot;[Organization rules](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/rules) in the REST API documentation.&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Administration&quot; repository or organization permission.

<a id="opIdrepository-ruleset/edited"></a>

`POST repository-ruleset-edited`

A repository ruleset was edited.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository_ruleset">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/transferred"></a>

`POST repository-transferred`

Ownership of the repository was transferred to a user or organization account. This event is only sent to the account where the ownership is transferred. To receive the `repository.transferred` event, the new owner account must have the GitHub App installed, and the App must be subscribed to "Repository" events.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repositories. For more information, see &quot;[About repositories](https://docs.github.com/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage repositories, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#repository) or &quot;[Repositories](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdrepository/unarchived"></a>

`POST repository-unarchived`

A previously archived repository was unarchived.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#repository">External documentation</a>

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-repository-vulnerability-alert-create](#schemawebhook-repository-vulnerability-alert-create)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» alert|body|[webhooks_alert](#schemawebhooks_alert)|true|The security alert of the vulnerable dependency.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|create|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|

|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-repository-vulnerability-alert-reopen](#schemawebhook-repository-vulnerability-alert-reopen)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» alert|body|[webhooks_alert](#schemawebhooks_alert)|true|The security alert of the vulnerable dependency.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/assigned"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-assigned`

A secret scanning alert was assigned.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/created"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-created`

A secret scanning alert was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to the locations of a secret in a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alerts, use the `secret_scanning_alert` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert-location/created"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-location-created`

A new instance of a previously detected secret was detected in a repository, and the location of the secret was added to the existing alert.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert_location">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/metadata-created"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-metadata-created`

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/metadata-removed"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-metadata-removed`

Metadata was removed from a secret scanning alert.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/publicly-leaked"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-publicly-leaked`

A secret scanning alert was detected in a public repo.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/reopened"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-reopened`

A previously closed secret scanning alert was reopened.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/resolved"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-resolved`

A secret scanning alert was closed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "resolved",
  "alert": {
    "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "locations_url": "http://example.com",
    "resolution": "false_positive",
    "resolved_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/unassigned"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-unassigned`

A secret scanning alert was unassigned.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a secret scanning alert. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; For information about the API to manage secret scanning alerts, see &quot;[Secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to secret scanning alert locations, use the `secret_scanning_alert_location` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-alert/validated"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-alert-validated`

A secret scanning alert was validated.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_alert">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">

## This event occurs when secret scanning completes certain scans on a repository. For more information about secret scanning, see &quot;[About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning).&quot; Scans can originate from multiple events such as updates to a custom pattern, a push to a repository, or updates to patterns from partners. For more information on custom patterns, see &quot;[About custom patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/using-advanced-secret-scanning-and-push-protection-features/custom-patterns).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Secret scanning alerts&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdsecret-scanning-scan/completed"></a>

`POST secret-scanning-scan-completed`

A secret scanning scan was completed.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#secret_scanning_scan">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-secret-scanning-completes-certain-scans-on-a-repository-for-more-information-about-secret-scanning-see-about-secret-scanninghttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitysecret-scanningabout-secret-scanning-scans-can-originate-from-multiple-events-such-as-updates-to-a-custom-pattern-a-push-to-a-repository-or-updates-to-patterns-from-partners-for-more-information-on-custom-patterns-see-about-custom-patternshttpsdocsgithubcomcode-securitysecret-scanningusing-advanced-secret-scanning-and-push-protection-featurescustom-patterns-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-secret-scanning-alerts-repository-permission-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-secret-scanning-scan-completed](#schemawebhook-secret-scanning-scan-completed)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|What type of scan was completed|
|» source|body|string|true|What type of content was scanned|
|» started_at|body|string(date-time)|true|The time that the alert was resolved in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» completed_at|body|string(date-time)|true|The time that the alert was resolved in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.|
|» secret_types|body|[string]|false|List of patterns that were updated. This will be empty for normal backfill scans or custom pattern updates|
|» custom_pattern_name|body|string \| null|false|If the scan was triggered by a custom pattern update, this will be the name of the pattern that was updated|
|» custom_pattern_scope|body|string \| null|false|If the scan was triggered by a custom pattern update, this will be the scope of the pattern that was updated|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» enterprise|body|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|completed|
|» type|backfill|
|» type|custom-pattern-backfill|
|» type|pattern-version-backfill|

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a global security advisory that was reviewed by GitHub. A GitHub-reviewed global security advisory provides information about security vulnerabilities or malware that have been mapped to packages in ecosystems we support. For more information about global security advisories, see &quot;[About global security advisories](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-global-security-advisories).&quot; For information about the API to manage security advisories, see [the REST API documentation](https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/global-advisories) or [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#securityadvisory). GitHub Dependabot alerts are also powered by the security advisory dataset. For more information, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot;

<a id="opIdsecurity-advisory/published"></a>

A security advisory was published to the GitHub community.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a global security advisory that was reviewed by GitHub. A GitHub-reviewed global security advisory provides information about security vulnerabilities or malware that have been mapped to packages in ecosystems we support. For more information about global security advisories, see &quot;[About global security advisories](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-global-security-advisories).&quot; For information about the API to manage security advisories, see [the REST API documentation](https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/global-advisories) or [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#securityadvisory). GitHub Dependabot alerts are also powered by the security advisory dataset. For more information, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot;

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a global security advisory that was reviewed by GitHub. A GitHub-reviewed global security advisory provides information about security vulnerabilities or malware that have been mapped to packages in ecosystems we support. For more information about global security advisories, see &quot;[About global security advisories](https://docs.github.com/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-global-security-advisories).&quot; For information about the API to manage security advisories, see [the REST API documentation](https://docs.github.com/rest/security-advisories/global-advisories) or [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#securityadvisory). GitHub Dependabot alerts are also powered by the security advisory dataset. For more information, see &quot;[About Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts).&quot;

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/cancelled"></a>

`POST sponsorship-cancelled`

A sponsorship was cancelled and the last billing cycle has ended.

This event is only sent when a recurring (monthly) sponsorship is cancelled; it is not sent for one-time sponsorships.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#sponsorship">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/created"></a>

A sponsor created a sponsorship for a sponsored account. This event occurs once the payment is successfully processed.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/edited"></a>

`POST sponsorship-edited`

A monthly sponsor changed who can see their sponsorship. If you recognize your sponsors publicly, you may want to update your sponsor recognition to reflect the change when this event occurs.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#sponsorship">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/pending-cancellation"></a>

`POST sponsorship-pending-cancellation`

A sponsor scheduled a cancellation for their sponsorship. The cancellation will become effective on their next billing date.

This event is only sent when a recurring (monthly) sponsorship is cancelled; it is not sent for one-time sponsorships.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/pending-tier-change"></a>

`POST sponsorship-pending-tier-change`

A sponsor scheduled a downgrade to a lower sponsorship tier. The new tier will become effective on their next billing date.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#sponsorship">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a sponsorship listing. For more information, see &quot;[About GitHub Sponsors](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/getting-started-with-github-sponsors/about-github-sponsors).&quot; For information about the API to manage sponsors, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#sponsorship). You can only create a sponsorship webhook on GitHub.com. For more information, see &quot;[Configuring webhooks for events in your sponsored account](https://docs.github.com/sponsors/integrating-with-github-sponsors/configuring-webhooks-for-events-in-your-sponsored-account).&quot;

<a id="opIdsponsorship/tier-changed"></a>

`POST sponsorship-tier-changed`

A sponsor changed the tier of their sponsorship and the change has taken effect. If a sponsor upgraded their tier, the change took effect immediately. If a sponsor downgraded their tier, the change took effect at the beginning of the sponsor's next billing cycle.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#sponsorship">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repository stars. For more information about stars, see &quot;[Saving repositories with stars](https://docs.github.com/get-started/exploring-projects-on-github/saving-repositories-with-stars).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage stars, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#starredrepositoryconnection) or &quot;[Starring](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/starring)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdstar/created"></a>

`POST star-created`

Someone starred a repository.

This operation does not require authentication

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to repository stars. For more information about stars, see &quot;[Saving repositories with stars](https://docs.github.com/get-started/exploring-projects-on-github/saving-repositories-with-stars).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage stars, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#starredrepositoryconnection) or &quot;[Starring](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/starring)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdstar/deleted"></a>

`POST star-deleted`

Someone unstarred the repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#star">External documentation</a>

|body|body|[webhook-star-deleted](#schemawebhook-star-deleted)|true|none|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. |» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. <aside class="success">

## This event occurs when the status of a Git commit changes. For example, commits can be marked as `error`, `failure`, `pending`, or `success`. For more information, see &quot;[About status checks](https://docs.github.com/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/collaborating-on-repositories-with-code-quality-features/about-status-checks).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage commit statuses, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#status) or &quot;[Commit statuses](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits/statuses)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Commit statuses&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdstatus"></a>

`POST status`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#status">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to sub-issues. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to sub-issues. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to sub-issues. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

<a id="opIdsub-issues/sub-issue-added"></a>

`POST sub-issues-sub-issue-added`

A sub-issue was added to an issue.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#sub-issues">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-sub-issues-for-activity-relating-to-issues-more-generally-use-the-issues-event-instead-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-issues-repository-permissions-2-responses">Responses</h3>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to sub-issues. For activity relating to issues more generally, use the `issues` event instead. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Issues&quot; repository permissions.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|User-Agent|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Event|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Github-Hook-Installation-Target-Type|header|string|false|none|
|X-GitHub-Delivery|header|string|false|none|
|X-Hub-Signature-256|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[webhook-sub-issues-sub-issue-removed](#schemawebhook-sub-issues-sub-issue-removed)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|
|» sub_issue_id|body|number|false|The ID of the sub-issue.|
|» sub_issue|body|[issue](#schemaissue)|false|Issues are a great way to keep track of tasks, enhancements, and bugs for your projects.|
|» sub_issue_repo|body|[repository](#schemarepository)|false|A repository on GitHub.|
|» parent_issue_id|body|number|true|The ID of the parent issue.|
|» parent_issue|body|[issue](#schemaissue)|true|Issues are a great way to keep track of tasks, enhancements, and bugs for your projects.|
|» installation|body|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|» organization|body|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|» repository|body|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|» sender|body|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|A GitHub user.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|sub_issue_removed|

## This event occurs when a team is added to a repository. For more information, see &quot;[Managing teams and people with access to your repository](https://docs.github.com/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/managing-repository-settings/managing-teams-and-people-with-access-to-your-repository).&quot; For activity relating to teams, see the `teams` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdteam-add"></a>

`POST team-add`

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#team_add">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to teams in an organization. For more information, see &quot;[About teams](https://docs.github.com/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

<a id="opIdteam/added-to-repository"></a>

`POST team-added-to-repository`

A team was granted access to a repository.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to teams in an organization. For more information, see &quot;[About teams](https://docs.github.com/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to teams in an organization. For more information, see &quot;[About teams](https://docs.github.com/organizations/organizing-members-into-teams/about-teams).&quot; To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Members&quot; organization permission.

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to watching, or subscribing to, a repository. For more information about watching, see &quot;[Managing your subscriptions](https://docs.github.com/account-and-profile/managing-subscriptions-and-notifications-on-github/managing-subscriptions-for-activity-on-github/managing-your-subscriptions).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage watching, see &quot;[Watching](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/watching)&quot; in the REST API documentation. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Metadata&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdwatch/started"></a>

`POST watch-started`

Someone started watching the repository.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#watch">External documentation</a>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a job in a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[Using jobs in a workflow](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow).&quot; For information about the API to manage workflow jobs, see &quot;[Workflow jobs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a workflow run instead of a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-job/completed"></a>

`POST workflow-job-completed`

A job in a workflow run finished. This event occurs when a job in a workflow is completed, regardless of whether the job was successful or unsuccessful.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_job">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a job in a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[Using jobs in a workflow](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow).&quot; For information about the API to manage workflow jobs, see &quot;[Workflow jobs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a workflow run instead of a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-job/in-progress"></a>

`POST workflow-job-in-progress`

A job in a workflow run started processing on a runner.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_job">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a job in a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[Using jobs in a workflow](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow).&quot; For information about the API to manage workflow jobs, see &quot;[Workflow jobs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a workflow run instead of a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-job/queued"></a>

`POST workflow-job-queued`

A job in a workflow run was created.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_job">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a job in a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[Using jobs in a workflow](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-jobs/using-jobs-in-a-workflow).&quot; For information about the API to manage workflow jobs, see &quot;[Workflow jobs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-jobs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a workflow run instead of a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_run` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-job/waiting"></a>

`POST workflow-job-waiting`

A job in a workflow run was created and is waiting for approvals.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_job">External documentation</a>

<h3 id="this-event-occurs-when-there-is-activity-relating-to-a-job-in-a-github-actions-workflow-for-more-information-see-using-jobs-in-a-workflowhttpsdocsgithubcomactionsusing-jobsusing-jobs-in-a-workflow-for-information-about-the-api-to-manage-workflow-jobs-see-workflow-jobshttpsdocsgithubcomrestactionsworkflow-jobs-in-the-rest-api-documentation-for-activity-relating-to-a-workflow-run-instead-of-a-job-in-a-workflow-run-use-the-workflowrun-event-to-subscribe-to-this-event-a-github-app-must-have-at-least-read-level-access-for-the-actions-repository-permission-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Return a 200 status to indicate that the data was received successfully|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a run of a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[About workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/about-workflows).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage workflow runs, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#workflowrun) or &quot;[Workflow runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_job` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-run/completed"></a>

`POST workflow-run-completed`

A workflow run finished. This event occurs when a workflow run is completed, regardless of whether the workflow was successful or unsuccessful.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_run">External documentation</a>

> Body parameter

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a run of a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[About workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/about-workflows).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage workflow runs, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#workflowrun) or &quot;[Workflow runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_job` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-run/in-progress"></a>

`POST workflow-run-in-progress`

A workflow run started processing on a runner.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_run">External documentation</a>

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## This event occurs when there is activity relating to a run of a GitHub Actions workflow. For more information, see &quot;[About workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/about-workflows).&quot; For information about the APIs to manage workflow runs, see [the GraphQL documentation](https://docs.github.com/graphql/reference/objects#workflowrun) or &quot;[Workflow runs](https://docs.github.com/rest/actions/workflow-runs)&quot; in the REST API documentation. For activity relating to a job in a workflow run, use the `workflow_job` event. To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App must have at least read-level access for the &quot;Actions&quot; repository permission.

<a id="opIdworkflow-run/requested"></a>

`POST workflow-run-requested`

A workflow run was triggered.

<a href="https://docs.github.com/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#workflow_run">External documentation</a>

|nvd_published_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|read-only|The date and time when the advisory was published in the National Vulnerability Database, in ISO 8601 format.<br>This field is only populated when the advisory is imported from the National Vulnerability Database.|
|withdrawn_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|read-only|The date and time of when the advisory was withdrawn, in ISO 8601 format.|
|vulnerabilities|[[vulnerability](#schemavulnerability)]|true|none|The products and respective version ranges affected by the advisory.|
|cvss|object \| null|true|none|none|
|cvss_severities|[cvss-severities](#schemacvss-severities)|false|none|none|
|epss|[security-advisory-epss](#schemasecurity-advisory-epss)|false|read-only|The EPSS scores as calculated by the [Exploit Prediction Scoring System](https://www.first.org/epss).|
|cwes|[object]|true|none|none|
|credits|[object]|true|read-only|The users who contributed to the advisory.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|reviewed|
|type|unreviewed|
|type|malware|
|severity|critical|
|severity|high|
|severity|medium|
|severity|low|
|severity|unknown|

|installations_count|integer|false|none|The number of installations associated with the GitHub app. Only returned when the integration is requesting details about itself.|

<h2 id="tocS_webhook-config-secret">webhook-config-secret</h2>

```

If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).

<h2 id="tocS_webhook-config-insecure-ssl">webhook-config-insecure-ssl</h2>

```json
"\"0\""
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|string|false|none|Determines whether the SSL certificate of the host for `url` will be verified when delivering payloads. Supported values include `0` (verification is performed) and `1` (verification is not performed). The default is `0`. **We strongly recommend not setting this to `1` as you are subject to man-in-the-middle and other attacks.**|
|*oneOf*|number|false|none|none|
