|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|edited|

          "body": "# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct\n\n## Our Pledge\n\nIn the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.\n\n## Our Standards\n\nExamples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:\n\n* Using welcoming and inclusive language\n* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences\n* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism\n* Focusing on what is best for the community\n* Showing empathy towards other community members\n\nExamples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:\n\n* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances\n* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks\n* Public or private harassment\n* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission\n* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting\n\n## Our Responsibilities\n\nProject maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response\n                  to any instances of unacceptable behavior.\n\nProject maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail address,\n                  posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be further defined and clarified by project maintainers.\n\n## Enforcement\n\nInstances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting the project team at [EMAIL]. The project team will review and investigate all complaints, and will respond in a way that it deems appropriate to the circumstances. The project team is obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.\n\nProject maintainers who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the project's leadership.\n\n## Attribution\n\nThis Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](http://contributor-covenant.org), version 1.4, available at [http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4](http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).\n",

          "url": "https://api.github.com/codes_of_conduct/contributor_covenant",
          "body": "# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct\n\n## Our Pledge\n\nIn the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.\n\n## Our Standards\n\nExamples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:\n\n* Using welcoming and inclusive language\n* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences\n* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism\n* Focusing on what is best for the community\n* Showing empathy towards other community members\n\nExamples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:\n\n* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances\n* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks\n* Public or private harassment\n* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission\n* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting\n\n## Our Responsibilities\n\nProject maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response\n                  to any instances of unacceptable behavior.\n\nProject maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail address,\n                  posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be further defined and clarified by project maintainers.\n\n## Enforcement\n\nInstances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting the project team at [EMAIL]. The project team will review and investigate all complaints, and will respond in a way that it deems appropriate to the circumstances. The project team is obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.\n\nProject maintainers who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the project's leadership.\n\n## Attribution\n\nThis Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](http://contributor-covenant.org), version 1.4, available at [http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4](http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).\n",
          "html_url": "http://example.com"

          "url": "https://api.github.com/codes_of_conduct/contributor_covenant",
          "body": "# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct\n\n## Our Pledge\n\nIn the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.\n\n## Our Standards\n\nExamples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:\n\n* Using welcoming and inclusive language\n* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences\n* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism\n* Focusing on what is best for the community\n* Showing empathy towards other community members\n\nExamples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:\n\n* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances\n* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks\n* Public or private harassment\n* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission\n* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting\n\n## Our Responsibilities\n\nProject maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response\n                  to any instances of unacceptable behavior.\n\nProject maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail address,\n                  posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be further defined and clarified by project maintainers.\n\n## Enforcement\n\nInstances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting the project team at [EMAIL]. The project team will review and investigate all complaints, and will respond in a way that it deems appropriate to the circumstances. The project team is obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.\n\nProject maintainers who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the project's leadership.\n\n## Attribution\n\nThis Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](http://contributor-covenant.org), version 1.4, available at [http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4](http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).\n",

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|alert|object|true|none|The code scanning alert involved in the event.|
|commit_oid|[webhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid)|true|none|The commit SHA of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|ref|[webhooks_code_scanning_ref](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_ref)|true|none|The Git reference of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|created|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|alert|object|true|none|The code scanning alert involved in the event.|
|commit_oid|[webhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid)|true|none|The commit SHA of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|ref|[webhooks_code_scanning_ref](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_ref)|true|none|The Git reference of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|fixed|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|alert|object|true|none|The code scanning alert involved in the event.|
|commit_oid|string \| null|true|none|The commit SHA of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|ref|string \| null|true|none|The Git reference of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|reopened|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|alert|object|true|none|The code scanning alert involved in the event.|
|commit_oid|[webhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_commit_oid)|true|none|The commit SHA of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|ref|[webhooks_code_scanning_ref](#schemawebhooks_code_scanning_ref)|true|none|The Git reference of the code scanning alert. When the action is `reopened_by_user` or `closed_by_user`, the event was triggered by the `sender` and this value will be empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|reopened_by_user|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pusher_type|[webhooks_deploy_pusher_type](#schemawebhooks_deploy_pusher_type)|true|none|The pusher type for the event. Can be either `user` or a deploy key.|
|ref|[webhooks_ref_0](#schemawebhooks_ref_0)|true|none|The [`git ref`](https://docs.github.com/rest/git/refs#get-a-reference) resource.|
|ref_type|string|true|none|The type of Git ref object deleted in the repository.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|
|workflow|[webhooks_workflow](#schemawebhooks_workflow)|true|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|false|none|none|
|environment|string|false|none|The name of the environment that has the deployment protection rule.|
|event|string|false|none|The event that triggered the deployment protection rule.|
|sha|string|false|none|The commit SHA that triggered the workflow. Always populated from the check suite, regardless of whether a deployment is created.|
|ref|string|false|none|The ref (branch or tag) that triggered the workflow. Always populated from the check suite, regardless of whether a deployment is created.|
|deployment_callback_url|string(uri)|false|none|The URL to review the deployment protection rule.|
|deployment|null \| [deployment](#schemadeployment)|false|none|none|
|pull_requests|[[pull-request](#schemapull-request)]|false|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|forkee|object|true|none|The created [`repository`](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository) resource.|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[installation](#schemainstallation)|true|none|Installation|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repositories_added|[webhooks_repositories_added](#schemawebhooks_repositories_added)|true|none|An array of repository objects, which were added to the installation.|
|repositories_removed|[object]|true|none|An array of repository objects, which were removed from the installation. When `repository_selection` changes from `all` to `selected`, this array is empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|repository_selection|[webhooks_repository_selection](#schemawebhooks_repository_selection)|true|none|Describe whether all repositories have been selected or there's a selection involved|
|requester|[webhooks_user](#schemawebhooks_user)|true|none|none|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|added|
|repository_selection|all|
|repository_selection|selected|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[installation](#schemainstallation)|true|none|Installation|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repositories_added|[webhooks_repositories_added](#schemawebhooks_repositories_added)|true|none|An array of repository objects, which were added to the installation.|
|repositories_removed|[object]|true|none|An array of repository objects, which were removed from the installation. When `repository_selection` changes from `all` to `selected`, this array is empty.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|repository_selection|[webhooks_repository_selection](#schemawebhooks_repository_selection)|true|none|Describe whether all repositories have been selected or there's a selection involved|
|requester|[webhooks_user](#schemawebhooks_user)|true|none|none|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|removed|
|repository_selection|all|
|repository_selection|selected|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|issue_id|number|false|none|The ID of the issue the relationship was removed from.|
|issue|[issue](#schemaissue)|false|none|Issues are a great way to keep track of tasks, enhancements, and bugs for your projects.|
|related_issue_id|number|false|none|The ID of the related issue. Only present when both issues belong to the same repository.|
|related_issue|[issue](#schemaissue)|false|none|Issues are a great way to keep track of tasks, enhancements, and bugs for your projects.|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|true|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|issue|object|true|none|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|label|[webhooks_label](#schemawebhooks_label)|false|none|none|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|issue|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|none|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|issue_field|object|true|none|The issue field whose value was cleared from the issue.|
|issue_field_value|object|false|none|The value that was cleared from the issue field.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|

|action|field_removed|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|issue|object|true|none|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|milestone|[webhooks_milestone](#schemawebhooks_milestone)|true|none|A collection of related issues and pull requests.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|issue|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|none|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|type|[issue-type](#schemaissue-type)|true|none|The type assigned to the issue. This is only present for issues in repositories where issue types are supported.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. |installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|issue|[webhooks_issue](#schemawebhooks_issue)|true|none|The [issue](https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/issues#get-an-issue) itself.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|checks_requested|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|reason|string|false|none|Explains why the merge group is being destroyed. The group could have been merged, removed from the queue (dequeued), or invalidated by an earlier queue entry being dequeued (invalidated).|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|merge_group|[merge-group](#schemamerge-group)|true|none|A group of pull requests that the merge queue has grouped together to be merged.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|destroyed|
|reason|merged|
|reason|invalidated|
|reason|dequeued|

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|hook|object|true|none|The deleted webhook. This will contain different keys based on the type of webhook it is: repository, organization, business, app, or GitHub Marketplace.|
|hook_id|integer|true|none|The id of the modified webhook.|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|null \| [repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|none|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|membership|[webhooks_membership](#schemawebhooks_membership)|false|none|The membership between the user and the organization. Not present when the action is `member_invited`.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|true|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|membership|[webhooks_membership](#schemawebhooks_membership)|true|none|The membership between the user and the organization. Not present when the action is `member_invited`.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|true|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|invitation|object|true|none|The invitation for the user or email if the action is `member_invited`.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|true|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|
|user|[webhooks_user](#schemawebhooks_user)|false|none|none|

|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. |organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. |package|object|true|none|Information about the package.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hook|object|false|none|The webhook that is being pinged|
|hook_id|integer|false|none|The ID of the webhook that triggered the ping.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|
|zen|string|false|none|Random string of GitHub zen.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|action|string|true|none|none|
|changes|object|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|project_column|[webhooks_project_column](#schemawebhooks_project_column)|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|project|[webhooks_project](#schemawebhooks_project)|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|false|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. |---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|number|[webhooks_number](#schemawebhooks_number)|true|none|The pull request number.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

|reason|string|true|none|none|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|milestone|[milestone](#schemamilestone)|false|none|A collection of related issues and pull requests.|
|number|[webhooks_number](#schemawebhooks_number)|true|none|The pull request number.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|[webhooks_pull_request_5](#schemawebhooks_pull_request_5)|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|number|[webhooks_number](#schemawebhooks_number)|true|none|The pull request number.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|reason|string|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|comment|object|true|none|The [comment](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#get-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request) itself.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|comment|[webhooks_review_comment](#schemawebhooks_review_comment)|true|none|The [comment](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/comments#get-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request) itself.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|review|object|true|none|The review that was affected.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|stack|[pull-request-stack](#schemapull-request-stack)|false|none|The stack information associated with a pull request.|
|number|[webhooks_number](#schemawebhooks_number)|true|none|The pull request number.|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pull_request|object|true|none|none|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|string|true|none|The SHA of the most recent commit on `ref` after the push.|
|base_ref|[webhooks_nullable_string](#schemawebhooks_nullable_string)|true|none|none|
|before|string|true|none|The SHA of the most recent commit on `ref` before the push.|
|commits|[object]|true|none|An array of commit objects describing the pushed commits. (Pushed commits are all commits that are included in the `compare` between the `before` commit and the `after` commit.) The array includes a maximum of 2048 commits. If necessary, you can use the [Commits API](https://docs.github.com/rest/commits) to fetch additional commits.|
|compare|string|true|none|URL that shows the changes in this `ref` update, from the `before` commit to the `after` commit. For a newly created `ref` that is directly based on the default branch, this is the comparison between the head of the default branch and the `after` commit. Otherwise, this shows all commits until the `after` commit.|
|created|boolean|true|none|Whether this push created the `ref`.|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Whether this push deleted the `ref`.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|forced|boolean|true|none|Whether this push was a force push of the `ref`.|
|head_commit|object \| null|true|none|none|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|pusher|object|true|none|Metaproperties for Git author/committer information.|
|ref|string|true|none|The full git ref that was pushed. Example: `refs/heads/main` or `refs/tags/v3.14.1`.|
|repository|object|true|none|A git repository|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. |organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|

|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|false|none|A GitHub user.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|The `event_type` that was specified in the `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` request body.|
|branch|string|true|none|none|
|client_payload|object \| null|true|none|The `client_payload` that was specified in the `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` request body.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|true|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|

|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|true|none|none|
|alert|object|true|none|The security alert of the vulnerable dependency.|
|enterprise|[enterprise-webhooks](#schemaenterprise-webhooks)|false|none|An enterprise on GitHub. Webhook payloads contain the `enterprise` property when the webhook is configured<br>on an enterprise account or an organization that's part of an enterprise account. For more information,<br>see "[About enterprise accounts](https://docs.github.com/admin/overview/about-enterprise-accounts)."|
|installation|[simple-installation](#schemasimple-installation)|false|none|The GitHub App installation. Webhook payloads contain the `installation` property when the event is configured<br>for and sent to a GitHub App. For more information,<br>see "[Using webhooks with GitHub Apps](https://docs.github.com/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/using-webhooks-with-github-apps)."|
|organization|[organization-simple-webhooks](#schemaorganization-simple-webhooks)|false|none|A GitHub organization. Webhook payloads contain the `organization` property when the webhook is configured for an<br>organization, or when the event occurs from activity in a repository owned by an organization.|
|repository|[repository-webhooks](#schemarepository-webhooks)|true|none|The repository on GitHub where the event occurred. Webhook payloads contain the `repository` property<br>when the event occurs from activity in a repository.|
|sender|[simple-user](#schemasimple-user)|true|none|A GitHub user.|
